9540: A man would like to promise his wife to stop drinking, but he fails to keep his word. For a while it goes well, until one evening he comes home drunk and falls asleep in front of the hearth. The next morning his wife finds a little heap of ash. That is all that is left of the man. She thinks the devil set him on fire. On the whitewashed chimney she sees the black print of a claw.
9556: The farmer's son cries nonstop whenever the farmhand is at the farm. The farmer talks to the farmhand about it, but he says he is innocent. The farmhand comes home and sees his wife busy at the stove. He does not trust her and hides behind the door. Then he sees his wife pressing two dolls against the stove. She says that one doll is the farmer's son. He must pay because the farmer's wife charges too much for the butter. The farmhand makes her promise to stop practising the black arts. From then on the farmer's son cries far less.
9649: For a man who is a conjurer but can also do magic, the prison doors open by themselves. He left the town at four places at the same time.
9650:
Stories about a woman who can foretell the future. She tells a girl that the man she marries will be rejected for military service. She tells another that she must marry quickly. A man who asks how his marriage will go is told he will go to the house of correction because he has something on his conscience. All the predictions come true.
Two people try to fool the fortune teller, but she sees through it and chases them away with the broom.
10675: The narrator cannot bear to stay in a certain spot because loud sounds of work can be heard there every night. It is a premonition: later a new house is built on that spot.
10676: People see a house on fire. It is a voorgezicht (a vision of a future event): later the house really does burn down.
10677: At a certain place cries for help can be heard from the water, though nothing is to be seen. It is an omen of an approaching drowning.
10678: A certain man born with a caul often foresees deaths in passing funerals. The clairvoyant also foresaw that Juliana would come to the throne. He also foresaw that a terrible war would come under Beatrix. That war would claim very many victims: only a small number of people would be left.
10679: A man taking three sheep away at night suddenly feels uneasy. The animals also become very restless. Something is wrong, but the man cannot say what it was.
10680: A scoffer boasts that he is not afraid of the devil. Promptly, on his way home from the pub, he is seized by the devil and thrown over the trees.
10681: An indifferent sinner is seized by the devil and hurled down. He is so badly battered that he can only reach his bed by crawling. When he is in bed, the devil also shakes the house back and forth to punish him. After these events the man began to behave a good deal better.
10682: If a dog howls eerily or the bell clangs at a funeral, another death is coming. A woman once foresaw the death of a little boy. The vision came true.
10684: One evening a cyclist is startled by a fat black dog. The animal keeps following him annoyingly and accompanies him to where he has to be. It is the devil.
10685: One evening a man suddenly sees two naked girls floating. They are ghosts.
10689: Witches have little dolls into which they stick pins and needles.
10691: One of seven girls in a household is a nightmare (a mare). To keep nightmares away you must put a wet floorcloth on or in front of the chair by the bed. Sprinkling flour on your face also helps. If the nightmare gets flour on her, she cannot get away. Nightmares enter the house through the keyhole. The narrator also tells that a certain barn is haunted.
10693: A dead girl who was buried in a shroud that was too short keeps wandering around her father and mother in the evenings. The minister addresses her spirit about the unfulfilled wish and then hands the girl a longer shroud. The girl now finds rest.
10694: Dead children who are not given a shroud keep haunting.
10696: Two sorcerers can make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit and march in rank.
10698: With a jack of spades you can conjure up a bottle of liquor.
10700: In the black mirror you can see whom you will marry in the future. If you remain unmarried, you see a coffin.
11485: A farmhand is much troubled by a nightmare, which the others see coming when they look between their fingers while saying grace before supper. He is advised to put his slippers backwards in front of his bed and draw a cross on the floor in chalk. After that he is never troubled by nightmares again.
11486: By bright moonlight a man sees a naked child that was not given a shroud and therefore cannot find rest.
11487: In the old days naked little children who had a wish danced around the barn beams.
11489: The Freemasons get money from the devil at the crossroads. They never lack money. Big Sije is a Freemason. He goes his own way. People say he has a wisseldaalder (a coin that always returns).
11492: In Drachten there was a loose wooden bridge over the canal. The prediction that someone would drown comes true, because an uncle of the narrator drowns at that spot.
11496: Never walk on the left side or in the middle of the road in the dark, or you will get a blow from the devil.
11497: The devil has twisted someone's head around.
11499: A house is haunted at night. Rattling is heard among the clogs, and then a coffin is carried up the ladder. The people move out, and afterwards everyone is afraid of that house.
11500: A woman sees that a man will drown in a canal.
11501: Women see in the cowshed that a cow's place is empty, with only the chain and halter lying there. A little later the cow is standing there again. A year later the cow dies. The chain and halter lie in its place just as was seen.
11502: A woman sees ships sailing over the heath with lanterns in their masts. Years later two canals were dug there.
11504: You get wisseldaalders (coins that always return) at a street corner.
11511: Bread in the keyhole or asafoetida under the threshold as protection against a nightmare that can come through the keyhole.
11517: During the war a woman hears the roof of the house nearly coming down, but when her husband comes home nothing has happened. A year later a few bombs fall near the house, causing exactly what the woman heard.
11518: Promises must be kept, or there is no rest after death. A man promises to take someone somewhere, but murders him on the way. Since then things have gone badly for the murderer, and he is often seen walking with the murdered man.
11519: A corpse that lies in the house over a Sunday means that someone else will soon die.
11520: A dead person gets no rest if people think about the dead.
11521: The first person one meets on the way to the churchyard shows who will be the next in the family to die. If one meets a man, a man will die first; if a woman, a woman; if a child, a child.
11522: One must not long for a beautiful deceased person, for then someone else in the family will die. That is why the dead look serene and beautiful.
11523: A magpie by the house means a letter announcing a death will arrive.
11525: Children buried in a garden later haunt the place.
11531: Men who have been boasting and drinking in a pub are flung about on the way home.
11532: A man who claims he is not afraid of the devil is suddenly lifted up and flung over a tree-lined bank. He breaks his legs and can no longer walk.
11534: A woman sees someone float diagonally across the canal to the churchyard.
11535: A man hears wailing without seeing anything. The next summer he hears the same wailing. It comes from a little boy whose father has been struck by lightning.
11536: At a haunted spot a dog cart is sometimes lifted up and then floats in the air.
11537: In a place without houses a man sees people carrying on wildly, but also shaking hands at the end. A football pitch was later built on that spot.
11538: A woman sees her house burnt down with a scorched elder tree, but nothing is wrong. Much later the house burns down, with a scorched elder tree beside it, just as the woman saw it.
11539: A warning to be careful at a bridge because someone will drown there, which indeed happens.
11541: A neighbour sees how the woman next door can fly by rubbing herself with an ointment and saying a spell. He does the same, but instead of saying over woods and trees he says through woods and trees. As a result he flies through woods and trees and gets filthy.
11544: The number of knots in the rope used to rock the cradle shows how many children a couple will have.
11545: A father who opposes his daughter's marriage and plans to kill one of them is fixed to the spot by a priest until they are married.
11548: Some people who die unexpectedly already carry little living creatures on them while they are alive.
11551: Two haunting lawyers cause so much trouble that they are taken to another place on a farm wagon drawn by two horses. The horses can barely pull the wagon. The land was named Advocatenland (Lawyers' Land).
11552: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck does no one any harm.
11553: Two mowers who one evening clearly see the Lange-Sleatterman standing by their lodging turn back at once and sleep outside.
11555: The parents of a little girl who remains sickly believe she is bewitched. They find wreaths in the pillow and throw them into the stove. A woman who is visiting the neighbour at that moment puts her hands over her face and goes home. The next day her face turns out to be burnt. The child recovers.
11557: The father of a sickly child suspects the neighbour woman of witchcraft. Together with her husband he watches her stick dolls with a pin in various places. At the same moment the child is in pain. The dolls were burned.
11558: A man suddenly sees that a row of houses has disappeared and been replaced by grass on which people are kicking and making a lot of noise. A football pitch was later built on that spot.
11559: The lights a man sees coming towards his house must have been the headlights of the cars that would later drive on the roads built afterwards.
11560: One evening people see all kinds of little lights, including red ones, just like the rear lights of today's bicycles and cars.
11561: A fireball and red streaks in the sky mean war.
11562: A woman born with a caul tells the neighbour's boy that they will both be at a funeral and that she will nod to him when he stands at the gap in the hedge. The boy's father dies. The boy resolves not to stand at the gap in the hedge, but he is pushed that way without noticing. When the neighbour woman sees him, she nods to him.
11564: A farmer sleeping on a praam (flat-bottomed barge) loaded with hay cannot get to sleep. He sees many people walking on the barge. Later a road was built on that spot.
11566: Dreaming of pigs or piglets means coming into contact with the police.
11567: To get a bottle of liquor, the jack of spades must be tied to the bottle, which must then be put outside with the door left ajar. It must be agreed who will take the bottle. Once nobody dares to take the bottle, so it stays floating in the air. Only the sick father dares to take it.
11569: Whoever is dealt the ace of clubs at cards will soon go to a strange place.
11570: A girl learns witchcraft from her mother, for example by turning herself into a little bird sitting on a colander.
11571: Witch's wreaths that have been put in a drawer are limp the next day, because the power has gone out of them. They should have been burnt at once; then the witch would have been taught a lesson.
11572: Witches and nightmares come through the keyhole or the drain hole. As protection, rye bread in the keyhole, because rye is holy.
11574: People are afraid to skate at the spot where, in summer, boatmen have seen skaters fall through the ice and drown.
12136: Long ago the Sint Odolfus monastery in Starum was given a bell as a gift by the people. When the bishop of Utrecht comes to visit, he hands it over to the devil because it has not been consecrated. Two devils come to fetch the bell at twelve o'clock at night, making a hellish racket. The bell ends up in the Fluezen. The next day a skipper sails onto the Fluezen and hears the bell ringing. He recognises the bell of Sint Odolfus.
12146: At a crossroads near Jistrum it was haunted at night. One evening, after a party, one of Durk Jaringa's sons passed that crossroads and saw a white figure floating just in front of him. He ran head over heels back to Jistrum. Later some others took him home past the crossroads, but there was no longer anything to be seen of the figure.
12147: There was once a man who went with his dog cart from Hardegarijp to Bergum. A white figure travelled with him the whole way.
12148: Somewhere between Quatrebras and Burgum there is a pool where the witte juffers (white maidens) would dance when it grew dark. When people came close, they were gone.
12149: The narrator is heading home with a few friends. On the way they meet a white girl moving quickly. She floats towards a cottage. They go to investigate. Later an old man hanged himself, and people say it was connected with this. The minister is very sceptical about the story.
12155: The narrator says he heard in a short conversation with Jannes Bosma that Bosma met someone on the road who had died shortly before.
12156: Piter Claus says he sees someone walking who is already dead.
12157: The narrator heard a story that an old woman was seen in the back of a car. But the woman had been dead for years.
12158: Klaas Boskje has been seen leaning against the gate of his old house. But Boskje died long ago.
12159: A woman misses her dead mother so much that she cannot sleep at night. She calls on the Lord and wants her mother back. Suddenly her mother is standing by the bed. After that she could bear to be without her mother.
12160: People are sleeping in the hay at a farm. At night they see the dead farmer come to tend the horses.
12161: The wilde lantaarn (wild lantern, a will-o'-the-wisp) suddenly appears out of nowhere and wanders across the meadow in the dark. You must not follow the lantern, for then accidents happen. The light looks like the light of a grave.
12167: A farm girl is pregnant by a farmer. It often happened that the farmer then paid the girl off, but this girl was very shy. She stayed with the farmer but found no peace there because the child cried a lot. She murders the child and later returns to her birthplace. But she keeps hearing the voice. She then calls on the devil for help. He is willing to rid her of the screaming in exchange for her soul. The girl is doomed to float over the heath forever.
12170: A merchant is murdered by three farmers because they think he is carrying a lot of money. Since then the place is haunted.
12171: A sister of the narrator lives in the convent. An acquaintance brings her butter. To reach the convent she has to take a little path. A small dog is walking on that path. When she heads home again she gets lost. She sees a dog and thinks there must be people nearby. The dog stands up and it is much bigger than she thought. She is frightened and flees home.
12172: A farm girl is courting a man. The relationship was not approved. They meet at a certain spot. As she goes home, she thinks she sees the young man walking. She follows him, falls into the water and drowns. Because she drowned for that man's sake, her ghost still floats around there.
12173: A farmer has two sons. One cannot be got out of bed in the morning, the other has to do all the work. At some point he is fed up with it and wants to wake his brother up properly. In doing so he hits him on the temple, and his brother dies. The family moves away because they can no longer cope. The linden tree has kept on blooming. The murdered boy still haunts the area.
12177: A woman works as a help in a house. Her employer tells her a story about ghosts.
12178: Near a copse a man murdered his daughter, and her ghost now wanders about in the form of a black dog.
12179: Someone was murdered, and at twelve o'clock at night the ghost wanders near a copse in the form of a black dog. The narrator's father warned about the dog.
12181: On the Lytse Kampen in Bolsward there are two little houses. Poor people live in one, a richer household in the other. In winter the woman of the large household sometimes lent the poor something. One day the rich woman died and her husband was left alone. The poor woman had no intention of paying back the borrowed money. When she comes back from town, a skeleton is sitting on the rain barrel. She thinks it was her neighbour coming to claim her money. The poor woman had no peace until she had paid back what she owed. The narrator also saw the ghost. It stood with a raised fist near twelve women.
12182: A woman is about to give birth. She has two children and murders them. She buries the little bodies under the railway. The children later haunt the place.
12194: At a crossroads you can get a wisseldaalder (a coin that always returns) from the devil.
12203: One evening a man sees a funeral procession pass; he recognises the dead person and the mourners. A blue and a brown horse pull the cart. No one believes what he saw, but some time later the person dies, and a blue-grey and a brown horse pull the cart, because the black horse is changing colour.
12204: A girl sees a horse go wild and die, then be strung up and taken away. When she tells of it the horse is healthy, but a day later what she saw comes true.
12210: A woman standing before a magic mirror is told that she will marry the man she knows who appears in the mirror. She does not want this man, but after some years she meets him again and likes him, after which they marry.
12213: In the past people would put rye bread in the keyhole of the money box and of the door. This served to ward off evil powers such as nightmares. This was done especially on winter days when people went out visiting in the evening.
12221: To prevent nightmares, one must place one clog far away from the other or put the clogs backwards in front of the threshold.
12223: Father, together with two mates, saw three white women. When they came closer, the women had vanished.
12225: Albert Alma is an odd one in his youth. He drinks and fights. When he once comes home around midnight, he thinks the devil is standing in front of him and he fights with him. The house is smashed to pieces. It turns out, however, that he has only been fighting the furniture. His father gives him a talking-to and since then he has been somewhat calmer.
12226: Someone is running along the road. Then someone as heavy as lead jumps on his back. This is the evil one. He has to carry him a long way.
12227: Someone goes to a devil-banisher with his sick child. He finds that the child is bewitched and gives him a potion. He also predicts that a dog will try to take it from him. On the way he meets a dog and hits it with a stick. Later an old woman is covered in bruises. Under threats she mutters a few words while stroking the child's head. The child recovers.
12228: A farmer's child is incurably ill. The farmer often goes hunting. He never hits a hare until one day, but the animal still gets away. When he gets home, his mother turns out to have a cloth around her head. The mother is the one who bewitched the child, and under threats she lifts the spell from the child. The mother can also change into a dog and a cat.
12229: Piter Poes is an exorcist. He also practises witchcraft. Once he suddenly appears as if out of nowhere. He sticks a needle into a doll. The person he has bewitched then feels pain.
12231: Everyone is afraid of the 'Sloten-mannetje' (little man of Sloten). He once murdered a woman. It was now haunted at the junction of four canals. Despite the warnings of others, a skipper moors at the spot where the man always stays. At night, however, his anchors are thrown onto the deck.
12232: Father-in-law sells small livestock and is once at a man's house. The man tells him that his wife's spirit flies around. The man also says he should not drink the tea she makes. The woman is bewitched.
12233: A woman is always ill. She is bewitched. An old woman gives her an apple, which she puts in a sugar bowl. When she wants to eat the apple, it has turned into a toad. The husband strikes the toad with tongs. Later the old woman has a cloth around her head.
12234: Suddenly an old woman is standing behind someone, while a moment before there was nobody to be seen anywhere. The other person concludes that this woman came flying.
12237: A woman can conjure soldiers out of the hearth pit.
12239: A man is a friend of the devil and even makes coffee for him; he was murdered by the devil.
12247: During a card game someone makes sure he gets the bottle of liquor every time.
12251: Parents heard hammers knocking at night, but there was nothing to be seen. The next morning, before the cows are let into the meadow, a gate is built, with the same knocking as in the night.
12252:
A man born with a caul sees a funeral procession; a few days later a woman dies.
He also dares to speak to the dead. A friend promises a dying man that he will see to it that a payment is made. He forgets, whereupon a ghost starts haunting the widow. After the debt is paid the ghost stays away.
12254: A werewolf is a kind of bird.
12255: After a man breaks his promise to his first wife that he would not marry again, she comes back and makes his life miserable. When he can bear it no longer, he hangs himself.
12259: A witch gives a boy a carrot; his father puts the carrot in a pot with a lid. When they later lift the lid, there are two frogs in the pot.
12260: A woman can change into a hare. When the hare is shot at, hit and runs off, the woman goes about bandaged the next day.
12261: A man says he will die because the little owl called down the chimney that he would die this month.
12263: A man throws a pinch of tobacco onto the road a few times and shouts that it is for the devil. Suddenly a sort of basket is sitting on his head. The next day the man is found dead, with his head turned backwards on his body.
12264: Before the tramline is built, people hear the sound of the tram.
12265: Of seven girls in a family, one girl is a nightmare. A nightmare is warded off by putting the clogs upside down in front of the door or making a cross on the path with the clogs. The nightmare cannot get past the cross.
12266: Howling dogs mean a funeral procession.
12267: Years in advance a man says that soldiers will march along a road that is being built.
12270: A man often has to get up at night to see something, usually funeral processions.
12271: The devil gives way to an unbelieving man, who is then converted. He does not want to become a church member together with others, because he also experienced his conversion alone.
12272: A man who drinks, curses and boasts says he is not afraid of the devil. On his way home the devil flings him across the road, because he has said too much.
12274: After a visit where ghosts were talked about, on the way home a big black dog walks right beside a boy, who arrives home wet with the sweat of fear.
12275: A boy was worried for a long time after seeing a funeral procession, but it did not come true.
12276: A bewitched child must drink water in which needles and pins have been boiled.
12279: A dirty stork means bad weather, a clean stork means fine weather.
12280: The call of the little owl means a death.
12289: A man notices that it is getting dark and starting to blow hard. The cause is a flock of starlings. He throws a hammer at the birds but cannot find it again, because there are so many feathers. When he sets fire to a feather, the hammer burns, but the handle remains. That is the work of the devil.
12297: A man hears an enormous noise in the cowshed, but there is nothing to be seen. The same sound is heard when the cows are in the shed.
12302: The devil comes out from behind the mirror when people mock and pull faces in front of it.
12307: Though no one can be seen, banging is heard on the front door, which is never used. The narrator says it means something. Her [family member] falls ill; nine days later the same banging is heard on the front door. It is the doctor.
12308: Women see ships sailing over the land where a canal was later dug.
12316: A wizard or a nightmare can be detected through a keyhole. To get rid of either, one must put rye bread in the hole.
12318: One Sunday grandmother goes to church in Surhuzum with the child. Mother stays home to see to the meal. Now and then she goes to the neighbours and closes the door. When she comes back from a visit to the neighbours, the wizard Hindrik Ophuis is sitting at the table. He has opened the lock of the door with hellish stones. He is eating from a pot of soup. The mother and the child dare not eat the soup. They first take a piece of rye bread and dip it in the soup. Hindrik Ophuis cannot bewitch rye bread.
12320: Hindrik Ophuis and Ruerd van der Veen were friends. They were the strangest characters in Harkema. Ruerd van der Veen was once struck by the devil.
12323: On the Lytse weg between Harkema and Ham a wit wief (white woman) wanders about. She appears in Wytseboer's garden. He murdered his aunt for her money and since then it has been haunted there. All this happens close to the spot where the house of strong Hearke once stood.
12330: There are funeral processions on the road at night. I have often enough heard the funeral clothes flapping.
12331: An aunt of the narrator always knows when a funeral is coming.
12332: Sjoukje Bonnema can see into the future. She saw her daughter's funeral.
12333: Hindrik Vaatstra saw a coffin standing in his yard. Some time later his wife died.
12344: Children are not allowed to skate on the Leeuwenpoel, because someone will drown in this pool. Nor may they wear a red cap, because the one who drowns will be wearing a little red cap.
12346: Reid Keuning is a bicycle repairman in Tille. He has a book of magic. When he reads from it, he can make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. When he reads the same thing from back to front, they go back again.
12347: Old Edzer Cent makes little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. There is a hole under the fire pot that holds ashes. That is where the little soldiers come from. He also walks around the churchyard with a black cat. He can work magic.
12348: A black cat was chased away here. That was Alberts Tet, the wife of Albert Alma, and not Alle Tet. The next day she was black and blue all over.
12349: Willem Ophuis is an uncle of mine. He went to his brother Piter near Eastemar. One evening he returns home. On the black road a foal comes up to him, and this foal keeps following him to his front door in Harkema. Then the animal suddenly disappears. This was the devil.
12350: Joaste Antsje's girl was once brought home at night by a piglet. It was a ghost animal.
12352: Sometimes people return after they have died. They then have a particular desire. If they long for money, the minister must come and speak to them.
12358: Our mother's mother-in-law was a difficult person. She did not go to church and tried to teach the children the wrong commandments. After her death she caused a number of problems and came back a number of times.
12359: I saw my mother after her death wearing a shroud.
12363: One night I heard the sound of hammering near my house. I woke my daughter, but she heard nothing.
12365: Once Feikje comes rushing in and says that soldiers are coming and the war is about to begin. This came true.
12372: My uncle had an encounter with a plaagbeest (tormenting beast). A big black dog came up to him and followed him everywhere. This was probably the devil.
12382: If you tie an ace of clubs under an empty liquor bottle and put it outside in the street, the bottle will be full again the next day.
12383: If a barn owl sits on the crosstree of the mast, it means a disaster will happen. Usually someone on the ship then dies.
12453: In Garyp a black dog always used to run from Koudenburch via the Achterwei to Easterein. People said it was a ghost dog. Jehannes Roels usually carried a stick so he could keep the dog off if need be.
12454: In the meadow of Skûlenboarch a ghost dog walks about with a knitting pot on its head. The narrator saw the dog once when he had to post a letter.
12455: Near Eastermar or the Heechsân a dog jumped up at a woman asking whether she knew him. The dog could evidently talk and it was a ghost dog.
12456: In a house near Skûlenboarch carpenters saw a ghost cat. They went after the animal but could not find it again.
12457: At a fork in the road near Westerein (Westereinde), under Kollumersweach (Kollumerswaag), a group of ghost cats was seen.
12458: A labourer, Sjouke Bijma, was once followed for some time by a black dog.
12459: In Eastermar a house once burned down. The dog that was in the house was burned to death. That night at twelve o'clock they heard the dog bark.
12461: In Boalsert there once lived a couple who had no children. They were jealous of a family with plenty of children. One of the jealous women then began practising witchcraft. She took a little doll and stuck pins into it. One of the children falls ill and the doctors can find nothing. Finally the man goes to an exorcist, who tells him the child is bewitched. The sorceress's husband also has his suspicions and, together with the child's father, keeps watch on his wife. The woman is caught and the pins are removed from the doll. The child then visibly recovers.
12464: Great-grandfather has books of magic. A red band is tied crosswise around these books, and you must read them from back to front. With these books great-grandfather made the horse and cart of someone he disliked stand still. Now that great-grandfather is dead, the children want to get rid of the books. But the books will not go away; even burning them does not help. The son of the late great-grandfather knows what to do: he takes the books to the churchyard and buries them at the head of his father's grave. There the books stay put.
12469: A sheep farmer always has enough money because he bought a wisseldaalder (a coin that always returns) from the devil. He may change the coin, but never spend it entirely. He got the coin by going to the churchyard with a black cat in a sack and calling up the devil there. At a certain spot by the dam the man is always afraid. For there, a man who had also received a wisseldaalder from the devil was robbed of his money and thrown into the ditch. Now the sheep farmer fears that the man will come out of the ditch again.
12475: In a family in Aldegea a child falls ill. The child has been bewitched, but the family does not know who the sorcerer is. The family wounds a black cat that often prowls around the house. The next day an old woman who often visits the family walks about with her hand in a cloth. The family now knows who bewitched the child and no longer lets the old woman into their house. After this the child gets better.
12476: A boy in a family is very often ill. One evening the boy is ill again. The boy's father goes outside and discovers a large group of cats sitting on the roof of the house. The father drives the cats away with spells, Bible verses and a pitchfork.
12486: If you want to obtain a magic coin, you must go with a dead cat in a sack to the crossroads or the churchyard and ask the man you see there (that is the devil) whether he wants to buy a hare for a daalder. Then you give him the sack with the dead cat and you get a magic coin.
12490: If you accept food from a witch, you must spit out the first bite. You must not accept biscuits or sweets at all.
12491: Somewhere it is haunted. Every evening a woman wearing a colourful apron and a cap runs into the lake and disappears in it.
12495: A man can make gnomes come out of the hearth pit.
12496: Rikele Myt is a witch. She threatens to conjure gnomes out of the hearth pit.
12497: A man has died on the moor. His wife says he now belongs to the devil, because he has a wisseldaalder (a magic coin that always returns).
12500: Fifty years ago a woman saw little lights going on and off along a sand road. Those were the later streetlights.
12505: The narrator's great-grandmother sees things that will happen in the future. She sees the lime tree in front of the house being sawn down. The great-grandfather is indeed planning to do that. Instead of sawing, he now chops it down. One branch, however, cannot be chopped and is sawn off. So the great-grandmother is right after all.
12519: Someone can make gnomes come out of the hearth pit.
12526: Some farmyards in Groningen are haunted. If you sleep in the barn you may suddenly be flung away, and sometimes the churning starts by itself.
12527: At the market there are sometimes tents with a mirror in which you can see whom you will marry. Some saw their own funeral procession in it.
12535: A mother troubled by her three boisterous daughters cries out that she wishes they would become wild swans. The neighbour, who can do magic, turns the girls into swans. When the mother misses her children, the neighbour tells her she must call for her eldest daughter to turn the swans back into people.
12542: An unbelieving man goes through the woods at night to the convent where his daughter lives. He meets someone who stops him and beats him black and blue. This is the devil.
12543: Somewhere there is a ghost that stops people.
12544: Somewhere it is haunted. This ghost does nothing. It just leans with its arms on the gate.
12545: Ghosts are cowards; they always come at night.
12546: Someone meets a woman who floats.
12547: Someone sees a ghost and speaks to it. Her brother, however, does not see it.
12548: Two men meet someone at night when there is a layer of snow. Suddenly he vanishes. When they go to look into it, there are no tracks to be found.
12550: Someone looks in a mirror. In it you see whom you will marry. And that always comes true. Grandfather also sees a woman in this mirror and marries her.
12556: To get a wisseldaalder (a coin that always returns) you must sell yourself to the devil and run around the churchyard three times with a black cat. Such a coin never runs out.
12957: A group of men are playing cards in an inn. A stranger wants to join in. At first he wins, but later the other men start winning. When a card falls to the floor, one of the men picks it up. He then looks under the table and sees that the stranger has a goat's hoof. The lamp goes out and the men fly out through the window. When they later return, the stranger has vanished.
12961: A man is not afraid of the devil. When one day he goes to milk cows at a farmer's, the farmer cannot breathe and turns out to have no feet. The man then gets a thrashing from the farmer. Since then the man has never missed a church service.
12962: A farmer drinks far too much. One evening he goes to the inn, where he challenges the devil and swears. He says he is not even afraid of the devil. Suddenly the door opens and the drunkard is sucked outside. His mates cannot find any trace of him. The next day his body is found in a lake three kilometres away.
12965: A woman says she saw a hearse drawn by two horses. She knows which farm the dead person comes from. She also says that one of the horses is not the farmer's own horse. A year later this comes true exactly. The farmer's wife dies, and one of the horses pulling the hearse is borrowed, because the farmer's horse has broken its leg.
12966: A midwife sees a funeral procession pass by. She is surprised, because as far as she knows nobody has died. A few moments later one of the three farmers who live at the nearest farm is standing there. He has probably had a fatal accident. A funeral exactly like the one the midwife has just seen follows shortly afterwards.
12967: A clairvoyant woman tells a man that they will soon be at the same funeral together. She will nod to him when he is standing in front of a gap in a hedge. The man does not believe it, but when his father dies he begins to believe it. He wants to make sure she is not proved right, and so means to avoid standing in front of the gap in the hedge. At the funeral the bearers want to change positions, and before he knows it the man is standing in front of the gap in the hedge. On the other side the clairvoyant woman nods to him.
12968: Our great-uncle is clairvoyant. One day he is mowing grass with some men. He tells the men to look up for a moment because a funeral procession is passing along the road. He says one of his men is in it, and that man's brother-in-law too. A few days later it comes true. When the great-uncle eats his break at his sister's, all the clogs have to be put aside. He wants to be able to get outside easily if another funeral procession comes along the road. He lost two of his daughters, and both times he had already foretold it.
12969: A man was born with a caul and is therefore clairvoyant. When he sees a funeral procession pass, he always has to go and look. Even in the middle of the night he gets up for it, otherwise he gets no more rest.
12970: A grandfather and grandmother see a funeral procession with five men, three women and two people wearing top hats. Grandmother says the procession is crossing the road diagonally. Grandfather does not believe it, but a year later they see exactly the same procession crossing the road diagonally.
12971: A clairvoyant woman is home alone because her husband is travelling. Two men with moustaches come in carrying a small coffin. They put the coffin on the table and then under the clock. Both men suddenly vanish, and so does the coffin. The woman predicts that their little daughter will not live much longer. A few years later the girl does indeed die.
12972: A clairvoyant woman sees a funeral procession come out of the schoolhouse in the middle of the night. The fourth man in the procession is wearing a grey suit, which is still very unusual at that time. Later someone does indeed die in the schoolhouse. The fourth man at the funeral is wearing a grey suit.
12978: A man goes fishing in the evening. When his dog starts howling frighteningly, the fisherman takes it as a bad sign. Suddenly he sees a big black thing approaching over the water, with smoke coming off it. The fisherman gets scared and flees. A few years later a steamboat sails on that same water for the first time. The fisherman had foreseen it all.
13004: Hinse is walking with a purse of money in his pocket. Thieves demand the money from him. But he puts the purse on the ground and draws a circle around it with his stick. Because of this magic circle the thieves can no longer reach the purse, and they flee.
13013: The narrator's great-uncle, Klaas Heddema, is afraid of nothing and no one. He visits Piter Poes, who reads from a book of magic. Suddenly there are black rooks all around the house. Then the door opens and soldiers come in and disappear into the hearth. Klaas is still not impressed and asks whether it can be done another way. Piter now reads the book of magic backwards, and the soldiers come back out of the hearth and walk out the door again. At that moment the rooks disappear too.
13019: Imke pulls leaves off a lime tree. He puts them in a top hat and they turn into guilders. A boy asks whether he may have a few guilders too. He may, but as soon as the boy tries to put the guilders away, they have vanished. The narrator's father often told this.
13023: Imke once punched a hole in a beam with his hand. Another time it looked as if he crawled through a beam. But a man who was born with a caul saw that he crawled behind it.
13024: Imke is in prison. At the same time, however, he is also standing at the market in Groningen. Closed doors are no problem for him. In the end he is released, because they cannot keep him imprisoned anyway.
13244: In a village all the people are rich except one woman. Since there is still a piece of land that belongs to no one, it is decided that the woman will get it. In return she must run naked through the church. She does so reluctantly. Later a wit wief (white woman) can be seen on the land she was given. People are convinced that the woman's ghost still haunts it.
13249: A woman does not dare pass the churchyard, believes she has seen her late husband, and has to be taken home when she sees two figures standing by a gate, which turn out to be two sheep.
13250: Children and servants are warned not to look in the mirror, or else Hansje Pik, the devil, will come and get you.
13258: The werewolf lives deep in the forest, stays invisible to people, punishes bad people and does no harm to good people.
13279: Of the two strangers who join in playing cards on a Sunday, one jumps out through the window after losing again and again; that must be the devil. Devil-banishers lift the spell with a herbal potion and special rituals, and warn that the first person to ask after the sick one is the cause of the illness.
13323: A man finds a rooster on the beach. He puts it in a sack and takes it home. The sack gets heavier and heavier. When he gets home he opens the sack and the devil jumps out. Another version of the story is that his wife was in the sack, wanting to know what her husband was up to.
13341: A robber is skilled in magic. While drinking a dram in an inn, he notices constables coming in to arrest him. As soon as he turns his empty glass upside down on the table, everyone freezes motionless. The robber calmly leaves and on the way asks a little woman to set the glass in the inn upright again. When she has done so, everyone starts moving again. They immediately want to arrest the woman, but she manages to make clear that she was only told to set the glass upright.
13400: A few rascals play a prank with a foal. They tie a heavy porridge pot filled with stones and iron around the foal's neck and chase it through the village. They do this because many villagers still believe the legend of the headless foal. But the prank goes wrong when the foal, in its fright, jumps into a ditch and drowns. The farmers punish the boys severely, and they have to pay back the value of the foal.
13401: A person born with a caul sees a hearse with a grey horse. Shortly afterwards a farmer's wife dies. Her husband harnesses two black horses to the hearse, but they will not move. Only when a white horse is also harnessed can the hearse go.
13413: In the old days people said you should not walk in the middle of the road after dark, or you ran the risk of being thrown to the side of the road or into the verge. It also happened that people were followed by a dog that kept walking along until they reached home. In wooded areas two fiery eyes would sometimes stare at people. Those eyes were the "Evil One", always lying in wait.
13415: On a dark night without moonlight the narrator sets off through the woods. On the way he hears a sound as if something is walking along with him. Each time he stops to see what the sound is, but each time he stops, the strange sound can no longer be heard. He almost starts to believe in phantom animals, until he finds out that the sound comes from a calf that has broken loose and is looking for company.
13416: A witch in the shape of a black cat bewitches a farmer's livestock. The cows no longer give milk and the horses pull the cart listlessly. The farmer discovers that the neighbour woman is the witch when he stabs the black cat with a pitchfork. The next day the neighbour woman walks about with a bandage.
13507: A farm where an executioner once lived is haunted. The executioner died a horrible death and now haunts the farm every year on the anniversary of his death.
13716: Near the 'Spoeketsiene' lies a piece of land called 'Àdvocatenland' (Lawyers' Land), because two dead lawyers are said to haunt it. The people hire an exorcist to get rid of the ghosts. He drives around with a wagon loaded with sacks of gold to lure the lawyers. Then he runs around the wagon, says some spells, and the ghosts are captured. They do resist, but to no avail. At the 'advocatenland' (near the 'Krúswetter') the ghosts are released. According to some, there is a connection between these lawyers and the 'Langesleatter man'.
14748: A cursing, indifferent man is found dead on the ice without any signs of violence. People think the devil had a hand in it, because the farmhand, sitting in a cold room, had said that hell would be better than this.
14751: A woman tells that she was chased by the devil on her way home.
14776: Whoever has sent out a playing card to fetch a bottle of gin must grab the bottle as it floats in, or else the devil will make that person die.
14777: A man who has committed blasphemy has said that if God or the devil exist, he would like to meet them. The next morning he is found dead, with his head turned around and badly battered as a result of a fight with the devil.
14779: A feverish man, while reading a book about the devilish practices of Rasputin, hears noise in the box bed, goes at it with a poker, and sees a figure vanish.
14782: People who do not work and still live well own a wissel(rijks)daalder (a coin that always returns), which keeps coming back into their purse after they have done their shopping with it. The coin is obtained by selling a black tomcat at midnight at new moon.
14785: The devil is beaten so badly by a shepherd, three times over, that he proposes they work together.
14798: A woman sells her soul to the devil, to whom she loses everything, and after the devil has broken her neck, her soul as well. At midnight the woman dressed in white haunts the place, lamenting her sins.
14804: A man is willing to race anyone at mowing with the scythe. His opponent keeps staying just ahead of him, so the challenger sticks a piece of iron into the ground. But the other, the devil, mows straight through grass and iron.
14805: Children are warned not to look in the mirror. The devil sits behind the mirror and grabs children who look in it and takes them away.
14806: Brief remarks on cases of haunting, voorloop (an apparition foreshadowing an event) of death, faces of card players' children marked by cards, drinkers who meet the devil, women who roam at night as cats, taking sick children to an exorcist, remains of material in a cut-open pillow.
14807: One evening a man is attacked by the devil in the shape of a big tomcat, which disappears when he calls on God.
14811: On the way there, the devil in the shape of a black dog walks along with two men. On the way back they meet a devil banisher who has also seen the dog and has banished the devil.
14815: A stranger asks some men to play cards with him. At first the men win everything, but when the stakes get higher they keep losing. When one of the men shouts that he seems to be the devil, the gentleman vanishes through a window that is standing ajar.
14817: One evening a card player can only get home by a detour, because tall men block his way at the entrance gate. The man gave up card playing at once.
14818: Three men playing cards on a Sunday evening let a stranger join in, who, as soon as he loses, smashes the window with his goat's hoof and vanishes. The men never play cards again.
14822: Attempts to approach a foal that walks along with a man in the evening fail. At the first houses of the village the animal disappears.
14823: An exorcist takes a feather wreath out of a sick mother's pillow. The boy who goes along with the exorcist finds that he can read minds and see a real event at a great distance.
14824: A farmer accuses his neighbour woman of bewitching his livestock. She must be the witch, because after the farmer has struck a black cat, the woman turns out to be injured the next morning. The help of the devil banisher in lifting the spell does not do much good.
14828: A skipper sells his soul to the devil. When the devil comes to fetch the skipper, the skipper's mate lights a candle and says that the skipper will go along when the candle has burned down. Before the candle has burned down the mate eats the candle, and the devil leaves angrily.
15507: A jack of spades can provide a new bottle of liquor. But you have to keep to a number of rules.
15508: In an inn a group of men hold a contest. The man who can curse the most and the loudest gets a bottle of jenever. Sjoerd wins the bottle, but is later thoroughly thrashed by the devil. He never fully recovers and lived for one more year.
15511: A man meets a big fellow at night and flees from him. Years later an electricity pole turns out to stand on that very spot.
15512: One day a woman walks past the house where a man has died and hears a hellish racket coming from the barn, as if planks and beams were being thrown around. Later, after an inheritance, the house is demolished and a new one is built on the same spot.
15513: One night while catching moles, two brothers see a small child of about three, wearing a little cap and a little skirt. Its feet are invisible, because the child is floating.
15518: A way to ward off nightmares: put a small heap of asafoetida under the threshold, or lay a handkerchief with asafoetida on the chest.
15521: The story goes around that a little child with red hair and a brown jacket will die in the 'Leeuwemeertje' near Harkema. This was seen in a prophetic vision.
15523: Some people try to stop nightmares by rubbing chalk or flour on their faces. You can also put the clogs outside, just over the threshold.
15524: On the way back from a game of cards, a man is invited in by his newly married friend. While he is having coffee, the other suddenly says: "All little soldiers out of the hut: march!" and to the guest's great astonishment little soldiers walk through the room, four abreast, in a column more than a metre long. On the friend's command, the little soldiers go back into their quarters a little later.
15525: There was a man who could make little soldiers come out of the hearth hole. They wore blue uniforms.
15527: You have to watch out with the devil: you can end up with a stiff leg.
15532: A man is walking through the woods on his way to the notary when he hears a voice close by asking: "Are you there?" He looks around everywhere but cannot find anyone, and he hurries away.
15537: A man who always swore and cursed is hurled over the dyke by an invisible force.
15538: A man was thrown into the water by the devil.
15589: One winter there was so much ice that a dead child could not be taken away across the water. But when the ice is about to be hacked away, a witch says it is not necessary, as it is going to thaw anyway. This prediction comes true, because the witch was born with a caul. Once she is also called in to cure a sick child, but she suggests fetching an exorcist, because the child is bewitched.
15592: A peat worker makes little soldiers come out of a hearth box. Another worker gets a bag of silver coins, which later turn into shells.
15596: Before the tram came to Sumar, some people saw a row of stoves with glowing coals in them. These were the carriages.
15597: Two men are walking along the road in the dark when one pulls the other aside and warns him of a funeral procession. It has passed by, but the other man has seen nothing go past. If the first had not pushed him away, he would have rolled over the hearse.
15607: Around 1915 Sikke Antsje foresaw that a child would drown in the Feanster canal. Soon afterwards a child drowns there.
15610: Some people in Harkema believe in the wisseldaalder (a coin that always returns). Such people sell themselves to the devil. The coin never runs out.
15611: A woman sees bicycle lights on a road in the distance. The lights suddenly come and go. Later these become bicycles.
15612: In Harkema it often happened that someone had seen a house or barn on fire. This was an omen, for later that building often really did burn down.
15620: Around 1886 a minister and an elder go to Smoarhoeke. Something is not right in Smoarhoeke; in the evenings something wanders about. The minister and the elder encounter it and are told that it is the prince of darkness. The minister then asks whether he should not give way to the prince of light. The devil disappears and is never seen again.
15621: One day there is very heavy thunder and lightning. A fireball comes down and a voice says that Friesland will last the longest, but will fare the worst.
15624: A newly married man goes to an inn in Kromelle for a drink. He stays a long time and has to go home in the dark. A little dog follows him past the firewood, down the paths that run diagonally across the fields. The little dog is a warning, and it makes sure the man never goes to the inn again.
15626: The merchant Bokke Noordman goes for a drink in a café on the Fean [Veen]. When he comes out drunk, he is hurled over the tree banks of the cemetery. After this he converted to the church.
15627: If the bell tolls in a deathly way, 'a dead person is hanging on the clapper'. Then someone will die later.
15629: A group of young men go into the café and, for fun, want to imitate the Lord's Supper. When they are about to break the bread, they are thrown out of the café with great force by an invisible power. They came home distraught and never knew peace again. Later things ended badly for them.
15632: A young man goes to the market in Ljouwert [Leeuwarden] and looks in the black mirror. First he sees a black-haired girl, who later becomes his wife. Then he sees his own coffin, and after that three children's coffins. The man and his wife do indeed lose their first three children. Then he sees the coffin of his future wife. His wife does indeed die before he does.
15670: A woman returns from the funeral and hears a voice saying: "The sword shall not depart from your house." Shortly afterwards the third child dies.
15672: A man is picked up by an invisible hand and slammed down some distance further on.
15675: A nasty carpenter was in league with the devil, until one evening he wanted to cross a ditch. He came face to face with a woman who wanted to cross the plank at the same time, but did not speak. Suddenly she picked him up and flung him down some distance away.
15676: A visitor leaves at once when he hears that the man of the house is fighting the devil in the coal shed.
15679: Martens Ale often buys groceries on credit. One day she sees a little heap of vermin lying there. The woman says "No, devil!" and the creature disappears.
15693: A farmer is warned by Antsje Duvelbander that their cat is bewitched. The three sons must catch the cat and break its legs. They do this. The day after, they see an old woman who lives close by with broken legs.
15694: When one morning a magpie keeps flying around the door of the house, a woman says this means someone in the family has died. The rest of the family laughs at it. Later they hear that a daughter of the woman's brother has died.
15695: An old couple has an old dog. One day the neighbours see the dog howling and raging on the east side of the house. A few days later the neighbour who lives to the east of the old couple dies.
15696: The Wargeaster lowland is not right. Someone secretly murdered a baby in a stable there. From that day on the place has been haunted. A girl cannot find her way back to the country house at night. Nothing is heard of her again.
15697: On the Zuiderzee a farmhand is put in a sack and thrown into the water. He drowns. Everyone who now sails past that spot sees the hand of the drowned young man sticking out of the water.
15698: Whenever a skipper comes to Potmarge he sees a little child on his boat, who suddenly disappears. When he speaks to her, it turns out the child had no shroud and drowned naked. The child tells the skipper how to fetch clothes from a woman, and he gives them to the child. After that he never sees the child again.
15700: Freemasons die a strange death. They have made a pact with the devil and once every seven years one of them must die.
15704:
No one dares to sleep on a farm, because at night there is a tremendous noise. There is hammering and sawing; every night it seems as if the place is being rebuilt.
A man refuses to believe it, so he stays there one night. At midnight he hears and sees carpenters climbing the ladders and runs away in fright. Years later the farm really is rebuilt, so it was a premonition.
15705: A man swears and chews tobacco, constantly mentioning the devil. One day he is found hanging dead and pitch-black in a tree: the work of the devil.
15708: Some people heard the sound of the tram long before the rails were laid, or saw its lights.
15709: A sorcerer gave a boy a few pears. Later they turned out to have become toads.
15711: A young man wants to get out of his military service. He keeps escaping from prison through a closed door and drives everyone to despair. When he was discharged, they cut the buttons off his coat and he was seen at four places at the same time.
15717: A man has no money, but the devil promises to give him money: a whole bootful. The man sticks the boot through the roof of the barn, but has secretly removed the sole. In this way he fooled the devil and got a whole heap of money.
15723: A man sees a funeral procession pass by, with a white and a black horse in front of the hearse. He says that someone will therefore die soon, but nobody believes him: there is not even a farmer with a white and a black horse. Yet he soon dies himself, and there are a white and a black horse in front of the hearse after all: borrowed from a neighbour, because the water was too high for the family's own horses.
15724: A man goes from Koaten to Koatsertille [Kootstertille]. On the way he sees a man by a privet hedge who keeps getting smaller. He smells a faint odour and the stranger turns into a child. Again the traveller smells an odour and the child takes the shape of a dog. The man walks on.
15725: A bachelor goes home after visiting a girl in Twizel [Twijzel]. On the way back he sees an old woman. He greets her, but she says nothing. He greets her again, again without reply. Then he sees that she is floating. He makes off as fast as he can.
15726: Two men are going from Jistrum back to Kollumersweach [Kollumerzwaag]. On the way a little woman joins them. Later she turns into a lane and the men see that she is floating. They are afraid.
15727: On a summer Sunday evening, a young man from Kollumsweach [Kollumzwaag] sees a man walking ahead of him. The young man walks faster to catch up, but cannot. The man stands on the dike and the young man does the same. Then the man flies away over the land.
15728: In Wedze there is a tree with a cross. A German was murdered there. One night two polecat hunters walked past. Their two dogs begin to howl and run off. They see something the hunters did not see.
15730: A farmer lives in Koaten. His wife dies and one day comes to him. He says he knows what she wants and that she must go away. Then he does things he had previously neglected to do.
15731: A woman dies in Egypte and visits her husband every day. The man fetches the minister and the woman tells the minister what she desires. The man does what the woman wants and since then there has been no more haunting.
15732: Sytske Koster sees in Eastermar [Oostermeer], in broad daylight, the funeral procession of a woman who died in childbed. Shortly afterwards two more women die in childbed, but neither funeral procession resembles the one Sytske saw. Twenty years later his sister-in-law or daughter-in-law dies. She had exactly the same funeral procession as the one Sytske had seen pass by.
15733: A soldier on leave during the First World War goes home. On the way he sees the coffin of his own child. A few days later his child dies.
15734: Behind the Ham, at a pond, some people hear the voices of two children. Later two children drown there.
15735: A skipper comes to Jistrum. He tells a grain miller that the church will no longer be standing that evening. That very afternoon the church burns down.
15736: A man from Twizelerheide [Twijzelerheide] is lying in bed and sees a coffin being carried inside. He wonders whether it is meant for him. A few weeks later a girl from Hamsterheide comes to stay, and she dies. The coffin is carried in just as the man had seen.
15737: One evening a girl tells her mother that old Antsje has already been laid out. The next day Antsje is still alive. A few days later, however, she suddenly dies.
15738: Sjoerd Klazes Nicolai walks along the sand path to Eastermar. On the way he meets three naked children who walk along with him for quite a while. They say nothing and then suddenly vanish.
15739: At a spot in Feânwalden [Veenwouden], dead people who died years ago come to the door in the evening.
15740: From the Wyldpaed a woman is seen flying with a bread cart. As a cat she flies through the roof.
15741: In Twizelerheide [Twijzelerheide] lives a man who is bewitched. One day seven cats sit in front of the window and leave scratches. The man goes after them, manages to catch a hare and kills it. He gives the hare to the neighbours. They cook the hare and eat it up, but later they had to vomit so hard that they nearly spat out their hearts.
15742: A man in Kollumersweach [Kollumerzwaag] is troubled by cats. One day eleven black cats and one yellow cat are sitting by the door. The man shoots at the yellow one and hits it in the neck. That same day an old woman in the village also has trouble with her neck. When the woman later dies, she is still warm after twenty-four hours.
15745: In Eastemar [Oostermeer] two men are hunting polecats. Then they hear women singing. When they go to see where it comes from, they see only cats in trees singing well-known songs. The men take to their heels.
15746: Someone from Twizelerheide [Twijzelerheide] saw six witches standing around a man. The man was smoking a pipe. The pipe had a blue bowl. The witches were holding a meeting.
15749: One day a woman is walking along the Wedze. She sees a creature with eyes as big as teacups that glow like fire. It happens in broad daylight.
15751: A man is a good sorcerer; his family can or could do magic too.
15755: Two farmhands see a woman walking. She goes through a field gate, and it looks as if she disappears under the ground.
15757: A man sees a woman come out of a tree and float over the land. When he recognises her and calls her name, she disappears.
15758: After his death the lord of a castle haunts the area and frightens people. A man who claims an encounter would not bother him gets a terrible fright all the same.
15760: A ghostly black dog walks along with people and suddenly vanishes.
15761: One evening some people in Kûkherne see a little boy on crutches walking onto the farmyard of a young couple. The following year a boy is born to that couple who later has to walk on crutches.
15762: A woman hears the trains from Grins to Harns and cannot sleep for the noise. Only later is the railway actually built.
15763: Two men hear hammering and knocking at night on a piece of land near the Kollumersweagerlânnen. Later a farm is built there.
15764: People hear a thud on the Twizelerheide, and some time later a barn is built on that spot.
15766: A castle once stood by the Skilige Piip. The lord of the castle was murdered and ever since it has been haunted there. People have seen his ghost by the Boppewei, sometimes even in broad daylight.
15768: In Koaten a big black dog haunted the place at night, frightening people. In Kollumersweach there was also such a dog about at night.
15771: In the evening a man is hurled from one side of the road to the other.
15772: A bad man lives in Kollumersweach. One night Hantsje grabs him and hurls him a long way off.
15773: One bright moonlit evening a group of boys from Koaten stand talking together. Suddenly they see a big fellow walking towards them. The man says nothing and just walks on. One of the boys follows him, but the man suddenly vanishes. The next day the boy goes to fetch a bucket of water from the yard where the fellow had been seen. He is then flung away, bucket and all, by the fellow. Afterwards he is quite ill.
15774: A strange man from Feanwâldsterwâl, when he is drunk, is grabbed by someone unknown and hurled away. After that he never goes to the inn again.
15775: A farmer in Zoutkamp has a new farmhand. Together with the youngest farmhand they must spread mud over the land. The first two days they do nothing, and when on the third day he asks whether anything will come of it, the new farmhand says it will be finished that day. He calls out: Now go, and the mud is spread over the land by invisible hands. Things do not always go well for the farmhand, for one day another man starts moaning that it is coming, and then the evil man leaves and takes the moaner with him.
15777: One morning a man drives to the market with two farmers. One of the farmers has a voorgezicht (a vision of a future event) of a fire. When they return in the evening, the farm turns out to have burnt down.
15778: Knjillis Veenstra was born with a caul. At night he often has to go out to see something, sometimes during the day too. Gates and doors then open for him by themselves. Once he says that a funeral procession will soon pass with a white horse in front. A week later that happens.
15781: A farmer's wife who gave too little butter when selling finds no rest after her death. After she appears to her children and her husband, he asks the housekeeper to ask her what she wishes. The woman asks for the shortfalls to be made up. Once the wish is fulfilled, the woman no longer appears.
15784: Lying the wrong way round in bed to ward off nightmares.
15788: The second time a man meets a black cat on the road, it follows him home. The man does not let the cat in, so the cat climbs onto the roof and makes such a racket that the house shakes.
15789: At night a man lying in bed sees a girl standing by the table, where a small light is burning. He looks at the girl, and when she looks at him she becomes frightened. He looks at the wall, and when he looks back into the room the girl has disappeared.
15802: In de Tike, clear sounds of carpentry are heard in a house one Sunday while the man of the house is not at home. Later the house is renovated; so it was a vision.
15803: Two people living on the Hege Wei hear hammering. They think someone is hammering outside but can see nothing. Later a new building is put up opposite their house.
15804: People see little lights by the road from Wierren. Later houses are built there. The cyclists' lamps were the lights the people had seen.
15805: People see the tram lights even before the tramline from the Hearrewei to Burgum is laid. That was an omen.
15806: A ghostly apparition haunts the Hearrewei.
15807: Somewhere in Geryp a piece of wood lies across the ditch. If you try to walk across it, you are attacked by the big heavy dog. The dog is thought to be the devil. A great curser was once badly mauled when he tried it.
15809: When children are born with membranes over their eyes, the doctor or midwife removes and keeps them. The child can then later see into the future. The child was born with a caul.
15811: A house in Aldegea still has to be finished. The people hear hammering in the attic, but no one can be seen. Afterwards the house is finished. So the hammering was an omen.
15812: People heard the tram over the Sumarreheide before it ran there.
15814: A fellow curses a lot and says he does not believe in God or the devil. His friends dare him to walk across the churchyard three times calling on God and the devil. The first two times nothing happens. The third time the friends hear a loud scream and see a black handprint on the man's shoulder. That was a sign of evil. The man lives only three more days.
15872: Reid Keuning from Koatstertille can make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. They then come marching across the floor.
15874: Some people send out a playing card (and so lose the game?). They have to finish off a bottle of liquor. If they do not manage it, they will not get away alive.
15875: Wibe Hut sits drunk in an inn in Eastermar. He says he would gladly fight the devil. As he walks home, he meets a little dog on the heath that keeps following him. When Wibe gets home and goes to sleep in the back of the house, the little dog, which is really the devil, flings him across the room.
15876: Piter goes home after midnight after visiting his girl. On the way he thinks he sees his father, mother and sister walking, but he cannot catch up with them. At the door of their house they suddenly vanish, and when he goes inside Piter sees that they are already asleep. It turns out they were home before midnight. Piter is afraid.
15877: On his way home from his girlfriend's, a man sees a wagon that is taller than normal. Later a car really does come to stand in front of the door. That is the car the man had seen.
15878: When a couple bring planks into the house to build a barn, at night they hear the sound of wooden planks being lifted onto shoulders. Only a week later does this really happen, and the husband and wife hear the same sound as that night.
15879: Someone clearly hears hammering. A fortnight later a new house stands on that spot.
15880: Edzers Griet says that a new house will be built across the road; she has already heard the hammering. Later a new house is built there, which Sibe and Gearte move into.
15882: A man marries for the second time at the age of 65. When he dies, the children and the second wife quarrel over where he should be buried. The quarrel grows worse when it turns out that the wife inherits everything from the man and that this inheritance will pass to her children and not to the children from the man's first marriage. Wopke, one of those cheated, curses loudly and then sees his father beside a great fire of hell. He is the only one who can see it. Only when Wopke promises to stop cursing does the vision go away. Wopke becomes a completely different person.
15883: A man sets out on a Saturday evening and passes the house of Anne Hoeksema. In the bend after it he is thrown to the side of the road, but nothing happens to him or his moped. A month later Anne Hoeksema has a child, and in the bend where the incident took place Douwe sees the coffin of the little child being carried to the churchyard.
15886: Ymke de Jong, a conjurer, is in the prison of Ljouwert. Every time he manages to unbolt the door, and in the end he escapes by way of the canal. He can sit on the water and resurface in a completely different place.
15888: It is haunted by the big oak tree near the concrete road. Alde Aen Klokje [Aen Alma] sees him and greets the ghost. The ghost says nothing back, and Aen remarks on this. When he looks round, the ghost has vanished. Then Aen becomes frightened.
15889: At the big oak tree, Alle Wagenaar, on his way home from work, is hurled across the road. His bicycle lies in the ditch.
15891: Someone sees a lamp burning on the heath, where there is nothing but broom. The mother says that a house will be built there. This turns out to be true.
15892: People often see flying little lanterns on the heath. Later, bicycles and mopeds come to ride there.
15893: Feikje Pot saw a tram running across the heath, but it never actually came. She also predicts that war is coming, because she has seen soldiers walking over the Feanster bridge. This really comes true.
15895: Teake Postma was born with a caul and can see future events. He sees the funeral of Lefferts Willemke in Bosk fourteen days in advance and sees exactly what the funeral procession will look like.
15896: Bouke Schievink swears a lot and his neck is wrung. The devil did it.
15897: Durk Tabak sees the future house of himself and his girl Sweantje on fire. However, it is the house next to theirs that burns down, not Durk's.
15899: Edzer Sint says that Aen can get money if at midnight he goes around the churchyard three times with a black cat and asks who wants his cat. Aen does not trust it and does not do it.
15903: Tryntsje goes to fetch milk from Jan Goaitsens. As she walks back past the churchyard, she is thrown into the ditch by an invisible force. All the milk is gone. There must have been a funeral procession that she could not see.
15904: Alle Tet is the greatest witch of the Heide. She is especially out to get children. She also tries to bewitch the child of Roele Akke. When the parents go out to the potato field, she tries to get the child in her power. Alle Tet sells pot lids. In Harkema they are called kruispannen (cross pans), because there is often a cross on the underside.
15907: Two men go hunting. One shoots a hare that somersaults twice. The second man shoots a hare that, as predicted, somersaults three times. When they go to fetch that hare, it has vanished. It was a sorceress who had turned herself into a hare.
15908: Cases of voorgezicht (a vision of a future event) of fire and building that came true.
15909: Light phenomena foretell the coming of the bicycle.
15910: A light phenomenon foretells the coming of a house.
15911: A fortune teller can successfully see into the future by laying cards. She sees marriages, deaths, accidents, lawsuits and earnings.
16029: When churning, the milk kept foaming and the butter-making failed. The farmer goes with a devil-banisher to the meadow, where the devil-banisher fights the devil and defeats him. After the milk has been thrown away and the churn thoroughly cleaned, butter-making succeeds again.
16035: A wizard uses a formula to spoil a conjurer's show (making the tricks visible), to the latter's fury.
16042: Freemasons always have money. They lend it to each other. There are also Freemasons who have a wisseldaalder (a coin that always returns). They have sold their souls to the devil. In Sneek there is a Freemasons' building; they have to enter it backwards.
16051: If wreaths were found in the pillow, they had to be burnt in the stove. But first the chimney had to be properly sealed so that the witch could not get in. If the chimney is left open, the burning of the wreaths will not succeed.
16054:
The narrator was coming back from his girl early one morning. At the Swadde [a body of water] someone ran very fast behind him. He was followed so closely that he had to run to a tree by the Swadde. Then the pursuer went past. It was the evil one, the devil.
Another time he was chased again. He grabbed his pursuer and threw him into the Swadde. It was Jan.
16056: A child was bewitched. It raved day and night. The father went outside with a gun. Five cats were sitting in the kale. One of them was three-coloured. He shot it through the throat. Later an old woman in the neighbourhood had a hole in her neck. She died of it. She was an old witch. The child got better again.
16058: A fortune teller once predicted to a capitalist that he would become as poor as the Lady of Stavoren. They became even poorer.
16059: The narrator's mother once saw a light burning. She predicted that a new house would come there, because the light was already burning. Shortly afterwards a new house came.
16060: Some people here heard and saw the railway line beforehand.
16061: Old Piter's Willemke was a nightmare (a mare). She came through the keyhole or down the chimney and would also let herself be locked in. Against a nightmare you must sprinkle flour. If they get it on them, they can no longer leave the house. Piter Kimp always heard the nightmare coming. One evening one was sitting on top of him.
16066: Sjoerd, the narrator's brother, said that one evening his mother warned him not to go out, but he said: "I'm going, even if the devil stood before me." A little later he was back. He had met a big black beast, like a large dog with eyes like tea saucers. A plaagbeest (tormenting beast). Evil itself.
16067: The narrator had seen the lamp of their house burning in advance. That spot was otherwise dark.
16068:
The narrator's family had heard the hammering on the Malmoune in advance (the Malmoune was a square house for four antisocial families; it was demolished a few years ago).
They also heard in advance the sawing and throwing of beams for the house that Sjoerd Stienstra came to live in.
16070: Sytske, the wife of Knjillis, said that once six magpies came one after the other to her at the pump. It was just like a funeral. Less than two weeks later her little daughter was dead. She was six years old.
16071: When the little daughter of Tryn, Willem's wife, was run over and killed by a flour wagon, three magpies came into her yard to bring her the news.
16072: When her niece Anne, the daughter of her sister Saek, was at the narrator's home, the magpies chattered loudly in a tree. The narrator said that an ambulance would soon be standing there. Indeed, the ambulance stood on that very spot when Anne broke her arm.
16073: A magpie came onto the windowsill at the narrator's grandmother's. It is bringing me the news, she said. Three weeks later she died.
16074: One night the narrator's father went out to a post to fetch fuel. When he came home her mother said something had been brought into the house. It had scraped against the door and thrown the clogs across the floor. A month later her four-year-old daughter died. When the little coffin was brought that evening, she heard the sound again and the clogs were knocked over again.
16075: A man once saw a foal with a porridge pot around its neck.
16077: Dogs howl eerily when someone is going to die. When Piter's mother had died, a fat, piebald dog stood howling eerily. However often it was chased away, it kept standing there howling.
16078: The narrator's uncle, Kees van Twijzelerheide, once went polecat hunting with her father (Wopke v.d. Bos) in the fields of Oostermeer. Her father said that suddenly a big dog came up to him and would not go away. His own dog crept between his feet in fear.
16083: The narrator's grandmother and her family lived in a haunted house in the Ham. An uncle who lived with her had a goat in the barn that was always untied by the devil. When Old Wagenaar and his wife came to live with them, their two half-year-old children died within a short time. It was a real haunted house, where clumping sounded every night. The narrator was once bewitched by the witch, who had put something in her coffee or tea. The devil had made her ill.
16085: Old Aeltsje is a witch. She put an apple in a pan with a lid on top. When she looked in the pan the next day, there was no apple in it but a toad.
16087:
The wreath must be put dry in a pan on the fire with the lid on. Then the witch has to show herself. Then she flees from the door.
Within seven years the witch must bewitch someone to death. If she does not succeed, she dies herself.
16088: When a witch goes out, her spirit is gone from her body. The body stays at home.
16090: Old Bouke Schievink often sent the jack of spades away to get a bottle of liquor. Someone else had to take the bottle. He was not allowed to do so himself. If there was nobody willing to take the bottle, strange things happened.
16094: A rijksdaalder that the owner of a wisseldaalder (a coin that always returns) throws against a fence sticks there. His brother also has a wisseldaalder and always has money. The whole family gets the nickname Sint (Money).
16098: Harm the Stutterer's shed needs repairing. Two thatchers and the men who lodge with Harm do the job. Harm goes to fetch milk and cakes and takes money for it from a tin cigar box that lay under a bundle of reeds beside the house. The box is full of money.
