18096: In a house a lot of cats were sitting around a pan of porridge. People heard a cat say that they were not allowed to eat any of it as long as the fat dove was not there. The people understood that the cats were witches, and they burned all the cats in the hot porridge.
18106:
One magpie seen: not good.
Two magpies seen: joy.
Three magpies seen: news from afar.
18107: One evening a woman predicted that she would be taken that night, because the magpies were cackling in front of her house. The next morning she lay dead in bed.
18115: A boy, Fokke, goes to visit a new mother. He brings apples, and suddenly a toad with a cloth around its head is sitting on the bed. Probably one of the apples turned into a toad. The toad turns out to be Fokke's mother, a witch. Fokke's sisters were witches too, and later they bewitched Fokke and his brothers as well. It really runs in the family.
18118: A gathering of cats sings Psalm 84. One of the witch cats is hit by a pitchfork. The next day Baeije is in great pain and cannot get out of bed. She was the witch in cat form.
18119: The youngest son of Jehannes Nicolai fan Twizel is a werewolf.
18124: You must never stand in front of the mirror, or you may get a blow from the devil.
18125: At a haunted spot a drunken man is suddenly lifted up and slammed down again a long way further on.
18127: Two men hear sounds of hammering at night. At first they think a coffin is being made for an unexpected death, but when they go to look, the sound stops. When they try to walk away, they hear the hammering again. Later a house was pulled down on that spot and a new house built.
18128: A married couple has a small plot of land in front of the house. The neighbours always see a little light burning there in the evening. When a child of the couple marries, the father builds a small house on that very spot. The lamp that burns there from then on is the same lamp the neighbours saw back then.
18129: At a haunted place people sometimes see a ghost counting its money on a bench.
18140: The narrator says that sometimes a voice of someone in great distress sounds from a small lake. This is said to foreshadow a later death by drowning.
18141: An old man, who is called a prophet, hears the sound of hammering at night. He also hears a voice calling 'make it strong, for it is for the devil'. Later the Reformed church came to stand on that spot.
18142: The narrator says that houses are often later built at places where people hear sounds of hammering.
18143: Two men are on their way home from a pleasant evening and meet a woman who has been dead for a year. They are very astonished and try to touch the woman. Their hands pass right through her and grasp at the air. The woman is a ghost.
18144: A carter is on his way home with a wagon of coal when he bumps into something and goes off the road. It turns out to be a funeral procession, but the carter did not see it himself.
18145: Two mates work as mowers for a farmer. One Sunday morning one of them gets up early to help the farmer's son milk the cows; the other stays comfortably lying in the straw. A little later the mower who stayed behind hears the other coming back from milking: his footsteps can be clearly heard in the barn. When he reaches out his hand to him, he feels nothing. The place beside him is empty.
18146: When the magpies start chattering, a death is often imminent.
18148: Someone sees a little lamp floating in the air at night. Later a factory was built on that spot.
18149: People often see a little light floating at a certain place. Later a new house was built on that spot. Such a floating light is a wilde lantaarn (wild lantern).
18150: People see a little lamp floating above the canal. Later modern electric street lighting was installed on that spot.
18156: Two boys are out on a Sunday evening and pass a place where the devil used to run riot. Suddenly they see two figures loom up in front of them. When they go to look, the two have disappeared. They were ghosts.
18157: To avoid being troubled by nightmares, one should not simply step out of one's slippers and leave them like that before going to bed. The nightmare could then step into them. They had to be placed with the heels against the bed.
18158: A linen merchant wants a roll of linen in his coffin when he dies. Once he has died, his relatives ignore his wish and bury him without linen. Since then someone runs around the house nearly every evening shouting 'Not enough linen! Not enough linen!'. The relatives understand that the merchant's spirit is wandering and still bring a roll of linen to the grave. Since then it has been quiet around the house again.
18160: A boy has a girlfriend, but they break up. When one day he is in a mirror tent to look at the image of his future wife in the mirror, he sees his former girlfriend. He goes to her and tells her they are destined for each other after all. They do marry, but it is not a happy marriage.
18161: Mike Ruerd is a carpenter and roofer. Because he does not feel like going the long way round, he runs straight across a pile of wood on his way home. The devil grabs him and throws him hard to the ground.
18162: A man is sitting by the fire when the devil beckons him from the doorway. The devil lures him to the back of the house and gives him such a going-over that the man is left lying on the ground for dead.
18163: A man born with a caul often has to get out of bed at night to see something. He often has visions because he is clairvoyant.
18164: A pubgoer feels like fighting, with the devil if need be. Promptly the devil appears and mercilessly throws him down.
18179: At a place where the sound of carpentry used to be heard now and then, houses were later built.
18180: At a place where the sound of carpentry could sometimes be heard in the past, new farms were later built.
18181: Someone saw a lantern for just a moment late one evening. When the same thing happened two weeks later, a baby was just being born.
18182: On a Sunday four boys were swimming. One sang: What blooms today, falls away tomorrow. Two hours later he drowned.
18183: In the old days naughty children were frightened by being told: "Mind yourself, or I'll make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit."
18184: People once saw a house on fire, but it was not really burning. Later it burnt down.
18189: A godless, cruel fisherman once wanted to catch an eel bigger than any he had ever seen. When he caught such an eel, it was the devil. Later the fisherman was found with his head turned around.
18190: Someone ran into a hearse at night.
18191: At a place where wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns) were often seen in the past, farms were later built.
18193: On the spot where a church now stands, organ music used to be heard often.
18195: The jack of spades used to be used to get a bottle of gin. But it was a trick: there was always someone in the hallway who was in on it.
18196: If magpies chatter in a farmyard, the man or the woman will die two or three days later.
18197: A mother and daughter often quarrelled. After her mother died, the daughter saw her coming back all the time. That was because of the farm, which the daughter had kept.
18205: A man could not go any further along a road because a large wave was washing over it. According to the man this was an omen of a flood, but that has not happened yet.
18209: Somewhere two little women haunt, holding each other by the arm.
18210: Late one evening two friends saw two girls walking. When they wanted to go up to them, they suddenly disappeared.
18211: One evening two friends saw two young women. When they wanted to speak to them at the bridge, they suddenly disappeared.
18212: The wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns) that were sometimes seen in the past were omens of the later bicycle lights and houses.
18213: Two friends once saw a black thing as big as a person. They wanted to catch up with it to see what exactly it was, but the thing stayed ahead of them the whole time.
18214: Tryn Snipel could read cards. Minse Griper could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit by reading his book of magic backwards. He could also undress people, unless you said: "You won't get me." He often summoned a bottle of liquor with the jack of spades, which then first floated around the lamp. These were devil's arts.
19306:
In the old days women at the market looked in a black mirror to see whom they would marry. If they saw a coffin, they would not marry.
A girl lived in with a shopkeeper who had seven children. When his wife died, the man asked the girl to marry him. She did not want to and went to look in the mirror at the market. There she saw that she would marry a widower with seven children. She then married him after all.
19313: At night a man runs into an exceptionally tall person. The man could not tell whether it was a man or a woman, and the person did not respond to his greeting.
19315: If one heard knocking, it meant a death in the family. If you listened closely it was quiet. But as soon as you stopped paying full attention to it, it started again.
19316: A boastful man always said he had fought the devil and had won every time. One morning he was found with his neck wrung. That time the devil had won.
19317: A boy claimed he could jump further than the devil. When one time he just could not win, it turned out to be the devil.
19318: One Sunday-to-Monday night young people were playing various throwing games when a dog as big as a cow appeared. The Evil One smashed everything and the young people fled.
19324: A widow is said to have killed her two little children. Every evening between dusk and dark the husband and the little children haunt the place.
19326: Magpies are telegrams. They bring people news of misfortune.
19327: At a building site the sound of hammering could often be heard in the evening, while nothing could be seen. It was the hammering of the following day.
19328: A father and son saw a dog on a path, as big as a calf and pitch black. The father did not like dogs and gave the beast a kick. When the beast made no sound, they knew it was not a dog and that it was something evil.
19329: A boy meets a very tall person who does not return his greeting. When he looks closely, he sees that the person has no feet.
19332: A couple's youngest son would never eat. The father took him to a devil-banisher, because they thought he was bewitched. The man would not confirm this, but he had the child eat a kind of chocolate powder three times a day. The boy soon got better. The pedlar who used to come to the door with his wares has not come since.
19334: A man was once cycling along a road when he was suddenly lifted up, bicycle and all, floated through the air and landed in the ditch. There was nobody to be seen, so he thought he had ridden into a hearse.
19335: A pious colporteur once stayed the night with some people. When he came into the bedroom, the devil was sitting on his bed. The man was startled, but not afraid. He prayed on his knees and so drove the devil away.
19336: A man was once talking with a man whose eyes were like burning coals. The sorcerer gave the man an apple, which he kept in the cupboard. The next day nothing was left of the apple but a very big caterpillar.
19340: The future can be foretold not only by laying out cards, but also by looking at coffee grounds in a cup. Someone who can do this is called a kopjeskijker (cup reader).
19342: A man once saw something in a tree and knew it was not right. Frightened, he said: "If you are an angel of light, come to me. But if you are of evil, go away." Then it suddenly vanished.
19343: Two old sisters very much wanted to make their profession of faith. Once one of them was lying in bed when a ray of light appeared in the middle of the night. To her that was a sign that she had to be converted. The other was once sitting in the privy when suddenly a big dog stood before her. This was the devil, who wanted to stop her from being converted. That same year she made her profession of faith.
19345: A man often heard flax being broken in the flax shed before anyone was at work there.
19346: A man who was in league with the devil once came home drunk. The door was already open and a meal stood ready on the table. The man went to the back of the house and climbed up to the loft with a ladder. There the Evil One was waiting for him, and they fought so terribly that the whole loft came crashing down.
19347: Two girls each got an apple from a sorceress. Their father put the apples in a basket, which he hung from the ceiling. A few days later there were two big toads in the basket.
19352: At night people often heard wailing and cries for help from a pond. If they went there, there was nothing. Later someone drowned in it.
19353: Reid Keuning could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
19357: In the old days, when people were drunk, they were often thrown off the road into the ditch by the evil one.
19361: A labourer ran along the dike to his work every morning. One day a very big man ran just as fast as he did on the other side of the dike. But when the labourer went round the bend, the man had suddenly disappeared.
19362: When Reid Keuning pierced a playing card and threw it over his left shoulder, the card fetched a bottle of drink.
19364: A man with a magic coin never lacked money. He had sold his soul to the devil. Sometimes he fought with the devil. The devil also sometimes walked long stretches with him.
19368: If a magpie chatters close to a house, there will be a death in that house.
19369: A fortune teller predicted to a man that he would not live another half year. He could live longer, but he would feel himself stifled. Six weeks later the man was taken off the threshing machine by the police and arrested. For stealing copper he got six months in prison. In the cell he felt so stifled that he hanged himself with a blue bottom sheet.
19370: A man once went to a fortune teller who read cards. After shuffling three times, she laid out three cards. At the first she said: "You do not value this." At the second: "You do not expect this." And at the third: "This will certainly happen."
19371: At the beginning of the Second World War a man had his palm read. The woman predicted that he would soon make a long journey. Shortly afterwards the Germans sent him to the south of France.
19374: If magpies chatter close to the door, someone in the house will die.
19375: If the ground coffee in the drawer of the coffee grinder lies unevenly mixed, a hard winter is coming.
19376: If the flame in the stove is blue, frost is coming.
19378: A few mockers were going to celebrate the Lord's Supper in a café. One had dressed up as a minister, and they had bought bread and wine. While the bread was being handed out, all the lamps suddenly went out. In the dark things got rough, and there was a terrible noise. Afterwards they no longer knew how they had got home. On his way home the disguised minister was flung across the canal three times by the devil. The landlord did not dare come into the café for two days.
19380:
To get a magic coin from the devil, you need a lot of nerve. With a black cat in a sack on your back, you must walk around the churchyard three times, saying: "Devil, what will you give for the cat?" After the third time a little man appears who wants to give a daalder. You must say that this is too little. Then you get a daalder in your hand, and the cat is gone from your back.
If you spend the whole daalder the first time, you lose it. After that you can spend all of it three times a day, and each time it comes back into your purse.
You will die a strange death. The devil comes to fetch you.
19383: If a dog howls eerily, someone will die.
19384: A woman who had been born with a caul called her neighbour's girl to come and look at a hearse. A few days later a farmer's little son died. Then they saw the same hearse in reality.
19385: At a place where a railway was built, the sound of a train running over the rails had already been heard earlier.
19388: In Westergeast a horse's head haunts, moving diagonally across the land. A foal haunts there too.
19389: At a certain spot you are always pulled off your bicycle and thrown aside in the evening.
19391: A man saw a coffin in a black mirror.
19392: A man was followed all the way home by something in a ditch.
19393: When a labourer wanted to leave a farmer, he fell ill. Every day a black cat sat on the window frame; it was the farmer himself. The farmer and the labourer quarrelled. The labourer left and promptly recovered.
19394: At a wedding a card reader predicts to one of the guests that he will court a black-haired woman and that to reach her he will have to cross the same water twice. Years later he courted a woman with jet-black hair, and to reach her he had to cross the same water twice by a little bridge.
19395: A card reader predicts to a young couple that much will 'come between' them during their courtship. A year later the girl began to ail, and she died.
19397: On a wall in Dokkumer Nijersilen there is a horseshoe print of the devil. That is where he is supposed to have jumped over the canal.
19402: A milk carrier was followed by a glowing ball and gave up carrying milk.
19403: If a black jackdaw sits on the post in the farmyard, it means a family member who lives far away will die. But if one sits on the windowsill, someone from the household itself will go.
19404: A woman once said that her dead husband often came back. In the end she asked him whether he wanted something. He did. Then she did what he wanted, and he never came again.
19409: Some labourers once went to a card reader to ask what would happen with the money their employer refused to pay them. But they had barely set foot over the threshold when the card reader told them to just go home. The money was waiting for them there.
19410: Two friends went to the card reader. The fortune teller told one girl that she would court a brown-eyed stable hand. The other would get a husband who would later get a stiff leg. It all came true exactly like that.
19412: It is claimed that an uilesprong is a devil's leap. The devil once jumped over the canal. On the stones where he landed, a print of his foot has remained.
19423: One day the voice of a woman is heard wailing: "Oh, my dear husband!" But the woman was not there at all, and nothing was wrong with her husband. A week later, at exactly the same time, the same thing was heard again. Her husband had then broken his foot on the road.
19424: As punishment for his fickle and wild youth, a man foresaw the deaths of all his children. One night he had stood listening to whether all his children were still alive. Six weeks later four died of measles. Another time the man saw a funeral in his own house. There were no more children at home and he thought he would die himself. But one of his daughters who lived away fell ill and came to her parents' house to die there.
19427: Once people heard a sound coming from the ditch. A few days later a little boy drowned in it.
19449: A dead woman kept coming back to her house and would stand by the side of the cupboard. A debt was still written on that side. When her husband quickly paid the debt, she stayed away.
19452: A young man once boasted that he would like to see the devil. That same evening he was lifted off the road and thrown into a ditch.
19453: A man is knocked off the road by a hearse.
19458: In an area where there were no houses at all, the sound of carpentry was heard one night. Not long afterwards new houses were built.
19461: Sorceresses have rag dolls. They stick needles or pins into them to torment people.
19463: A man is on his way home with his dog cart when the dogs refuse to pull any further. Once he reaches his farmyard, a very strange, large light appears. The light makes the grass and trees even greener than in daytime. As quickly as it had come, it disappeared again.
19464: One evening a man is knocked off the road by a hearse.
19476: Ruerd van der Veen could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. So could Reid Keuning. He could also make liquor come out of the hearth pit.
19482: It sometimes happened that the dead came back when people did not keep the promises they had made during the dead person's life. The minister then had to come to ask the dead person what he wished.
19487: Out of a group of boys, one was suddenly lifted up and flung away. He was ill from it for days.
19490: Four young men once heard the sound of carpentry while nothing could be seen. Not long afterwards there were builders' huts there.
19491: A girl with red hair drowned in a pond from which cries for help had been heard earlier.
19492: Freemasons write their names in blood when they are behind thick walls. They always have money. They have a magic coin. They must renounce the Supreme Being and accept the devil.
19493: Antsje and Tryn Snipel used to tell fortunes with cards. They also sometimes sent out a card to get a bottle of drink.
19494: At a place where farms were later built, wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns) had been seen before.
19495: Oeds Eilander could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit with his book of magic. When he read backwards, they disappeared again. He could also make you stand rigid, or make your clothes drop.
19504: If magpies chatter in the farmyard, someone who lives there will die. Also if a dog stands howling eerily towards a house.
19505: When someone was drunk and raging, it sometimes happened that the devil threw him into the ditch a little later.
19506: In the Grinzer Pein a foal runs about with a porridge pot around its neck.
19508: A farm maid once sent for the minister because she was regularly visited by a ghost. The ghost told the minister that the previous maid had made it a promise but had not kept it. The minister went to ask that maid to fulfil the promise, and then the ghost found rest.
19511: You should never eat anything from Rikele Myt, because then you would turn into a toad. If she gave you an apple, you had to put it under a cup. After three days you would find a toad under the cup. In the evenings Myt sat sticking pins into dolls.
19512: The daughter of Rikele Myt had learned witchcraft from her mother. A dog was very afraid of her, and she magicked the animal away.
19513: You should never walk in the middle of the road, because then a hearse can suddenly push you aside.
19517: One morning people heard glass shattering in the kitchen, but nothing could be seen. In the afternoon a large painting fell upstairs. The glass of the painting and the vases on the mantelpiece broke. It made the same sound they had heard that morning.
19518: A man once recognised the footsteps of an acquaintance at the door, but no one was there. Hours later he heard the footsteps again, and this time the acquaintance was indeed at the door.
19519: One evening two men heard the sound of carpentry at a place where nothing could be seen. Not long afterwards a house was built on that spot.
19520: Cries for help were once heard from a pond. People assumed someone with red hair would drown in it. Later a man drowned there while paddling.
19521: It was said that Ruerd van der Veen could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit with a book of magic.
19522: Witte wijven (white women) haunt the Kruisweg in Harkema.
19528: A farm girl once became pregnant by the farmer. She killed the twins she had given birth to. The farmer who later came to live there kept seeing two small naked children while milking. He sent for the minister. The minister found out that the children wanted grave clothes. The next day the farmer laid out grave clothes, and after that he never saw the children again.
19531: A woman often saw little lights at a certain place in the evening. Later street lamps were put up there.
19533: A girl always haunts the railway in Westereinde.
19534: The sound of carpentry could often be heard at a certain place, but nothing could be seen. Later a farm was built there.
19535: A man once saw a coffin being carried into a hearse in front of a house. Not long after, the occupant of the house died.
19536: A man born with a caul once did not want to get out of bed when there was a knock at the door. But the knocking continued, and then he had to get up. He ran at a trot, as if they were after him. But he arrived in time. There was a drop of sweat on every hair.
19541: In Harkema there was a small farmer who brought Christianity to the village. He held his sermons in a little shed. At night people heard hammering at that spot, but nothing could be seen. Not long afterwards a church was built.
19542: People once heard cries for help from the Leeuwepoel. Someone is still bound to drown in it.
19544: Some people saw a house burn down. In reality it was not burning. But later the house really did burn down.
19545: A man often had to get out of bed at night. Outside he would see a hearse go by. He always counted the people walking behind it. But he never knew who had died.
19546: An old woman saw her son's funeral in miniature on the table before he had died.
19547: Ruerd van der Veen could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. When he struck with his magic wand, they began to march.
19548: A man was once thrown off a little bridge into the ditch by the devil in the shape of a woman.
19554: The wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns) of the past were forerunners of the later street lamps. It was sorcery.
19556: One night a man saw an old woman sitting in the middle of the road, grinding coffee. The man wanted to chase her away, but when she stood up she was suddenly a very big woman. She picked the man up and threw him in the ditch. After he had climbed out of the water, she walked beside him for quite a while. Until she suddenly just sank away into the ground.
19559: The father of a bewitched child was given a potion by Wopke, the devil banisher. On the way home something jumped on the man, and the father had to go back to Wopke for a new potion. Back home the man put asafoetida under the threshold and burned the wreaths he found in his child's pillow. That same night his house was full of cats. He hit one with a shot. The next day the witch lay lame in bed.
19567: The little lights that could be seen in the past were the lamps of the bicycles on which people later went to a quack healer.
19568: Through the window of a house a man saw a coffin being slid out. The coffin was laid on the cart, and the women in the procession behind the cart wore rain clothes. Not long after, someone really died in the house, and everything happened exactly as the man had seen beforehand.
19570: A voice calling for help was once heard from a stream. A few years later a young fellow drowned.
19573: Reid Keuning could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit and then have them march through the room.
19574: The devil once ran ahead of a man and left footprints. Right in front of the man's house the footprints suddenly stopped. There the devil had made a great leap.
19585: At her mother's deathbed a girl had promised to break up with her boyfriend. But she did not keep her promise. Once, as she came out of her boyfriend's house, she suddenly saw her dead mother standing there in a white cap. The girl wanted to run to her, but was thrown back so hard that she fell unconscious.
19586: One night people heard hammering and boards being broken away in the house, but there was nothing to be seen. When the father died about two weeks later, the same sound was heard. Because the coffin would not fit into the small house, boards had to be removed.
19587: One night a man was knocked off the road. A funeral procession had probably passed by.
19592: Before an extra bed was added to a house, the occupants had already heard sawing and hammering.
19593: Before a chicken coop was built by the house, a man had already heard hammering.
19596: A married couple were lifted over the trees, dog cart and all, and thrown into the ditch.
19598: In the past a little light could be seen on the heath, even though there was not a single house there. Later a house was built.
19599: The wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns) that people used to see often were omens of the later bicycles.
19601: If you dream of fish, there will be a death in the family.
19602: A man regularly had to get out of bed at night to see funeral processions.
19603: When a child was bewitched, people went to Wopke, the exorcist. He usually gave them a bottle of potion to take home, with the warning that on the way they would probably meet someone or something that would want to break the bottle.
19615: One day in 1862 a fireball was seen in daylight over a large part of Friesland and a terrible roar was heard. The next day the train from Leeuwarden to Groningen ran for the first time.
19617: One evening a young man heard someone say 'halt' three times in front of his house, but no one could be seen. His mother predicted that war would break out within half a year. Three weeks later three German troops halted in front of the house one after another.
19620: Between Surhuizum and Harkema a sow with twelve piglets haunts at night.
19621: At the churchyard of Surhuisterveen a man haunts with a basket of cakes on his arm.
19623: A man sees a ghost on the road, but his daughter and wife see nothing.
19624: A widower married a second time, although he had promised his first wife not to remarry. One day his second wife suddenly stood beside him, and she never left his side again. That was his punishment.
19625: A widower wanted to marry again. But his girlfriend had some objection to his three children. One evening the man put the three apples she had given him for his children in the cupboard. The next day the apples had turned into toads. The man broke off the relationship with the sorceress.
19627: An old woman once saw a little light in her room that made the sound of a train. It had been an omen.
19628: Hammering at night means that busy times are coming.
19629: Old Metske Smit was born with a caul. At night he often had to get up to watch funeral processions.
19631: At the end of the Wâl a foal haunts the place with a porridge pot around its neck.
19635: An old gentleman haunts a certain place. He sits backwards on a horse and shines a lamp. A treasure lies in the ground at that spot, and in this way the gentleman keeps watch so that nobody gets to it. But nobody can reach the treasure, because the deeper you dig, the deeper the treasure sinks into the ground.
19638: Jehannes Meerstra could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit, he could sail against the wind, and on the ridge of the barn he made a brood of chickens walk with the rooster in front. Someone at the sugar factory fancied some pickled herring. Outside they heard 'pickled herrings' called three times. But when they went outside, there was no seller to be seen. Jehannes had done that.
19646: A card player was once thrown over the trees by the devil on an old muddy road.
19647: A group of sorceresses turned themselves into cats at night. Their leader was the cat Mozes. Every morning they sat around him and sang: "Cat Mozes is such a beautiful cat."
19648: The father of a bewitched child was given a potion by Wopke, the exorcist. Wopke told the man to make sure he held the bottle tightly in his hands when he went through the gate. The man forgot this and had to ask Wopke for a new bottle because the other one had fallen and broken as he went through the gate. With the second bottle the man got home safely.
19654: From the grave of a little boy who hit his mother, the child's right hand grew. The minister told the mother to strike the little hand with a birch twig, and then it would go back into the grave. And so it happened.
19656: A man played cards with his mates every evening. Things always got so rowdy that his wife warned him it might go wrong some day. Then one time a gentleman came who wanted to join the game. He won all the cards and all the money. That was the devil. After this warning the men never played cards again.
19662: A man was warned by several people not to walk along a certain road in the evening. But the man paid no attention and went anyway. When he did indeed meet a ghost, he told the two ministers of the village. The Reformed and the Dutch Reformed minister went together to ask the ghost woman what she desired. She said she had been buried in the wrong grave and therefore could find no rest. The gravedigger then dug her up and laid her in her parents' grave. Since then the road has no longer been haunted.
19663: A widower's second wife wore the first wife's clothes. But the children sometimes saw their first mother haunting in the wardrobe. The father did not believe it, but in the end sent for the minister. The spirit wanted clothes for her children to be made from her clothing, not for them to be worn by another woman.
19664: Wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns) are forerunners of paved roads, bicycles, cars and stations.
19677: People sometimes heard someone approaching or the door latch moving. Yet there was no one to be seen. Later the person they had heard earlier always did arrive.
19689: On the Luitenantslaan near Rottefalle someone always haunts in the shape of a horse.
19690: On the Dwarsvaart a foal walks about with a porridge pot around its neck.
19692: If a dog howls eerily, someone will die. Also if magpies chatter.
19696:
A farmhand is born with a caul and often has visions of the future. He lives in a small cottage on the farmer's land. The farmer has two sons, and one of them has made a girl pregnant. The farmer wants nothing to do with it, and the son asks whether the mother-to-be may live with the farmhand in the cottage for the time being. The farmer's son soon backs out, and in the end the farmhand marries the girl because he has come to care for her a great deal. One day the farmhand sees, in the middle of a funeral procession, a coffin with a white sheet. It is a vision: his wife gives birth to a daughter but dies in childbed.
Another day he is woken at night because he has to take the eldest farmer's son to the doctor. On the way back he again sees a funeral procession, but now with a very grand coffin. He foresees that an important person will die and tells the farmer. Some time later the youngest son is killed riding a wild horse. The funeral procession is the same one that had already been seen. The farmer beats the farmhand to death. The farmhand's daughter, who has grown up considerably by now, tells the farmer he will pay for the murder of the farmhand. The farmer cuts himself on a plant and gets an infection. A little later he dies of fever.
19700: Three witches would like a husband, but nobody wants to marry them because they practise the vrije kunst (the black art). Three Reformed church elders want to know more about these devil's arts and one evening go to see how things stand with the witches. The men let it be known that they will only marry the witches if the witches also teach them the basics of the vrije kunst (the black art). The witches take the elders to a dark barn. The men have to say that they curse God and follow the devil. But the men say it the other way round: they curse the devil and follow God. At that moment the whole barn lights up and the elders suddenly see three horses standing in the barn. The men get away as fast as they can.
19705: There is a haunted barn called 'The barn with the white door'. People often spend the night in the barn, but no one may sleep too close to the white door. A newlywed couple ignores the warnings and makes a bed right by the door. In the middle of the night a scream suddenly rings out. The wife lies unconscious on the floor because she has been hurled back and forth through the barn.
19706: 'The barn with the white door' is a haunted place and nobody dares to sleep by the door. Once a great many families with children spend the night in the barn. Everyone avoids the sleeping places by the door, but a little old woman who was born with a caul promises to keep an eye on things. In the middle of the night she gets up to move a small child away from the door because she senses disaster approaching. When the danger has passed, she puts the child back again.
19707: A big, sturdy man is on his way home at night. As he is about to walk across a plank, he hears something. The next moment he is roughly thrown down.
19712: A farmhand finds his sister terrified because she hears crackling sounds. He brushes her fear aside. When he comes home from work a week later, the stove has fallen over burning onto the floor. There is wood in the stove too, and the farmhand hears the wood crackling. The sister had foreseen the fire.
19714: A man is on his way home deep in the night when a female figure with a black face crosses his path. The woman goes through a gate of the church and the man follows her. A moment later the woman has disappeared and the man makes off, trembling with fear.
19715: A labourer has cursed God and renounced the faith. One time he is hurled down so roughly by the devil, in the form of a little fellow, that he calls on the Lord for help and promises to mend his ways.
19716: A man often sees little lights, wilde lantaarnen (wild lanterns), floating. He thinks they were the omens of modern bicycle lights.
19717: Two men always see two small creatures - little children - haunting the garden of a married couple. When they ask about it, the couple blush. It is whispered that they murdered their children and buried them in the garden.
19718: A man dies and his wife takes the fine silver buckles off his shoes. She promised her husband that their little son would get the buckles. A time of poverty begins and the woman is forced to sell the buckles to the neighbour. The dead man promptly appears at the garden gate and keeps wandering there. When the minister finally asks him about his unfulfilled wish, the dead man reminds his wife of her promise. The woman buys the buckles back and gives them to the boy. The dead man's spirit only has rest once the promise is kept.
19723: A widow had four daughters, but two of them died. One day the two remaining girls see two naked girls dancing in the garden. They are the dead girls: they cannot find rest and keep haunting because a promise was not kept. The minister is called in and learns from the girls what their unfulfilled wish is: they were buried without a shroud. The girls arrange with their mother that she will lay out a shroud the next evening at eight o'clock. That evening the family does indeed hear voices and the dead girls put on their shrouds. Because it is a little too big, one of the girls tears a strip of cloth off her shroud and leaves it on the chair. The girls never haunted again.
19724: A man is often troubled by a nightmare (a mare) in the shape of a dog. The dog lies down on top of him.
19725: At a haunted spot, a sack of nuts often rolls back and forth across the road at night. Once a man wants to cut the sack open with a knife, but just then the sack is nowhere to be seen.
19727: A man always foresees things, for example impending deaths in the family. Once he also knew that a woman would tear her skirt at a funeral - and this happened too.
19731: Two women take a sick cow to the devil-banisher Hinse. Hinse asks whether they were troubled by anything at a certain place on the way, a haunted spot, and the women say no. Hinse foresees that on the way back they will be followed by something that wants to walk between them. He advises them to keep walking very close together. A beast that looks like a black sheep does indeed try to squeeze in between the women. The women stubbornly hold firm and the phantom beast slinks off.
19734: The card reader Hinke Kaert can predict the future from cards. She predicts to two brothers what will happen on their way back home, and it does happen. Hinke tells the brothers' mother that one day she will cry harder than she ever has in her life. When one of the brothers is later murdered, the mother indeed begins to wail uncontrollably.
19740: Whenever a man has to pay for something, he always steps outside for a moment. He then receives money from the devil, because he has made a pact with the devil.
19741: The wizard Ymke Modder, better known as Ymke de Jong, can escape from hermetically sealed prisons.
19743: A few men are playing cards and send a jack of spades away to fetch a bottle of drink. When a filled bottle of gin comes floating into the room, one of the men shouts that the bottle must be taken, otherwise it will burst.
19770: An impatient, rough farmer wants a large piece of land ploughed before evening. The farmhand refuses and tells the farmer he can take his proposal to the devil. The farmer takes this literally and enlists the devil's help. The next morning the land is ploughed. His dealings with the devil cost the farmer dearly: on his deathbed he was fetched by the devil.
19771: A man is born with a caul and is therefore clairvoyant. He foresees all funerals: he urges people to step aside because a funeral procession wants to pass.
19772: A rich farmer promised his wife on her deathbed that he would never marry. But not even a year later he stands at the altar again with a niece of his late wife. As the man and his new bride are about to get into the carriage, his dead wife suddenly appears. She reminds him of his promise and the newlyweds undo the marriage. The spirit of the dead can only find rest once a promise made before death is kept.
19781: A married couple are always playing cards. The husband can curse terribly. He also sometimes sends an empty bottle away with a card. The bottle later comes back filled. That is the work of the devil.
19782: At night a man very clearly hears hammering and other sounds connected with building a house. When he goes to look, there is nothing to be seen. A year later a house has been built on that spot. It was an omen.
19784: A man who has had too much to drink is seized by an invisible hand and thrown down some distance away.
19785: A married couple is suspected of murdering their children. They are said to have buried the children behind the sheep shed. The couple often saw the little children dancing around a post in the sheep shed. Their souls could find no rest.
19786: A man promised his wife on her deathbed never to remarry. He does not keep the promise and marries a second time. The first, dead wife starts haunting because he did not keep his promise. Sometimes, for example, the barn doors open by themselves. In the end the dead woman even appears to the man, whereupon he flees to America.
19788: A man can make little soldiers come out of the stoke hole and march across the floor. He is a sorcerer.
19789: At a haunted spot a foal runs about with a porridge pot around its neck.
19790: The devil twisted a man's head around.
19791: At a haunted spot a man with a cow always wanders about. It is a ghostly apparition: the man was murdered at that spot long ago.
19792: An apparition always sets all the ships loose again. Not a single ship can stay moored.
19836: A farmstead is not right: it is a haunted place. The farmer offers his farmhand a coin if he can make the haunting stop. The farmhand calls in the minister and together they take up position in the haunted room. At the stroke of midnight the door opens and seven ghosts come in, a black one in front and six red ones. The minister asks the ghosts what their unfulfilled wish is. The ghosts point to a spot in the floor and instruct them to remove the two chests of money hidden there. The men dig up the treasure and the ghosts finally find rest. Then the haunting was over.
19840: When someone has been tormented by a nightmare for a while and is freed of it, this is called 'het opstijgen der moer' (the rising of the mare). A witches' broom is also called a 'nachtmerrienest' (nightmare's nest).
19842: A farmer is working with his farmhands when he suddenly sees a small cloud of steam in the air and hears a rumbling sound. Later the train makes exactly the same sound. The farmer had foreseen that the railway would come there.
19845: A party on a sailing boat fancies a drink. They send an empty bottle away with a note attached; a little later the bottle comes floating back, filled. The man who gave the order tries to persuade the others to take the bottle, because it will end badly if he does it himself. At first no one wants to take the bottle. The man half loses consciousness, and the bottle has already gone round almost three times. At the last moment someone did take the bottle. If the bottle had made three full rounds, the man would have been dead. The first glass is for the devil and is thrown over the left shoulder.
19846: A man has spent an evening amusing himself with the women, and on his way home he comes upon a large, dark dog blocking his path. Piter first waits a while to see if the dog will go away by itself. When the animal stays put, he decides simply to walk past it. Suddenly he finds himself in the ditch with the dog. A moment later the dog has vanished, and Piter runs home terrified. It was a phantom animal.
19847: An unbelieving carpenter swears and rages so terribly that even other unbelievers take offence. One day, as the man goes home with his toolbox on his shoulder, he boasts that he is afraid of no one, not even if as many devils came at him 'as there are tiles on a roof'. The tough fellow sets off cheerfully, but is soon punished for his arrogance. An enormous force throws the toolbox off his shoulder; a moment later he himself is seized and flung to the ground. Although he can barely stand, he hurries home as fast as he can. There he declares that he has learned a great deal from the incident and will never mock again.
19849: A farmhand once quarrels with the farmer. The farmer threatens to go for him, and the farmhand says: 'I'm not even afraid of the devil, let alone a farmer. The devil is just a pathetic little man: with one really hard kick I can send him flying a long way through the air.' The farmer says the farmhand will regret his words later. Some time later he is walking home at night by moonlight with his sister-in-law. At a certain point a small black man the size of a dog is walking beside them, and the farmhand and his sister-in-law freeze with fear. They have to jump over a narrow ditch in the meadow, but the devil jumps into the water right in front of them without making the water ripple at all, and stops them from crossing by running alongside them the whole time. In mortal fear the farmhand calls on God, and the little devil vanishes at once on hearing these words.
19850: A tough skater boasts that he is not afraid of the devil. He even hopes the devil will cross his path some day. When the skater, by moonlight, has strapped on his skates again, he soon senses a companion skating beside him. When he reaches the bridge, he is seized and hurled against the wall. The next day other skaters found him dead there. He was completely blue.
19852: A farmhand often hears footsteps on the stairs to the attic at night. The farmer says those are the ghosts of the former farmhands.
19853: Sometimes at night the butter churns suddenly start rattling for no reason.
19854: A group of young people are standing together. Suddenly one of them is picked up and thrown down again some distance away.
19855: A man hears a sound coming from the canal. When he goes to look, there is nothing to be seen. Later someone drowns in the same canal. The sound was a portent of the drowning.
19858: A single mother throws her child to the pigs in despair. When she later goes to feed the pigs, the child's ghost keeps appearing. The child keeps putting its little hands on the pig trough.
19861: A father warns his children never to walk in the middle of the road, because a funeral procession might pass.
19862: A drunkard mocks the Supreme Being. On his way home he is suddenly seized and swung around. They say the devil got hold of him.
19864: A farmer is a great scoffer. He claims he is not afraid of the devil and that he believes in nothing. His housekeeper detests his foolish talk and warns him that scoffers will get the 'scoffer's reward'. She tells a story about two brothers. One of them was always mocking terribly, and was promptly punished by the devil.
19865: A farmer, a scoffer, suddenly gets a hard blow on his arm at night. That was the devil.
19871: A wit wief (white woman) haunts a haunted spot.
19872: At a certain spot a foal sometimes runs about with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a phantom animal.
19873: Many people dare not go near the Reformed church in the evening, because it is haunted. When a man cycles past the haunted spot, he is suddenly seized and thrown into the canal, bicycle and all. Something is said to have happened at that same spot long ago.
19874: A young couple is frightened by a phantom animal. It is a large black dog with glowing eyes.
19875: It is said of witches that they turn an apple into a toad if you keep the apple too long. The narrator suspects that her sister was also a witch and never trusted it when the sister brought food for the narrator's children.
19876: Witches can turn themselves into cats. Sometimes they hold a real cats' meeting where there is beautiful singing.
19877: At a haunted place a pig always runs about at night. No one can catch the animal. It is a ghost pig.
19878: If the clock strikes wrongly and the dogs start howling eerily, a death is coming. Both are omens.
19879: A boy passes a funeral procession and recognises all the people walking behind the coffin. The deceased also seems familiar to him. Later the man really dies. It was an omen.
19880: A man's cottage went up in flames after a lightning strike. Later it turns out that people had foreseen the fire.
19882: A man is married to a nightmare and is much troubled by it. To ward her off, he puts a page from the Bible under his pillow or scatters a handful of flour in the bed. The woman is one of seven sisters.
19883: Many people heard the sound of the train long before it began to run. It is an omen.
19884: A man foresees that someone will drown in the pond. It is someone wearing a red skirt, the man says. Later a boy with red hair drowns in the pond.
19885: A man has cancer and is dying. On his deathbed he is startled by knocking on the window: 'death', says a voice. A little later the man is dead.
19886: Stammerige Harm is a sorcerer and can change himself into a cat. The narrator's father once gave the cat a tremendous wallop. The next day Harm has a bruised arm.
19889: The mother of Stammerige Harm, a witch, has a little shop. One evening they are sitting cosily drinking coffee when the mother suddenly says, 'my time has almost come'. At midnight she indeed breathes her last. In life the witch had always had plenty of money, as is always the case with people who sell their soul to the devil, but now there was only a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) in her purse. Harm too has made a pact with the devil: he also has a wisseldaalder.
19892: Two men have been sitting and talking, and one man walks the other back to his little houseboat. On the deck of the boat an animal runs back and forth. It looks like a big black dog, but it is not. It is a phantom animal.
19893: A fisherman sees a lady in white clothes and decides to follow her. But the wit wief (white woman) vanishes as quickly as she appeared.
19894: A married couple goes to have coffee with acquaintances and leaves the children to mind the house. One of the children hears a cock crowing, although the family has no cock. When they go to the shed with a little lantern to see what is going on, the sound stops and there is nothing to be seen. This happens again. The children never found out where the sound came from.
19895: People often see wilde lantaarnen (wild lanterns) at a certain spot. Later modern lighting was installed there.
19896: Some people once visited a family of sorcerers. On the way back they are chased by a large dog. They can only shake the animal off with difficulty. It is a phantom animal.
19898: In the old days, if a woman had a cloth around her backside, she was usually a witch. (She had probably been kicked while in another (animal) shape; the next day the witch in 'woman's shape' then showed the same injuries.)
19900: A man born with a caul, a clairvoyant, often sees funeral processions passing at night. The man foresees deaths.
19901: If a dog starts howling eerily, the death of a Jew is coming.
19902: At a certain spot people often hear hammering. It is an omen: later a new house is built on that spot. Work on this new house was even done on Sunday. People suspect the house will burn down because you are not allowed to work on Sunday. So far it has not happened.
19903: A sorcerer has changed himself into a cat and untied the cattle. The sorcerer's son catches the cat in the cowshed and kicks it. The next morning the sorcerer wears a cloth around his head. The son realizes that his father was the cat and becomes terribly angry.
19906: A window cleaner is suddenly seized roughly and thrown into the water some distance away. Strangely enough, his tobacco stayed dry.
19908: A witch sometimes kills children by magic. A couple has already lost three children through the witch's sorcery.
19910: Two men are cycling to church on a Sunday evening when one of their bikes suddenly becomes very heavy to pedal. The man thinks he has the devil in his wheel. His friend urges him to 'crush the devil's head', but the man can only make progress with difficulty. A little later he can pedal normally again.
19916: Two men are out hunting polecats at night when they are suddenly startled by a large black dog with fiery eyes. The men are very frightened because they think it is the devil. Just as one of the men is about to give the dog a kick, the beast has vanished. It is a phantom animal.
19917: At night a hunter suddenly sees a house on fire. It is a voorgezicht (a vision of a future event): later the house really burnt down.
19918: If a dog howls eerily, a death will come within three days.
19919: A woman is out late in the evening and is pushed aside twice because a funeral procession wants to pass.
19920: A woman has sometimes been bothered by a nightmare (a mare): the nightmare is a red-haired boy with freckles. He crawls on top of her from her toes and squeezes her throat shut.
19923: A widower does not dare walk past the churchyard alone in the evening, because the ghost of his dead wife then approaches him.
19924: A cyclist is thrown off the road, bicycle and all, twice. The third time he even ends up in the ditch. The cyclist cannot understand it, because there is no one to be seen.
19925: A farmhand often sees a large black dog roaming around the farm. The farmer says this is impossible. The farmhand becomes frightened and quits. He later shot himself in the head.
19926: A witch wants to bewitch a little girl and keeps visiting her in the shape of a cat. The girl's father roughly chases the cat away. The next day the witch Alle Tet has a bruise on her head. She was the witch in cat form.
19930: A sorcerer can make little soldiers dance on the table.
19931: A witch torments her victims by sticking needles into little dolls.
19932: A sorcerer can make little soldiers come out of the stoke hole.
19935: Ruerd van der Veen was once thrown over the dike for no reason near a haunted house.
19939: Someone who owns a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) has sold his soul to the devil. The wisseldaalder never runs out and always returns to its owner's purse.
19944: A wizard can make all doors open. No one can ever hold him in prison.
19953: A clairvoyant woman tells the owner of the pottery shop that one of these days there will be a loud 'rattling'. Some time later a whole lot of earthenware does indeed fall down.
19954: A clairvoyant woman sometimes sees funeral processions passing at night. The woman foresees impending deaths.
19955: A man sometimes sees little lights floating. It is a forerunner of the later, modern lighting.
19956: At a haunted spot a donkey runs about with a porridge pot around its neck. The beast flaps its ears. It is a phantom animal.
19957: When a child is born with a caul, the doctor keeps the caul. If the caul is kept, the child sees things in advance; if the caul is destroyed, the child loses its clairvoyant powers.
19958: A scoffer denies that there is a Supreme Being. On his way home he is suddenly seized and hurled to the ground.
19962: A little boy sees an old man digging a grave. A few days later someone dies and the boy sees exactly the same thing. It was a voorgezicht (a vision of a future event).
19963: A werewolf is a human in the afternoon and an animal in the morning.
19964: Two poachers see a man who has been dead for a few years walking towards the churchyard. They become terribly frightened and run off.
19965: A man sees someone who has been dead for some time walking towards the churchyard. The man becomes very frightened.
19970: A widow treated her late husband so badly during his life that he keeps coming back to haunt. The whole family is afraid when the man stands with his arm on a hay bale in front of the house.
19972: When witches go out to do magic, they leave a tripe behind.
19974: A nightmare is a devil that sits on your chest and tries to strangle you. If you try to grab it, it suddenly vanishes. The nightmare sometimes also takes the form of a woman. There are various customs to ward off nightmares: scattering flour in the bed and placing the clogs backwards and apart in front of the bed. When horses are tormented by nightmares, buckwheat husks are put on their backs and under their tails.
19975: If the magpies chatter in front of your house, someone will die. Also if a dog starts howling eerily, a death is coming.
19976: If the bell tolls the death knell, a death is coming. It is an omen.
19978: A farmhand sleeps in the barn and is startled at night by a ghostly thing that throws itself down on him from the collar beam. The farmhand is terrified and the farmer gives him another place to sleep.
19979: In a haunted barn, the sleepers are sometimes flung from one side to the other for no reason.
19980: A group of cursing men is startled by a black thing. The thing has singled out one of the companions and flings him mercilessly hard towards a small lake. The man crawls into the lake in fear and a little later has to be taken home on the cart.
19982: A witch can turn herself into a cat or a toad. When she sets out to do magic, she leaves a tripe on the bed. A man once gets two apples from a witch; later the apples turn into toads.
19983: Hindrik Pyk is sitting in a thicket, stripped to the waist, picking off lice, when his children suddenly spot him. The children run home to tell their mother, but when they get home their father is already sitting at the table. He has flown home with wings. Hindrik is a sorcerer. Later a son of Hindrik wears asafoetida (devil's dung) on his chest and his shirt back to front to ward off his father's witchcraft. Remarkably, Hindrik is also called a witch, a female sorcerer.
19984: The wizard Imke de Jong can fix someone to the spot so that he cannot take another step.
19985: A group of friends sends an empty bottle away with a jack of spades. A little later the bottle comes floating into the room filled with drink. The one who sent the bottle away may not take hold of it.
19986: In the old days, men at markets could see the image of their future wife in a black mirror in mirror tents. If they would not marry, a coffin appeared. The men had to take care to walk out of the tent backwards.
19990: If you want a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin), you must walk around the churchyard three times with a cat in a sack, calling 'who will buy my cat for a daalder?'. On the third time the devil takes the cat and gives you a wisseldaalder. With this you sell your soul to the devil.
19994: There are various ways to ward off nightmares: putting an odd number of rye grains on the chest, laying the stockings crosswise in front of the bed, or wearing asafoetida on the chest.
19998: The mother of a little boy hears the dog howling eerily. The dog then goes and stands with its face to the wall. Fourteen days later the child dies; the little coffin stands against the wall.
19999: The chattering of magpies is a harbinger of death.
20000: If a swallow taps on the window, a death follows within three days. The narrator illustrates this with the death of a baby.
20001: People speak of a 'doodskloppertje' (little death knocker) behind the wallpaper, also called a 'wekker' (alarm clock) or a 'wild horloge' (wild watch). When people hear that sound, it means a death is coming.
20002: If a bell tolls as it does at a funeral, a death is coming.
20003: If a horse pulling a hearse stops in front of a certain house and scrapes its hoof, someone in that house will die three to seven days later. The same horse will then also pull that coffin.
20004: When you are about to have an accident, you are always warned by the birds. A man is screeched at three times by magpies before he is hit by a car. He survived.
20005: If your nose itches, you will get a quarrel or a drink.
20013: A woman has been bewitched to death by a witch. The wreaths in her pillow are burnt. To ward off witches further, you must make sure that all holes and cracks in your house, even the chimney and the keyhole, are sealed. Many people in the narrator's area have at some time been victims of witchcraft.
20014: A white ghost wanders about a haunted spot. Anyone who wants to pass the apparition must keep well to the side, or they are seized by the ghost and flung some distance away.
20015: At a haunted spot, a vijfschacht (a five-pronged fork) is often set in motion at night by an invisible force. The ghostly thing rolls back and forth across the road. Everyone is very afraid of it.
20019: The narrator's father, Wibe, wants to buy a calf but is short of money. Fortunately the wizard Stammerige Harm is willing to lend money - as the owner of a wisseldaalder (a magic coin that always returns), Harm always has money in abundance. Harm foresees that the farmer will come home with a red-pied cow, but Wibe laughs and says he doesn't see that happening soon because he isn't fond of red-pied cattle. At the cattle market Wibe finally gives in to a fine red-pied calf after all: Harm's prediction has come true.
20020: A clairvoyant often foresees a death. He has to get out of bed at night and then sees funeral processions passing.
20025: A man visits a mirror tent and sees the image of his future wife in the black mirror. He must take care to leave the tent walking backwards.
20026: A woman tells how she saw her uncle lying bareheaded in a coffin. When the uncle actually dies, he lies exactly as the woman had seen earlier. It was a vision of the future.
20027: A man sees his uncle lying in a coffin. A fortnight later the uncle actually dies: he lies just as the man had seen earlier. It was a vision of the future.
20028: As a little girl, a woman once bumped into a hearse. It was a vision of an impending death.
20029: At a haunted spot funeral processions can often be seen. Everyone must always step aside to let the procession pass.
20031: A clay worker suddenly sees a small coffin while at work. He hurries home, where his little son lies dying. He has only just got home when the boy dies. The little coffin was a vision of the future.
20032: A woman is fixed to the spot by a female wizard. For a good half hour she cannot take a step.
20033: Some animals cannot be hit with a gun. The devil dwells in such animals.
20038: Doodstikkertjes (little death tickers) are spiders behind the wallpaper. When they start ticking, a death is coming.
20039: If three drops of blood fall from someone's nose, he will soon die.
20040: An old woman's skirt catches fire. She becomes very frightened because she knows it is an omen of an impending death. The woman does indeed die. (The recorder wonders whether this might have something to do with 'purgatory'.)
20041: The wizard Imke de Jong is very often thrown in jail (even as a soldier he was very often in the cells) but always frees himself effortlessly. He was also sometimes seen in three places at once.
20043: At a haunted spot a black dog with curly hair always roams about. Everyone is afraid of the animal. It is a phantom animal.
20046: A man named Edzer Sint has a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) because he sold his soul to the devil. He got the nickname 'Sint' (cent) because he never lacks money.
20047: As a little boy a man often saw a little light floating. On the spot where he saw the wilde lantaarn (wild lantern), a new house was later built.
20048: Two brothers on their way home have to jump aside for a passing funeral procession. A few weeks later someone really dies and they see the same funeral procession. It was a vision of the future.
20050: When a witch goes out at night to do magic, she leaves a tripe in bed beside her husband.
20054: A bewitched child turns out to have two little birds made of feathers in her pillow, with their beaks pointing towards each other. If the two little beaks had touched, the child would have died. The parents discover it in time and burn the feathers in the stove.
20055: A bicycle repairman who is fond of a drink often invites young people to his home. He then makes little soldiers, or a bottle of liquor, come out of the stoke hole. The man is a sorcerer.
20056: The wizard Imke de Jong can fix both people and animals to the spot. For example, he likes to bring horses to a sudden halt.
20060: At a haunted spot a dog roams about at night. It is a phantom dog.
20062: Two men see something coming towards them, but a moment later it has vanished again. It is a ghostly thing.
20063: Two young men suddenly see a woman dressed in light blue coming towards them on a bicycle. As suddenly as the woman appeared, she has vanished again. She is a ghost woman.
20066: A cursing company is suddenly startled by a black man in a top hat: the devil. The scoffers immediately begin singing psalms and the devil makes himself scarce.
20069: Every night a woman sees a funeral procession pass. Someone of about seventeen lies in the coffin. The woman can no longer bear it and moves away. Shortly afterwards the new occupants lose their seventeen-year-old son. The previous occupant had foreseen his death.
20070: A woman who sells butter always cheats her customers by never giving exactly the amount asked for. When she keeps haunting after her death, the minister asks her about her unfulfilled wish. The woman wants all her former customers to receive the butter they were owed, without having to pay for it. This is done and the woman finally finds rest.
20074: A woman born with a caul always has to get up at midnight and then sees things that later come true. In this way she sees beforehand the fire in an inn and a shelf giving way in a pots-and-pans shop, so that the pots and pans fall and break.
20078: If you dream of a funeral, a wedding will follow.
20081: Towards the end of the night a baker sees a woman pass his bakery. Because he does not trust it, he follows her. She turns out to be a well-known woman born with a caul who always has to go out at night to see something. She tells the baker she sees a funeral procession passing. Some time later someone really does die.
20082: A few people hear the fisherman Hanne moaning in his little boat, but when they go to look there is nothing to be seen. Two days later the same fisherman breaks his leg and moans exactly as had been heard before.
20083: Three brothers hear people chopping wood three evenings in a row. When they go to look, there is nothing to be seen. On the fifth day people really are chopping wood. It was an omen.
20084: If it is cold at the moment you receive an omen, what you have seen or heard will happen in the distant future; if it is warm, in the near future.
20085: What at first look like bales of hay turn out, up close, to be a moving white horse, after which a dog begins to howl eerily.
20086: At a haunted spot a foal runs about with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a phantom animal.
20087: A man passes Piter, the narrator's father-in-law. Piter greets him kindly but gets no reply. Piter takes the man to task for his rudeness, and only then does he see that the man hurrying ahead of him is a man who recently died.
20088: A man hears hammering at night and a while later the house is actually renovated. It was an omen.
20089: A man born with a caul often has to go out at night to see things. He often sees funeral processions pass. The Lord frees him of his second sight, because the boy finds it very hard to bear.
20090: A man is in poor health and one day foresees that within half a year he will be taken to the churchyard on the hearse. His son consults the doctor, who predicts that the father will die within two weeks. Fourteen days later the son, a clay worker, does indeed receive a telegram saying his father is on his deathbed.
20092: A sorcerer reads from his magic book and at once little soldiers come marching out of the stoke hole. When he reads the book backwards, the little soldiers disappear into the stoke hole again.
20093: Wilde lantaarnen (wild lanterns) are forerunners of a house to be built later.
20094: You often cannot see a funeral procession, but you can feel it pass. People are often simply pushed off the road, or driven to the side because the hearse has to get by. This is an omen, a harbinger of death.
20098: A man born with a caul sees a witch combing the horse's mane. He has a premonition that the horse will soon die, and so it does.
20099: A woman visits a friend and brings a cake. The friend does not quite trust it and eats only a very small piece of the cake. She puts a large piece of the cake in a basket. When she looks in the basket the next day, there is a toad in it. Now the woman is sure she has had a witch visiting.
20100: Two dead little children who were buried without shrouds keep haunting naked. The mother then lays two little shrouds on the chair and the children find rest.
20103: In a certain barn, people spending the night are flung from one side to the other. Room must also be made, because something has to pass through. It is a haunted barn.
20104: One night a woman suddenly can no longer move because she has to see something. A coffin stands against the wall. The woman tells her husband, who tells her to keep quiet. Seven years later the husband actually dies. His coffin stands in exactly the same spot the woman had seen earlier. It was a vision of the future.
20107:
Witches conjure wreaths into the pillows of those they bewitch. When three wreaths are finished, the person is done for. If you are in time, you must burn the wreaths to ward off the witchcraft.
Two well-known witches, Jeltsje and Lutske, stick needles into homemade dolls. Small children then scream with pain.
20110:
Nightmares can pass through the neck of a bottle. You can keep nightmares away with rye flour, because rye is holy.
On a sultry day the narrator's father does not sleep in his bed but on the floor. Suddenly he sees a small red-and-white dog approaching outside. All at once the dog is standing in the room and father picks it up. Then the dog changes into a huge beast. Father is terrified and shouts to his wife to turn on the light. But the dog has vanished: it had come in through the keyhole and left again through the keyhole. It was a nightmare.
20113: The son of a woman who used to be clairvoyant turns out to have the same gifts his mother once had. One day he sees an empty coffin standing in the room. The mother predicts that it will be almost two years before her son dies. And indeed, within two years he dies.
20114: A man visits a fortune-teller together with his wife's sister. The fortune-teller sees that the sister has had a very hard time and predicts that she will soon give birth to a fatherless child, a girl. This comes true exactly. The fortune-teller also predicts that the man will end up in a place where he will no longer need his own butter and milk. This is also right: the couple later have their own farm.
20115: A cursing drunkard is seized by an invisible force and thrown down right in front of the church. That was the devil's work.
20117:
The narrator, the former neighbour of the sorcerer Stammerige Harm, says that Harm always had money. After all, he owned a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) because he had sold his soul to the devil.
Despite his wealth, he was terribly stingy. For example, he always relieved himself in a handkerchief. Afterwards he rinsed the handkerchief out.
20118:
People cannot close a gap in the hedge. One day a woman stands in the gap and speaks to the woman of the house. She predicts that her resting place after death will be in this gap.
Then the woman suddenly falls through the gap: she had to stay in bed for a good fourteen days.
20126: Nobody dares to pass the phantom pig.
20129: Of two traders, one has sold his soul to the devil. The devil is often in his company and gives him money. The other man cannot see the devil.
20131: An old man has seen a funeral procession twice, but he stayed standing in the middle of the road.
20133: Of two farmhands working for a farmer, one is a nightmare (a mare), who makes the other farmhand's nights a misery. The farmhand threatens to leave, after which the farmer sends the nightmare packing.
20137: Imke de Jong had a magic wand and could fix people to the spot. He also fixed someone who mocked his skills, and that person could only move again after Imke touched him with the wand. They did lock Imke up, but he always managed to escape.
20144: An old woman tells a farmer that she has seen a funeral procession somewhere. The farmer says that is impossible, because the procession would drive into the water there. Later the farmer takes on a farmhand, whom he has to house in a boat by the water. One of the farmhand's children dies, and the funeral procession does pass just as the old woman saw it.
20145: A man was born with a caul and foresees the death of his brother.
20154: A man wants a fistfight, even if it is with the devil. Thereupon he is indeed beaten black and blue by the devil, so that he has to stay in bed for days.
20155: On his way a man hears a bicycle bell, but sees only a little dog coming past. "If you are of the devil, I'll deal with you," the man says. But the opposite happens: the dog gives the man a severe beating.
20162: At a clog maker's house there is always a lot of card playing. Again and again a cat comes inside. Whether they put the cat out, throw things at it or shoot at it, nothing helps. One evening a card player who says he is not afraid of the devil is attacked by a little dog. At the clog maker's house he no longer dares to go home. Then the cat comes in again too. This time they load the gun with rye, and that works. The next day the witch turns out to be wounded.
20170: A man is a werewolf; he is the seventh son. When he comes home, his wife throws him a child's dress. To a puzzled visitor his wife explains that he is the seventh boy, a werewolf who, when he has a fit, must have something to tear apart, or else he attacks people.
20171: A couple about to be married take a drive in the cart. The bridegroom-to-be asks the woman whether she has a skirt for him. The woman is surprised but gives him the skirt. The man quickly makes off, but his wife follows him. She sees him tearing the skirt with his teeth; foam is around his mouth. The man confesses that he is a werewolf and had to bite into a cloth, because otherwise he would have had to attack a person. The woman calls off the wedding at once.
20177: A man is on his way to a cunning doctor. The doctor is also a piskijker (a healer who diagnoses by examining urine) and can see in the man's urine exactly where he lives.
20178: A freemason died in a strange way. His head was turned backwards on his neck. People suspect the devil wrung his neck.
20179: In a house two pots are smashed by lightning. A little later the whole house burns down. It was an omen.
20180: A cursing company is suddenly startled by the devil. When they flee in mortal fear, the devil chases them all the way to their front door.
20183: One time a man sees a coffin in a black mirror. It turns out to be the coffin of his wife, who dies shortly afterwards. Later the man remarries.
20184: A woman visits a fortune-teller. The fortune-teller predicts that the woman will die within the year. The woman becomes frightened and wastes away completely. She grows weak and spends almost a year in bed. When she is still alive after a year, she suspects the fortune-teller has deceived her and cheerfully jumps out of bed. The woman recovers at once and eventually lives to a great age.
20185: A woman is seriously worried about her future. The fortune-teller Hinke Kaart reassures her and tells her that she will soon live in a little wooden house with lots of fine tall trees around it. The woman goes home reassured. Shortly afterwards she dies and is buried in a wooden coffin in a churchyard where tall trees stand.
20222: The narrator has seen someone who was murdered years ago.
20224: Two people step aside for a funeral procession; a short time later someone actually dies.
20225: A nightmare (a mare) comes to a man and sits on his chest to take his breath away. The nightmare leaves her belly behind at home.
20228: While playing cards, people sometimes have the jack of clubs fetch drink. The bottle then comes floating in. Whoever sent the card may not touch the bottle. Someone empties the first glass over his right shoulder.
20231: At night light phenomena are seen. They are omens of the later flying machines.
20232: A phantom foal wanders about with a porridge pot around its neck.
20235: A gathering of seven dressed-up cats is really a meeting of witches.
20237: A young man gets two apples from a sorcerer. He puts them in boots, and the next day they are toads.
20239: A wizard once fixed someone to the spot. That person had also once been thrown through the air by the devil.
20241: A woman has a seriously ill mother. One time the daughter hears people outside bumping a coffin against the wall. She suspects her mother's death is imminent. When the mother does die, the daughter warns the pallbearers not to bump the coffin against the wall. It happens anyway. It had been an omen.
20243: A girl lifting potatoes warns her friend, who is about to visit a witch. Everything she gets from the witch and eats whole will turn into a toad, the girl says. The witch does indeed give the girl two apples, but the girl first removes a little piece of each apple with her fingernail. That way the witch gets no hold over her.
20244: A few young people are looking for peat by moonlight when they suddenly see a little red light floating. The light sometimes disappears, but keeps reappearing and follows the peat gatherers. They become very frightened and run home. There their mother says it was a warning of approaching disaster.
20245: When the narrator and a friend are coming back from shopping, they are startled by a thing floating through the air. It looks like a large dog. When the narrator later tells about it at home, it turns out the mother has seen the same thing. It is a phantom animal.
