20246: A boy has been out shopping. At some point he sees the trees along the road bending right down to the ground for no reason, although there is no wind. The boy becomes terrified, and when he tries to run home he is also startled by a fellow who vanishes as suddenly as he appears.
20248: A man born with a caul always has to go out at night to see something. Once he sees a young girl being taken to the churchyard: he can see the whole funeral procession clearly. A week later the girl really dies. It was a vision of the future.
20249: A man born with a caul always has to get up at night to see things. He often has visions of the future.
20250: A poor widow always works hard to scrape together a day's wage; she leaves the housekeeping to her two daughters. The daughters never have things in order when the widow comes home, because they are always distracted by two naked little children in the garden. The widow does not trust it and goes to the minister. When the naked children appear in the garden again, the minister addresses them. The children say they were murdered and buried without a shroud. The minister tells the widow to make a burial shirt for the children, so that their souls may find rest. The widow does so and since then the children have haunted no more.
20251: Three white ladies, sisters, always haunt a haunted spot. Later that place was also said to be called the 'Susterwei'.
20257: Young people would send away an ace of clubs to get a bottle of drink back.
20258:
A wizard lodges with two people. When he is called for tea, he answers that he is coming. When the people go to see what is keeping him, he turns out not to be in his bed at all, even though he answered. He turns out to be out doing magic. Wizards can be in several places at once, which is why the people heard his voice.
The narrator's mother always warned her children never to eat anything at the wizard's house.
20260: When people in the old days saw wilde lantaarnen (wild lanterns), they knew that something was going to happen at that spot: for example, a new ditch would be dug or a new house built.
20262: At an old farmstead, money was hidden in hollow wooden beams. When the rats ran around, you could hear the money jingle. When the place was later demolished, they found all the money. It was a haunted place.
20267: Witches turned into cats sometimes hold a meeting. Once every forty years the witch cats must bewitch someone to death. If they do not, they die themselves. Witch cats have a pact with the devil.
20268: A cursing drunkard is startled by the devil, who throws him into the canal. That is the punishment for his foul language.
20269: Sometimes people are suddenly driven to the side of the road because an invisible funeral procession has to pass.
20270: A wit wief (white woman) haunts a certain haunted spot.
20273: A freemason often hangs an empty purse on the door in the evening. The next morning the purse is filled with money. Freemasons are never short of money, because they have a pact with the devil. Of one freemason it is known that he was cut open after his death because the devil had taken him.
20275: A woman drunkard full of wicked tricks is found dead one day with her head turned around on her body. The devil did that to punish her.
20276: At a haunted spot, someone with a large white thing on his head often wanders about. It is an apparition.
20278: At a haunted spot a foal always runs about with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a phantom animal.
20279: At a haunted spot, someone with a paraffin cart was once lifted up, cart and all, and thrown over the dike.
20281: To keep nightmares away you must put asafoetida under the threshold. The nightmares always torment the horses by braiding their tails.
20282: A man is coming back from the pub and suddenly sees a white thing in the meadow. When he kicks it, the thing sits down on his clogs. The thing then simply flings the man onto the verge.
20286: A father warns his children never to walk in the middle of the road because a funeral procession might pass.
20288: A number of people often heard the sound of the train, while the railway was only built years later. It was an omen.
20289: People often heard hammering at a certain spot. Later a new house was built on that spot. It was an omen.
20292: People born with a caul can foresee things that are going to happen in the future. Sometimes, for example, they see a funeral procession pass by: later someone really does die. People born with a caul have other gifts too: they can also heal the sick.
20300: If a bird calls differently than usual, a death is imminent.
20301: A mother always tries to frighten her naughty children by saying there are ghosts in the cabinet. She also often threatens to make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
20302: Someone once foresaw that one of the bridges on the Groningen-Leeuwarden railway would collapse during a festive occasion. Fortunately it has never happened so far.
20308: A young woman once very clearly sees her mother walking towards her, holding her youngest daughter by the hand. As suddenly as they appeared, they vanish again. The next day the mother and daughter come walking up in exactly the same way as the woman had seen before. It was a vision of the future.
20311: While at work, a clay worker suddenly sees his wife and child before him, together in a coffin. Shocked, he hurries home, where he actually finds what he had seen. It was a vision of the future.
20312: Three labourers are on their way home when one of them urges the other two to step aside because a funeral procession wants to pass. Only he can actually see the procession, because he was born with a caul.
20317: A cyclist with very good bicycle lights suddenly sees a couple running at night. When he gets off to take a better look, there is no one to be seen. The same man also sees a fire burning very clearly in the meadow. When he goes to take a look, there are no flames to be seen anywhere.
20318: At a haunted spot by a lake, a woman is suddenly nailed to the ground. She cannot take another step. She breaks out in a cold sweat of fear, and with the greatest effort she finally manages to break free.
20319: A scoffer is seized by the devil and thrown to the ground. The man was ill from it for a very long time.
20320: A group of mockers in a pub make a bet: one of the men will go to the churchyard in the middle of the night and loudly speak foul words and curses. When the chosen one starts cursing, he is suddenly seized and flung over the hedge. The man was left permanently maimed.
20321: A man says he would like to see three naked women some time. On his way home he really does see them. They are ghostly apparitions. Terrified, he runs home.
20322: A farmhand is on his way to the farmer along a wooden plank path when he suddenly sees something on the path that looks like a nightcap. The farmhand is so frightened that he immediately turns back home. The plank path is known to be often haunted.
20323: No one dares to use a certain plank path any more, because it is always haunted there. The help of a brave minister is called in. The minister learns the unfulfilled wish of the wandering ghost: a white handkerchief must be laid out on the planks. Since then people have never again been troubled by the ghost on the planks.
20324: At a haunted spot a sheepdog always roams about. It is a phantom animal.
20326: The help of devil-banisher Piter Poes is called in to cure a bewitched girl, Griet. Piter sets up a number of crosses by the house to ward off further witchcraft. Griet must also boil a packet of needles in hot water. Piter predicts that the next morning a completely burnt old woman, the witch, will appear at the door. This indeed happens. Griet recovers.
20330: A cheerful man suddenly becomes very gloomy and quiet. He assures his wife that nothing is wrong, but remains downcast. In the end he tells his wife that they are about to lose two children, because he has seen their funeral. Some time later it comes true exactly. The man was born with a caul and can foresee things that are going to happen in the future.
20331: Will-o'-the-wisps, floating little lights, were often seen at a certain spot. Later a new house was built on that spot.
20333: At a haunted spot a foal runs about with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a phantom animal.
20335: At a haunted spot a few girls often run back and forth at night. It is said that one of the girls was murdered there long ago.
20336: At a haunted spot a large black dog runs about on which no head or tail can clearly be made out. It is a phantom animal.
20342: A witch once bewitched a child so badly that it eventually died. The same witch could also change into a cat. The narrator's uncle once gave the witch in cat form a hefty wallop. The next morning the witch was covered in bruises.
20343: Freemasons never lack money, because they own a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) that can never run out. They got the wisseldaalder by running around the churchyard three times with a cat in a sack, calling 'who will buy my hare?'. In the end the devil himself bought the cat in the sack for a wisseldaalder.
20344: Sometimes people send away a jack of spades to fetch a bottle of drink. They must make sure that the one who sent the bottle away does not take hold of it, and that the first glass is thrown away.
20345: A man born with a caul sees a funeral procession pass at night. It is a vision of the future.
20346: A woman born with a caul predicts the death of her neighbour, because she has already seen her funeral. Three or four weeks later the neighbour does indeed die.
20347: A man, Douwe, urges another man to step to the side because a funeral procession has to pass. Only Douwe can see the procession.
20353: When a witch goes out in the evening and at night to do magic, she often leaves a tripe behind.
20354: A witch cat often gets a hefty wallop. The next day a woman beaten black and blue turns up. That was the witch in cat form.
20355: If a barn owl calls on the owl board, a death in the neighbourhood is imminent. It is an omen.
20356: A golden wagon is said to have once driven at a haunted spot. It was a ghost wagon.
20366: A floating little light can often be seen at a certain spot. Later a house is built on the same spot. The will-o'-the-wisp was an omen.
20367: A sorcerer can make little soldiers appear from the stoke hole. He can also have a bottle of liquor fetched by means of a playing card.
20368: In the old days many people went to a card reader to see their future in a black mirror. Some did not dare, because they were afraid of seeing a coffin.
20369: A man is seized and thrown to the ground by the devil in the shape of a small black fellow.
20370: A man with a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) goes bankrupt. This is remarkable, because it is said that owners of wisseldaalders can never lack money, since this coin can never run out.
20372: A boy hears hammering at night. Shortly afterwards a new chicken coop is built. It was an omen.
20373: A group of boys were waiting for a man with a wheelbarrow. When they heard the sound of a wheelbarrow, they thought he was coming. But when they went to look, there was nothing to be seen: the man would only actually appear an hour later. The sound of the wheelbarrow was a forerunner.
20375: A man born with a caul often has to get up at night to see things. Usually he sees funeral processions pass by. The processions foreshadow an impending death.
20376: Children are warned not to walk in the middle of the road because funeral processions may pass. The processions are a harbinger of a death.
20378: A merchant with his horse and cart wants to pass a tree but cannot get by because he is pushed off the road.
20380: At a certain place people often heard cries for help coming from a pond. A few years later someone did indeed drown in that pond. The cries for help had been a harbinger of the coming death by drowning.
20381: Two brothers see a glowing white thing that looks like a small child floating at night. It turns out to be a ghostly apparition: long ago a child was murdered at that spot.
20385: A few hunters are startled three times by a cat on the road. They are very frightened because they think it is a witch cat.
20386: A few men were each, separately, seized for no reason at a certain spot and thrown down some distance away.
20387: People who own a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) have sold their soul to the devil.
20390: During his military service the wizard Imke de Jong was often thrown in jail. Imke always freed himself from his cell effortlessly because he could pass through closed doors.
20391: At a haunted spot a large black dog roams about. The animal approaches people but disappears as suddenly as it appeared. It is a phantom animal.
20392: A man born with a caul often has to get up at night to see things. He often foresees deaths in passing funerals. Although the man's caul was destroyed at his birth, he always has visions of the future.
20393: When a death is imminent, a dog always starts to howl eerily. The dog foresees the death.
20394: If the bells ring in a certain way, a death is coming. It is an omen of an approaching death.
20396: At a certain spot people often see two little lights floating in the evening. Later two new houses are built on that spot. The will-o'-the-wisps were an omen.
20397: People often see a little light floating over the heath. Later the tram will run at that spot. The will-o'-the-wisp was an omen.
20399: In the old days people sometimes saw houses on fire that later really burnt down. These were voorgezichten (visions of future events).
20400: At a certain spot people often see little lights floating. Later a new house is built there. The will-o'-the-wisps were an omen.
20401: At a certain spot people often hear hammering. Later a new house is built there. The hammering was an omen.
20425: A cat gets a good beating. The next morning an old woman is lame. The woman is a witch: she was the witch cat that was beaten the day before.
20426: A cat gets a hefty wallop. A day later an old woman walks about with her arm wrapped in a cloth. She is a witch: she was the witch cat that was beaten the day before.
20427: If you eat something you got from a witch, you turn into a toad.
20428: If you send an empty bottle away with a jack of spades, the bottle comes floating back into the room filled with drink. The narrator wonders whether this is a kind of spiritualism.
20429: A man can conjure little soldiers out of the stoke hole and make them march.
20430: A man hears a cat making a racket in the attic. When he goes to look, the animal is nowhere to be found. An hour later he hears the same sound and this time the cat is there. The sound was an omen.
20431: One night a boy hears his brother, who is a soldier, come home. A little later he sees him very clearly reading the newspaper in a corner. A month later the brother actually comes home and withdraws with his newspaper in exactly the same way as the boy had seen before. It was a vision of the future.
20443: A married couple drinks tea at a witch's house and shortly afterwards the wife is tormented by severe ear and head pains. The pain returns every day at the same time, three o'clock in the afternoon, and lasts for a year. At exactly three o'clock in the afternoon there is also always a strange cat in the garden. The husband gives the cat a hefty wallop and at once the pain disappears. The day after, the couple's neighbour woman walks about with a cloth around her head. The neighbour is a witch: in cat form she made sure the wife kept suffering pain.
20445: Stammerige Harm has a pot of money buried in the ground. He got the money from the devil because he made a pact with the devil.
20447: A man born with a caul urges his companions to step aside for a passing funeral procession. The seer predicts that a man will be killed in an accident and how it will happen, and he sees the whole funeral pass before him in detail. Fourteen days later the man in question actually dies when he falls between two wagons. Everything happens exactly as the man with the caul foresaw.
20448: A woman foresees that a train accident is about to happen.
20449: A girl sees a funeral procession pass: all her relatives walk behind the coffin, but she herself is missing. She thinks it possible that she herself will soon die, or perhaps someone else.
20450: One night a girl sees a funeral procession with a dead person pass. A little later a coffin is also placed in the kitchen. These are omens: shortly afterwards her little sister is killed in a traffic accident. The funeral takes place exactly as the girl saw it earlier.
20451: A man sees the whole course of a funeral pass before him in detail. Shortly afterwards the person in question actually dies. The man often foresees things: they are visions of the future.
20452: A clairvoyant always has to go out at night to see things. Once he stands by the road in his underpants to watch a funeral procession pass. He had been driven out of bed with such irresistible force that he had no time even to pull on his trousers.
20466: A cunning doctor knows a great deal about curing cattle and foresees things that come true.
20490: At a haunted spot a foal runs about with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a phantom animal.
20493: On his way home, a carpenter comes upon a black man who blocks his way. Suddenly a magpie flies out of the tree and the man hears a strange sound. At the same moment the man is roughly seized and thrown down.
20494: If magpies chatter at night, a death is imminent. It is an omen.
20499: In a mirror tent you were supposed to be able to behold your future bride in a black mirror. The narrator once saw a woman with a broad golden oorijzer (traditional metal headpiece) in such a mirror, but he never married a woman who looked like that.
20507: Many people are troubled by nightmares (mares). The nightmares, mostly women, enter the house through the keyhole and crawl on top of people. Nightmares may not take anything from the house they have been in. A man who was often tormented by nightmares once threw flour over a nightmare: the next morning the nightmare stood in the back of the house brushing off her clothes, because all the flour had to be removed before she could leave the house.
20510: At a haunted spot a foal runs about with a porridge pot and a ladle around its neck. It is a phantom animal.
20511: A farmhand living with the wizard Stammerige Harm wakes up at night and sees not Harm but a tripe lying in Harm's bed. Terrified, the farmhand then sees a big cat approach the tripe. The cat keeps circling the tripe and grows smaller and smaller. While circling, the cat shrinks to the size of a little mouse. When the creature has finally vanished completely, Stammerige Harm is suddenly lying in bed again. Harm had been out doing magic as a cat and had left a tripe in the bed.
20512: A witch's cat often roams about a certain place. People want to burn the cat in the fire, but they can never catch the animal.
20513: At a certain place a coach with a horse in front suddenly comes up out of the ground. It is a ghost coach.
20514: A cheese porter once comes upon a singing cats' meeting around a small fire. He listens to the songs for a while, but soon runs off in fear. When he looks back after a while, there is no trace of fire or cats to be seen. They are witch cats.
20515:
Children used to be warned never to eat anything that came from a witch: the food would immediately turn into a toad.
Witches also often had little dolls that they stuck pins into.
To keep witches away, children used to put a cross in the meadow.
20517: At night naked little children sometimes knocked on the window. They could not find rest because they had been buried without a shroud.
20518: A treasure chest in the ground can never be dug up, because the chest sinks a little deeper into the ground just as the diggers are about to grab it. In the end flames even shoot out of the chest. It is said that the treasure chest will only stop sinking when a white billy goat runs over the spot.
20519: In a certain haunted barn, everything is flung aside or straight out of the barn. A bunch of daredevils decide to spend the night in the barn anyway, and nothing happens to them.
20520: A man on his way home is suddenly seized near the railway and thrown into the ditch, without anyone to be seen.
20525: A fortune-teller who can see the future in coffee grounds always has many visitors. Card readers also get many callers. A card reader predicts that a woman will soon marry, and it comes true exactly.
20529: A man who wants to sell his soul to the devil hangs a boot in the barn, which the devil will fill with money. When the boot is completely full, the pact with the devil is sealed. The man apparently has doubts after all and has knocked the sole off the boot. The devil cannot fill the boot and eventually gives up. Thus the man outwits the devil.
20531: A man never lacks money because he owns a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) that never runs out.
20533: Two men take turns owning a devil's book. When they read from the book, they can make magpies and little soldiers appear from the hearth pit. The two also work for a farmer, but never feel much like exerting themselves. Once, when the men are told to spread manure over the land, they first settle back comfortably, and only towards evening do they start the job, with the help of a big black dog. The dog is the devil, and with his help the job is done in no time. Later people see the print of a horse's hoof in the ground: proof that the devil really was there.
20536: A sailor's wife is very anxious about her husband's fate and calls in the help of the minister. The minister asks her if he may sleep on her bed for a while to see how the man is doing. The minister stretches out comfortably and is soon fast asleep. When he gets up a short while later, he says the woman need not worry about anything, because her husband, the sailor, has just posted a letter that will probably arrive within a few days. It comes true exactly as the minister predicted. Afterwards the couple want nothing more to do with the minister, because they believe such arts are the devil's arts.
20537: At a haunted spot, wandering witte wieven (white women) hang with their arms over the gates.
20538: At a certain spot wilde lantaarnen (wild lanterns) were sometimes visible. These will-o'-the-wisps are forerunners: it happened that a house was later built on the same spot.
20539: A woman once, long ago, stood face to face with a glowing devil.
20540: At a haunted spot a very large dog with a tail like a broom often roams about. It is a phantom animal.
20541: A witch initiates an apprentice into witchcraft. The apprentice has to repeat after the witch: 'Here we sit beneath the willows, cursing God with all his saints'. But the apprentice says: 'Here we sit beneath the willows, cursing the devil with all his followers'. Nothing ever came of her career as a witch.
20543: A married couple hear hammering at night, but when they go to investigate there is nothing to be seen. Later the carpenter's house is built on that spot. It was an omen.
20554: Hinse the devil-banisher is fond of a drink and, dead drunk, lets a boy escort him home. Because the boy has been promised a reward of ten guilders, Hinse has to consult the devil in the churchyard for some money. The terrified boy takes to his heels and lets the devil's money pass him by.
20563: A woman always chased the neighbours' chickens off her yard. The day after she had also hit a strange cat, the woman fell ill. She found wreaths in her pillow and burned them. She also sealed all the holes and cracks in the house. Then the neighbour woman's daughter came to ask whether she would come to her mother because she had such a sore foot. The woman refused and said: "One time it is the one's turn, and the other time it is the other's turn."
20566: A farmhand was sitting at the table late one evening. Suddenly he saw the hunchbacked woman he lodged with come in through the cat flap as a cat. And then she was just sitting on a chair in her true form, wearing her oorijzer (traditional metal headpiece) and her floppy bonnet.
20570: A young man was sitting in the privy when suddenly a very large beast came up to him.
20571: In Westereinde a foal haunts with a porridge pot around its neck. In that porridge pot is a ladle.
20572: At a place where a few girls were murdered and buried, people sometimes see girls strolling with a pool of blood between them.
20579: One evening a farmhand heard hammering three times, but there was nothing to be seen. Three years later the front of the farmhouse was rebuilt.
20580: One evening people saw a silent man suddenly sink into the ground.
20581: In Drogeham a white foal walks around the churchyard in the evening.
20582: In the old days children were not allowed to walk in the middle of the road because of the funeral processions.
20586: One evening people once saw two witte wijven (white women).
20587: The wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns) that people used to see were forerunners of the later cars and bicycles.
20591: Sorceresses can turn themselves into black cats. They must not be allowed near children and livestock.
20603: One evening a young man heard a splash in the water behind the flax-breaking sheds. A few days later a neighbour drowned at exactly that spot.
20604: A brother and sister were once on their way to fetch their mother when they were followed by a white cat. They did not trust it and went back. Near a churchyard the white cat suddenly vanished and an old woman came by who knew they wanted to go to their mother. That woman was a witch who could turn herself into a white cat.
20606: When the mermaid came into the shipping lane, it was a bad sign.
20608: If you put an empty bottle outside the door with a jack of spades, it is filled again. The first dram must then be thrown away over the shoulder, for the fetcher, the devil.
20609: The husband of a pregnant woman once saw people carrying a coffin into his room. A few days later his wife died in childbirth, as did the baby. Then he saw exactly the same thing as a few days before.
20613: Two friends were once walking along the middle of the dyke. One man said they had to step aside because a funeral procession was coming past. The other man saw nothing. A few days later an old woman died, and she was carried over the dyke.
20614: If you put a corner piece of peat in the stove, unexpected visitors will come.
20615: If the gate bangs, unexpected visitors will come.
20616: A family was so poor that they almost never had money for meat. Once in a while they smelled roast meat. A few days later they would indeed eat meat.
20617: A skipper's wife always heard clapping two days before the ship came back.
20622: An old woman once told a passer-by on the dyke that he had to step aside. She saw a funeral procession with rearing horses approaching. A few days later the carriage really came past.
20624: A woman had seen a farm burning one night. A few days later the farm did indeed burn down; the hay had overheated.
20631: Old Foppe, the sorcerer, could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. The little soldiers would then skip around the house.
20634: A farmer had promised his wife that he would have her buried in Oosterbierum if she died. But he did not keep the promise and had her buried in the place where they lived. The woman then came to haunt him. After six weeks he had her dug up and buried in Oosterbierum.
20637: Klaas Kunst once rode out of the gates at four corners of the town at the same time.
20643: If the clock stops, it is an omen that someone will soon die.
20644: A man saw a fire in a house somewhere. When he looked at the front of the house, he saw a small lamp burning on a counter. At the back he saw fire everywhere inside. And yet there was no house there at all. Later a bakery was built there. The bread would be sold by the lamp on the counter, and the ovens would be at the back.
20645: A widow heard hammering in the house night after night, but in reality there was nothing. Later her brother-in-law did carpentry work there.
20646: A young man once saw a house on fire by the bridge. But his mother saw nothing, and when he looked again a little later, he no longer saw it either. Exactly two years later a house burnt down on that spot.
20647: A young man once saw a house on fire by the bridge. Exactly two years later a house burnt down on that spot.
20648: A man born with a caul saw the water mill on fire one evening. A little later there was nothing to be seen. Not long afterwards lightning struck the mill and it really burnt down.
20649: In the old days wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns) were seen above a small lake. They were omens of bicycle lamps.
20651: One night a man had walked around the church three times with a cat in a sack. At the door he called each time: "Who will buy my hare for a daalder?" The third time the devil gave him a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin). The man must take care not to spend the whole daalder.
20660: A man had sold himself to the devil. He had a magic coin and could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
20661: In Harkema at least ten houses have burnt down that people had seen beforehand would burn down.
20666: A woman saw things in advance. She said there would be wagons without horses and that all sorts of things would travel through the air, flying just like birds. Those were the later cars and aeroplanes.
20667: In places where hammering was heard, a new house was later built.
20671: If a dog howls eerily, there will be a death within three days.
20672: You must never walk in the middle of the road, but always at the side. A funeral procession might come along that you cannot see.
20675: A man once saw a white lady during a polecat hunt.
20676: Two small naked children were sometimes seen behind the little lake. They had been murdered there and could find no rest.
20677: A man had let it be known that he wanted to be buried standing up. Then he could look out over the land. But the people had not done so. Then he came to haunt his family and knock at the door. They had a minister ask him what his wish was. They then dug him up and buried him standing up.
20678: A drunk man was once thrown across the ditch and landed on a tree stump. From then on he was afraid of the dark and always walked with his clogs in his hand, so he could run away quickly.
20682: A mocker was once coming out of the inn when he was thrown over the trees. He died of it.
20684: On a spot where the sound of hammering had once been heard, a house was later built.
20685:
A man often had to get out of bed at night to see funeral processions.
People walking in the middle of the road are sometimes suddenly set aside at the edge of the road. Then a funeral procession is passing.
20686: Stotterende Harm dealt in small livestock. If people did not want to sell him anything, he would briefly run his hand over the animals, and the next day they were dead. He always kept his wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) under his pillow. Thanks to this magic coin he never lacked money.
20687: Reid Keuning could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. He made them march. He also sent out cards to fetch a bottle of liquor.
20689: One evening a man saw a farm on fire. But in reality it was not burning. A year later it burnt down.
20690: One night two brothers heard hammering in the back of the house. Not long afterwards the back of the house was rebuilt.
20691: A man was thrown over the poplars near the little house at the churchyard. He was unhurt.
20692: At midnight a man saw his father bringing barley to the cow. But in reality his father was simply lying in bed.
20710: Three boys were strolling about when one of them suddenly jumped aside. He saw a black carriage drawn by two horses approaching. The others saw nothing.
20711: A man foresaw that war would come. Blood ran into the canal, so fierce was the fighting. But it did not happen.
20712: A doctor once came into an inn completely shaken. He told the innkeeper he had nearly been run over by a train. But there was not even a railway.
20713: A postman once walked into a tree, though there was no tree there at all. Later a telephone pole was put there.
20714: Two men who were born with a caul saw funeral processions now and then.
20717: Some boys once got some apples from a friend whose mother was a sorceress. They did not dare eat them for fear that they would turn into a toad or a snake.
20718: To stop a sorceress, people sometimes made a cross on the road.
20724: A minister's dead wife kept coming back and standing by the fire of the hearth pit. She wanted the money hidden in the hearth pit to be divided among the orphans and widows. The minister handed her a white handkerchief as a sign that it would be done. The handkerchief burned in his hand. After that she never came back.
20725: The farmer did not allow the workers to go to a certain spot in the barn. At night some people then saw a woman with a child at her breast at that spot, above the rafters.
20726: In some barns in Groningen, you were sometimes thrown from your place for no reason.
20727: A man was once coming out of the inn when he was suddenly lifted up and thrown into the ditch.
20728: You must never walk in the middle of the road in the evening. For if you meet a funeral procession, you are pushed aside. It also happened that people walked right into the front of a hearse. Then they fell.
20732: One evening a mother and her children saw a whole group of women wearing oorijzers (traditional metal head ornaments) and caps. When they came close to the women, they suddenly vanished. They had been witches.
20735: If you get an apple from a sorceress, you must never eat it all. Otherwise you get a live toad in your body. If you say 'yes' three times in a row, a sorceress gets you in her power. In the past children learned from their mothers to say a rhyme when an old woman passed by: 'One, old devil, two, old devil, three, old devil. No, old witch, you won't get me!'
20736: A sorceress stuck needles into dolls to torment her victims. Her son told her that she would die if he had bewitched her. But he died himself.
20788: Some people sent out the jack of spades. Then a little later there was a bottle of drink on the table with the card attached.
20790: When a sorceress wanted to bewitch someone, she conjured wreaths into the victim's pillow. As soon as three wreaths were finished, the bewitched person was dead. In the old days, as soon as people felt anything in their pillow, they unpicked it. The wreaths then had to be burnt.
20791: A man found out that the local notables were using his little boat at night. When they spoke a magic spell, the boat flew straight to Paris, where they partied all night. He decided to do the same with his friends, and they had a fun night in Paris. But when they wanted to go back, the man spoke the spell wrongly. Instead of 'over the woods, over the trees, over the mountains, etc.' he said 'through the woods, through the trees, through the mountains, etc.' Because of this the way back was very rough, and everyone was badly shaken about. And the boat was so damaged that it could never be used again.
20796: To get an empty bottle filled again, people used to tie a jack of spades to the empty bottle. One of those present carried it to the door, walking backwards. A little later there would be a banging on the door. Someone else then had to receive the bottle from the devil, also backwards. The first dram was not to be drunk but was thrown on the hearth fire.
20799: Black mirrors were often set up at the markets. There you got to see your whole life story. If a coffin appeared, you would soon die.
20801: At midnight a skipper hears his ropes being thrown onto the deck. He gets out of bed to tie them up again. The next day the skipper ahead of him asked whether he had been able to stay moored at that spot. A woman used to live there who did not want a ship lying in front of her house. A deckhand drowned then, because she had taken away the planks. Ever since it has been haunted there and no skipper can stay moored there.
20802: A woman who was born with a caul saw funeral processions.
20806: A large black dog haunts the Garijp dike.
20810: A fisherman's daughter once sailed to a man on the other side of the water. When she reached the man, she suddenly vanished. It was the tall Sleatterman.
20813: During a storm a married couple saw a dung wheelbarrow fall from the sky.
20819: If you heard hammering at the carpenter's at night, another death would soon follow. A coffin was being made then.
20822: An old man once said he had seen the mill turning with only one sail. A year later the mill was struck by lightning, and only one sail was left.
20829: A little boy once shouted that there was a fire, but nobody saw anything. A few days later two houses burnt down on that spot.
20837: After a woman had died, the neighbours stood waiting in the yard out of neighbourly duty. They heard a sound of iron going over iron, but there was nothing to be seen. Later the tram ran past at that very spot. It was exactly the same sound.
20842: One magpie brings bad luck, two magpies mean visitors.
20843: If the windmill stood with its sails in a cross, it meant death.
20848: A widow always sat on the same side of her sick son's bed. The woman had been born with a caul. When one day she sat on the other side, the boy understood that his mother had seen a coffin in the place where she usually sat. Three days later the boy died, and indeed the coffin was placed in that very spot.
20849: A rider on a white horse used to haunt the Swichumerijk.
20854: A black lady haunted the little wood near Kootstermolen.
20859: One evening a few neighbours saw a funeral procession pass by. A few days later a little boy from the neighbourhood died.
20861: A mother told her son they had to step aside because a funeral procession was coming. The child had seen nothing.
20864: A white lady haunts the Kletten at night.
20866: At the Noorderkerkhof in Drachten people always saw little lights. Those were the bicycles that came later.
20867: A woman often heard hammering in places where building later took place.
20871: In the west of Buitenpost a foal walks about with a porridge pot around its neck.
20875: In Eestrum a foal walks about with a porridge pot around its neck.
20877: One night a man saw two women in hoop skirts floating across the field.
20880: A son had promised his mother to pay her debt for the buckwheat. But when she died, he did not keep this promise. Then his mother came to haunt him, and in the end he paid the debt after all.
20881: Someone lived on the Tike who could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
20882: Carpenters saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns). Later bicycles and cars came.
20883: If hammering started up somewhere at night, a house was later built on that spot.
20884: Some people on the Tike saw funeral processions beforehand.
20886: In Oostermeer, by the thick trees, a foal haunts the place with a porridge pot around its neck.
20888: In the old days, when someone came along the Zwarte Weg drunk, someone stood there who would throw him. That was the evil one.
20889: A man who was born with a caul warned another man to step to the side of the road and take off his cap. A funeral procession was coming past, which the other man could not see.
20892: When a skipper's wife died, she made her husband promise to sell her jewellery. With that money he was to have their little daughter, who had club feet, taught to sew. But the man did not keep his promise. The woman came back as a ghost, and the skipper had the minister ask her what she wanted. She wanted him to keep his promise. When the minister held out his white handkerchief to her as a sign that it would be done, it burned in his hands. The skipper kept his promise, and the woman was never seen again.
20896: A man who was born with a caul often had to go out at night to see funeral processions. Once the weather was so bad that he wanted to stay in bed. But then a huge black dog with glowing eyes came, and the man got up quickly after all.
20897: Dogs often howl eerily beforehand when a death is coming.
20904: A farmhand saw in the black mirror that he would marry someone he did not like. It did indeed happen, and the couple quarrelled a lot. The farmhand had to leave the tent backwards.
20907: Witches have a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin). In the evening they hang an empty sack on the door, and the next day it is filled with money.
20911: An old spinster often had to get out of bed at night to see funeral processions. Once she refused to give way to something she saw coming, and she got a crack in her head. When she grew too old to get out of bed at night, she opened the curtains and saw everything through the window.
20912: Old Bontsje Knjillis foresaw all kinds of things. He often had to get out of bed at night to see funeral processions. Once he did not want to get up, but then a big dog with glowing eyes came to him. Another time a farmhand died after coughing up blood for some time. Knjillis believed it was his fault, because he had once given the farmhand a severe beating.
20913: One summer evening a man was sitting on the little bridge in front of his house. He saw a funeral procession approaching, but just before it reached him, he could no longer see it. A moment later he saw the procession again, and it had already passed the bridge. A few days later the maid died. That was why the man had seen the funeral procession.
20914: On the Lange laan in Westereinde, Anne Elzinga saw a great many people who had long been dead.
20915: An old woman who was born with a caul often saw funeral processions pass her house.
20926: A labourer once heard a roaring coming from a small cloud in the sky. A year later the train came there, making exactly the same sound. So it had been sorcery.
20930: A man once saw a woman in a red petticoat flying through the air on a broom.
20933: A man now and then saw a naked newborn baby go along a road and over a dike.
20948: Five weeks before a fire, a woman had already seen the house burn down.
20949: A woman had heard the sound of hammering a year in advance on the spot where her later house was built.
20950: A man could not pass a house because he saw a funeral procession standing there. The woman of the house asked him whether it was her son who would die. But the man had not been able to see who was in the hearse. A week later the son died.
20951: One night a woman heard the sound of hammering. Later a new house was built.
20953: A man was sleeping on his back when a nightmare (a mare) came to him. By turning onto his side, he was freed of her.
20955: Near Surhuisterveen a horse haunts. The animal stands with its head over the gate. When one comes closer, it suddenly can no longer be seen.
20958: A man said he would kill anyone he met, even if it were the devil himself. The first thing he met was a small black dog. The man came home more dead than alive.
20959: While a man was urinating in the bushes, he saw a fellow sitting at the top of the thicket. That fellow grabbed him and threw him over the dike twice. When he came back a little later with his brother, the fellow was already gone.
20964: One evening a man saw something that was not right. But he was a believer and he said the Lord's Prayer. Then his heart felt lighter.
20966: A woman had seen a house burn down in advance.
20968:
Minse Griper was a devil banisher and Tryn Snipel was his wife. People often came to her to have their cards read. Once she wished a woman into the canal, and the woman flew straight into the canal.
People send out a jack of spades for a bottle of drink. The first dram was thrown into the fire.
20970: When the first bicycles with lights came, people said: "Here come wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns)."
21008: A skipper never did any work and lived well all the same. He had sold himself to the devil. Now and then he hung a stocking on a string under a pipe over the canal. He would then receive money in it.
21010: A skipper always saw a naked baby at a certain spot, and it was clear that the baby had a wish. He fetched a minister, and the child told him its wish. The skipper had to go to a dike in Leeuwarden. A lady in black would be walking there with a parcel in her hand. He had to ask for that parcel and give it to the baby. The skipper did so. He handed the parcel to the child with a well hook. The parcel was scorched. The baby was never seen again. The baby had probably drowned there, had no shroud and could find no rest.
21011: A few boys looked in at crazy Jelke's, having heard that something was not right there. They saw the man pour a cup of coffee for someone else and talk to them. But there was nobody else there. Later that day the boys peeked in again. Then the man poured a bowl of sheep's milk for someone else. Suddenly they saw a woman appear out of nowhere. She had no feet, but floated through the air.
21013: When bad weather is coming, the mermaid rises up.
21014: A young man often sawed boards from tree trunks his father bought. One night he heard the sound of tree trunks being thrown. But when he wanted to start sawing the next day, there was no tree at all. The trees only came the following week.
21015: A man went to a devil-banisher because his nephew was ill. He was given a substance that no one else was allowed to see, which he had to put on the child's clothes. The man did this. He also opened the child's pillow. In it he found three wreaths, but the third was not quite finished. He burnt these wreaths. The next day he asked a woman at his work what was wrong with her. She said she had burnt herself the previous evening. Then he knew she was the one who had bewitched his nephew.
21017: The bakers of Himrik knew beforehand when someone was going to die, because then the cake boards were thrown about at night.
21018: When the dogs howl eerily, someone will die.
21020: When someone is murdered, that person later haunts the spot. A girl was once murdered in Oranjewoud. Afterwards she always floated over the dike in the evening, with her hair loose and dressed all in white.
21023: At night two women in white robes walk about on the Singel in Jobbegea.
21024: In the ninth district of the Jobbegeaster Compagnie a white horse with a porridge pot around its neck walked about at night.
21026: Hinke Kaert was born with a caul. She had to go out at night to see funeral processions.
21029: In Terwispel a foal walks about with a porridge pot around its neck. A horse haunts there too. And a magpie with a burnt head haunts there.
21030: It is haunted at the Godloze Tolhek (Godless Tollgate) in Zwaag. Two drunks once lay down on the rails and were run over by a tram.
21034: In Terwispel lived someone who could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit and make them march. There was also someone who sent out a jack of clubs to get a bottle of liquor. And some had a wisseldaalder (a magic coin that always returns to its owner).
21038: A married couple heard beforehand the wailing of their child in its death throes. Because of this they knew they would lose the child.
21039: The wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns) of the old days were omens of the later lampposts and the lights of bicycles and cars.
21040: A man used to see funeral processions all the time. He would then step aside to let the procession pass.
21041: In a neighbourhood people once heard a voice. Not long afterwards a child drowned.
21049: A man and a woman were very poor. They had once bought a piglet, which they were going to fatten for the winter. But the man died before winter, and the woman sold the piglet to pay for the funeral. But she had promised her husband to slaughter the animal, and now she did not keep that promise. Because of this her husband could find no rest in death, and now and then he appeared to her. Then she bought the animal back and slaughtered it, and since then her husband has not appeared again.
21065:
A man always had to go out at night. Sometimes he did not even have time to dress properly. Once he did not want to get up and stayed in bed. But then a huge dog with eyes like saucers came and pulled him out of bed.
The man also saw his own daughter's funeral in advance.
21066: A plain-clothes policeman once saw a woman, long dead, standing leaning over a gate. He told an acquaintance that he had not seen the old woman but her skeleton with a cloth wrapped around it.
21068: The witches sometimes went to the wine cellar in Spain.
21071: A nightmare (a mare) drops onto someone's feet and then slowly moves up to the neck. Then it wraps itself completely around the throat.
21073: Piters Willemke was a sorceress. She often flew through the air on a broomstick. At her place a bag of money hung in the tree. When she died, the neighbours did not dare to dress her. The policeman's wife did it then.
21075: Stotterende Harm had a magic coin. Those who traded with him always found a daalder missing from their purse when they got home.
21080: On his way back from his girlfriend, a young man saw a funeral procession pass. A few days later old Meike died.
21081: A young man once saw a funeral procession.
21082: A mother already knows beforehand that her little child will soon die; she has heard knocking.
21083: On the way back along the railway, a young man saw a large white ghost. Terrified, he knocked at the nearest house. The woman there looked after him until he was well past the ghost.
21084: A man once saw a whole crowd of people who had died long ago. It made such an impression on him that he was completely changed by it.
21085: A sorceress stuck pins into rag dolls.
21087: An old man haunts a spot where a chest of money is also buried in the ground.
21088: Two little brothers were playing in the house. Suddenly a small girl came. She put both her little hands on the table, turned around and looked at the boys. Then she disappeared again behind a door. The boys went after her but saw nothing more. They told their mother what they had seen. They also described the girl's clothes. The mother said those were the same clothes their sister had been wearing when she died.
21090: A woman in bed at night always heard the sound of iron on iron. Her husband heard nothing. Later the tram came past there. It made exactly the sound she had always heard.
21091: In Westereinde there once lived a man who was born with a caul. Sometimes someone knocked on his window and then he went outside. When he came back in, he said that soon there would be another death. Outside he had seen the whole funeral: a farm wagon with a coffin and lots of people following it. It always came true.
21092: A small child began crying and raving every night between one and two o'clock and could not be calmed. An acquaintance said the child was bewitched. In the child's pillow they found a wreath. When a black cat came along, they threw stones at it. Later an unmarried pedlar came to the door with bandages all around his head. He must have been the sorcerer.
21093: A woman had sometimes said during her life that she wanted to be buried wearing a white cap. But when the woman died, people no longer remembered it. A few days after the funeral there was knocking, but nothing could be seen. This went on for a few days, until the people consulted someone. He asked whether it had anything to do with someone who had died. Then they thought about it, and remembered the white cap. The man advised them to put a white cap on the chair in the evening. They did so, and since that time they have never been troubled again.
21096: If you eat something from a sorceress, you get a toad in your body. To get rid of it, you must boil a certain amount of green soap with a few pins and a certain amount of water. You must pour off the liquid and drink some of it now and then. Then you become sick, but you get rid of the toad, or it dies.
21097: Once magpies were chattering behind an old woman's house. The woman believed this meant someone would soon die, which did indeed happen.
21101: The wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns) of the old days were omens of new houses.
21102: A soldier was keeping watch in a horse stable. He was lying in the straw when a nightmare (a mare) came to him. He asked, 'What do you want, devil?' But he should never have said that, for then she handled him very roughly.
21103: A woman was often troubled by nightmares (mares). Her husband said she should wake him the next time it happened. The next time a nightmare came to her, she woke her husband. He struck the nightmare right through the bed boards. The woman always had her slippers placed backwards against the bed when she lay in bed.
21110: An orange seller came to a poor woman's door. He said he could help her get money. She would have to go with her black cat to the church in Peize and walk around it three times. At the church door she would have to say each time: "I commend myself to the devil's arts." The third time a man would be standing there who would give her a magic coin for the cat. Then she would never lack money again. But the woman said she would never do that.
21111: Several people heard the tram beforehand, before it ran.
21113: A man once saw a wagon with a dead cow on it. He saw someone stumble over the dead cow. When the wagon reached the man, he was suddenly thrown over the trees.
21115: A man once walked past a woman wearing a broad golden oorijzer (traditional metal headpiece) on her head. As he passed her, she lifted him up and threw him onto the field across the canal.
21117: A woman once saw her hut in flames. But when she came closer, nothing was wrong. Later, however, the hut did burn down.
21121: Jehannes [Meerstra] was a cheese merchant. That is why he was also called Jehannes Kaas. He could also make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit.
21125: A man who cared about nothing had once played 'What the devil can play! What the devil can dance!' on his accordion all evening in the inn. When he went back home he was thrown over the dike several times. He came home black and blue all over.
21129: A man had seen his wife's entire funeral beforehand.
21130: A woman once heard hammering and throwing, as if the place was being torn down. But there was nothing to be seen. Some time later a new house was built on that spot.
21135: A spot where an old woman was murdered has been haunted ever since.
21136: Two men clearly see a person. They both step aside to let that person through, but suddenly they no longer see anyone.
21138:
One morning an old woman told her granddaughter that a nightmare (a mare) had been with her that night, and that she had tried to wake her. The granddaughter asked what she should have done. The grandmother said that if she had sung a psalm, she would have been freed.

To women, men come as nightmares, and to men, women come. Of seven boys or girls born in succession, one is a nightmare. A nightmare is an evil spirit. You must put your slippers with the heels against the bed.
21140: Children always made a cross in the sand with their clog when Alle Tet came along. Then she could not get past it, because she was a sorceress. When she was dead, her body stayed completely limp.
21141: If a dog howls eerily, someone will soon die.
21142: A scoffer was once thrown from one side to the other by the devil.
21143: Never walk in the middle of the road, or you might walk into a funeral procession.
21153: Mike Ruerd was always at odds with the devil, who sat in his loft. Once he threw a whole load of peat at the devil in his loft, in an attempt to kill him. Sometimes Ruerd had to leave the room for a moment. Then he fought with the devil in the shed. People could hear him groaning then, so badly did the devil thrash him.
21157: In the past some people sometimes heard a train running through the dug-out peat canal. But a train never came.
21166: Nobody wanted to live in a certain house. Something was wrong there. The trees shook there, even when there was not a breath of wind.
21168: A girl warned a man not to go to the churchyard, because a woman with a basket of cakes stood there. The place was haunted. The man paid no attention and made a joke of it. But he came to regret it bitterly.
21171: Near Bakkeveen there used to be little lights. Later houses were built there. So it was sorcery.
21177: A man once saw a woman who had died in childbirth being laid out in his house. After that he no longer wanted to live in that house. Other people came to live there. Not long afterwards the woman died during childbirth. The previous occupant had already seen it beforehand.
21178: A few scoffers once celebrated Holy Communion in an inn. They drank and swore a lot. One of them slept that night in the hay at a farmer's. The next day he was found with his head turned around on his body.
21185: One night someone saw a coffin being slid through a window. A few days later that really happened. The coffin would not go through the door.
21186: A man was born with a caul. In the daytime he always saw funeral processions. Then he had to step aside.
21189: A dead man often came tapping on the windows in the evening, because his relatives had not given him the things he was entitled to in the grave. They fetched the minister, who advised them to lay the things beside the house one evening. The people then put them in the coffin, and placed it at the foot end.
21192: One evening a butcher was walking across the churchyard. He saw a white ghost looking at him and was so frightened that he lost his tools.
21194: To get free drink, you must send the empty bottle away with a jack of spades attached.
21199: A farm maid and a farmhand heard hammering every night, although building only went on during the day. It was sorcery.
21200: On his way back from his girlfriend, a young man sees a light. When he comes closer, it suddenly disappears. Later a house was built there. It was a wilde lantaarn (wild lantern).
21201: A young woman was coming back from dancing when she saw two undertakers. She did not hear their footsteps in the snow: they were floating. Later an old woman from the neighbourhood died.
21204: One evening a boy who still lived with his parents saw a white goat dancing and leaping in the field. He was so frightened that he ran into the house and jumped under the covers with his parents.
21207: A young man once went out with Reid Keuning. When they came back, Reid asked if he would come in for something to eat and drink. Inside, Reid made little soldiers come out of the hearth pit, marching two by two. They wore blue uniforms and had rifles over their shoulders. He also made them disappear into the stove again.
21211: Late one evening two men saw two glowing men on bicycles. It was just as if they were on fire.
21212: On the Kleine Weg a woman with a bread basket always haunted.
21215: One evening a man did not return another man's greeting. The other became angry and wanted to grab him. But his hand went right through him. It was a ghost.
21216: On the Veensterweg a foal always haunts with a porridge pot around its neck.
21219: A man sometimes mocked the Bible. At such times he would see a black cat that nobody else saw. When the man lay in his coffin, the coffin was still open just a tiny bit. And the window was open a crack, the width of a matchbox. The relatives saw a black cat come out of the room under the window. An ordinary cat could never get through such a narrow gap. When the relatives entered the room, they saw that the old man's nose had been bitten off. The cat must have done that. The cat must have been the devil.
21220: A woman heard hammering at the back of the house three nights in a row. Ten weeks later a new back was built on.
21221: A woman once heard something going through the thatched roof, and she thought there was a break-in. But there was nothing and no one to be seen. A few days later potatoes were stolen. Then exactly the same rustling could be heard as before.
21222: A girl heard children singing, and she saw little lights. She also heard the clatter of children's clogs and the words: "You must sit still." In reality there was nothing. But later a Sunday school came, and then it all came true.
21223: A woman saw a wagon with no horse in front of it, which almost drove her and her niece into the hedge. In reality there was nothing. A month later her son murdered a carpenter. Then the police came to drag him from his bed. They drove one of the first cars.
21227: A man prospered so much financially that people said he had a magic coin.
21230: In Surhuizum some scoffers celebrated Holy Communion in the pub. Afterwards one of them was so beaten and thrown about on his way home that he never again dared to walk outside alone.
21233: A young man always mocked God and His commandments. Once some people warned him that a certain place was haunted, but he said he was not afraid of even seven devils. When he came to that place, there were suddenly seven black figures. It was a terrible journey, and since that day he has been converted. He became Reformed and taught Sunday school to the children himself.
21235: A man cursed and swore and drank heavily. Once he said he wanted a girl, even if it were a donkey. On the way back a donkey suddenly came walking alongside him. He was so frightened that he knocked on someone's door, and that person brought him home. This person did not see the donkey. Once home, he smashed the windows out of sheer fear.
21237: On the spot where a Reformed church now stands, psalm singing was heard in the old days.
21239: A woman once borrowed flour and eggs from the shopkeeper's wife to bake pancakes. While she was busy baking, a cat suddenly appeared and asked whether she could really bake with borrowed things. The woman asked whether the cat wanted one too and threw a red-hot pancake onto the cat's head. The cat ran off. The next day the shopkeeper's wife lay ill in bed with a burnt face.
21248: Two brothers were once chasing a very big sheep. The animal jumped onto a dyke and was suddenly a woman. She laughed at the brothers' foolish faces and at how she had made them run.
21249: A man was given to drink and always mocked the devil. Once he was suddenly thrown over the bushes, after which he lay as if dead. The next day his wife brought him home on the cart. He was ill for a long time afterwards.
21250: A boy was once given pancakes by an old woman. When he came home, he vomited up lots of snakeskins. His two sisters angrily went to the old woman, but she slid like a snake between the two women.
21251: A father and son were once breaking flax. An exceptionally fat cat came up to them and the father hit the animal with a stick. The next day the neighbour woman lay in bed deathly ill.
21252: A woman once borrowed flour and eggs from the shopkeeper's wife to bake pancakes. While she was busy baking, a cat suddenly appeared and asked whether she could really bake with borrowed things. The woman asked whether the cat wanted one too and threw a red-hot pancake onto the cat's head. The cat ran off. The next day the shopkeeper's wife lay ill in bed with a burnt face.
21256: A farmhand had been to see the maid. On the way back he was suddenly put into a small lake by a stranger. The next day his cap was still floating in it.
21257: A drunk man was coming out of the pub when a very small little man lifted him up and threw him into the canal.
21265: In Burgum a foal haunts at night with a porridge pot around its neck.
21287: In Westereinde two girls always haunt at night.
21288: One night a man heard his son calling out in fear. He went to look, but the boy was sleeping peacefully. He also heard himself wailing. Six weeks later the son got lost in the fog on the mudflats and drowned. When the father received the bad news, he wailed just as he had heard himself do before.
21289: In Strobos they say that if a watch ticks wildly, someone will soon die. The same happens if a dog howls eerily, if the pigeons make a racket around the house, and if black jackdaws fly around the tower.
21290: A man was on his way from Strobos to his parents in Dokkum. His father was in a very bad way. On the way jackdaws flew over his head calling 'kaah-kaah'. Someone asked him what that meant, and he said they were calling 'too late, too late'. They were telling him he would reach his father too late. And indeed his father had already died when he arrived in Dokkum.
21292: A nightmare (a mare) is a big cat. From the chair in front of the bed it jumps onto the victim's shoulders.
21293: In Harkema people used to be buried wrapped in a white sheet. But the cloth was not allowed to reach past the ankles, because then one might trip at the resurrection. Once someone was laid in the coffin without a piece of the sheet being torn off. That person then began to haunt in a long white sheet, saying over and over 'too long, too long'. The exorcist advised telling the ghost that he should tear a piece off. They did so and they heard the tearing. A piece of sheet was thrown into the room, and since then the ghost has never come again.
21294: If a little bird taps against the glass, there will be a death or an accident. This also happens when the magpies chatter, when the convent bell rings or when the rain cloths flap. And when people in a funeral procession do not walk properly in line, and when the weight of the clock falls.
21296: One night two men were out hunting polecats. Suddenly they heard the dog howling as dogs do at ghosts. They thought another dog had attacked theirs, but that was not so. They saw a little child in a white cloth floating over the heath towards a small lake.
21297: Knjillis and Piter Alma, two brothers, were once coming back from their sister's. Piter saw something coming towards him; Knjillis saw nothing. Piter saw a man, as red and glowing as fire and without clothes. He said 'good evening' and the man greeted him back.
21299: In Uithuizermeden there was a haunted barn. In one half of the barn nobody could sleep. A man with a clay pipe always haunted there. He made sure he had a free path and was not disturbed.
21300: A man always cursed and raged terribly. The evil one then threw him across the canal. When he came home, dinner was on the table. He was given a fork in his hand to eat with. Then he got a beating.
21301: A boy was working when he had to go and relieve himself. He did not come back, and when people went looking for him, they found him with his head on the dike. He had been beaten by a very small little man, who had flung him from the dike onto the field, and from the field back onto the dike.
21302: A group of mockers once celebrated Holy Communion in an inn. That same night one of them ended up in the dredging pit. The next morning they found his body hanging in a tree.
21307: A man was sleeping in the hay. Once a nightmare (a mare) grabbed him by the toe. The man went completely cold, and his neck was squeezed shut.
21309: To get a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin), you must walk around a church three times with a black cat. At the church door you must call each time: "Who will buy my cat for a daalder?" The third time the door is opened a crack and a magic coin is given for the cat.
21324: A figure with eyes like dinner plates once sat by a scoffer's bed. He did nothing and said nothing. It was the devil. The man was so frightened by this that he converted and from then on always went faithfully to church.
21325: The devil throws an alcoholic over the trees and fights with the man. Later the devil converts the man, who afterwards goes to church regularly.
21328: A child is so ill that her devout father goes to a devil-banisher, who gives him a potion. To keep out whoever bewitched the child, a cross must be placed on the causeway. On the way back the man is so harassed by cows that he thinks the devil has a hand in it. Everyone can cross the causeway except the neighbour woman. In the child's pillow there is a wreath, which is burnt, at which the neighbour woman screams with pain.
21331: A young man was once coming back from his girlfriend's when he saw a white goat standing in the road. He tried to catch the animal, but suddenly it had vanished. It must have been a sorceress.
21333: A man was lying in bed when he suddenly saw very clearly a road with cars driving over it. Later that road was indeed built.
21336: Melle Tsjibbe's wife was a sorceress. She changed herself into a cat. Once they had hit the cat with a poker. The next day the old woman was lame.
21339: In Sumarreheide a few people saw the lights of the tram beforehand, before the tram was there.
21340: A little girl once saw a tram locomotive turn the corner, while in reality there was nothing. Some time later the tram came.
21341: Freemasons have a magic coin. They get it from the devil in the dark churchyard.
21342: A man once wanted a new bottle of drink. He threw a playing card from the boat into the water. Then a bottle floated onto the table. He threw the first glass over his left shoulder.
21343: The Iniaheide was haunted. Every evening a white hand came over the lower half-door of two old people's house.
21350: A man from Burgum who drove a dog cart was always lifted off the cart at the Poel in Tussendijken and flung onto the field. In the end he no longer dared to go past there.
21352: When a woman died, a neighbour said that she had already heard a dog howling eerily by the back of the house that week.
21353: One evening a girl saw a man go through the wall of a house and die. Her father told her that a path used to run there where a man had been murdered. The man still walked the same path.
21355: In Augustinusga people used to often see lanterns flying through the air.
21359: A big dog haunted the Tilleweg at night. Several people did not dare to use that road at night.
21360: A pregnant girl once heard the bells ringing while she was working. Another girl heard nothing. She said that the ringing of the bells meant she would die in childbirth. And that is what happened. The little daughter she bore survived, but she in turn died in childbirth.
21363: A man was once thrown over the dike with his paraffin cart and two dogs. When they landed, the paraffin cans were still standing upright in the cart. The man never dared to drive there again.
21365: A farmhand said he was not afraid of anything. Once someone stood waiting for him on a little bridge. He could tell it was no good sort. The man lifted him up and threw him into the water. After that the farmhand changed his tune considerably.
21367: Near Garijp a foal haunts with a porridge pot around its neck.
21368: One evening a fisherman suddenly saw his mother on the boat. His mother had long been dead. After that he no longer dared to fish at that spot.
21369: A certain Paulus once had a pair of shoes with silver buckles made. He made Klas promise not to sell them after his death. But Klas got into great need of money and sold them anyway. Then Paulus came to trouble him, and Klas made sure the shoes were returned.
21377: After a group of young people came out of the pub after a wild evening, the devil murdered one of them. He was found the next day with his legs in the water and his neck wrung.
21379: Imke de Jong could always say exactly how much money someone had on them. He could also make people stand still.
21380: What the black mirror predicts does not always come true. A sickly, not very sturdy fellow was once shown a coffin. But he did get married later after all.
21382: A man with a long white beard once asked a family if he could come in to lay out cards. The children asked if he could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. The man then made them march.
21383: On the spot where a woman often heard hammering at night, a new building was later put up.
21384: A woman sometimes saw funeral processions. Once she saw her own husband dressed in black walking back and forth through the church. A week later the niece died, and the man did indeed walk through the church like that.
21385: In the Boerenstreek a foal haunts with a porridge pot around its neck.
21387: A man once stood in front of the house of a married couple who could practise witchcraft. Inside he saw lots of dolls lying on the table, which the man and the woman were sticking with pins. He was so frightened that he walked backwards off the yard. He was lifted up and could no longer feel his legs.
21391: A man was once pushed off the road. He had seen a funeral procession in which he knew all the people.
21396: A man saw in the black mirror at the market who his future wife would be. He said he did not want to marry her, but later it happened anyway.
21401: Between Blauwhuis and Pool's farm a big dog always haunts at night.
21404: The wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns) of the old days are supposed to be today's street lamps and lights.
21405: A young man was once visiting an elderly couple when he suddenly saw a coffin standing there. A fortnight later the woman was dead.
21406: A man often heard things in advance. He often heard hammering in places where new houses were later built.
21407: A man often heard strange noises in his house at night, but saw nothing. Later Salvation Army soldiers came to that house, and they often made a great commotion until late in the evening.
21409: A woman once predicted at an acquaintance's house that there would soon be a death because the clock was running wrong.
21410: In the old days people were afraid when magpies came to the door, because that meant a death.
21412: Minse Griper could summon a full bottle of drink by sending out a jack of spades. The first dram had to be thrown over the shoulder. He could also make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. His wife, Tryn Snipel, could tell fortunes with cards.
21413: In the old days in Boelenslaan it happened quite often that people were pushed off the road by an invisible funeral procession.
21414: A naked child haunts the Goudberg.
21419: A man who was born with a caul often saw funeral processions in advance.
21425: In the old days many people went to the market to look in the black mirror. There they were shown the man or woman they would marry. And if they were not going to marry, they were shown a coffin.
21426: A wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) never ran out; the money always grew back.
21434: One evening a woman saw a funeral procession pass by. Her daughter saw nothing. A few days later someone in the village died and the funeral procession really did pass by.
21435: One winter afternoon a woman heard a car in the yard, but she saw nothing. There were no car tracks to be found in the snow either. But the next day there was an accident on the road, and lots of people and cars came into the yard.
21436: A woman predicted to her son-in-law that his 88-year-old mother would not die in hospital but would come home again. The son-in-law did not believe her, but it came true all the same.
21437: A woman very often heard hammering in places where new houses were later built.
21438: A woman once heard planks and beams being thrown about, and she predicted that a new house would soon be built on that spot. That came true.
21439: A man was once unable to cycle any further along a road. A few days later he had to stop there because a coffin had to pass.
21440: A woman could always tell from the ringing of the bell that someone else was going to die.
21441: A woman can always hear on the radio in advance whether a plane is going to crash.
21442: A woman often hears a voice in her dreams that makes predictions to her. She also often hears the sound of hammering in places where new houses will be built.
21443: A girl cycled very fast for a stretch because she saw a funeral procession coming and wanted to get round the corner first. The following week a funeral procession did indeed come.
21446: A woman once saw part of a house on fire, but when she came closer there was nothing to see. A few weeks later the paraffin stove in the house caught fire.
21449: A woman once heard noises in the attic. The next day a heavy thunderstorm destroyed part of the attic. When it was being repaired, the woman heard the same noises she had heard before.
21450: A woman once saw a car standing in her son's yard, and a man in a black hat got out. But when the man came closer, he and the car suddenly vanished. The woman told her son that a car would soon be standing on that spot in the yard. The very next day the doctor came in his car. The daughter-in-law had unexpectedly had a baby.
21455: A farmhand often had to get up at night to see funeral processions. Once his mates put sacks of rye in front of his bed so that he could not get out. When they removed the sacks the next day, they found their friend more dead than alive. He had turned completely blue.
21461: Old Tet was once at an acquaintance's to trade earthenware for rags. When she left again, the weather was very bad. The rye began to shake and then Tet flew over it.
21463: A woman once threw something at a strange cat. Suddenly the cat had vanished. The next day she met an acquaintance who was completely black and blue. She asked whether she had hit him like that the day before.
21466: One night in the woods a man saw two naked girls dancing around a tree. It looked as if blood was running from their necks down to their breasts. The girls were probably murdered there.
21467: In Westereinde many people had seen the train running beforehand. A few had also already heard the whistle.
21469: People once gave a strange cat in their house a blow. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood was lame. She was a sorceress.
21470: People once threw hot water over the paw of a strange cat. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood walked about with her arm in a cloth. That woman was a sorceress.
21472: One evening a dog howled eerily towards the box bed. There was nothing wrong with the child. But a week later it was dead.
21473: In a farmer's barn there was a haunting near the door. If you lay down to sleep there, you were thrown away.
21474: People were sometimes suddenly pushed off the road for no reason. Then a funeral procession would pass by.
21475: The men often sat playing cards in a barn until late at night. Things got rather rough there. Once, in the middle of the night, someone struck the table. The gang boss told them to play on, but nobody dared say anything any more.
21476: A fortune-teller who read cards was once found with a broken neck. Her head was turned backwards on her body. That was her punishment for reading cards.
21480: The lord of the white castle on the Bovenweg died in an accident with a donkey, and that is why he still haunts the area with a donkey.
21481: Whoever accepts an apple from a sorceress gets a toad in their stomach.
21536: In the inn de Hossebos, card players always sent out a jack of spades for a bottle of gin. The devil would then bring the bottle.
21537: A boy was once sitting in a tree when he saw his mother coming. But she had been dead for years. He told her to go back to where she came from, and she did.
21538: A few people were once chasing a hare, but however much they shot, the animal kept on running. When they reached a dike, the hare was gone and suddenly a woman stood there laughing.
