21539: At a house a ghost came to the door every evening and said nothing. They had the minister address the ghost. It turned out that the ghost had not been given grave clothes and so could find no rest. That evening they laid grave clothes on the chair, and the next day they were gone. Since then the ghost has never come again.
21540: A group of labourers who always slept on the floor grew tired of a woman coming down from the loft every night. One evening they took the ladder away, but at night the woman stood wailing that she had to come down. She was born with a caul and had to get up at night to see funeral processions.
21541: A man told his companion to step aside. A funeral procession passed by which the other did not see.
21543: Sorcerers stick pins into dolls to torment people.
21547: A newborn baby made very strange noises. Suddenly the people in the house heard a strange bang. The next day the baby died. When the little coffin was carried out of the house, they heard the same sound as before. It had been an omen.
21548: A man was troubled by nightmares (mares). He always tried to catch them, but never succeeded.
21550: Anne Herder could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
21552: In Harkema someone was once buried in a shroud that was too long. He kept coming back and would say: "Too long."
21554: In the old days you could see in the black mirror at the market whom you would marry. If you were not going to marry, you were shown a coffin. Some saw the devil, to whom they would sell themselves.
21555: A farmer had sent his labourer to the field to spread out the haycocks. He did nothing until just before the farmer came. With a wave of his hand it was done. When the farmer had gone again, the haycocks were back.
21558: A labourer with a magic coin never lacked money.
21559: Two men once saw a man walking over the sand. But when they saw his footprints, they were the prints of dog's paws.
21565: A man always worked in Groningen during the week. He did not want his wife to visit her family then, because he had quarrelled with them. Once the wife wanted to go anyway, but halfway there she suddenly saw her husband's figure. She quickly went back home. An hour later the man came home. His figure had been a warning.
21567: A boy once secretly peeked into someone's house. He saw lots of dolls lying on the table, and the people were sticking pins into them. The boy was so frightened that he walked off the yard backwards.
21572: A child was ill, and the neighbour woman regularly came to ask how it was doing. She never came further than the threshold. One time a black cat came, just at the moment the neighbour woman had left. They beat it terribly. The next day the neighbour woman lay ill in bed, and she died fairly soon afterwards. Her corpse stayed limp, so then they knew for certain that she was a witch. In the child's pillow, wreaths were found instead of feathers.
21576: A man who had emigrated to America could do magic. He could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit, and he could ventriloquise. Whenever he was out of money again, he borrowed from a great-aunt. She would say she had nothing, but he could tell her exactly how much money she kept and where. And when he looked at the sky, he knew exactly what time it would start to rain.
21582: A woman knew in advance that someone would die. She often heard it. People always die in a triangle. If someone dies here, then one there, then someone in the third corner dies too.
21583: Two sisters were once sitting in the dark with a tea light lit. One woman saw someone come through the door, but the other saw nothing. A little later someone really did come.
21584: Whenever the bells rang, a man always said that in three days someone else would go to the churchyard. It always came true.
21587: A woman once heard a lot of noise in an adjoining room. But there was nothing to see. The next day a relative fell through the floor and landed in that room. That was the sound the woman had heard the day before.
21588: A woman had seen beforehand that a house would burn down.
21589: A man was once cursing terribly. People asked him what he would do if he ever came into contact with the devil, but he did not care about that. That evening the devil got hold of him. The man was brought home dead.
21590: Three horsemen once chased an old woman's sheep. One of them laughed at the woman when she got angry about it. She told him he would not come home that evening. That same evening he had a fatal accident.
21592: Two old women were once robbed of their money and murdered. Ever since, the spot in question has been haunted.
21597:
If a dog howls eerily, someone will die.

A dog always howled on the evening before someone was taken to the churchyard. People found this so unpleasant that they sold it.
21602: A man claimed to crawl through a beam, but Imke de Jong said he was sitting on top of the beam. Then the man could do nothing more until Imke had gone.
21603: If a mirror falls, there will be a death. If the mirror does not break, someone far away will die. If the mirror does break, someone nearby will die.
21604: If three drops of blood fall from someone's nose, he will die.
21606: Stotterende Harm had a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin). If he spent a guilder, a moment later he had it back in his pocket.
21608: A woman once heard someone knock on the window, but there was nobody to be seen. Fourteen days later there was a knock again at exactly the same time. This time it was the neighbours' boy; his father had been taken ill.
21609: One evening a couple hears an old woman wailing, but there is no one to be seen. Not long afterwards three boys fall through the ice. When the grandmother of one of them watched the bodies being taken out of the water, she wailed just as the couple had heard earlier.
21610: One night a woman heard the sound of hammering. Later a house was built on that spot.
21611: Someone often hears 'volk' (anyone home?) being called. Then someone always arrives.
21612: A man who was born with a caul often had to get up at night to see funeral processions.
21613: A man once saw a fireball coming towards him. It passed right by his bicycle and exploded in the ground.
21614: By reading in a devil's book, a man could make old rooks come out of the hearth pit. When he read it back, the rooks went back into the hearth pit.
21620: An old man once saw a lady on a donkey riding through field gates. But his younger companion on the polecat hunt saw nothing.
21624: Will-o'-the-wisps are forerunners of the lamps of bicycles and cars.
21625: At the spot where men were building a bridge, one of them said he did not believe the devil could jump over the water there. But the next day there was a print of a horse's hoof in the concrete.
21626: Two men were once hunting polecats when they saw two horses. The animals stood dead still, as if they were statues. They were phantom horses.
21628: A woman often saw all kinds of events in advance. For instance, she had seen that a beautiful white house would stand on a certain spot, and it was indeed built there.
21629: A boy once pulled his brother off the road so that he nearly ended up in the ditch. Angrily he asked what that was for, but the other said he had nearly walked into a funeral procession.
21630: Two brothers were once out hunting polecats when one of them saw a coffin with a white cloth. The other saw nothing. A white cloth over a coffin meant that the person had died in childbirth.
21631: A boy once saw something that frightened him. His brother saw nothing.
21633: One night the husband of a pregnant woman saw two men enter his bedroom and put a child's body in a coffin. When he got up, there was nothing to be seen. From then on the man was convinced that the child they were expecting would be stillborn. The child was not stillborn, but died a few hours after the birth.
21634: A boy once saw a mother and a daughter flying together on a broomstick over a neighbourhood.
21635: Near a heath pool a man was suddenly seized and crushed. The moment he was released, an angel came out of the heath. The angel hovered a little and disappeared again. Then something came along further on, but the man never wanted to tell what it was.
21641: At a certain spot a phantom horse always used to walk through the field. For not a single ear of grain was ever flattened.
21643: When Alle Tet came along, the children always made a cross on the road with their clogs. They thought she would not be able to get past it.
21647: A woman had forgotten to tell her husband that one of the young cows was in heat. Only in the middle of the night did she think of it again. The man hurried to the animal, afraid she would get to the bull. But when he reached the field, the gates flew out of the stable and through the air. The farmer was frightened and went back. The next morning the gates were back in their places as usual.
21655: Whoever does not see a funeral procession does not need to step aside.
21656: In a group of women, an old woman is pushed to the ground. This was done by a funeral procession. The other women had not seen the procession. The old woman explains that whoever does not see the procession does not have to step aside either. She did see it, but stepped aside too late.
21659: If you draw the ace of clubs at a fortune-teller's, you will get a letter. It is an omen.
21660: If a little bird taps on the window, a message will come. It is an omen.
21661: If a magpie comes onto the land, there will be news, for the magpie is a bringer of news. It is an omen.
21662: If the cat washes itself, visitors will come. People should keep a close eye on the cat. It is an omen.
21663: What the cat looks at does not die. A sick person recovers at once if the cat casts a glance at the patient.
21664: If a cat runs across the barley of a mown field, the farmer need not worry about the hay, because it will not rain.
21669: A woman treats her mother, who lives with her, very badly. When the daughter once again leaves her mother to her fate, the old woman dies. Later the mother's ghost often haunts the place.
21670: If a toad crosses your path, you should be on your guard.
21671: Where a swallow builds its nest, luck will come. It is an omen.
21672: A woman sees a hearse standing at her neighbours' door. A week later the neighbour dies and the hearse stands in the same place. It was a voorgezicht (a vision foreshadowing an event).
21673: The narrator has had visions of the future since childhood, and they always come true.
21674: Someone sometimes smells cigar smoke in the morning when a visitor who smokes cigars is coming in the afternoon. It is an omen.
21675: In the morning a woman smells food burning, although she has nothing on the stove yet. Around mealtime the food really does burn, because she is standing at the door talking to someone. It was an omen.
21676: Lights are sometimes seen at the place where a new road will be built. These will-o'-the-wisps are an omen.
21677: A card reader who also reads cups, that is, coffee grounds, often makes predictions about the future. Her predictions always come true.
21679: A woman predicts that her daughter-in-law will be visited by her mother in the afternoon. It comes true exactly.
21680: At a certain spot people hear a cock crow at night, but there is nothing to be seen anywhere. Ten years later a small farm with hens and cockerels stands on the same spot.
21681: A grandmother is convinced she had already seen her grandchild in a blue dress that morning. The girl was indeed wearing a blue dress in the morning, but did not actually visit her grandmother until the afternoon. The grandmother had had a voorgezicht (a vision of a future event).
21682: It is a bad sign if you meet a black cat at night. You should then be on your guard.
21683: At a haunted house where a woman was once murdered, all kinds of eerie things still happen. Several people have seen a big black dog running in front of the house. The storyteller's daughter was once approached there by a man only she could see. It was a ghostly apparition.
21684: A man foresees a fire at the school building. The voorgezicht (a vision of a future event) does not come true, however.
21687: A prisoner is often tormented by a nightmare that enters the cell through a small hole in the barred window. The hole is closed up and the man is no longer troubled by the nightmare.
21688: Two cyclists are startled by something that comes out of the ditch and puts out their bicycle lamps. It is a ghostly thing. The men then end up in the ditch with their bicycles.
21695: In the past many will-o'-the-wisps were seen. People were often afraid of them, because they thought they were ghostly.
21696: A man who has sold his soul to the devil lies on his deathbed. From time to time the devil himself appears at the bedside, whereupon all those keeping watch quickly flee. Two brave men decide not to be chased away by the devil and to stay at the bed at all costs. First they witness two animals drop dead; then they see the devil, in the shape of a black fellow, wring the sick man's neck with his own hands.
21721: Great-grandmother dies and grandmother prays every night for her mother to return. One night the mother's ghost does appear at her bed. She makes a scratch in the stone floor. From that moment on the narrator's grandmother was no longer sad.
21722: On his way to sell mats, the narrator's father sees two armies approaching in the clouds. The clouds descend and a battle is fought. It is an omen of the First World War. When the real war breaks out, the father knows he will live through the whole war and that in the end neither side will win it. This came true.
21735: A man wants to know why his little boat always lies in a slightly different place. It turns out that sorcerers take little flying trips in the boat at night. Once they flew all the way to Spain.
21740: A girl lifting potatoes who has toothache is advised to find a rusty nail in the churchyard and hold it against the sore tooth. When she is lying in bed that night, she is startled by knocking on the window. A voice keeps calling 'My nail! My nail!'. In the end the girl becomes so frightened that she takes the nail back to the churchyard.
21742: A farmhand warns his mates in the field to hurry up, because a ship is sailing towards them. His mates think he is mad, because there is no water to be seen anywhere. A year later the seawater rises so high that the ship really does sail past. The boy had had a voorgezicht (a vision of a future event).
21743: Someone foresees that during the building of the church someone will fall from the tower. It really did happen.
21758: A widower is visited at night by the ghost of his dead wife. The minister is only willing to address the figure if she is dressed in white, not if she is in black. When the minister asks what her unfulfilled wish is, she says that money belonging to the poor is hidden in the house. Only when the poor get their money back will her soul be able to find rest. Her wish is fulfilled and the woman has never come to haunt again.
21759: A man who treats his mother badly is seized for no reason and thrown down some distance away.
21760: Around midnight a man is always startled by rattling at the back door. When he goes to look, there is nothing to be seen.
21761: In the past a gambling game with a money pit was often played at a certain spot. The recorder knows it mainly as a game of marbles. The game was often accompanied by fierce cursing. Later that spot is uncanny: it is a haunted place.
21762: A little boy is startled by a tall, unknown man who says nothing. When the boy follows him past the barn, the man disappears as suddenly as he appeared. The help of a Catholic man is called in, but he cannot reach the man either. It is a ghostly apparition.
21763: Someone was once roughly seized and flung a long way across the land.
21764: A scoffer who is fond of a drink is once roughly seized and flung across the ditch.
21765: A married couple live in discord and make each other's lives difficult. The woman firmly promises the man that after her death she will keep haunting to do the housework. When the woman dies shortly afterwards, the man hears her rummaging in the kitchen every night.
21766: A pottery pedlar is in the habit of leaving the baskets with his wares at a certain spot overnight. At night the pottery promptly starts to clink and rattle as if human hands were rummaging in it. It is a foreshadowing of what will happen the next day.
21767: Late in the evening a man is overtaken by a phantom horse.
21769: A man walks a female visitor home and feels as if someone is following him. He never again dares to take the woman home alone.
21773: A sorcerer can make soldiers appear from the hearth pit. This is used as a way to frighten whining children.
21778: The devil-banisher Piter Poes foresees when someone is coming to fetch a healing potion.
21781: At a haunted spot a foal runs about with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a phantom animal. Wilde lantaarnen (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) are also often seen at the same spot.
21785: A minister is being driven home by horse and cart when a stone wall blocks the horse's way. It is a voorgezicht (a vision of a future event): later a bridge is built on that spot. If the vision comes in the small hours, it takes a long time before what was seen actually happens; if it comes in the early part of the night, it takes only a short time.
21789: A man who wants to sell his soul to the devil hangs a sack in the barn, which the devil will fill with gold. When the sack is completely full, the pact with the devil is sealed. The man apparently has doubts after all and cuts the bottom out of the sack. The devil cannot fill the sack and eventually gives up. Thus the man outwits the devil.
21790: At a haunted spot a foal runs around with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a phantom animal. This story is often told to frighten children.
21794: At a certain place a man thinks he sees a monster with glowing eyes. He also hears a whistling sound as if a heavy storm were blowing. Later the tram station is built on that spot: the glowing 'eyes' - lamps - and the whistling sound were a forerunner of the steam tram.
21796: A cow is to be put down because it supposedly has lung disease. Hinse the devil-banisher says the cow is not ill but has a piece of leather in its throat. Hinse reaches into the cow's mouth and promptly pulls out an old shoe sole.
21797: Three rascals want to fool the devil-banisher Hinse and add their own urine to that of the cattle. Hinse examines the water and predicts that whoever added his urine last will soon die.
21800: The devil-banisher Hinse foresees that polecat dogs will steal his turnips.
21806: If a few drops of blood fall down, there will be a death in the family. It is an omen.
21807: One night a farmhand, Jan, sees a coffin with a dead person in it standing in the room. Jan cuts a lock of hair from the dead person. The next morning Jan himself has a piece missing from his hair. Frightened, Jan quits his job and flees. When weeks later he nevertheless returns to his old master, he promptly drops dead in the farmyard. His coffin is placed in the same spot Jan had seen earlier. It was a vision of the future.
21813: A man sees a white horse haunting a haunted spot. The rider wears a white bib collar.
21814: A skipper hears cries for help, but when he goes to look there is nothing to be seen. Later someone drowns at the same spot. It was an omen.
21815: In the evening a man hears hammering very clearly, although there is nothing to be seen. The next day a new cattle shed is built. It was an omen.
21827: A man regularly hears caulking and hammering at a shipyard, which means there will be a lot of carpentry the next day. The yard boss thought this was very good, as it meant work was coming.
21828: A fisherman often goes out at night to see things.
21829: A skipper hears wailing coming from the water. A week later a cattle dealer's son drowns and the same sounds can be heard. It was an omen.
21830: In a play, the leg of one of the actors has to be amputated. A week later the same man's leg really has to be amputated.
21832: Someone thinks he sees a boat coming across the land. It is an omen: later a canal is dug at that place.
21833: A man sees a hearse with a coffin. A little later the same hearse passes by: an old woman has died. It was a foreseeing vision.
21834: A man often has to get up at night to see things. He has visions of the future.
21835: A man always has to get up around midnight to see things. He has visions of the future.
21836: A little old woman foresees a disaster in the pottery shop: a few days later all the goods are smashed to pieces.
21837: Boatmen see a terrible disaster on the ice in which all sorts of people drown. The vision never came true, but the 'place of doom' has been avoided ever since.
21844: A man is addressed by a ghost woman in rain clothing. She tells him to fetch a parcel from another woman. The man gives the woman in the rain garment the parcel. It scorches in her hand.
21846: A man owns a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin).
21847: If you send away a playing card, you get a bottle of drink back with the card in the punt of the bottle.
21849: At night a boy hears a sound as if the weight of the clock is falling down. When he goes to look, the weight is still hanging on the clock. Some time later the weight really does fall down. It was a portent.
21850: At a certain spot a farmhand is often tormented by an invisible ghostly thing that makes pig noises.
21851: A cursing carpenter is followed closely by someone. When he turns around in annoyance and declares he is not afraid 'of the devil', he is roughly seized and flung down some distance away. The curser's son meets the same fate: he is hurled twice over the lower half-door of the back house. It is suspected that the devil has taken this family of cursers in hand.
21852: Two farmers are going to milk the cows early in the morning when one of them sees a figure walking on the other side of the ditch. The farmer's greeting is not returned: it is a ghostly apparition that disappears as suddenly as it appeared.
21856: A drunkard constantly shouts New Year's wishes. He is never short of money because he owns a wisseldaalder (a magic coin that always returns to its owner). The same man can also conjure little soldiers out of the hearth pit.
21861: At a haunted place a ghostly thing in human form rises out of the water.
21864: If a bird comes onto the path beside the house, a death is coming. It is an omen.
21865: In the evenings a man often sees a figure come out of the bushes and run off across the meadow. It is a ghostly apparition.
21866: A black lady keeps haunting a haunted place. Her soul cannot find rest because during her life her father would not accept her sweetheart.
21867: At a haunted spot a foal wanders around with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a phantom animal.
21868: A very good fisherman has a pact with the devil: when he dies, his head is turned around on his body.
21869: A man born with a caul predicts that his horse will perish. The prediction comes true: the animal dies in a fire at an inn.
21870: A man sees the cattle market next to the inn full of smoke. It is a voorgezicht (a vision of a future event): a few years later the inn burns down.
21871: A clairvoyant predicts where two lost sheep are: the shepherd does indeed find his animals at that spot.
21872: A folk healer is taken home after successfully helping with a cow's difficult calving. At a farm he says that there is a cow there about to calve, but that all will go well. On inquiry this turns out to be true.
21873: Children murdered by their parents often keep haunting. Because they were buried without a shroud, their souls cannot find rest. Two aansprekers (funeral announcers) must ask the ghosts about their unfulfilled wish. The shroud is laid down at the haunted spot and the wandering spirits find rest.
21874: A man sees smoke at a certain place, as if there is a fire. Some time later a fire really breaks out at that place. It was a voorgezicht (a vision of a future event).
21875: A woman born with a caul hears a horse kicking and stamping. Some time later the horse perishes in a fire, kicking and stamping.
21876: At a haunted spot a foal wanders around with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a phantom animal.
21877: On a slope, mysterious sounds announcing a future event can often be heard. They are portents.
21878: At a haunted spot people have sometimes seen an angel fluttering.
21880: A man hears a dog howling eerily. A few days later, at the same spot where the howling was heard, a man dies after falling off his bicycle. It was an omen.
21884: A lazy farmhand turns out to be able to spread manure over the land very quickly. The farmhand can work magic: by speaking a magic formula the job is done in no time.
21893: You must never eat anything you got from a witch: it can turn into a toad.
21894: In a haunted barn, workers spending the night see a large figure. It is a ghostly apparition.
21896: Witches stick needles into little dolls that represent children: the children later turn out to be bewitched.
21898: If you pull the caul upwards on children born with a caul, they will be clairvoyant and have visions of the future. If you pull the caul downwards, they will not.
21903: A woman hears a rattling in the air. It is an omen: later the tram runs at that place.
21904: At a certain place, wild lanterns can often be seen. They are the forerunners of the later bicycle lights.
21905: Around and after midnight you must never walk in the middle of the road, because something may well cross your path.
21906: The ghostly howling of dogs, the chattering of magpies and the strange ringing of the bell are portents of a death.
21907: Nightmares come in through the keyhole.
21915: A man sees a coffin with a white thing on it floating. A fortnight later someone actually dies and the coffin is carried past the same spot. It was an omen.
21916: You can catch a nightmare by throwing chaff or flour on her.
21918: A bridal couple is on the way to the town hall when the bridegroom-to-be suddenly bites a piece out of his bride's apron. The man is a werewolf; the girl breaks it off at once.
21919: At a haunted spot a foal wanders around with a porridge pot.
21921: A woman hears a strange sound outside. When she goes to look, there is nothing to be seen. The following winter she hears an odd fellow making the same sound. It was a portent.
21922: Two rich merchants, father and son, are suddenly lifted up for no reason and thrown into the ditch.
21923: Six farmhands in a row have already died when they had to grind for the miller at night. The seventh farmhand arms himself and waits to see what happens. When six cats appear, the farmhand starts lashing out wildly at the animals. One of the cats loses a paw with a gold ring around it. The next day the miller's wife lies ill in bed: she is missing her ring finger. The woman is a witch: together with the other witch cats she had been after the grinding farmhand.
21926: Challenging the devil by setting out a plate for the devil too. The man was killed by the devil.
21927: A man sees a house on fire a few days before it actually burns down. It is a voorgezicht (a vision of a future event).
21929: A scoffer boasts that he will throw the devil down 'like a toad'. Outside he is promptly seized by the devil and thrown down some distance away.
21930: A hunchback is murdered in the woods. A year later the dead man is suddenly walking along the road beside two of his relatives. When the two men look away for a moment, the hunchback has vanished again.
21932: A sorceress, who is also a card reader, sometimes sends away a playing card to get a bottle of drink back.
21935: Nothing can stay on a certain bed: even the potatoes are thrown off it.
21936: If the gable sign of a certain farm, a skull, is removed, the haunting begins.
21938: People see a ship come sailing across a dry plain.
21939: At night, boatmen suddenly see a little woman in a rowing boat. As suddenly as the little woman appeared, she disappears again.
21941: A large pike sometimes chases people. It is whispered that it is the evil one.
21945: A man born with a caul often has visions of the future. Sometimes he has to get up at night to see funeral processions pass.
21948: A baker advises his young apprentice not to eat an apple he received from a witch.
21951: When a bishop curses unconsecrated bells, evil takes hold of them. A member of a family of devils once throws a bell into the water. The muffled sound of the sunken bell sounds the same as the call of the bittern. That is why everyone thinks they hear a sunken bell ringing when the bittern calls.
21952: At a mooring place for fishermen, the net is continually thrown onto the deck as soon as the fisherman has fallen asleep. The anchors will not hold either. It is a haunted place.
21955: At a haunted spot a dog with glowing eyes runs around with a porridge pot around its head. Children are very afraid of this phantom animal.
21957: At a haunted spot a terrifying white apparition can be seen.
21961: A family involved in spiritualism experiences many strange things. One of the family members is once offered a hand out of nowhere. The barn doors also blow open by themselves.
21963: If you eat something you received from a witch, you get a toad in your stomach.
21965: People are very afraid of a wild phantom pig.
21968: On one of his outings a poacher suddenly feels something like a cobweb brush past his head. He never knew what it was.
21971: At night a daughter hears her mother making clogs, although her mother was not going to start that work until the next day. It is a portent.
21973: By moonlight two little boys see a small black dog grow bigger and blacker and bigger. It is a phantom animal.
21975: A group of boys relieving themselves in a field are startled by a white lady. It is a ghost. They run off with their trousers undone.
21980: A sorcerer makes little soldiers appear from the hearth pit and stroll all through the room.
21984: A dead girl lies in her coffin with a smile on her lips. A rag dealer suspects, given the girl's joy, that another death is approaching. A week later another man does indeed die.
21986: If a mirror falls down, someone will die within six weeks.
21987: A woman who has just buried her husband suddenly hears a loud bang. When she sees that the mirror has fallen down, she suspects there will be another death within six weeks. Exactly six weeks later a woman does indeed die in childbirth.
21991: A mother suddenly sees her three dead little daughters sitting at the table. The daughters tell their mother they have come to fetch her. The mother resists fiercely and the three ghosts vanish again.
21992: A widower tells his children - among them one unfortunate child - to look after the allotment garden. One day while the children are working, the ghost of their dead mother appears to them. When the minister asks the wandering mother about her unfulfilled wish, the mother says she can only find rest when saved money lying under the bed is set aside for the unfortunate child. Her wish is fulfilled and her spirit finds rest.
21993: A man born with a caul urges bystanders to step aside for a passing funeral procession. Since there is nothing to see, everyone stays put, laughing a little. Promptly one of them is struck by the horse and cart.
21994: A clairvoyant is often driven out of bed at night to see things, for example funeral processions. People say it is a torment from the devil.
21996: Strange things happen in a haunted house: at night the chickens shriek as if they are being slaughtered, and in the morning the horse is sometimes loose in the stable. The barn door also always springs open by itself. A resident who puts his bed against the haunted door at night is forcefully hurled away, bed and all.
22000: A man is startled at night by a knock on the window. When he goes to look with his dog, the animal creeps away in mortal fear. Later a man dies. The knock on the window was a portent of the approaching death.
22002: A sorcerer can make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit. He also has a magic book.
22003: A father wants to sell the caul of his clairvoyant child. Whoever owns the caul is bulletproof.
22006: When short of money, a Freemason always hangs an empty purse on the door. The man has a pact with the devil: the devil fills the bag with money.
22007: Freemasons are freemasons for life: if they want to turn their back on freemasonry, they must also turn their back on life. Freemasons often have a pact with the devil.
22009: A woman suspects that a red-and-white cat is a witch and beats the animal hard. The next day a woman with a body beaten black and blue has to stay in bed. She was the witch in cat form.
22011: A clairvoyant predicts that a little boy called Ealse will drown. Forty years later an Ealse does indeed die by drowning. An old woman had also foreseen this.
22012: At a fair, a girl visits a mirror tent to learn her future. In the black mirror the girl sees seven little heads. Later she marries a widower with seven children.
22013: A woman predicts that her sister, who lives in great poverty, is now past the hardest times. It comes true exactly.
22014: A woman tells her sister that her husband has bought a house. It comes true exactly.
22015: A woman predicts to her unmarried, pregnant niece that the future will not turn out badly for her. It comes true exactly.
22016: A woman already had visions of the future as a young girl.
22017: One evening a woman sees her husband, who works in Germany, standing at the window. The woman foresees his speedy return home: a few days later he is indeed on the doorstep.
22018: Half an hour before the newspaper arrives, a mother and a daughter already hear the paperboy calling. It is a portent.
22019: Early in the morning a woman hears loud wailing and crying. The next morning a woman wails and cries in exactly the same way because her little daughter has died. It was an omen.
22021: At night a woman very clearly sees a coffin with a cat on it in her room. The cat jumps to the floor with a thud and starts climbing up the woman's body from the foot of the bed. It is a nightmare. The wife of a later occupant comes to lie in the coffin. It is a vision of the future.
22022: New houses are built at a place where will-o'-the-wisps can be seen. They are forerunners.
22026: The wizard Ymke is arrested for an offence and locked in the tower. But Ymke frees himself effortlessly.
22030: A woman has a nightmare (a mare) for a sister: often she cannot sleep a wink because the nightmare tries to squeeze her throat shut. The woman also knows a witch, dressed in a hoop skirt, who bewitches children to death.
22034: At night a widow hears knocking on the window. Once it is a drunken fellow; the other time there is nothing to be seen. It is a forerunner of something that is going to happen in the future.
22035: Card reader Antsje Snipel foretells the future of a group of friends in a mirror tent. One of the men will have an accident in the water. The same man will also marry soon and become the father of two daughters and a son, according to Antsje. The man is convinced the predictions will not come true. To please the card reader, he deliberately falls into the water himself. He never married, however.
22040: A farmer has two barns. One of them is a haunted barn: spending the night in it is not advisable.
22041: If someone is born with a caul, you would do well to burn the caul. Otherwise the person will be constantly driven out of bed at night to foresee deaths in passing funeral processions.
22042: At night a man hears hammering. A few months later he hears the same sounds when a new house is built close to where he lives. The hammering heard earlier was a forerunner.
22045: A woman sees will-o'-the-wisps at the place where her later house is built. It is a forerunner of the later lighting in the house.
22050: A married couple are woken at night by the sound of hammering. When the man goes to look, however, there is nothing to be seen. A year later the couple build a little shop onto their cottage. The same hammering can be heard.
22051: A woman sees a house on fire, but nobody else sees any flames. It is a premonition: a year later the house in question really does burn down.
22052: A woman thinks the world is ending when she sees a 'wagon without a horse, all full of fire'. It turns out she had a premonition of a later invention: the car, with its lights on.
22054: At a place where a murder was once committed, a man tries in vain to shoot a ghostly apparition, a white maiden.
22055: It is said that of seven daughters, one remains childless. It does not always come true, for in one particular family all seven daughters had children. One of those girls always has visions of the future: she often has to get up at night to see funeral processions pass by.
22056: Wopke the devil-banisher gives a man tormented by nightmares a potion to take home. He must guard the bottle well on the way home, for the devil will try to take the medicine from him to prevent his cure, says Wopke. Wopke's prediction comes true: a little man smashes the bottle with a stick. When the man sets off home a second time with a new potion, Wopke predicts that a fellow with two dogs will come towards him. Wopke advises the man to keep his hand firmly on his chest while he walks in a wide arc around the fellow. The man follows Wopke's advice and manages to escape his second attacker.
22058: The notorious policeman De Vries, known for his motto 'And we play with you, De Vries stays boss in Surhuisterveen', fails to keep a drunken Imke de Jong behind bars. The wizard Imke escapes and taunts him, calling out 'And we play with you, De Vries'.
22059: Freemasons are never short of money because they have a pact with the devil.
22060: Two witte wieven (white women) always stroll about a haunted spot. At the same place a funeral procession once got stuck: the wagon ended up in the ditch, coffin and all.
22061: Wild lanterns are often forerunners of houses yet to be built.
22062: A farmhand bears so much hatred toward the farmer that he stabs the farmer's horse to death. When he gets out of prison, the horse's ghost keeps running beside him all the time.
22063: Witches often turn themselves into cats. Such a cats' meeting is often found singing. The fat tomcat is in charge.
22065: Chattering magpies by the house herald an imminent death.
22067: A reckless drunkard boasts that he is not afraid of the devil. The devil promptly seizes him and throws him roughly into the ditch.
22068: A drunken scoffer sings the Ten Commandments to the tune of a drinking and cursing song. The devil promptly seizes the scoffer and throws him over the gate. The drunkard later converted and became an elder in the Reformed church.
22069: A man is suddenly seized and flung away.
22072: The wizard Ymke de Jong fixes police officers to the spot.
22074: A witch torments people by sticking needles and pins into little dolls.
22076: In a pub, a bunch of men perform devil's tricks. One of the men asks the narrator to think of one particular playing card. That card, the eight of hearts, promptly sticks to the wall when the man throws the pack of cards against the wall. The men also make a bottle of drink float into the pub after sending away a jack of spades.
22077: In the past many people consulted a certain fortune-teller, Thomas Klare, when they wanted to know the future.
22078: Two men have a little old woman tell their future from coffee grounds. It comes true exactly as the woman predicts.
22080: A werewolf is a little person, half man, half woman.
22085: The wizard Imke de Jong is often thrown in jail but always frees himself effortlessly. Sometimes he is also seen in two places at once.
22090: A sick woman turns out to have been bewitched by a witch. When an apple received from an old woman turns into a toad, the bewitched woman hits the toad on the head. Two days later the old woman herself appears with a cloth around her head and is unmasked as the witch.
22095: At a haunted spot two naked little children always haunt the place.
22097: A small band of apple thieves is startled by a wit wief (white woman) on a bicycle. The lady vanishes as suddenly as she appeared. Later one of the companions comes home to a shaking house. The man is forced to eat: an invisible hand hands him a fork. He also hears a ghostly voice.
22099: A man suddenly sees two dogs with glittering collars. Just as suddenly as the animals appeared, they vanish again.
22100: A man once fought with the devil. The devil pressed a fork into his hand.
22113: A man born with a caul wants to convince his friend of his gift of second sight and takes him out at night to see things. The seer urges his friend to step aside for a passing funeral procession. A week later a funeral really does pass by at the same spot.
22114: A man visits a mirror tent to behold his future wife in the black mirror. Twice a woman appears: the first woman with twelve children, and the second woman also surrounded by offspring. The man eventually marries twice and has twelve and eleven children with his first and second wife respectively.
22115: People think they have beaten a cat to death, but they are mistaken. A man lies in bed moaning with pain. The man is a witch: the cat was the witch in cat form.
22118: A widow sees her dead husband lingering around the house several times by moonlight.
22119: If you spill coffee, winter is on its way. It is a portent.
22120: A card reader tells a woman that she is going to have a very hard time. Shortly afterwards the woman is widowed and left with nine children. Coffee-ground readers are also often consulted to foretell the future.
22122: A widower who always treated his late wife badly during her life is repeatedly harassed by a white ghost on his way home past the churchyard. The ghost of his dead wife wants revenge. The minister has to step in to drive the ghost away: he touches the ghost with a white handkerchief and speaks the formula 'Go away, devil in the shape of a woman!'
22123: A man who always treated his housekeeper badly is harassed every night after her death by her wandering ghost.
22124: A mother keeps harassing her daughter, who let her go bankrupt, as a ghost even after her death.
22133: A man visits a mirror tent to behold his future wife in the black mirror. When he sees a woman with one eye closed in the mirror, he declares he will never marry a woman who looks like that. The prediction comes true anyway: he always accepted his wife's closed eye.
22134: Witches can enter the house through the keyhole. If you accept something from a witch, it can turn into a toad.
22135: Witches often turn themselves into cats. The cats often hold a cats' meeting at which they sing psalms.
22138: A man is closely followed by a sturdy fellow. When the man boasts that he is not afraid of the devil, he is promptly seized and flung away.
22146: A woman often hears hammering. A while later a new hut is built at the same place. It was a portent.
22147: 'Foartsjirmerij' (a foretelling sound) is a mysterious sound that announces an event. If you also see something, it is a vision.
22155: A drunken scoffer is punished for his cursing: on his way home he is seized by the devil and hanged.
22156: A boy on his way home is startled by a small fiery red little fellow who keeps following close on his heels. The little fellow is the devil.
22158: If a white butterfly comes towards you, you will get a letter. It is a portent.
22159: A sorcerer makes ducklings appear from the hearth pit.
22164: At a haunted place a naked woman haunts between twelve and one at night. It is a ghostly apparition.
22168: A card reader tells a woman that she will not marry her current boyfriend. The courtship will soon end and shortly afterwards the woman will marry another, blond, man. It turns out exactly that way.
22169: A number of men sometimes conjure up a bottle of drink. When the drink comes floating into the room, everyone is afraid to take the bottle. Whoever takes the bottle must throw the first glass over his head behind him.
22173: An unbelieving scoffer challenges the devil and is punished: he is seized and roughly thrown down.
22174: A scoffer boasts that he would like to see the devil. When the man then comes face to face with the devil, he breaks out in a cold sweat.
22175: At night a man hears the sounds of threshing in the field. It is a portent: the next day there really is threshing.
22176: A farmhand sees a funeral pass by at night. Three days later someone really does die and the same procession passes by. It was a foreseeing vision.
22177: A superstitious man suspects his neighbour woman of being a witch. When a black cat comes into his house at night, he lames the animal with the poker. When his neighbour then turns out to be lame, he is convinced she is a witch.
22179: A man on his way home is suddenly startled by a figure with a big broom. The figure keeps silently accompanying him. It is whispered that it was the devil.
22180: A man sees a funeral pass by in thick fog. It is a foreseeing vision: a few days later someone really does die and the same procession passes by.
22181: At a haunted spot a man sees a white thing floating ahead of him. As suddenly as the ghost appeared, it disappears again.
22186: A sorcerer can make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit and make them march. His son is very afraid of his magic: he always wears his shirt back to front to ward off the sorcery.
22187: A group of scoffers who want to imitate Holy Communion in the pub are joined by a 'minister' with a wooden leg. It is the devil.
22188: Two poachers suddenly see a black cat. Because the animal keeps annoyingly following them, they decide to beat it to death. But the men cannot manage to hit the cat. Later they hear that a woman suspected of witchcraft was out that same evening. The men know enough: the witch had turned herself into a cat that evening.
22189: Witches often turn themselves into cats. They then hold cats' meetings on the heath, singing psalms.
22193: An alcoholic on his way home cannot continue because a thick black vapour suddenly surrounds him. When he walks back, a small bird keeps accompanying him. At home all the cups and pans on the table start to dance. It is the work of the devil.
22194: A boy on his way home suddenly sees a large fire with stones around it. A big fellow is warming his hands at the flames.
22196: The wizard Imke de Jong is often thrown in jail but always frees himself again effortlessly.
22197: The wizard Imke de Jong makes a police officer freeze on the spot. The officer cannot take another step.
22203: By sending away a jack of spades, you can summon a bottle of drink.
22204: A witch can turn herself into a black sheep.
22206: A fortune-teller who reads cards is punished by the devil: she is found with her head turned backwards on her body.
22209: At a haunted spot a foal wanders around with a porridge pot around its neck.
22211: A sorcerer can make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit and make them dance.
22212: A man who once stumbled over a corpse at night takes care not to run into a funeral procession a second time.
22213: A farmhand thinks he is greeting a woman with a milk churn, but it turns out to be a cat. It is a witch cat.
22214: Witches, as cats, often hold a cats' meeting.
22217: To keep nightmares (mares) away you must sprinkle flour on your face, hands, blankets and the edge of the bed board. For if a nightmare gets flour on her, she cannot get away: she must then stay sitting at the foot of the bed. A group of men try out this remedy but get a terrible itch because the flour is old.
22218: To keep nightmares (mares) away you must hang two new needles crosswise above the bed board. After all, the nightmare cannot crawl through the eye of the needle.
22219: To keep nightmares away you must put all the clogs in the house upside down in the hallway. A man who is very afraid of nightmares claims that those who are nicest by day are often the worst by night.
22222: A man claims to have seen a funeral procession at night. It may have been a foreseeing vision.
22223: The ghosts of three children who burned to death cannot find rest because they were buried without a shroud. Around midnight they wander about at a haunted spot by a pool.
22225: A cyclist at night is suddenly startled by someone at his side. When the man speaks to his sudden companion, the companion stays silent. The cyclist only loses his escort when it suddenly vanishes into thin air.
22227: Children do not dare accept an apple from an old woman – a supposed witch – because they are afraid the fruit will turn into a frog.
22229: A man relieving himself is suddenly thrown roughly away again and again. They say it is the work of the devil.
22230: A man sold his soul to the devil by walking around the churchyard three times with a black cat, calling 'Who will buy my cat for a daalder?'. Afterwards the same man never lacked money: he could buy so much drink that he turned blue from it.
22231: A farmer hears hammering behind his house and goes to see what is going on. He sees nothing, but is held fast in a certain spot by an irresistible force. The man is commanded to learn the gospel. He builds a small wooden church and begins to preach the faith. Later the Reformed church was built at the same place.
22232: A man born with a caul often foresees deaths at night in passing funeral processions. At birth, the caul of a seer often has to be anxiously hidden from greedy doctors.
22233: You should never walk in the middle of the road at night, because a funeral procession may pass. Only certain people who often have visions of the future see such a procession go by.
22234: A drunken scoffer boasts that he would like to come face to face with the devil. Promptly the drunkard and his companions are seized by the devil and thrown across the canal.
22235: A tough carpenter with gold earrings is stopped on his way home by a little woman. The carpenter roars that he will get through, even if the little woman is the devil herself. The little woman turns out to be Satan himself: the carpenter is roughly seized and thrown down some distance away.
22243: At a haunted spot a foal haunts the place: a phantom foal.
22245: If the dead are buried without a shroud, they keep haunting.
22247: A group of clay workers spends the night in a haunted barn: the doors keep springing open by themselves.
22248: You can get a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) by walking around the churchyard with a black cat, asking who wants to buy the animal. The devil then exchanges the wisseldaalder for the cat. A wisseldaalder always stays in your possession.
22249: In a certain house there is a hole that can never be closed.
22250: At night a man hears hammering. Sometimes he also sees lights floating. They are forerunners: a few years later new sheds are built.
22251: Some people are driven to the side of the road at night because a funeral procession wants to pass.
22252: A woman born with a caul often has to get up at night to see things.
22256: A man sees a funeral procession at night and flees in fear.
22257: A man sees a funeral procession pass at night.
22258: A little child is given an apple by a woman. The next day the apple turns into a toad: the woman is a witch.
22259: A man beats a strange cat almost to death. The next day an old woman lies black and blue in a corner of the room. She was the witch in cat form.
22263: A man often has to get up at night to see funeral processions pass.
22266: A man sees a funeral procession pass and runs off in terror as fast as his legs can carry him.
22267: At night a man sees two naked little children haunting. Their souls cannot find rest because they were buried without a shroud.
22269: A scoffer boasts that he would like to come face to face with the devil. Promptly he is seized by a little man and thrown away.
22270: Out of frustration over the food, a man urinates in the pan of kale. Outside, the quarrelsome husband is punished: the devil crosses his path. The frightened man runs back to his wife.
22273: One of seven daughters is a nightmare. Nightmares climb up over your body from the foot of the bed and try to squeeze your throat shut. You can stop the nightmare from entering your house through the keyhole by leaving the key in the lock at night. Putting the clogs upside down or scattering flour are good ways to keep nightmares away.
22282: A man excitedly tells that he has seen a closed wagon with no horses in front of it. It is a vision of the future: much later the car is invented.
22283: In the black mirror men can behold their future wife. If they remain unmarried, they see a coffin.
22286: Sorcerers make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit and march through the room. It is said that such sorcerers have connections with Satan.
22288: A woman often hears hammering. Later a new house is built at the same place. It was a portent.
22289: A man sees will-o'-the-wisps floating. Much later cars drive at the same place. The little lights were a portent.
22290: A girl thinks she already hears the baker's cart, although it does not actually arrive until a quarter of an hour later. It is a portent.
22291: A woman hears hammering. Shortly afterwards a new house is built at the same place. It is a portent.
22292: A woman runs into a funeral procession and boldly climbs over the hearse.
22293: A clairvoyant woman is often driven out of bed at night to see things.
22296: The farmer's horses are suddenly set upon by a group of cats. The cats - witch cats - start braiding the horses' manes and make sure the animals cannot take another step.
22297: A woman who always curses terribly is startled by a big sheep. It is the devil.
22298: At a haunted spot a naked little child always runs around in the evening. It is a ghost child.
22300: The husband of a witch discovers a sheep's tripe next to him in bed at night. His wife is out doing magic and has left the tripe behind.
22301: At a haunted spot the ghost of a dead person wanders about at night.
22302: One evening a man sees a fierce dog standing in the street. The animal bares its teeth menacingly and blocks the man's way. It is a phantom animal.
22303: A drunkard on his way home is suddenly seized and flung away.
22304: A woman sees a funeral procession pass and suspects a death is imminent. Shortly afterwards a boy dies.
22305: Near the churchyard a sinner is startled by a cat that claws him open. It is the devil.
22307: A curser on his way home from the pub is, as punishment, seized and mauled by a fat dog.
22308: A poacher hiding in a tree is shaken back and forth by the devil.
22309: The spirit of a woman keeps wandering about after her death. Several people have seen the ghost.
22310: Various people have seen a ghost sitting on a milk churn. It is unknown whether the ghost was a woman or a man.
22311: A cyclist comes across a small black little man with glowing eyes. It is the devil.
22312: The souls of two murdered children cannot find rest: they keep haunting, naked.
22314: On a certain path people are startled by a big black fellow. It is the devil.
22316: A mother sees a funeral procession pass at a certain spot and runs away in fear.
22317: You should never walk in the middle of the road at night, because a funeral procession may come up behind you.
22318: A woman in labour sees a funeral procession pass. It is a foreseeing vision of her own death: the woman dies shortly afterwards in childbed.
22319: As punishment, a scoffer is seized and flung away.
22320: A scoffer on his way home suddenly sees an arm coming through the hedge. The arm belongs to the devil: the devil wants to seize him.
22321: Cries for help from a pond are a portent of an imminent drowning.
22323: The wizard Imke de Jong always frees himself effortlessly from jail. No lock can withstand his magic.
22324: A farmer discovers small, marching little men in his barn.
22325: One of seven daughters is a nightmare. Nightmares enter your house through the keyhole and try to squeeze your throat shut. You can keep nightmares away by putting the clogs upside down or laying asafoetida in front of the door.
22327: At a certain place many will-o'-the-wisps are visible. The floating lanterns are forerunners of car and bicycle lights.
22328: Freemasons have a pact with the devil. A freemason receives a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) in the churchyard. This coin can never run out.
22330: A card reader tells a woman that she will have two children. It turns out exactly that way.
22337: An apple you get from a witch turns into a toad.
22338: A witch sticks needles and pins into little dolls to hurt other people.
22341: To receive a bottle of drink, you must send away a playing card. The one who sent the bottle away may not take hold of it if he wants to stay alive.
22342: A clairvoyant farmhand with a sore arm turns out to have been injured at night when he was roughly thrown out of his bed to see things.
22343: A man born with a caul foresees the arrival of German soldiers in the Second World War twenty-five years beforehand.
22344: A little boy is born with a caul. The doctor fears that the child will have visions of the future at night all his life.
22676: A married couple see light shining through windowpanes. It is a vision of the future: later a new house is built at that place.
22677: A man on his way home in the dead of night is startled by a bright bluish light.
22678: You should never walk in the middle of the road, because you may be pushed aside by a funeral procession.
22679: A man foresees the funeral of his daughter, who drowned.
22683: Stammerige Harm is a sorcerer. Harm can turn himself into a cat and likes to bewitch livestock. Harm also owns a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin).
22684: At a haunted spot a foal runs around with a porridge pot around its neck. A large black dog has also been seen at the same place.
22685: Two friends see a boy and a girl of four or five years old walking hand in hand at night. They are ghost children.
22687: A man on a tricycle is suddenly seized and flung away.
22688: With a jack of spades, the devil, you can summon a bottle of drink. It is important to throw the first glass over the left shoulder: a gift for the devil.
22693: No one wants to borrow money from the sorcerer Stammering Harm, because he has a pact with the devil. When Harm hangs an empty purse on the door in the evening, the devil fills it with money during the night.
22694: A sorcerer – half man and half woman – can conjure little soldiers out of the hearth pit and make them march.
22698: Will-o'-the-wisps turn out to be a foreshadowing of the later tram lights.
22700: Witte juffers (white maidens) haunt a haunted spot.
22702: At a haunted spot a foal wanders around with a porridge pot around its neck.
22709: At a haunted spot a white lady on a horse used to be seen often. She is a ghost woman.
22712: A witch can change herself into a cat. When the witch-cat is beaten, the woman walks with a limp the next day.
22713: A man, Rinse Loonstra, always foresees fires. This has earned him the nickname Rinse Brander (Rinse the Burner).
22714: A curser is thrown to the ground by the devil as punishment.
22715: A man is suddenly seized and flung down.
22718: A magpie close to the house points to an imminent death.
22720: In the old days, when a fat cat came towards a group of children, the children all thought it was the witch Alle Tet.
22726: Some witches have little dolls that they stick needles into.
22731: At a haunted place the ghosts of the dead float above the house. The ghosts cannot find rest because these people were treated badly during their lives.
22732: In the days when no train ran yet, the sounds of the train could already be heard. It was an omen.
22735: A man born with a caul has to get up at night to see things, such as funeral processions. A caul must not be destroyed.
22736: A man is startled by a large dog with glowing eyes. It is a phantom animal.
22737: A woman playing cards is suddenly startled by a black thing in the back room. It is said that it was the devil.
22739: A wizard can fix people to the ground.
22743: A group of cursers is startled by a black thing. It is the devil.
22745: A man on his way to his girl is startled by a white thing. The white thing disappears as suddenly as it appeared.
22750: Someone hears hammering at night. It is a forerunner: shortly afterwards a boat is built.
22751: At night someone sees a ship sailing straight across the meadow. It is a forerunner: the following year a canal is dug at that place.
22752: A group of young people see a ship come sailing over the land. It is a forerunner: later a canal is dug at that place.
22753: At a haunted spot near a bridge a skipper is startled by a large black dog with glowing eyes that jumps into the water in front of his boat.
22754: One night a boy is startled by a large, pitch-black dog at his side. It is probably a phantom animal.
22755: At a haunted spot the ghost of a girl haunts. The naked ghost child turns out to have been murdered and cannot find rest because she was buried without a shroud. The minister advises fulfilling the unfulfilled wish and lays out a shroud for the girl. Now her spirit finds rest.
22758: A ghost wagon is said to drive at a haunted spot now and then.
22763: A litter of pigs that will not grow turns out to be bewitched. Wopke the exorcist advises giving a good whack to the hare that keeps getting into the pigsty. The animal loses an eye. A day later a one-eyed old hag is walking about: the witch.
22764: With cards you can summon a bottle of drink. The bottle floats from one table to another.
22765: A clairvoyant often has to get up at night to foresee funerals.
22766: A clairvoyant often has to get up at night to foresee funerals.
22767: A girl foresees that her mother will die during the night because she has seen her lying in a coffin. The vision comes true.
22768: At a haunted spot a foal wanders around with a porridge jug around its neck. It is a phantom animal.
22769: A woman - a witch - can change herself into a cat. When the witch-cat gets a whack, the witch lies sick in bed the next day.
22770: A sorcerer conjures little soldiers out of the hearth pit and makes them march.
22771: In a mirror tent you can behold your future wife in the black mirror. Sometimes a coffin appears as well.
22778: Before the tram started running in a certain place, people already saw its lights.
22779: A man promised his - first - wife while she was alive that he would not remarry after her death. When he later marries for the second time after all, the ghost of the first wife appears. Her spirit cannot find rest because her husband did not keep his promise.
22780: You should never run in the middle of the road, because you might be pushed aside.
22782: If you get an apple from a witch, you must never eat the fruit entirely. If you do, you get a toad in your body.
22788: A woman heard the tram before it was even running. It was a portent.
22789: At a haunted place a man always sees a little old person come out of a small lake. It is a ghost.
22790: To keep a witch away, a child always makes a cross.
22791: At a haunted spot a foal wanders around with a porridge jug around its neck.
22792: A man once told how he struck right through a black dog coming towards him. It is a phantom animal.
22793: A man predicts a death because he has heard the dog howling eerily. The prediction comes true: shortly afterwards someone dies.
22794: If the cat washes itself, you will get visitors. It is a portent.
22798: In a bakery the oven door always opens by itself.
22824: If you step on a snail, it starts to thunder.
22825: Many young girls visit a coffee-ground reader to have their future foretold.
22829: People see a house on fire. It is an omen: only some time later does the house really burn down.
22831: Whoever has a caul can see into the future.
22832: A woman's dead little child was buried naked in an unknown place. The child keeps haunting naked.
22833: A man and his wife treat his mother, who lives with them, very badly. When the old woman has died, she keeps haunting them, wherever the young couple move to.

22838: An unbelieving scoffer is seized by the devil and horribly mistreated. The man is converted.
22839: An unbelieving scoffer is startled by a large black dog. The man prays to the Lord to take the animal away from him. The Lord answers his prayer.

22842: A woman foresees when she will get visitors.
22845: In the old days the churn was often bewitched.
22847: A man foresees deaths in passing funeral processions.
22848: A woman always foresees sad things such as illnesses and deaths.
22849: Some people can change themselves into cats. Once a cat gets a hard whack. The next day an old man has a terrible headache. He was the cat.

22851: If the dog howls eerily, a death is coming.
22852: A family loses a child. An old woman had already foreseen the death because her dog kept howling eerily.
22854: At a haunted spot a foal wanders around with a kettle around its neck. It is a phantom animal.
22855: A woman claims that her neighbour always comes in through her keyhole.
22856: The sorcerer Stammerige Harm can turn himself into a cat. He also owns a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) and so never lacks money.
22858: A man is seized for no reason and set down in the ditch some distance away.
22859: A baker looks into a black mirror to see his future. All the predictions made to him came true.
22860: People make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit and march.
22862: A small group of scoffers wants to imitate Holy Communion. The devil intervenes.
22872: A skipper is frightened because his anchor keeps being thrown on board while no one can be seen. The minister's help is called in: he prays on the ship and from then on the anchor stays in its place.
22873: A boy claims he can make a dead person appear in a mirror blackened with soot. When the boy begins to mutter and call out, a girl's dead father appears.
22874: A woman who cannot bear the death of her mother prays to have her mother back. At once her mother appears to her, barefoot. Her mother disappears again, but the loss is now more bearable.
22875: A fortune teller makes predictions to two men about their future work and home and warns them to be careful of loose pieces of wood on the road to avoid accidents. Her predictions come true exactly.
22876: A fortune teller tells a man that he will receive an inheritance, but that his brother will receive more than he does.
22877: A fortune teller tells two women that one of them will have five more children and the other one more. It turns out exactly that way.
22878: A fortune teller predicts that a boy held on suspicion of arson will be released. It turns out exactly that way.
22879: A fortune teller makes all kinds of predictions about a man's future. Nearly all of them come true.
22887: A man is pursued by a white figure.
22901: At a haunted place three lawyers gather around a campfire. They are ghosts. After the minister has addressed the ghosts, they are driven away by horse and wagon to a certain piece of land. That piece of land is still called Advocatenland (Lawyers' Land).

22909: Two poor children sent out to look for peat are startled by an ominous rustling of the reeds. Fire even comes out of the reeds. The frightened children run home.
22910: Two girls on a footbridge are suddenly seized by an invisible force and set down some distance away.
22913: A farmhand who is very foul-mouthed is roughly thrown against a beam. Later he meets a man by an oak tree. He greets the man kindly twice, but gets no answer. 22914: In the old days will-o'-the-wisps were often seen: forerunners of new roads.
22915: A girl sees a fire very clearly in her dream. It is a premonition: the next night the house next door burns down.
22918: A sorceress makes little soldiers appear from the hearth pit and jump and dance.
22919: A sorcerer can summon a bottle of drink with the help of a jack of spades.

22922: One of seven boys always has to get up at night to see things. He is clairvoyant.

22951: The devil has been seen at a certain place.
22952: Near the barracks a man is approached by a large black dog. He can only shake the animal off with difficulty. The man realises it is no ordinary dog.
22953: A large dog haunts a haunted spot. It is a phantom animal.
22954: A group of women returning from a sewing club in the middle of summer suddenly see snowballs. The devil is throwing snowballs.
22955: A sinner is roughly seized by the devil and thrown over the dike.

22967: A beautiful black cat is suspected of being a witch. Someone steps on its paw. The next day a woman has a sore leg: she was the witch-cat.

22970: You should never walk in the middle of the road at night, because you could take a nasty fall from a passing hearse.
22974: People hear the sound of milk churns and a pump in the evening. It is a portent: later a dairy factory was built on that spot.
22979: A nightmare has fastened a sleeping labourer's coat so tightly around his neck that he can barely get the coat loose.
22980: A man has an uneasy premonition that someone is going to drown. Half a year later someone does indeed drown at the same spot.
22981: A young lad foresees where he will live later on. It turns out exactly right.
22984: At a haunted spot a foal runs around with a porridge pot around its neck.
22989: If you step on ground ivy, it starts to thunder.
22990: Witte wieven (white women) have been seen at a haunted spot.
22991: Wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps, are portents of bicycles and cars.
22992: A farm labourer is seized by the devil and thrown away.
22993: If you walk in the middle of the road at night, you are sometimes pushed to the side by an invisible funeral procession.
22995: With a magic book of spells, a sorcerer can make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit and make them march.
22996: Through a jack of spades one can summon a bottle of gin. It is the devil's gin.
23000: When the farmers could not churn, they said things were bewitched. Then they fetched Piter Poes.
23001: With the jack of spades one could summon a bottle of drink.
23007: A poor man made his wife promise never to part with the silver buckles on his shoes, but to keep them for their son. 23011: A married couple living in a shack would dearly love to live in an ordinary house. But they are very poor. One evening the woman hears the voice of the good Lord telling her she must be patient for two more years. And indeed, after two years they are able to move into a house.

23014: A man was once out hunting polecats when his dog did not dare to cross a gate. They saw a naked little child come floating along. She hovered still before the gate for a moment, and the man let her pass. Then she floated on and the dog dared to cross the gate again.

23018: One should never promise anyone anything on their deathbed. It may be that one cannot fulfil it, and then the dead person comes to haunt. They then find no rest.
23021: Near the Blauwhuis there is always a jingling in the ditch in the evening.
23025: Some witches can change themselves into animals. If you hit such an animal, the witch has a black eye the next day.
23026: A man who was born with a caul always saw funeral processions in advance.
23028: At a place where there was nothing, a man heard the whistle of the tram. Later a tram came.
23029: A man lay sick in bed; he was bewitched. At the back of the yard there were lots of black cats, but they could not be wounded. Wreaths were found in the sick man's pillow.

23031: In the Spookbosje in Garijp a big dog with big glowing eyes haunts.
23032: At a place where a convent of white nuns had once stood, witte wijven (white women) later haunted.
23033: It is haunted at a spot where long ago a countess is said to have sunk into the ground, coach, horse and all.
23034: Wild lanterns were the portents of flying machines, because they were in the air.
23037: A strange, rough fellow was once thrown up into the air three times in a row. It changed him completely.
23039: Several people heard the sound of hammering at a certain spot, but there was nothing to be seen. Later a new house was built on that spot.
23040: A few men out hunting polecats once saw a light, as if it were burning in a house. But there was no house there at all, and they could not manage to get any closer to the light. Later a house was built there.
23041: In Garijp a foal haunts with a jug around its neck.
23042: On his way to work in the morning, a man always saw two ghosts sitting on the church steps.
23044: The wild lanterns were the portents of cars.
23048: With a jack of spades one can summon a bottle of drink.
23057: A man often saw lights in the sky in the evening. Those were the later street lamps.
23059: One night a man saw a funeral procession while in reality there was nothing there. A week later the funeral procession really came.
23063: A cow is once very frightened of an approaching figure. Only then does the animal's owner see that the one coming is an acquaintance who died a few weeks earlier.
23064: Some people once saw a mill on fire, but in reality there was nothing. Years later the mill really did burn down.
23065: One night a woman heard lots of bangs outside. The next day lots of planks were thrown over the fence, and that made exactly the same sound.
23067: One night people heard a strange sound three times in a row, as if someone were being murdered. They quickly went back home.
23068: One night a man heard the sound of hammering. A week later a new shed was built in his back house.
23069: At night a man always heard something banging on the door, but when he went to look there was nothing to be seen. He also always shut the door properly, but every time it opened again by itself.
23070: At a certain spot people have sometimes heard cries for help. They say that someone is still bound to drown there.
23071: A man was once looking for his goat. He felt as if the animal was frolicking around him the whole time, but he saw nothing. A bit further on he did find his goat, and the animal was indeed frolicking around him.

23074: A man once heard a loud noise on a sandy road. Suddenly he was lifted up and thrown off the road. It was probably the devil.
23077: A woman once saw a stately lady dressed in white go through the garden gate at the neighbours'. Suddenly she had vanished again. A few days later someone died at the neighbours'.
23079: A man saw his own funeral in advance. He saw the number of carriages and recognised all the people who were there.
23082: If a dog stood howling in the street, there would be a death, people always used to say.
23083: If a painting or mirror fell from the wall, a death would follow.
23086: A boy and a girl once saw a fire from a distance, but when they came closer there was no fire at all. A year later a fire did break out at that spot.
23088: A married couple once saw two ghosts in rain clothes floating.
23089: At the place where the devil jumped over a canal, prints of a horse's hoof can still be seen in the ground.
23091: One evening a newly married couple hear wailing and moaning moving back and forth. But they saw nothing. Later the woman's mother came to live with them. She had a heart condition and often walked up and down the room moaning.
23094: In Garijp a foal haunts with a porridge pot around its neck.
23095: In Garijp a fat dog haunts.
23097: A family once hears the sound of hammering and of planks and stones being thrown. But there was nothing to be seen. Later the back of the house was rebuilt, and exactly the same sounds could be heard.
23098: A boy once heard the sound of hammering. A few months later a room was built on that spot.
23099: A girl once saw people unloading flour from a ship. But there was no water there at all. Not long afterwards the canal was dug there.
23115: With a jack of spades one can summon a bottle of drink.
23116: A man who was born with a caul often had to get up at night. Then he saw funeral processions and knew who was going to die.
23120: When the churn was bewitched, people always fetched the duivelbanner (exorcist) Piter Poes.
23124: A man who curses a lot hears at night that he is being followed by a cart or a wagon. He flees and is flung over a ditch, over barbed wire and over a gate, one after another. That was the devil, who had brought him home. Since then he has become a pious man and goes to church faithfully.
23125: A scoffer was once lifted up by the devil on his way home and flung down. Later he became a churchgoer.
23134: Before the tram came to run in a certain place, several people had already heard the sound of the tram there.
23135: A man who was born with a caul often had to get up at night to see funeral processions. Because of this he always knew in advance that a death was coming, but he did not know who would die.
23142: A mother often warned her mocking son that the devil would come to fetch him. One day his body was found with his head turned backwards on his body. The devil had wrung his neck.
23147: An old woman is a witch who can fly on a broomstick. Someone once shot at her and hit her, but the shot from the gun did not harm her.
23152: A newly married man had put up a hedge but had not got round to the boards, as he had to go and work on the Frisian clay. When he came home after a week, the fencing was finished.
