His wife came to tell him that it was exactly the same sound she had heard before.
23345: A man who was born with a caul often saw funeral processions in advance. Once he pulled his wife to the side because he saw a coffin being pulled along on a sledge. His wife saw nothing. Some time later someone died, and his coffin was pulled across the ice.
23346: In the old days children were warned never to walk in the middle of the road. An [invisible] funeral procession might come along and push them to the side.
23355: In the past, the narrator's family often had to carry out emergency slaughtering at other people's homes. Often there was already a knock before the people had even reached the narrator's house. This happened both at night and during the day. Sometimes the sound was like a stick tapping on the window. Then a little later someone would come with a stick and tap it on the window. Sometimes a fortnight passed between the omen and the actual event, but it always came true.
23372: Omens of death: a) The ghostly howling of a dog. Within three days someone dies. b) A magpie in the farmyard: a letter announcing a death. c) The death-tick, sometimes in the ribbons of the oorijzer bonnet (a traditional headdress with a metal head-band). d) When the owl calls. e) Three drops of blood falling from the nose. f) If a horse on its way to the farmyard scrapes with its hind leg, someone will die in the house in front of which it scrapes. g) If the weight of the clock falls down. h) If the bell tolls dully. Then a corpse hangs from it, people say. i) If the dead person looks beautiful. One must never covet the corpse, for then someone else will die. That is why the dead person is content and beautiful. j) If the corpse lies in the house over a Sunday, there will soon be another death. The wish of the dead person is then fulfilled. k) Whatever one meets first on the way to the churchyard will be the first to die in the family. If one meets a man, a man will die; if one meets a woman, a woman; if one meets a child, a child.
23373: The wild lanterns of the past were omens of the later bicycle lamps.
23384: Wild lanterns are portents of new houses.
23385: Just before a funeral it sometimes happened that people were suddenly pushed off the road.
23389: If a dog howls ghostly, someone in the neighbourhood will die.
23400: A married couple once saw something burning from their yard. But nothing stood there yet. Later a house was built, and later still it did indeed burn down.
23401: The wild lanterns that people used to see flying around are the later cars.
23402: Two men once saw a great light. Later a new house was built on that spot.
23403: A man once saw a great light next to a house. Later a lamp post was put there.
23406: A man could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. They would then make a round of the room and disappear into the hearth pit again. The man gave them commands.
23407: A man always saw funeral processions in advance.
23414: A group of boys once hear hammering, and some of them see lights. In reality there was nothing. But later new houses were built on that spot.
23415: A boy and his parents once hear a younger child calling and raving, but when they go to look nothing is wrong. Some time later the child really raved and died.
23418: Near Westereinde two girls wearing little red aprons haunt.
23419: The wild lanterns that people used to see were the portents of the later bicycle lamps.
23424: A scoffer coming out of the pub was thrown into the ditch as many as seven times. That was the devil's work.
23437: On Saturdays one always ties a bundle of flax around the flax brake, otherwise they go on braking on Sunday.
23478: In Boelenslaan a dog with a little pot in its mouth haunts. Sometimes that dog turns into a lady wearing a black gown.
23481: A man who was born with a caul saw funeral processions in advance.
23483: One night a man heard sawing and stones being thrown. But there was nothing to be seen. Half a year later a new house was built on that spot.
23489: A man once heard a voice in the middle of the night telling him that his father-in-law had died. The next day he received word that his father-in-law had indeed died at exactly that time.
23491: A young man once saw a house on fire, but when he came closer nothing was wrong. Three weeks later he saw it again, but this time the house really burned down.
23492: One evening in bed a man saw three Dutch labourers come walking up. But in reality there was nothing. Three days later the three really were there.
23497: In the past wild lanterns floated over the heath. That meant an accident was coming.
23498: If you see a fireball, it means a storm is coming.
23499: Between Rottevalle and Witteveen a foal haunts with a porridge pot around its neck.
23505: One must eat nothing from a sorceress, for it will turn into a toad.
23507: Witches have dolls that they stick needles into, which causes pain.
23509: Ymke de Jong could make people stand still. He could also crawl through a beam and make himself invisible.
23513: A man promised his sick wife not to remarry after her death. 23517: Several people sometimes heard strange sounds coming from a house. Later the sixteen-year-old daughter, who was treated rather badly, hanged herself in the barn. When her parents found her, they screamed. That was exactly the sound people had heard before.
23518: One night a man heard the sound of hammering. But there was nothing to be seen. Later the house was rebuilt.
23519: A young man once saw a funeral procession in front of a house. Not long afterwards a little daughter died.
23520: A young man once saw a coffin standing in front of a house. When he tried to touch it, his hand went through it. Not long after, a child from that house died, and the coffin was really there.
23521: A man who was born with a caul often had to get up at night to see funeral processions.
23524: The bicycle repairman Reid Keuning could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
23527: A man once thought he had seen a covered wagon with no horses in front of it. It was going terribly fast. Later the cars came.
23531: Some children were once looking for blackberries when the black cat that was with them suddenly vanished and a woman appeared. She was a witch.
23534: A man asks his sweetheart for a handkerchief and disappears with it. When he returns, red threads from the handkerchief hang between his teeth. He confesses that he is a werewolf who must tear something apart now and then, and had asked for a handkerchief so as not to tear her apart.
23536: At the Wopkepoel a few girls haunt at night.
23539: A married couple once went to the duck decoy early in the morning. The woman heard a voice singing there, but the man heard nothing. No one was to be seen. They quickly went back home.

23557: If a dog howls ghostly, someone will die in the direction the dog is howling. If magpies chatter in the farmyard, a death will also follow.
23562: In Oenkerk there are gates at a farm that always open by themselves at night.
23565: There was once a house no one wanted to live in because it was haunted. A couple wanted to give it a try anyway. But every morning everything they had nailed together the day before lay in pieces again.
23567: At a farmer's place two St. Bernard dogs always lay in the yard on either side of the little bridge. Long after the farmer had stopped living there and the animals had died, people still saw those two dogs lying there.
23568: On a farm the farmhands kept leaving, because there was always haunting going on at night. All kinds of strange noises could be heard then. And when one went to look, there was nothing to be seen.

23572: A man once saw two women floating in the early morning.

23589: At a spot where a child was once bewitched, the child still haunts.

23597: In the old days, when someone died on the Veensterheide, that person was always seen again afterwards.

23611: One night two sisters heard a noise at the front door, quiet talking, and something being pushed in front of their box bed. A few days later their brother drowned. When his body was brought in, people talked quietly, and the coffin was placed in front of the box bed.

23647: A man once heard strange noises coming from a ship. Later the person living on the ship was attacked, and the same noises were heard.
23648: One night a man heard a bang. He saw a few men running off in different directions. Later an accident happened, and it was exactly the same scene.
23658: In the Spooklaan in Eestrum, Jantsje-met-de-veren (Jantsje-with-the-feathers) haunts.
23659: On his way back from work, a carpenter once kept having a woman get under his feet. When he said something about it, he was flung back and forth.
23666: A woman once saw a nightmare coming to her. It was a small black fellow. She could not utter a word.
23668: Ruerd van der Veen kicked in his own wife's chest. He and his accomplice bet on who could say the strangest things. They were both thrown down.
23673: A man claimed that no devil could jump further than he could. But one time someone jumped just a little further than him every time. The next day he found a print of a horse's hoof in a stone by the canal. He had been jumping with the devil.
23674: In a certain part of a barn no one could sleep. A newly married woman was once flung a long way there.
23676: One evening two women saw a funeral procession pass by. A few days later a man died and the funeral procession passed by in reality.
23677: On the Roekekamp, three small naked children haunt.
23685: A man had a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) because he had sold himself to the devil. However often he spent his money, a little later there was always a daalder in his pocket again.
23689: Where the devil jumped over a pond, a human footprint can be seen on one side, and the print of a horse on the other.
23700: The wild lanterns that people used to see were the portents of the later bicycle lamps.
23701: Sometimes a ghostly tree would appear across the road.
23705: One morning on his way to the farmer, a man once saw a plaagbeest (tormenting beast) standing by part of a house. It was brownish and flapped its ears wildly.
23706: A man once saw three men on a mill, but when he came closer, there was no one to be seen.
23708: A dead person must be buried with what he is entitled to, such as a shirt. If that does not happen, the dead person finds no rest and comes back to haunt.
23709: One should never walk in the middle of the road in the evening or at night. Sometimes you are suddenly pushed to the side when a funeral procession is coming.
23710: Old Anne Leegstra was once thrown down by the devil.
23716:
Some people got a bottle of liquor when they sent off a playing card.
Someone once threw a pack of playing cards up in the air. One of them stuck to the ceiling.
23719: A woman asked for a promise that if she died, her golden leg would be buried with her. But her husband did not keep his word. The first nights after the funeral the man woke because there was tapping on the windows. He then heard his dead wife asking for her golden leg. On the third night he put the leg outside the door. The next morning it was gone, and his wife never came to haunt him again.
23724: One night a man heard wooden planks being dragged. Half a year later wood was delivered at night, and the sound was really there.
23728:
Two brothers once saw a woman's body rise up out of the ground while they were working. A little rhyme was made about it that was often sung:
I saw something by Bearn on the heath,
I saw something by Bearn on the dam.
23729: A father and son once saw a woman floating across the road. They ran away as fast as they could.
23737: The wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) of the past were portents of the later train.
23742: A man once heard people singing in the church. But the church was empty. The next day they sang exactly the same psalm in the church that the man had heard the day before.
23745: At a certain place a foal haunts with a porridge pot around its neck.
23747: Two men were once followed all the way home by a plaagbeest (a tormenting spectral beast). When one of them later went outside to relieve himself, the beast struck him. It was the devil.
23750: One night a woman saw an acquaintance lying in a coffin in a white garment. That same night the man had indeed died.
23751: One evening a young couple saw a strange woman float past.
23752: One night a man saw a strange man with eyes glowing like burning coals.
23753: People should never walk in the middle of the road, because they can suddenly be pushed to the side. A funeral procession might pass by.
23754: A married couple were once on their way when suddenly lots of trees fell onto the road in front of them.
23755: In the west of Augustinusga a large, red-spotted dog always haunts in the evening. It walks right past people, but does nothing else.
23758: A man heard the train before it was running.
23766: At midnight a white thing always haunted the railway bridge in Westereinde. It seemed to float and throw pebbles.
23767: A man once spent a night in a haunted barn. In the middle of the night the doors opened and a horse and cart came driving in.
23768: Two men in a small boat once saw something white walking back and forth across the railway at Westereinde. When they tried to hit it with their oar, it suddenly vanished.
23769: On the Langepad in Westereinde, two little children always haunted at night. The Langelaan was haunted too.
23770: A man who was born with a caul often had to get up at night to see funeral processions. He also saw his own child's funeral procession in advance.
23775: On the Koopmansweg in Westereinde, a dog always haunts at night.
23780: A man who was born with a caul saw a funeral procession pass by. The next day the funeral procession really passed by.
23781: The father of a sick girl tries to shoot a cat. He fails, and the animal disappears near a house nearby. The next day the man accuses the neighbour of having bewitched his daughter. The child has recovered.
23785: Once, on the way back, a small woman came walking beside another woman. She did not return the greeting and suddenly she was gone again, as if she had sunk into the ground.
23787: A woman had not been given in her grave what she was entitled to. Because of that she could find no rest and kept haunting her family. Until a minister addressed her and found out what the problem was. Her family put the things on a chair, and the next day they were gone. The family never saw her again after that.
23791: Minse Griper made little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. They would then start to dance. He could also get a bottle of liquor by means of a playing card. But once nobody wanted to accept the bottle of liquor and he nearly died.
23794: A boy was treated rather badly in the home of some people. He drowned there. Later, when a woman passed by early one morning, she saw the boy standing by the gate.
23796: In a house where a child was once murdered, the door always opens again by itself. They can never keep it shut.
23797: The little bridges in Houtigehage used to be haunted.
23799: One night a man met another man who did not return his greeting.
23804: When a man read from his magic book, jackdaws came out of the hearth pit. If he read the same thing backwards, the birds disappeared into the hearth pit again.
23807: A woman who was born with a caul often had to get up at night to see funeral processions. Because of this she always knew in advance who would die.
23808: One evening a woman heard groaning in the cowshed, but there was nothing to be seen. A few days later she heard exactly the same groaning again. It was a cow lying there groaning.
23810: In the past people saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps). They were portents of the tram.
23811: If a dog howled ghostly at night, someone died.
23813: One must never remove a stork's nest; it brings luck.
23823: On his way home, a man was once lifted up several times and thrown over the ditch.
23827: One night a ship riveter heard the sound of riveting. But there was nothing to be seen. The next day riveting really took place.
23828: The gates of a churchyard were always open again the next day, no matter how many locks and chains had been used to close them.
23829: In Hardegarijp there stood a castle whose gates opened by themselves every night.
23831: The voice of a child was often heard coming from a small lake. It is said that someone will yet drown in it.
23838: The three children of a dead woman claimed now and then that their mother had been with them. The father did not want to believe it, but fetched the minister anyway. He asked the woman what her wish was. She then said that she had hidden some money in a certain place. New clothes for the children had to be bought with it. That was done, and the woman did not come back.
23841: In the old days people thought houses would be built on the heath because they saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, ghostly lights) there. That did happen.
23843: If a dog howls ghostly, someone in the area will die. If a cat washes itself, visitors often come the next day.
23845: A place where a man hanged himself is haunted.
23846: In a house, all three men who lived there one after another committed suicide. Since then the house has been haunted.
23852: Some boys once heard planks being thrown about, but there was nothing to be seen. Later a new house was built on that spot.
23853: People once heard the churn going in the cowshed. But no one was churning. That only happened the next day.
23854: People sometimes heard the clattering of the flax brake. Then the next day they began breaking flax.
23855: A man once saw something flying towards the north. It was twelve or thirteen wagons in a row, without a horse, and it made a puffing sound. Later a train came past that spot.
23857: A dog once howled ghostly and terribly in front of the gate of a house where a sick girl lived. Three days later the girl died.
23859: A scoffer once heard the flax brake clattering. He went to see what caused it, and was grabbed by the scruff of the neck by the devil.
23860: A couple of scoffers once celebrated Holy Communion in a pub. But when they went back home, terrible things must have happened. One of them never dared go out on the street alone again.
23861: Two brothers were terrible cursers. One evening they came out of the pub together and each went a different way. On the way, one of them was thrown into the ditch several times by the devil.
23868: In Groningen the labourers slept in the barns. In some spots in those barns they were not allowed to sleep, because those spots were haunted.
23874: Witches boil needles in a pan and then stick them into dolls.
23903: A neighbour of a sick girl once went to Wopke, the exorcist. Wopke gave him a potion and said that if the bottle broke on the way, the child was bewitched. And indeed the bottle broke. Wopke had also said that a woman would come who wanted to give the child food, but they must not allow it. That evening they sent the woman who wanted to come and feed the child out of the house. Not long after, a whole lot of cats were sitting by the door. One of them threw a stone at a black cat. The next day the little woman lay in bed with an injured leg.
23910: If you have promised someone something and do not do it once that person has died, they will come to haunt.
23911: One evening a woman saw two girls wearing little aprons and little hats. They were ghosts.
23912: A man was once walking between two other men when he was suddenly picked up and thrown over the dike. The devil did that.
23914: A man was once lifted over the ditch, bicycle and all. People thought funeral processions sometimes passed by at that spot.
23920: It has happened in the pub that people got a bottle of liquor by sending out a jack of spades. The first dram must then be thrown away over the left shoulder. The measuring cup of liquor first floats around above the table.
23923: A man had walked around the churchyard with a black cat in a sack and had said: "Devil, will you buy my cat too?" The cat was then taken from him and he received a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin).
23924: A woman was once baking pancakes with flour she had just borrowed from the baker's wife. While she was at it, a black cat came and said: "Baking pancakes and borrowing flour?" The woman threw a red-hot pancake onto the cat's head and the cat fled. The next day the baker's wife's head was completely burnt.
23928: At the spot where the devil jumped over a canal, a print of a horse's hoof has been left behind.
23930: The Liuwepoel is dreadfully deep. Cries for help have sometimes been heard there at night. This means that someone will drown in it.
23933: A man once had the feeling that his wife was dead, and he saw her corpse. The next day the woman really died.
23934: A woman once saw her own ghost in the ditch when she was drawing a bucket of water from it. Since then she never dared to draw water from the ditch again.
23937: A man once came out of the pub drunk. He claimed he would throw the first person he met across the field, even if it was the devil himself. But then he himself was thrown across the field by the devil.
23944: Once, at a certain spot, a woman heard psalms being sung. Later a Reformed church was built on that spot.
23945: A woman once saw something burning fly through the sky. She predicted that in the future cars would fly through the air. Those turned out to be the later aeroplanes.
23946: People regularly heard clearly that someone was coming to the door. But when they went to look, there was no one. Yet later that day someone always did come.
23947: Someone once saw the town hall on fire. A little later it really burned down.
23951: A cat often came in the evening to a sick woman. Once the woman's husband gave the cat a beating. The next day he met an acquaintance who was suddenly limping. She claimed it was because she had tripped. But the man knew better. The old woman never visited them again, and neither did the cat. And the sick woman got better.
23953: A few men were once on the road with a horse and cart. Suddenly the horse got scared and jumped to the side. The men saw nothing. Someone came by and said that this happened more often. That man, like the horse, then saw a funeral procession pass by. If it was a white coach, all was well, then it was spiritual. If it was a black coach, then it meant death.
23955: In the old days people were warned never to walk in the middle of the road. A funeral procession might pass or even make you fall.
23959: Reid Keuning was a bicycle repairman and a drunkard. He could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
23960: A man once heard hammering at a place where nothing could be seen. Shortly afterwards a new farmhouse was built there.
23961: A man once saw lights at a place where there was nothing, and thought a waterway would come there later. But a motorway came instead. The lights were not from ships, but from cars.
23962: A man once saw a funeral in his house and feared one of his youngest sons would die. But it was his eldest son who died.
23964: Around midnight a woman once went to see whether her husband was coming yet. She saw someone approaching with something heavy around his neck. When she glanced at the moon and looked back, he had vanished. She quickly went inside, for that was not right. A girl had once starved to death at that spot.
23968: A sorcerer could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
23994: Two men had earned good money from their work and went on a drinking spree at the inn. They swore and raged terribly. A little further on their lifeless bodies were found afterwards. The devil had wrung their necks.
23995: With a jack of spades one can make a bottle of liquor come.
24005: Ate Jager could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. Then the little soldiers would start to march.
24006: Animals are often clairvoyant. A dog knows two hours in advance that a thunderstorm is coming. Then it is restless and frightened.
24007: A man always saw in advance that someone was going to die.
24008: A man who always cursed a lot once had to fetch some things from an attic. But every time he was halfway up the ladder, he was flung off it. Then someone else did it, and nothing happened.
24010: One night a woman heard a sound as if a beam were tapping on the table. Later her little daughter died. Then she thought it had been an omen.
24012: One night a man was walking alone on a lonely road. He wished there were someone to keep him company. Suddenly a man was walking in front of him with a gallows slung across his back. He walked ahead of him for a while, and then suddenly disappeared.
24013: One evening a man was walking outside when another man came walking beside him. The stranger said nothing. Then suddenly the man was lifted up and thrown over the trees into the ditch.
24015: One night a man saw a wagon driving without a horse in front of it. That happened a good thirty years before there were cars.
24016: People once heard something bang against the wall in the hallway. Not long afterwards the man of the house died. When the coffin was carried out of the house, it banged against the wall. This made exactly the same sound they had heard before.
24017: One dark evening about four men were playing cards. They wanted a bottle of liquor and handed the jack of spades over at the door. Then one of the men had a bottle of liquor placed in his hand.
24022: Two men were once walking in the moonlight when they saw the apparition of a person in front of them. A little later the apparition had disappeared again.
24023: A boy was supposed to wake his two brothers, who slept together in a box bed. But he saw not two but three lying there. When he came back a little later, there were two again, and only then did he wake them.
24031: There was once a witch who could fly. She flew over woods, over trees, over all the streams. She went to the wine cellar in Spain.
24039: People once saw a little light at a certain spot. But when they came closer, there was nothing to be seen. Later a house was built on that spot.
24040: By the railway in Westereinde people sometimes saw a wilde lantaarn (wild lantern, ghostly light). Later a new house was built on that spot.
24041: A man once saw a house on fire, but when he came closer there was nothing to be seen any more. Two years later that same house burned down.
24042: On a very narrow road people once saw a wide wagon of peat pass by. In reality that was quite impossible. Later a proper road was built.
24049: One of seven sons is a werewolf. You must never quarrel with a werewolf, because then he will kill you. A girl always did sewing at other people's homes. Her suitor once asked her for a handkerchief. She gave it to him, and outside he tore the thing to shreds. After that he was normal again. He turned out to be a werewolf. Then the girl broke it off.
24050: Ytsje Jelle and Tytsje Jelle had a devil's book. They could hardly get rid of it. When they read from the book, gnomes and little soldiers came out of the hearth pit. When they read the same thing backwards, they disappeared again. There was also once a farmer with such a magic book. One time he read from it while spreading manure. Rooks came flying in from everywhere and tore all the manure heaps apart. That way the manure was spread over the land very quickly.
24054: A man cursed a lot. He damned God and his commandments. Once, when he had been drinking in the pub, he was suddenly lifted up and thrown down. He was black and blue. The devil had done that.
24057: Stotterende Harm had a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin). One night someone saw him praying beside a path. The next day he had lots of money again.
24059: A man had promised his wife to pay off the debts they had. The woman died, but the man did not keep his promise. Because of this the dead woman could find no rest. Many people have seen her haunting at night in a black garment.
24060: On the path from Zwagerveen to de Triemen a foal with a wooden head always haunts at night.
24061: A man had a sick little son who was bewitched. One day a black cat came into the yard. He shot at the animal and hit it. The next day an old witch from the neighbourhood was lame.
24062: If you make three little crosses on the road, a witch cannot catch you. You must never say 'yes' three times in a row to what a witch asks, because then she gets you in her power. If you have a crust of rye bread in your pocket, a witch cannot get a hold on you.
24064: At a certain spot people often saw a great many lights and often heard knocking. Later new houses were built there.
24071: If you walk in the middle of the road at night, you can suddenly be set aside to the edge.
24085: At a certain spot a foal haunts with a porridge pot around its neck.
24086: On the Groningen clay there are barns in which it is not safe to sleep in some spots. At night you can suddenly be flung away.
24087: A man grew some rye on a small plot of land he rented from a landlord. He paid the rent with the rye. Once he was ill. He asked a farmer to thresh the rye for him and pay the landlord with it. The farmer promised to. But the man died and the farmer forgot his promise. From then on, when the farmer and his wife went to bed in the evening, they heard noise in the attic. They fetched Piter Poes. According to Piter something had to be wrong. The wife remembered that they had not yet paid the landlord with the rye. The next day they did so after all, and they were never troubled again.
24091: People once hit a cat on the head with a stick. The next day a neighbour woman walked about with a cloth around her head.
24093: When the magpies gather, someone will die.
24094: A thatcher once told an acquaintance that that day magpies had been flying all around his house making a great racket. Not long afterwards the thatcher died.
24095: If a dog howls ghostly, someone will die. A woman was once ill. When she and her husband were lying in bed in the evening, they heard a dog howl ghostly. Two weeks later the woman died in hospital.
24096: A dog once stood in the middle of a potato field howling ghostly towards the northwest. Not long afterwards someone who lived in that direction died.
24097: If magpies chatter close to a house and fly off in all directions, someone in that house will die.
24101: If you put an apple or a carrot that you got from a witch under a cup, by the next day it has turned into a toad or a frog.
24102: If you eat something from a witch, you spit out snakes and scales.
24108: If one wants a bottle of liquor, one must hand over a jack of spades at the door. A little later a bottle of liquor comes floating in. Someone must take the bottle, but not the one who handed over the card. Otherwise he dies.
24111: In the old days young people would sometimes stand before the black mirror.
24112: In the old days some people could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
24119: A man who was born with a caul always has to see everything in advance. He sees that people will die, because he saw funeral processions.
24120: A man went to church with his son every Sunday. Another man, who often foresaw that someone would die, warned that if the churchgoing man took his son to church again that Sunday, the son would die. The man paid no attention. That Sunday the boy died in an accident with a milk cart.
24121: A man foresaw that a girl would shoot herself dead with a gun. Her brother had joined the marechaussee (military police) during his military service. Her boyfriend now wanted to do the same. The girl was afraid of losing her boyfriend, and so she killed herself.
24122: A man foresaw that another man would come home dead that evening. That is indeed what happened. The man had suffered from the heat and died.
24123: At night a man often saw funerals as an omen of the coming day. He was then driven out of his bed and had to watch.
24130: If a dog howls ghostly, a death usually follows.
24131: By the old church in Rottevalle a foal haunts with a porridge pot around its neck.
24135:
A man who was born with a caul often had to get up at night to see a funeral procession. A few days later someone really died.
A midwife sometimes delivered children with a caul. That was a thin membrane. No strange eyes may look upon it. The caul must be removed in a particular way. The midwife would then secretly take it with her and burn it as soon as she was alone. Doctors are mad about such cauls.
24140: In the old days people sometimes still saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, ghostly lights). Those were the lights that are now on bicycles and cars.
24142: The Kleine Laantje was haunted. People have seen an old gentleman wearing a hat haunting there.
24146: If a dog howls ghostly, someone will die. If magpies chatter near the houses, someone will also die.
24147: Someone was once thrown down by the devil. He had said strange things.
24152: A witch can change herself into a cat. When people had once given a cat a few good blows, the witch lay sick in bed the next day.
24153: When witch's wreaths are burnt, the witch is racked with pain. The witch also suffers pain when needles are stuck into a witch's wreath.
24157: Jehannes Meerstra went around selling cheese. He made little soldiers come out of the hearth pit and made the chairs dance just like that. He could also make people stand still, and he could make women's clothes drop down.
24159: With a jack of spades one can make a bottle of liquor come.
24160: In the old days people at the market would sometimes look into the black mirror. In it they would see their future wife.
24163: One night a man saw himself lying dead in a coffin. He took out insurance for ten thousand guilders. Then he died. His wife received the payout and married his brother.
24168: When Imke de Jong left the town, people saw him go out through the gate at three places at the same time.
24169: Imke de Jong could crawl through a beam.
24170: With a jack of spades one can make a bottle of liquor come. Two men must make a pact. Another person puts an empty bottle with the playing card outside by the door, and it is agreed who will take the bottle. That must be yet another person. A little later the bottle comes with jenever. The first dram is thrown out over the left shoulder.
24171: In the old days there were fortune-tellers' tents at the markets. In them you could look into the black mirror. You were then shown the woman you would marry, or a coffin. That meant you would not marry.
24178: An old woman was always spinning. People often used an old shirt as a burial shirt. When the old woman had died, they dressed her in a shirt that was missing a sleeve. But once the woman lay in her grave, she began to haunt. She came to the people she had lived with and said: "Always spinning, always spinning, and still only a shirt with one sleeve." The people were afraid and fetched a minister. The minister said they should put a sleeve on the windowsill. They did so and the next day the sleeve was gone. The ghost never came again.
24179: If you see a funeral procession coming, you must step aside. Otherwise you are thrown to the side. People who do not see the funeral processions are pushed aside too.
24181: People once heard noise as if there was fighting, but there was nothing at all to be seen. They thought a pub would come there. Later a coffeehouse was built. Once there was a terrible fight there.
24182: People did see wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) at a place where the tram later ran.
24183: Whenever people found a cat in front of their door, something always happened. Someone died of the cold or a child fell ill. That cat was a witch.
24190: In the old days people sometimes sent out a card for a bottle of liquor.
24195: A woman once saw something float over the houses. She did not know what it was; it was something ghostly.
24196: A man saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, ghostly lights). That could mean all sorts of things: new houses, new roads, bicycles, cars, street lamps, etc.
24197: A man could leave his yard by two routes, but used only one of them. According to him, the other way was haunted.
24198: A man was once suddenly lifted up and set down again some way further on.
24199: A man always saw funeral processions passing along the road that nobody else saw.
24208: A dog once stood whining by the water. Later its owner drowned there.
24218: In the old days a woman always saw lots of wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, ghostly lights) on the dyke at Murmwoude. She claimed that Murmwoude would later turn into a town. The place did not become a town, but if you stand on the dyke in the evening now, there are so many lights to be seen that it does look like a town.
24219: In winter a baker often cycled across the ice to work, because it was much shorter. One day his wife warned him not to go across the ice that day. That night she had seen him fall through the ice and drown. But the man went across the ice anyway, and indeed he drowned.
24221: A woman could always tell a neighbour what had been said whenever he had had visitors in the evening. When the man saw a black cat sitting by his house one evening, he understood how. He kicked the animal. The next day the woman lay in bed with a bruised head.
24223: In Groningen some farms were haunted. At night the wagon sometimes rattled across the floor. That was a forewarning of the bustle of the coming day.
24226: A place is haunted: a fellow wearing a skirt is said to make strange noises there.
24227: At a haunted place, wailing and groaning can be heard at night, as if someone is in distress.
24229: A man was once chased by the devil, who bared his teeth at him.
24234: Wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, ghostly lights) are often forewarnings of, for example, bicycle lights.
24235: At a haunted place, a man haunts who looks as if he is on fire. The fire man never comes close to people.
24237: To keep nightmares away you must put your clogs upside down in front of the door for 89 evenings. Scattering flour on the edge of the bed or on your face and hanging up elder branches are also good ways to stop nightmares. Nightmares often enter the house through the keyhole.
24238: Witte wieven (white women) used to haunt a haunted spot.
24239: At a haunted spot a dog haunts with a porridge pot around its neck.
24240: If someone keeps haunting after death, they often could not fulfil a promise in life because they died early. If the minister addresses the dead person, the unfulfilled promise can still be fulfilled. Only then does the dead person find rest.
24241: At a haunted spot little children who cannot find rest after their death sometimes haunt. They dance in the chimney at night.
24242: Sounds from a small lake are interpreted as an omen of death by drowning.
24244: A father warns his children never to walk in the middle of the road in the evening.
24245: A man born with a caul often has to get up at night to see things, for example a dead person being carried out of a house.
24247: Food received from a witch and set aside turns into a toad. Many people sew a toad into their clothes.
24248: Witches travel through the air on a broomstick.
24250: Some wizards can temporarily fix people to the spot.
24251: People living in a caravan hear their neighbours hammering at night. It is a forewarning of a new house to be built.
24252: A man born with a caul often has visions of the future. For instance, he foresees exactly when his neighbour's sick child will die and what the funeral will be like.
24253: A man born with a caul advises his wife not to buy school things for their child, because he foresees that the child will die before then. It turns out exactly that way.
24254: A man born with a caul often has to get up at night to see things.
24255: A man born with a caul foresees countless deaths.
24257: A clairvoyant woman, born with a caul, often foresees funerals.
24258: When the narrator dreams of horses, there is always a death in the family. The more calmly the horses walk, the further off in the future the death is.
24259: In a haunted house noise, busy footsteps, can always be heard at night. There is also often knocking on the door, although no one can be seen. A girl was once murdered in the house.
24260: A farmhand is suddenly startled by a dog. The next moment he is struck terribly hard.
24262: A sorcerer makes little soldiers appear from the hearth pit and march neatly in rank. He can also make people stuck in place. Sometimes he makes a bottle of liquor come with a jack of spades.
24263: Of seven daughters, one is a nightmare. A man lies with his back against the bed board because then the nightmare cannot get him.
24267: A cyclist on the railway is suddenly hurled from his bicycle. He thinks it has something to do with a funeral procession.
24269: A dog with four eyes is a ghost-howler. When the dog begins to howl ghostly, it is usually an omen of an impending death.
24272: A horse is troubled by nightmares. A merchant advises hanging a scythe above the animal and scattering a handful of bread in its mane. The horse has not been troubled by nightmares since.
24273: At a haunted spot a foal haunts with a porridge pot around its neck.
24280: A witch can change herself into a dog. When the dog goes out bewitching, the witch lies senseless in bed. A man shoots the dog in the head. The witch then also has a bullet in her head.
24287: If a painting falls down, a death is coming. It is an omen.
24288: In a small haunted room a white man can always be seen at twelve o'clock at night. The man takes some stones out of the wall and takes out a purse of money. He counts the money and puts the purse and the stones back in their place. The occupant of the house, a baker, sees the ghost counting the money and removes the secret treasure the very next day. He sells his bakery and moves to America. The house is no longer haunted.
24289: People hear a sound coming from the water. It is an omen: later someone drowned.
24293: In the shed of people who hire out cars, the cars start humming by themselves at night. It is a forewarning. Ticking can often be heard too. That is also a forewarning: a house will later be renovated.
24294: A man born with a caul foresees the death of his own daughter.
24299: With a jack of spades you can make a bottle of liquor come. Whoever has a jack of spades, the most important card in the deck, among his cards always wins.
24300: Anything you want to see, you can see in a black mirror. Some people see nothing in the black mirror.
24301: A sorcerer can make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit.
24302: A sorcerer can make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit. The sorcerer is also a devil banisher: he regularly supplies medicines for bewitched people. The sorcerer's wife is a card reader: she can foretell the future.
24309: In a haunted house, the door springs open again by itself at night.
24310: A scoffer boasts that he is not afraid of the devil. On the way home he is promptly seized and thrown down.
24312: A boy turns out to be courting a witch. When he takes her home, a fat dog with eyes as big as teacups comes towards him. When he tries to wound the dog, the girl - the witch - also complains of pain.
24313: At a haunted spot a little dog runs around with a small basket in its mouth. It is a phantom animal.
24314: At night people hear sounds as if a coffin is being made. It is an omen.
24315: Wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, ghostly lights) turn out to be a forewarning of the later street lighting.
24316: A man suddenly sees a few men carrying a coffin along. It is an omen: the next day someone actually dies.
24321: A man is startled at night by a white ghost woman who looks into all the cups on the table.
24322: Children who are buried without a shroud keep wandering restlessly after death.
24327: One of seven daughters born in a row is a witch. A witch can change herself into a cat. If you thrash such a witch-cat, the witch also shows injuries the next day.
24328: A man sees four lamps burning and suspects that a school will be built. No school came, but a house for four families did. It is an omen.
24329: Near a meadow a woman clearly hears sounds as if stones are being thrown. It is an omen: the meadow later became a brick-paved road.
24330: A man urges his companions to step aside for a passing funeral procession. A child is being buried. It is a premonition: shortly afterwards a little child really dies.
24331: A woman is driven into the ditch by a funeral procession.
24332: The narrator's mother often has a premonition that certain things are about to happen.
24333: A man is driven into the ditch by a passing funeral procession.
24335: Children's screaming is heard by the water. It is an omen: later two children are narrowly saved from drowning.
24336: At a haunted spot a foal runs around with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a phantom animal.
24337: Someone foresees that a red-haired girl will drown in a pool. The vision has not yet come true.
24341: A dead woman cannot find rest because she was buried in a shroud that is too long.
24342: Wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, ghostly lights) are a forewarning of the later bicycle lights.
24346: A sinner is seized by the devil and thrown down. The sinner promptly mends his ways.
24349: One Sunday evening a woman very clearly sees a man with a lantern in his hand surveying the meadow. It is a voorgezicht (a vision of the future): later the land is surveyed and new houses are built on that spot.
24350: At a carpenter's house, wood for coffins is clearly heard being moved in the attic at night. It is an omen: the next day someone comes to order a coffin for a deceased person.
24351: In the old days, cursers were often tricked by the devil.
24352: A sorcerer can make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit.
24353: Someone makes a bottle of liquor come with a playing card. If nobody takes hold of the bottle, which floats above the table, someone will die. The first glass is thrown over the shoulder.
24355: A wizard can fix people to the spot.
24356: When the wizard Imke de Jong was in military service, he tormented a high-ranking officer by fixing him to the spot in the rain.
24357: The wizard Imke de Jong cannot be held in any jail: he always gets out.
24358: The wizard Imke de Jong can predict the future.
24362: Scoffers boast that they are not afraid of the devil. The men start quarrelling and one stabs the other to death. That was the devil's punishment.
24363: Drunkards are often seized and flung down.
24366: The wizard Imke de Jong has many gifts: he can do ventriloquism and fix people to the ground. During his military service Imke had great trouble telling 'forward' from 'backward'.
24369: Someone lying in bed feels his neck being squeezed. When he feels his neck, he feels two smooth little hands.
24372: At night a man clearly hears beams being thrown about. It is a forewarning of later carpentry work on a new house.
24373: A witch bewitches and torments cattle.
24374: When a funeral procession approaches, the dog already starts to howl ghostly in advance.
24376: With a devil's book, a sorcerer can make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit. When he reads the book backwards, the little soldiers go back into the hearth.
24377: A fortune teller who read cards came to a bad end: the devil twisted her head around.
24378: A sorcerer can make a bottle of liquor come with a playing card. When the full bottle floats in, he cannot take it himself. If the person who sent the bottle away takes hold of it again, he dies.
24379: At a haunted spot a foal wanders around with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a phantom animal.
24380: A young man on his way home from his girlfriend is startled by a large black dog.
24381: A widow tells a shopkeeper that the ghost of her dead husband sometimes visits her. The shopkeeper does not believe it, but shortly afterwards he is startled by the ghost of the dead husband.
24382: A father and son are startled by a fat black dog. It is a phantom animal.
24383: A man born with a caul sees a funeral procession pass in windless weather. The people in the procession, mostly wrapped in rain clothes, can barely stay on their feet because of a violent storm. It is a premonition: when someone dies later, there is a violent storm as well.
24384: A woman hears sounds as if a coffin is being made ready. It is a portent of her own funeral: when she herself dies, the same sounds can be heard.
24385: A drunkard is roughly seized and flung down several times in a row.
24391: A wilde lantaarn (wild lantern, ghostly light) is an omen.
24393: A witch turns herself into a hare. Because witches are bulletproof, a man fails to shoot the hare dead. You can only hit a witch with grains of rye.
24394: A woman keeps haunting after her death because people neglected to dress her in a shroud. When the minister fulfils the unfulfilled promise, the woman finds rest.
24395: A drunkard tries to stab the devil with a knife. The devil promptly throws him across the field.
24397: A witch changes herself into a cat. When the cat gets a whack, the witch soon afterwards walks about with a cloth around her head.
24398: If you eat something you got from a witch, it turns into a toad.
24400: A witch was once seen flying through the air.
24401: Witches stick needles into dolls to hurt people.
24403: A man is suddenly fixed to the spot by the devil along his way.
24407: You get a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) from the devil. This devil's coin can never run out.
24410: At a haunted place, the doors always spring open at night.
24416: Two clay workers see a storm coming and ask a farmer for shelter for the night. The farmer refuses at first because he is troubled by haunted doors, but finally agrees. The two workers decide to keep watch on what happens with the doors. At midnight the doors open and the farmer's wife comes in. But the farmer's wife has been dead for some time. She has kept haunting because the farmer neglected to pay a certain sum of money. When the farmer meets his obligation, the woman finds rest.
24417: At night a man sees a little old person approaching. When he greets the little woman, she does not greet him back. When the man looks after her, she has suddenly vanished. It is a ghost woman.
24418: A scoffer boasts, in coarse words, that he is not afraid of a little thunderstorm. He is promptly struck dead: scoffers get a scoffer's reward.
24421: When someone is going to die, the dog begins to howl eerily. The dog keeps its head turned toward the one who will die.
24422: At a haunted place, a gate always springs open at midnight. It is a ghost gate.
24423: In a certain house there is a hole that can never be closed.
24424: Never run in the middle of the road at night: a funeral procession may pass.
24425: One hunter urges the other to step aside for a passing funeral procession. The one man foresees that a certain woman is going to die, and it turns out exactly so.
24426: A girl is given a piece of cake by a woman - a supposed witch. The mother manages to get the cake away from her daughter. The next day the cake has turned into a toad.
24430: Two well-known card readers are Thomas' Clare and Tryn Snipel. Tryn was better at it than Clare.
24431: A group of men visits a mirror tent with a black mirror. One of the men is advised to treat his wife a bit better.
24440: A man just cannot shoot down a white cat. The cat is bulletproof: it is a witch's cat.
24442: A woman - a witch - was once seen flying through the air on a broomstick.
24443: A house that has burned down several times is not right. In the evening a naked man often stands in the corner of the room. It is probably the arsonist himself, who could not find rest after his death.
24444: A married couple lives in poverty. Of sixteen children the woman has been able to keep only three: thirteen died on the day they were born. When she is pregnant again, she gives birth to twins. The twins soon die. After death the twins kept haunting naked.
24445: On a moonlit night a man is suddenly startled by a dog the size of a calf with eyes as big as teacups. The man's Reformed mother thinks it was the devil.
24446: A man hears sounds of hammering, but there is nothing to be seen. It is an omen: later a house is built on the same spot.
24449: When there is a sick person on board at sea, the fish come swimming around the ship. It is an omen: the sick person will soon die.
24450: When a mermaid comes near a ship's rudder, bad weather is on its way. Porpoises are also forewarnings of storms.
24451: A card reader tells a young couple in love that they will not stay together. It turns out exactly that way: the woman later commits adultery.
24453: Wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, ghostly lights) are said to be forewarnings of the later car and bicycle lights.
24454: A folk healer often cures people, especially children. The healer and his son once stood face to face with the devil in the shape of a little man.
24458: A nightmare is sometimes a man as well: the narrator's brother is said to have been tormented at night by a fellow who sat on top of him.
24467: During the First World War, an illiterate old man predicts that yet another war will break out in 1940. The man predicts that a city in the south of the country will suffer heavily and that the queen will flee. The man makes more predictions connected with the war. All the predictions have come true.
24468: Some people visit an illiterate card reader; others want nothing to do with fortune telling.
24469: A man hears sounds of hammering, but there is nothing to be seen. It is a forewarning: later new houses are built on that spot.
24470: A man suddenly hears shouting, although there is nothing to be seen. It is a forewarning: the next day he hears the same sounds when a boy who cannot swim almost drowns.
24471: A man born with a caul always has to get up at night to see things. He often foresees funerals at night. He even foresaw the funerals of his own son and daughter.
24472: People see a house on fire. It is a premonition: later the house really does burn down.
24473: A man hears cries for help from the water and clearly sees the face of the person in need. It is a foreshadowing of an impending drowning: that same night the drowned person is dragged up from the water.
24476: A nightmare, one of seven daughters, torments a man. The man throws flour over himself so that the nightmare cannot escape.
24478: A nightmare comes to people through the keyhole or the gotegat (drain hole).
24484: Three comrades spend the night in a shed. In the shed stands an animal that keeps growing: a phantom animal.
24485: At a haunted spot a foal with a porridge pot around its neck haunts the place. It is a ghost animal.
24488: A scoffer is seized by the devil and thrown down.
24490: The sorcerer Imke de Jong was once seen flying through the air.
24493: You should never walk in the middle of the road at night: you can suddenly be set aside to the edge.
24494: Two slightly tipsy men are on their way home with their wagon. On the way the devil is suddenly sitting on a turning wheel of the wagon. The devil breaks the wagon's glass.
24498: A wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) is a rijksdaalder that you get from the devil. You must never spend the whole wisseldaalder. If you keep some of it, even just a dubbeltje, it then turns back into a rijksdaalder.
24502: A number of people hear the mill creaking. According to two women it is a forewarning of something bad.
24504: A man sees a house burn down. It is an omen: later the house really does burn down.
24509: Magpies near the house, a dog howling eerily, a barn owl calling and the death knell of the bell are all omens of a death.
24510: If a magpie comes into the yard, you will get visitors.
24511: In the old days people often saw green lights. They were the forewarnings of the later tram lights.
24512: Someone hears sounds of hammering, although there is nothing to be seen. It is a forewarning: later a new house is built on that spot.
24513: A woman born with a caul often has to get up at night to see funeral processions pass by.
24514: An orphan raised by his uncle keeps seeing a man appear while mowing. The man disappears as suddenly as he appeared: he is a ghost.
24515: At a haunted place three gentlemen haunt about with papers in their hands.
24516: A poor woman sighs in despair that she would so love to have a twenty-five guilder note, even if she got it from the devil himself. At once a yellow note lies right in front of her. The woman wisely leaves it there.
24517: A shameless curser is so roughly handled that he remained lame for the rest of his life. Since that day the sinner has changed: not one foul word passes his lips anymore.
24518: A curser is seized by the devil and roughly thrown down.
24523: At a haunted spot a foal with a porridge pot around its neck haunts the place: a ghost animal.
24524: A witch can turn herself into a black cat. Some witches stick needles into little dolls to hurt people.
24525: A man spies on his wife, a suspected witch, and concludes that his wife is rightly accused of witchcraft. His wife sticks needles into a little doll. The man throws the doll into the stove while his wife is asleep. The woman suffers terrible pains and dies when the doll has burnt up completely.
24530: If you eat an apple you got from a witch, the apple turns into a toad.
24531: Some witches stick needles into little dolls to torment people.
24532: A bewitched churn will not make butter. Hot water in the churn can solve the problem.
24536: Just before their wedding, a young couple sees death in a black mirror. The prediction of death comes true: the woman dies soon after.
24542: The wizard Imke de Jong asks the driver of a wagon if he may ride along. When the man refuses, Imke makes a wheel come off the wagon. The wagon is stuck.
24547: At a haunted spot, the stakes used to moor a ship to the ground are thrown onto the deck again and again. A funeral procession once had to pass the place where the ship lies.
24548: At a haunted spot by the water a naked little child haunts.
24551: A woman urges a companion to step aside for a passing funeral procession. Only the one woman can see the procession.
24552: Two mates spend the night at the farm 'De nachtmerrie'. Sure enough, one of the men is tormented by a nightmare. The nightmare climbs up the man from his feet. To keep nightmares away you must put your clogs upside down. Horses are sometimes plagued by nightmares too.
24556: On her deathbed a sick woman asks her husband to give her clothes to the housekeeper after her death. The man agrees, but after his wife's death gives the clothes to someone else. A while later the man's children say that their mother is still haunting. When the minister asks the dead woman about her unfulfilled wish, she says her housekeeper must get her clothes. The woman agrees to the minister's proposal to give the housekeeper new clothes. Now that the promise has been fulfilled in this way, the woman finds rest.
24559: A sick woman turns out to be bewitched. Her husband tries to shoot a suspicious black cat. The next day a woman is missing an eye: she was the witch in the shape of a cat.
24561: A woman who sells potatoes - a supposed witch - sometimes has trouble selling her wares, because many people think the potatoes are bewitched. Another woman is also suspected of witchcraft because pears she hands out turn into toads.
24566: People see a house burn down. Only later does the house really burn down: it was a premonition.
24567: A man born with a caul often foresees funerals. If the caul is pulled forward at birth, the person has no visions of the future. If the caul is pushed upward, the person does have visions of the future.
24568: In the old days a jack of spades was sent out to fetch a bottle of jenever. There were also people who could make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit.
24570: A farmhand spending the night in a haunted barn sees a little light moving over the walls at night. It is said that someone once hanged himself in the barn.
24571: At a haunted place, something always comes driving over the bridge at midnight. Only a shadow can be seen.
24574: At a haunted spot a wit wief (white woman) runs around at night.
24575: Wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, ghostly lights) are forewarnings of new houses to be built.
24576: Wild lanterns are harbingers of houses yet to be built. Will-o'-the-wisps are also often seen before the houses are there. If they bob up and down hard, they are harbingers of the later bicycle lights. If they move calmly, the lights mean nothing.
24577: By a little bridge lies a stone with the print of a horseshoe in it. The print dates from the past: when a rough man, jumping over the canal, boasted that 'no devil could copy him', the devil promptly jumped over the canal. With his leap he left a print of his horse's hoof in the stone.
24580: A man deals roughly with a pack of troublesome, singing cats. He gives one of the cats a hard whack with a broomstick. The next morning the wife of a friend has her arm in a sling. She was the witch in the shape of a cat.
24586: If you promise someone something and do not keep your promise, that person keeps wandering after death. If you want to be rid of the restless dead, you must put a new frame in the door through which the body was carried out at the time. Sometimes the minister asks the dead person about their unfulfilled wish, for example a shroud. The shroud had to be thrown outside the door while calling 'here devil, have your garment'. You cannot hand over the garment yourself, for then you burn your hands, because the one who desires it is under the power of the devil.
24587: A very foul-mouthed carpenter is stopped on his way by something that tries to drive him off the path. Shortly afterwards he is suddenly lifted up and flung into the canal.
24588: Labourers working with the hay are startled by a young lady who suddenly rises out of the ground. When one of the labourers holds out a pitchfork to her, she disappears as suddenly as she appeared.
24591: Wild lanterns are harbingers of the later bicycle lights.
24595: In a barn the barn doors always spring open at night around midnight, without anything being seen. People suspect it is the wandering ghost of someone who once fell to his death through the loft hatch.
24596: A man urges a companion to step aside for a passing funeral procession with a hearse drawn by a white horse. It is an omen: a week later a dead person is taken to the churchyard. Because the black horse refused, a white horse was harnessed to the hearse.
24598: A sorcerer makes mice appear from the hearth pit. The mice, some seven or eight at a time, immediately start dancing. The sorcerer can also chase them back into their 'hole'.
24600: A dog howling eerily is an omen of an impending death.
24603: A cursing fisherman is roughly seized and shaken by the devil.
24605: A man born with a caul predicts the time of a farmer's death to the minute. He also foresees that the neighbour's horse will be harnessed to the hearse, because the farmer's own horses refuse.
24606: A labourer astonishes those around him by selling his favourite sheep. When people ask him why he sold the beloved animal, he answers that he has 'his reasons'. Two days later the sheep drowns. The labourer had foreseen the drowning.
24607: A man born with a caul predicts that the inn will burn down on market day. It turns out exactly that way.
24609: A man born with a caul predicts the moment of a farmer's death to the hour. The clairvoyant also foresees that two black horses will refuse to pull the hearse. In the end a piebald horse will be harnessed to it. It turns out exactly that way.
24610: A fisherman with a pact with the devil always pours an extra cup of coffee for the devil. When the devil then starts rocking his little boat back and forth, he becomes terrified and never pours coffee for the devil again. The fisherman is found dead with his head twisted around on his trunk: the devil's work.
24611: A woman and a maid hear footsteps and the sound of a key in the lock, although there is nothing to be seen. It is a voorloop (an apparition foreshadowing an event): later someone appears and the same sounds are heard.
24612: At a certain spot, the sound of carpentry can be heard at night. It is an omen: later a new house is built on that spot.
24613: Two children see a funeral. It is a premonition: shortly afterwards their mother dies.
24614: Someone used to see lights floating over the heath and hear rumbling. It was a portent: later the tram runs nearby.
24615: A farmhand warns his mates to leave, because a ship is coming across the water. It is a vision of the future: a year later the land floods.
24616: A man foresees that he will fall from the church tower when the church is built. The vision comes true.
24625: A fisherman often sees will-o'-the-wisps. They are harbingers: later new houses are built on that spot.
24626: A devil-banisher scratches his own head open and then claims to have fought with the devil.
24629: A coffee-ground reader predicts that a girl will find a packet of thread.
24630: Floating lights are harbingers of the later bicycle lights.
24631: Someone foresees a funeral in a passing funeral procession.
24633: People hear the sound of carpentry at night. It is an omen: later a house is built on that spot.
24634: A man foresees the death of his own wife in a passing funeral procession.
24637: Everything you get from a witch turns into a toad.
24638: When the tram was not there yet, people already heard the tram gliding over the rails and already saw its lights. They were omens.
24639: A devil banisher, who is also a sorcerer, can make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit and fix people to the ground. He also likes to bewitch pigs. He can also foretell when people will come to ask him for advice.
24642: A person born with a caul often has to get up at night to see funeral processions pass. If the caul of a person born with a caul is not burned at birth, that person has premonitions.
24644: If you keep an apple accepted from a witch, the fruit becomes a frog.
24648: At night a woman hears sounds as if posts and wood are being thrown down. It is an omen: later a shed is built for someone.
24650: The narrator knew people who declared they had seen a house on fire. It was an omen: later the house really burned down.
24654: At a haunted spot a foal with a porridge pot around its neck haunts the place.
24655: At a haunted place there is a house whose window always opens and closes by itself.
24659: A married couple hear the sound of carpentry at night, although there is nothing to be seen. It is an omen: later a new house is built on the same spot.
24660: A woman sees her little house on fire. It is a premonition: six months later the little house really does burn down.
24661: A man often goes poaching with his dog and a relative. After a night of poaching the man goes home; the relative looks for shelter elsewhere. As the man lies in bed, he hears knocking on the window. He recognises it as his relative's 'tap': long-short-short-short. Because his dog does not bark, the man concludes that no one can be at the house. The same scene repeats itself. Six weeks later there is knocking again one morning. This time the relative has really come home. The tapping in the night was an omen.
24662: A man born with a caul often foresees funerals, down to the smallest details. He also predicted the funeral of his own daughter.
24666: To keep a nightmare away you must scatter flour on your chest. Of seven daughters, one is a nightmare. The narrator was once bothered by a nightmare: she crept on top of him from the foot of the bed. Nightmares also like to braid horses' manes.
24667: At night a boy sees in the corner of the room a 'small wooden box with a black cloth over it'. It is a vision of the future: the following year the family loses a daughter. Her little coffin is placed in the same spot in the corner.
24668: A woman sees little lights floating through the air. It is a harbinger of the later bicycle lights.
24669: A man hears a number of magpies chattering. It is an omen of an approaching death.
24670: A mother and son are driven out of bed at night to foresee deaths in passing funeral processions.
24671: A man sees a house on fire. It is a premonition: later it really does burn down.
24673: A man is driven to the side of the road at night by a passing funeral procession.
24674: Warning: never walk in the middle of the road at night.
24675: A poor woman who is still working even at night is startled by the ghost of her late aunt. The aunt comes to bring her poor niece money for a little cap she never paid for. The poor woman tells God that she wants to give the money to her aunt, if He grants her rest. The aunt's ghost never haunted again.
24676: To keep a nightmare away you must hang herbs in front of your bed, put your clogs upside down in front of the door or scatter flour on your blankets and your face. The nightmare can get through anything and sits on your chest.
24677: A miser finds a whole row of rijksdaalders on the road. He does not dare pick them up, because he is sure it is the devil's work.
24678: A man on his way home from his girlfriend is startled by a cat. Because the cat keeps annoyingly following him, he strikes at it with a stick. To his bewilderment the stick passes right through the animal: it is a ghost animal.
24679: A man hears sounds coming from the small lake. He suspects that something is about to happen.
24680: At a haunted spot a foal runs about with a porridge pot around its neck: a ghost animal.
24682: One of seven boys or seven girls is clairvoyant.
24685: A barn where a girl once hanged herself is haunted.
24686: Braggarts and cursers are sometimes seized by the devil and thrown down.
24687: A card reader predicts to a girl who already has a few children born out of wedlock that she will soon give birth again. It happens exactly so.
24692: A sorcerer makes a bottle of liquor come with a jack of spades.
24693: A sorcerer makes little soldiers appear from the hearth pit.
24694: Of seven daughters born in succession, one is a nightmare or witch. A nightmare often enters the house through the keyhole. A woman who is often tormented by nightmares puts her shoes or clogs back to front, because the nightmare follows people's footsteps.
24695: A haunted spot by a small holly grove is haunted. A large dog is sometimes seen by the grove as well. When the grove is later cut down, the haunting stops.
24696: A man suddenly sees a funeral procession. It is a premonition of an approaching death.
24697: A poacher coming home at night sees a number of cats sitting by his door. He tries to shoot the cats. When his mortally ill wife dies, the nightly visits by the cats suddenly stop. When his second wife is expecting, he suddenly sees a funeral procession. He is very afraid his wife will die in childbed, but this fate befalls another woman.
24698: Before the war broke out, a man had already seen troops of people: a vision of the future. The same man also often went door to door with strange wares. He also often went door to door singing New Year's songs.
24702: Exorcist Minse Griper can make people stuck in their place. He also sometimes makes a bottle of liquor come with a jack of spades. He may not take the bottle himself when it comes floating in, filled. The first two glasses are thrown over the left shoulder.
24704: The exorcist Jehannes Hinses (according to Jaarsma it should be Hinse Johannes - VW) suspects that the cattle of a farmer, a widower, are bewitched. When Jehannes visits the farm, he starts cursing in the stable. A little later the horses pull an enormously heavy load, which they cannot see, out of the stable on the wagon. Jehannes shouts 'Get off, Satan!' and throws the wagonload into the water. Later it turns out that the dead farmer's wife is tormenting the animals with evil spirits to punish the farmer.
24705: At a certain spot will-o'-the-wisps can be seen. They are harbingers of the later car and bicycle lights.
24707: A group of children often see will-o'-the-wisps in the dark. It is a harbinger of the later bicycle lights.
24708: A trader out late comes upon some twenty dark cats by moonlight. When he tries to open the door of a shed, four or so cats leap at his arms. When he gets home, he finds his wife with a wailing child. The man immediately goes outside and shoots one of the cats, which keeps sitting there staring at him boldly. The next day his neighbour tells him she spent the whole night tending to her own old neighbour, who was bleeding because she had supposedly fallen out of bed. The man knows enough: the old neighbour was the witch in the shape of a cat. The old woman does indeed turn out to have shot in her chest. In the shape of a cat she had tried to bewitch the child. The child recovers; the witch died of her wounds.
24724: Minse Griper sits in the loft and fights with the devil.
24810: Warning: never walk in the middle of the road, because of passing funeral processions.
24812: Two poachers see a strange, glowing thing moving up and down by the bank: a ghostly thing.
24813: A girl predicts that an accident is going to happen. That same evening she breaks her arm.
24814: A labourer predicts that an accident is going to happen. That same day he himself has an accident and dies.
24815: A man born with a caul often has to get up at night to see funeral processions pass.
24822: A witch flies through the air on a bundle of straw. When Dreyfuss was on Devil's Island with the lepers, a witch came to him in a hollow tree.
24826: Card reader Kjille predicts to two men that one of them will never amount to anything. The other will go quite far, according to Kjille. It happens exactly so.
24829: Freemasons have a pact with the devil, signed in their own blood. If you want to join the freemasons, you must sign in blood. If you want to leave the freemasons, you pay for it with death. You can escape death if you did not sign the pact with your own blood but, for example, with the blood of a goat. Once you have signed, you must leave the building walking backwards. Freemasons are never short of money: they receive money from the devil. If they hang an empty purse on the door handle in the evening, the devil has filled it with money by the next morning. Freemasons keep doing odd jobs on their houses forever.
24830: Stammerige Harm owns a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) and so never lacks money.
24838: At a haunted place, a gate springs open by itself at night: a ghost gate.
24840: In the old days people often heard death knocking. If there were three knocks, death came to fetch you.
24841: Witches can change themselves into cats and then hold cat meetings. A man once heard such a cat meeting singing psalms. He starts shooting at the witch-cats with his gun. The man hits one of the cats. The next day his neighbour woman is lame: she was the cat that was shot.
24844: With people who have fallen prey to the devil, a print of a goat's or horse's hoof is often found under the coffin.
24845: A woman has a sick daughter. One time in her house she suddenly has to turn around. Something catches her attention, but she cannot see what it is. The next day a stretcher is carried into her house because her sick daughter has to be taken to hospital. That is what the woman saw the day before.
24846: A woman asks what 'those three calves' are doing in the stable. The stable, however, is empty. It is a vision of the future: the next day there are three calves in the stable.
24847: A woman hears the sound of carpentry. It is an omen: later the house is renovated.
24848: A woman predicts that a mortally ill man will not die. Everyone declares her mad, but the woman is proved right: the man is still alive.
24849: A woman always hears the bells ringing when a death is approaching.
24856: At a haunted spot a foal runs about with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a ghost animal.
24862: A sorcerer makes little soldiers appear from the hearth pit.
24864: Wild lanterns are often seen at a certain spot. It is a harbinger: later new houses are built there.
24865: Two men see a tram running, while there is no tramline yet, or even a road. It is a vision of the future. Later roads are built. The men suspect that what they saw back then were buses. Those have yet to start running.
24866: A man sees some stacks of peat on fire. The next day the peat stacks are still there. It is a premonition: a while later the peat really burns.
24867: At a certain spot the sound of carpentry can often be heard. It is an omen: later a new house is built on that spot.
24870: A baker keeps taking on journeymen who soon die. A new journeyman is promptly approached by four witch-cats. The cats discuss whether to throw him into the sourdough vat, but decide to wait until 'Miss De Bonte' arrives. The journeyman has heard everything and stabs Miss De Bonte - also a cat. The next day the baker's wife lies in bed with a sore, injured foot. The baker's wife was the witch-cat: she had thrown all the previous journeymen into the sourdough vat.
24874: A man is shown a coffin in the black mirror. He never dared to marry afterwards.
24880: A young couple is strolling about, discussing when to get married. A cat keeps following on their heels. The next day everyone knows the couple intends to marry: the cat, a witch, has spread the news.
24881: A woman likes to bewitch pigs. The bewitched pigs refuse to eat. A man with sick - bewitched - pigs once sees a rat by the pig trough. He gives the rat a hard whack. The next day a woman lies in bed with a cloth around her head. She was the witch in the shape of a rat.
24882: At a certain spot wild lanterns often float about. It is an omen: later a house is built on that spot.
24883: A girl is warned about a witch: if she gets an apple from her, she must throw away the core.
24884: A clairvoyant often has to get up at night to foresee deaths in passing funeral processions.
24895: A man born with a caul often has to get up at night to see funeral processions pass.
24899: Someone sees a little ship sailing and predicts that a canal will be dug. The vision has not yet come true.
24900: At a haunted spot, a gate always swings open by itself at night.
24901: A man says he once came face to face with a fat cat. The cat, running on its hind legs, was as big as a sizeable dog. The cat struck the man with its tail. It was a ghost animal.
24902: A boy is thrown into the ditch by an invisible force.
24903: A log path is haunted. A big fellow with eyes as big as teacups was once seen there. Several ghost animals also roam the haunted spot: a pig that does not grunt, a dog with a porridge pot around its neck, and a fat, dark dog that keeps following at people's heels.
24905: In the evening a man hears the sound of carpentry, although there is nothing to be seen. It is an omen: later new houses are built on that spot.
24907: A man worriedly tells a colleague that he has seen the colleague's house on fire. It is a premonition: later the house really does burn down.
24908: Once a child's screaming was heard at a small lake. People suspect that a child will drown.
24909: Cries for help can be heard at a pond. It is an omen: later the same sounds are heard when people fall through the ice. The people are rescued.
