24910: On a moonlit night a man sees a creature resembling a black foal lying on a heap of earth. When the man looks away for a moment, the animal has suddenly vanished. By daylight there are no tracks to be seen. The neighbour has also seen the animal running. It is a ghost animal.
24911: A boy sees horseshoe prints in the sand. It is a vision of the future: only later will his father buy a horse.
24912: A woman married to a bicycle repairman is treated very badly by her husband. One night someone strikes the anvil in the workshop hard with a hammer. It turns out to be the girl's dead father: he wants to make clear to his son-in-law that he must stop hurting his daughter. The son-in-law flees, scared to death.
24913: At night a man sometimes hears the key turning in the cabinet. It is an omen of something that is about to happen the next day.
24914: A skipper's daughter hears cries for help. She suspects someone has fallen through the ice, but there is nothing to be seen. It is an omen: a few days later someone drowns.
24915: When rooks sit on the roofs two days in a row, a death is coming.
24916: When the dog howls eerily, a death is coming.
24930: A woman nursing a skipper's wife who has just given birth points out a strange cat to the skipper. The skipper gives the cat a whack. The next day an old woman - already suspected of witchcraft - lies in bed with a cloth around her head. She was the witch in the shape of a cat.
24934: A group of noisy, scoffing card players is startled by a small, soot-black little fellow with a pipe. The little house where they are playing turns black with smoke. The card players become so frightened that they put down their cards. The little man disappears again. The deck of cards is burned and they never play again.
24935: An old man has a pact with the devil. A boy who often visits the old man often sees the room door swing open in the old man's house, although nobody comes in. The old man sets an extra chair at the table and seems to communicate with the invisible guest. When the door later swings open and shut again, the old man puts the chair back in its place.
24936: The narrator knew a man with a pact with the devil. At the man's house he often saw the door open and close. It often seemed as if the man was quarrelling with his 'invisible guest'. Afterwards the man, still talking, would often stir a pot of mixed peas and beans.
24937: A strange old fellow has a pact with the devil. The old man has an enormous garden with spruces in it. When the spruces have to be hauled away, he finds a neighbour willing to help. When the neighbour backs out at the last moment, the old man cries angrily 'that the devil will do it then'. In the dead of night the devil does the whole job for the man.
24941: A certain hare, supposedly a witch, cannot be hit. Several people have shot at the animal.
24942: A man promises his wife not to remarry after her death. He breaks the promise and marries again. When he returns from the town hall with his new bride, his first, dead wife is also waiting in the bridal carriage. His first wife keeps tormenting him constantly. The man becomes so distraught that he hangs himself.
24943: The ghost of a dead person keeps wandering if the dead has not been given what was promised to him.
24944: You must never walk in the middle of the road at night, because a funeral procession may pass. A man was once driven into the ditch by a funeral procession.
24946: A woman born with a caul foresees funerals.
24947: A midwife sometimes warns of passing funeral processions.
25045: Witches fly through the air on a broomstick.
25059: In a certain barn there is a hole that cannot be closed. The hole always opens again by itself.
25060: By a stretch of water there is the print of a human foot on one side and the print of a horse's hoof on the other. The devil, evil, jumped over the water there.
25061: The gate of a castle is always open in the morning, even though they carefully lock it the evening before. It is a haunted gate.
25063: A certain place in Leeuwarden is built on cow hides.
25066: A man born with a caul warns a comrade that a funeral procession will soon pass. He already knows the name of the deceased as well. The comrade ignores the warnings and stays standing in the middle of the road. He is promptly seized by the procession and thrown off the road.
25068: Parents warn their children never to accept an apple from an old crone. The old crone might be a witch; the apple might turn into a toad.
25069: Witches travel through the air on a broomstick.
25070: A sorcerer makes a bottle of liquor come with the help of a jack of spades.
25073: A man short of money makes a pact with the devil. When the man hangs his hat on the door, the devil will fill it with money. The man outwits the devil by removing the top of the hat. The devil's contract no longer holds, because the devil had agreed to fill the hat. But the hat never gets full. The man is free and may keep the money, a wheelbarrow full.
25078: At night two boys suddenly hear all the bells of the surrounding villages ringing. It is an omen: when the First World War breaks out in 1914, all the bells ring.
25081: A man who is ploughing suddenly sees a witte juffer (white lady) on a white horse approaching. As suddenly as the woman and the horse appeared, they vanish again. The man hurries home, scared to death.
25083: A father warns his children never to walk in the middle of the road at night. After all, they might run into a funeral procession.
25085: In the old days people already foresaw that there would be carriages without horses and ships without sails. The premonitions have come true.
25087: A horse rages terribly at night because it is tormented by a nightmare. She braids the animal's mane. People suffer from nightmares too. To keep nightmares away you must put paper in the keyhole, put your slippers upside down in front of the bed and tuck asafoetida under the threshold. Nightmares can fly and often come over the water.
25088: Card reader Hinke Kaart often makes predictions about the future that come true.
25090: A man born with a caul often has to get up at night to see funeral processions pass.
25094: A scoffer boasts that he is not afraid of the devil. On the way home the sinner is promptly seized by the devil and thrown to the other side of the dike. The scoffer gets a scoffer's reward.
25107: Wild lanterns are harbingers of the later bicycle lights.
25111: People keep watch over a mortally ill woman. Suddenly at night sounds are heard in the outbuilding, as if something is falling. However, nothing can be seen in the outbuilding. When the woman dies shortly afterwards, the carpenter makes a coffin. When another woman trips over the coffin, the same sound is heard as during the earlier vigil. It was a voorloop (an apparition foreshadowing an event).
25114: A man hears cries for help and sees wailing women wearing white caps. They are omens: later someone drowns.
25116: At a haunted spot a foal runs about with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a ghost animal.
25117: A witch can change herself into a cat. A man shoots into a group of cats and hits one. The next day a woman - with a cloth around her head - has to stay in bed. The woman later dies of her wounds. She was the witch who was shot in the shape of a cat.
25118: Witches often hold meetings in the shape of cats.
25119: Omens of a death: a dog howling eerily, a barn owl calling and spiders ticking against the wallpaper - the so-called 'wilde horloges' (wild clocks). A falling mirror also points to something bad about to happen. Chattering magpies in the yard announce a letter of mourning.
25121: A poor, dying woman instructs her husband to make socks for their two daughters from leftover yarn. Because the promise goes unfulfilled - socks are made for someone else - the mother's ghost keeps haunting. When the minister asks the mother about her unfulfilled wish, she says the yarn was used wrongly. The mother is promised that her daughters will still get socks. The woman's ghost then finds rest.
25122: Two naked little children wander about a haunted spot. Because the children were buried without shrouds back then, they cannot find rest.
25123: The sound of threshing can sometimes be heard in a barn at night. It is an omen: the next day there really is threshing.
25124: A boy breaks off his courtship with his girl because she is a witch. As punishment the witch fixes him in place on the road, to force him to return to her. When the boy walks back - after all, he can no longer go forward - the witch makes him promise that he will come back to her. The boy promises and the witch lets him go. The boy does not keep his promise and quickly runs off.
25125: Wild lanterns indicate that a new house will be built.
25126: As punishment, a voyeur is roughly seized and flung away by the devil.
25128: If someone walks in the middle of the road, it may happen that he is seized by an invisible funeral procession and flung over the hearse.
25130: A man foresees the funeral of an acquaintance down to the smallest details. The premonition comes true: a few days later the acquaintance dies.
25131: A man foresees the death of his own little son. He urges his mother to step aside for the coffin being carried through the hallway. The vision comes true.
25132: A man often sees funeral processions pass during the day. They are premonitions.
25134: An apple received from a witch should not be eaten but put away. A few days later there is a big caterpillar in the cupboard and the apple has disappeared. If you drink coffee at a witch's house, you die.
25136: A witch travels through the air on a broomstick.
25138: It sometimes happens that the sounds of churning are heard at night without the horse running at the churn. It is a harbinger of what is about to happen the next day.
25139: A man hears sounds at night, although there is nothing to be seen. A few days later a lot of little posts suddenly appear. The night-time sounds were a harbinger.
25141: In a barracks a bottle of liquor is fetched with the help of a jack of spades. The one who sent the bottle away may not take hold of it. When a certain soldier takes the bottle, it bursts.
25142: A card reader makes all kinds of predictions. She predicts to two young women that they will each get a new bicycle. The two women each have a child.
25145: A man with a pact with the devil is short of money. He agrees with the devil to hang a basket from the collar beam. The devil will fill the basket with rijksdaalders (silver coins). The man outwits the devil by removing the bottom of the basket. The devil cannot keep his promise because the basket never fills up. The man is now not only freed from the pact but also rich.
25152: A strange man sees little soldiers appear from the hearth pit.
25153: A sorcerer makes a bottle of liquor come with the help of a jack of spades.
25158: A witch travels at lightning speed by broomstick to do some shopping.
25159: An impatient boy often calls on the devil, cursing, when his work goes badly. As punishment, the sinner is lifted from his bed several times at night by a small and a large fellow. The large fellow always intends to drown the boy; the small fellow manages to stop his comrade. After the fellows have wandered about by the water with the boy for a while, they bring him back.
25160: From a floating lantern, a man predicts the building of a house.
25161: At the spot where the devil once jumped over the canal, a footprint can still be seen in a stone.
25162: A man suddenly notices that the devil is walking along with him. He recognises the devil by his horse's hoof. The devil confirms that he is the devil and says he will do the man no harm. The man may be a curser, but he is 'sound inside', according to the devil. The devil needs someone who is rotten inside as well.
25163: A man walking home from his girlfriend's by moonlight suddenly hears footsteps. The footsteps keep pace with his own. When he stops, he sees a headless man flying across the road. The man flies straight through a beech hedge. A while later an old man is murdered at that haunted spot.
25165: A boy points out a floating figure to his girl. The girl's dead mother turns out to still be wandering because the father did not keep a promise. The minister asks the mother about her unfulfilled wish. When the father finally fulfils his obligation, the mother finds rest.
25166: At night a family suddenly hears a loud bang in the little hallway, though there is nothing to be seen. It is an omen: when the father of the house dies, the hallway has to be hacked away because the coffin cannot get through. If the noises are heard before midnight, the death will not be long in coming. If they are heard after midnight, it points to a death further in the future.
25167: A woman and her little nephew see a funeral procession approaching. Shortly afterwards they are both flung into the ditch. It is a premonition: later a girl dies.
25168: People born with a caul are bulletproof. Doctors are very keen on the cauls.
25169: People have had a premonitory vision of two people drowning. The vision has not yet come true.
25170: A married couple is often tormented by a nightmare. The man tries in vain to keep the nightmare away by sleeping on the floor with the light on. Bread in front of the bed or elder shoots on the bed board help, because bread and elder are holy. A woman once fought with a nightmare. The nightmare has very small hands.
25171: The youngest or eldest of seven boys born in succession is a nightmare. The narrator's sister once courted a nightmare. When the sister married someone else, her ex-lover, the nightmare, often bothered her at night. The woman uses elder branches and rye to keep the nightmare away.
25172: The witch Frânse Hinke often bewitches pigs by stroking their bodies. The owner of the pigs places elder wood in front of the threshold and asafoetida (devil's dung) under the threshold to keep the witch out.
25173: A group of boys learns from a witch how to bewitch small children.
25175: A nightmare from England, a little woman, enters a man's house through the keyhole. Because the man has thrown flour over the blankets, the nightmare can no longer get away. The man catches the nightmare and stuffs up the keyhole so that she cannot escape, for the nightmare can only leave through the hole she came in by. The nightmare is not allowed to open a closed hole. The man marries the nightmare and has children with her. One day the nightmare urges her children, now grown bigger, to listen to 'how beautifully the bells are ringing in England'. She asks her children to open the keyhole and disappears.
25177: A woman, wife of a werewolf, is suddenly bitten in her red woollen skirt. As a werewolf, her husband regularly has to bite into something. Red yarn shows in his molars. Werewolves especially like to sink their teeth into red wool.
25179: Near the churchyard a man comes across a couple wearing rain clothes. When his greeting goes unanswered three times, he suspects he is dealing with ghosts.
25180: In a haunted house a woman is suddenly startled by a wandering dead person. When the minister addresses the dead person - a woman - it turns out she finds no rest because a promise made to her during her life was not fulfilled. When the obligation is finally met, the woman finds rest.
25181: A boy who is courting a witch suddenly sees the life drain out of his sweetheart in the middle of the night. The girl sits there like a lifeless bundle of rags. She sits in the chair as if dead, because at the same time she is out bewitching in the shape of a cat. The young man feels very uneasy and does not know whether he will keep visiting her. The girl makes him promise to come back, threatening to fix him to the spot in the yard. Reluctantly the boy agrees. But he never went back.
25189: A man rents, for a trifling sum, a haunted house that nobody dares to live in. All kinds of eerie things happen in and around the house: cattle rattle their chains; cows are found loose in the stable in the morning; a door springs open by itself. A widow who lived near the house was once caught in a thunderstorm while bringing in hay with her three daughters. One of the daughters was struck dead by an enormous ball of fire. The man sometimes sees the dead daughter wandering near the house. He suspects the door is always open because the soul of the dead girl roams about.
25191: At night a poacher hears a quarrelling couple approaching. The woman reproaches the man for having sold a piece of land. The two troublemakers turn out to be people who died long ago.
25194: A desperate farmer offers his soul to the devil in exchange for a bootful of money. The devil agrees, but declares he will 'grab' the farmer at once as soon as he has filled the boot. The crafty farmer cuts the sole off the boot so that the devil cannot fill it. The farmer escapes the pact and is left with a large amount of money.
25196: Stammerige Harm owns a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin).
25200: A scoffer boasts that 'not even the devil' can match him in jumping over the canal. At once the devil appears: he nimbly jumps over the water. On one side of the water there is the print of a human foot; on the other side the print of a horse's hoof.
25201: A reckless boy mocks the devil while competing with a group of friends to see who can jump the farthest into the water. The boy does not come back up. His dead body is found a little later. The boy has drowned. The devil punished him for his recklessness.
25202: On a piece of land a fellow on a white horse is sometimes seen. As suddenly as the rider appeared, he vanishes again. He is a ghost rider on a ghost horse. A castle used to stand at that spot. The ghost rider is the former lord of the castle. Later the rider is banished by exorcists to another piece of land. The narrator once saw the lord too: a reddish fellow with a pockmarked skin.
25203: A ticking sound can be heard in an oak stump. A young farmhand raking by the tree is suddenly lifted up and flung away, though no one can be seen.
25211: A man sees a dead little child lying on a chair. It is a premonitory vision: a few days later a little child dies.
25212: A sick woman turns out to be bewitched. The woman's brother hits a suspicious cat with tongs. The day after, an old woman - a suspected witch - has her arm in a sling. She was the witch in the shape of a cat.
25214: An exorcist ties a jack of spades to an empty bottle and puts the bottle outside the door. Shortly afterwards a hand appears around the corner of the door holding a full bottle of jenever. Everyone is terrified to take the bottle. The exorcist may not take the bottle himself.
25215: At a haunted spot a dog runs about with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a ghost animal.
25216: A tough fellow is driven out of bed at night and hunted by the devil. Only when an old woman intervenes does the man get peace again.
25218: A man has to step aside for a funeral procession. It is a premonition: a few days later someone dies.
25219: A card reader keeps drawing a card showing a little black man with a yellow note and suspects it means something. It is an omen: the following Monday a little black man appears with a telegram, a 'yellow note'. The card reader's father turns out to have died.
25220: At a certain spot a man often hears hammering and carpentry, although there is nothing to be seen. It is an omen: later a new bridge-keeper's house is built on that spot and the same sounds are heard.
25221: In burning lights, a man foresees the coming of the tram. The vision comes true.
25222: A farmer's maid hears the sound of the churn, although there is nothing to be seen. It is an omen.
25223: A woman repeatedly sees a scantily dressed man walking to the water. It is a premonitory vision: shortly afterwards an alcoholic drowns himself. The alcoholic is dressed only in his underclothes.
25225: A witch can change herself into a cat, but also into all sorts of other things. A man once saw a suspicious pile of peat and shot at it. The next day an old woman - a suspected witch - has a wound in her neck. The day before she had changed herself into a pile of peat.
25229: A devil banisher can make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit.
25230: With the help of a jack of spades you can make a bottle of liquor come. You must take hold of the bottle backwards.
25233: Pub-goers who have spoken mockingly are seized by the devil and thrown down.
25234: The narrator tells of two men who often saw funeral processions. You must never walk in the middle of the road, because an invisible funeral procession can drive you off the road.
25235: In a mirror tent men and women can see their future spouse in the black mirror. If they remain unmarried, they see a coffin.
25236: A man coming out of the pub is annoyingly followed by a cat. The man calls the animal 'devil' and shouts irritably that he will 'settle accounts' with it. The scoffer is promptly thrown over the ditch by the cat. The cat was the devil himself.
25241: If you want a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin), you must put a pitch-black cat in a sack. At night you must walk around the churchyard three times, calling 'who will give a daalder for this black cat?'. Then the devil appears: he gives a wisseldaalder in exchange for the cat. The wisseldaalder can never run out.
25246: If you want to conjure up a bottle of liquor with a jack of clubs, you must first agree who will take the bottle. The one who handed the bottle with the card to the invisible hand outside the door may not take the bottle when it comes floating back, filled. If the one who promised to take the bottle fails to do so, the one who sent the bottle away dies.
25247: A farmer short of money is approached by a splendidly dressed man. The man, the devil, asks how much money he would like. The farmer says he wants a bootful. At twelve o'clock at night the devil comes to fill the boot. The farmer escapes the pact because he has cut the sole off the boot. The devil does not manage to fill it.
25254: A farmhand sees someone in the orchard and greets them. His greeting goes unanswered twice. Suddenly he sees someone, a giant of a fellow, on the cycle path. When the farmhand looks away for a moment, the giant has vanished again. The trees begin to creak ominously.
25255: A group of friends see a house on fire from a distance. When they go to look, however, there is nothing to be seen. It is a premonition: shortly afterwards the house really does burn down.
25256: At a haunted spot a foal runs about with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a ghost animal.
25257: At a haunted spot a fat dog haunts the place. It is a ghost animal.
25259: Wilde lantaarnen (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) were omens of the bicycle and car lights that came later.
25261: A man, born with a caul, urges a companion to step aside for an approaching funeral procession. The companion ignores his warnings and keeps walking on the road. Promptly he is lifted up by a hearse.
25262: A boy sends away a playing card for a bottle of liquor. When a full bottle of liquor and the card float into the room a little later, nobody dares to take the bottle. The boy who sent the card away urges the others to take the bottle, because otherwise things will go badly for him. When the boy does indeed turn blue, one of the others overcomes his fear and takes the bottle.
25263: The sorcerer Imke de Jong frightens women out of their wits by conjuring little soldiers from the hearth pit with a little stick.
25265: During his military service the mischievous wizard Imke de Jong repeatedly frees himself effortlessly when he is locked up. Imke then fixes the jailer and the captain to the ground.
25266: In a black mirror you can see the woman you will marry later.
25267: A fortune teller reads a man's palm and predicts that he will not marry his current sweetheart and will receive a large sum of money from an inheritance. The predictions come true.
25271: A woman predicts a drowning from a voice coming out of the water. The prediction has not yet come true.
25272: A man hears the sound of hammering although there is nothing to be seen. It is an omen: later a new house is built on that spot.
25273: A man gives a strange cat that keeps prowling around him a firm blow with a stick. The next day a woman has her arm in a sling. She was the witch in the shape of a cat.
25274: A witch travels through the air on a broomstick.
25275: Two poachers see a strange animal at night when they look over the left shoulder of one of them. The animal looks somewhat like a horse in the shape of a sheep and is covered with rijksdaalders (silver coins). When the two men strike at the beast, it lifts its legs and flies up into the air.
25285: A man foresees that a hearse will have to take a detour because the road is flooded. The premonition comes true.
25287: A scoffer boasts that he wants to meet the devil on the ladder to his attic room. He is promptly thrown off the ladder three times. Since that event the scoffer has been converted. He never challenged the devil again.
25288: One of seven daughters born in succession is a nightmare. A man is once visited by a nightmare that climbs onto him from the foot of the bed. The man can barely breathe and breaks out in a cold sweat. A friend advises the man to put his clogs upside down to keep the nightmare away.
25297: A witch can change herself into a white cat. Once, when the narrator's brother comes back from poaching, he sees a white cat sitting by the water. He urges his dog to catch the cat, but the dog does not dare. The poacher then shoots at the white cat. A few days later an old woman is lame: she was the witch in the shape of a cat.
25298: A sick child turns out to be bewitched. The child's father suspects an old woman of having bewitched his child and hurries to her house. Through the window the father sees the old woman working on a little doll with needles. The father throws a large stone through the window. The child recovers.
25302: A person born with a caul is one from a family with an odd number of boys. Those who see funeral processions are werewolves.
25304: A cattle dealer in hard times is approached by the devil. The devil promises the dealer a lot of money if he does exactly what the devil says. The dealer agrees. The devil warns the dealer that his clothes will always hang loosely about his body. It turns out exactly so: the dealer becomes rich but goes about looking scruffy.
25305: A sinful hunchback tells a doctor he wants to keep his hump, because it protects his back against blows. In reality the sinner once accepted a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) from the devil in exchange for the hump. The hump now belongs to the devil. If he loses the hump, he also loses the wisseldaalder.
25309: A man born with a caul often has to get up at night to see things.
25310: A farm wagon is driven off the road. The horse seems to sense something. It was a funeral procession.
25311: A witch is also a trader in goods. The witch sometimes floats.
25312: A boy gets a fish from a witch. He does not eat the fish. A few days later the fish is all swollen up.
25314: The wizard Imke de Jong can fix people to the spot and make them scream. Imke also sometimes makes someone's clothes fall off their body.
25315: During his military service the mischievous Ymke de Jong is often thrown in jail. Ymke can always free himself effortlessly by making the doors spring open. Shortly afterwards Ymke de Jong is seen in four places at once.
25316: You can get a bottle of liquor for free by swearing and sending away a playing card. When the full bottle floats above the table, the one who sent the card away may not take hold of it.
25317: If you want a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin), you must run around the churchyard three times with a black cat in a sack, calling 'Who will buy my cat for a daalder?'. The devil then gives you a wisseldaalder.
25319: A man on his way home from his girlfriend comes upon a small black dog. The man hurries back to his girlfriend.
25320: A brave man agrees to close the haunted gate of Hardegarijp. When he reaches the gate, he does not dare after all. However well it is tied shut, the gate always swings open at midnight.
25321: At a haunted spot, a horse's head haunts.
25323: On a summer night a man hears banging coming from the shed three times. When he goes to look, however, there is nothing to be seen. Half a year later the man gets a horse. He builds a stable for it in the shed. A year after that he hears the same sounds coming from the shed that he heard before. It turns out to be the horse stamping its legs on the stones. The earlier banging was an omen.
25324: A man intends to build a hay barn. Shortly afterwards the sounds of sawing and hammering are heard three times at night, although there is nothing to be seen. In the nights that follow, working sounds can be heard as well. It is an omen: when the hay barn is actually built, the same sounds are heard.
25325: At a farmer's place the barn doors always swing open at midnight. It is a haunted spot.
25327: A man who likes telling ghost stories claims that a fat dog once approached him. The dog supposedly turned first into a lion and then into a gentleman. The man walks a little way with the gentleman. When the man reaches his house, the gentleman continues on his way.
25332: The sound of hammering is often heard at a certain place. It is an omen: later there is renovation or new building on that spot.
25334: At a haunted spot a gate will not close: a haunted gate.
25335: When a barn owl sits on the roof, a death is coming. It is an omen.
25336: When the dog howls eerily, a death is coming. It is an omen.
25337: Before his death, a farmer marked with a small post where he wanted to be buried in the churchyard. When his heirs fail to bury him in that spot, the farmer's ghost keeps wandering. When the farmer is finally buried by the post, the haunting ends.
25339: One night a man suddenly sees two white women. The two women sit down on his cart. The man becomes so frightened that he quickly runs off.
25340: A married couple is suddenly startled by a fat black dog. The animal, which floats, keeps following at the couple's heels. Suddenly the animal vanishes again. It is a ghost animal.
25341: A scoffing drunkard is seized by the devil: the next day the sinner is found with his neck twisted around.
25344: A bicycle repairman, who is also a sorcerer, can make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit.
25350: The caul of a newborn is burned or pocketed by greedy doctors. The caul of a person born with a caul is worth a lot of money. People born with a caul have premonitions and often have to get up at night to see, for example, funeral processions.
25351: A scoffer is seized by the devil and thrown down.
25352: A carpenter, an exceptionally wicked man, thinks he will take a quick way home but comes upon an apparition at a wooden footbridge. Cursing, he threatens to beat the figure to death if it does not step aside. The carpenter is seized and roughly thrown back and forth twice. At that same spot people were often lifted up and thrown away.
25356: A man nicknamed 'Cent' sits by the waterside counting his money. When his father expresses his amazement at the enormous amount of money his son has, the son claims that the father can become just as rich. The father only has to run around the churchyard three times with a black cat. Then he will get money from the devil - a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) - according to the son.
25357: Pub-goers sometimes make a bottle of liquor come with the help of a playing card. The full bottle floats above the table.
25358: The wizard Imke de Jong can fix people to the spot.
25359: The wizard Imke de Jong never stays in prison long: Imke magics the closed doors open.
25360: A man becomes completely distraught when he is driven off the road by a funeral procession. He has to be escorted home and never dares to show himself at that spot again.
25361: When a dog howls eerily, a death is coming.
25362: It sometimes happens that a dead person cannot find rest because a promise made to him was not kept. If the minister addresses the dead about his unfulfilled wish and that wish is then fulfilled, the dead finds rest. If something still has to be handed to the dead, you must roll it up in a handkerchief and hold the corner of the handkerchief. If you do not do it this way, your skin will be scorched off.
25364: A person born with a caul whose caul was removed the wrong way at birth often has premonitions. Usually such people see funeral processions. The narrator knew someone who was often driven out of his house to see things.
25365: At night invisible funeral processions sometimes pass. A farmhand was once flung across the ditch by such an invisible funeral procession.
25367: If you get an apple from a witch and keep it, the fruit turns into a toad.
25369: A witch travels through the air on a broom.
25370: The witch Welmoed works on children's dolls with a red-hot awl.
25372: When a witch turns into a hare or another animal, the witch-animal can only be hit with a silver bullet.
25382: At a fair a man seems to crawl through a beam. When a spectator hits the man with a stick, it turns out that the man is deceiving them. He does not crawl through the beam, but past it.
25393: Freemasons sell their souls to the devil. They often hang up a boot without a sole. The devil throws money into the boot. Freemasons also own a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back). They get the wisseldaalder by running around the church three times with a black cat. The devil then gives them a rijksdaalder. Once you are a Freemason, you are a Freemason for life.
25395: A certain man was born with a caul.
25396: One evening a few people see wilde lantaarnen (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) floating. The will-o'-the-wisps stop at three spots. They are omens: houses and a school are later built on those three spots.
25399: Someone hides a great deal of money in the churchyard, saying 'devil, keep watch over my money, so that no one will take it away'.
25403: A sorcerer sometimes bewitches the churn so that it will not make butter.
25405: At a haunted spot a foal roams about with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a ghost animal.
25406: A witch can change herself into a cat. A man married to a witch's daughter once sees a strange cat drilling around him like a soldier. The man suspects the strange animal is a witch and gives the cat a tremendous whack. The next day his mother-in-law wears a cloth over her eye because she has lost an eye. She was the witch in the shape of a cat.
25407: A woman's husband was bewitched to death by the well-known witch Rikele Myt. Once, when she watched Myt through the window of her house, she saw all sorts of little soldiers marching on the table. When the woman tries to steal some apples from the witch, Myt makes sure the woman is fixed in place. Only when she throws the apples away can she get across the water.
25408: Four times in a row a poacher fails to shoot a hare from very close by. It turns out to be a witch-animal. Such a witch-animal cannot be killed.
25409: A poacher tells that a witch would sometimes change into a fat black starling. In that shape she went out to work magic.
25411: An irreverent scoffer boasts that he is not afraid of the devil. At once the man is seized and thrown some distance away.
25413: A scoffer boasts that he is not afraid to go to a certain haunted spot. At the haunted spot he meets a fellow. The fellow grabs him and throws him into the ditch three times. The scoffer suspects that the devil seized him.
25414: A man once had an encounter. He was roughly thrown about by the figure.
25415: A man coming out of the pub is thrown across the canal by a little dog.
25422: At a haunted spot a grey dog in slippers haunts the place. It is a ghost animal.
25423: When magpies chatter in the garden by the house, a death is coming. It is an omen.
25425: If you sell your soul to the devil, you get a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back). The wisseldaalder can never run out. To get the wisseldaalder you have to run around the churchyard three times with a black cat.
25431: A man is married to a witch. When his wife goes out at night to do witchcraft, only a tripe lies beside him in bed. The man himself has sold his soul to the devil. When short of money, he hangs an empty purse on the door handle in the evening. The next morning the purse is filled with money.
25435: The sorcerer Stammerige Harm owns a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back).
25436: If you want a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back), you have to run around the churchyard three times with a black cat in a sack, calling 'Who will buy my cat for a daalder?'. The devil then takes the cat and hands you the wisseldaalder.
25443: The wizard Imke de Jong frees himself effortlessly from prison: he throws his cap against a closed door and the door promptly springs open.
25445: A fortune teller makes all kinds of predictions to a former prisoner. The predictions come true exactly.
25455: A certain place is haunted because a little child was once murdered there. The child's ghost keeps haunting that place.
25462: A woman often hears hammering at night. It is an omen: later her new house is built on that spot.
25463: One night the narrator's daughter saw all kinds of bustling people in the house. It is a premonitory vision: when the daughter drowns fourteen days later, the house is swarming with people.
25464: One evening a woman hears a sound as if something is being thrown on the floor. It is an omen: when her daughter is killed the next day, the coffin bearers make the same sound.
25465: A boy cannot get into his house through the front door. When he manages to open the front door three quarters of an hour later, he sees someone opening the door of the room. The light in the back of the house is also on. It is a premonitory vision: the men were undertaker's assistants. A week later the boy's sister dies.
25467: At a haunted spot a foal with a porridge pot around its neck haunts the place. It is a ghost animal.
25472: A certain witch can turn herself into a cat: sometimes a white cat, sometimes a black one. When the children are screaming with pain one night, their father hurries to the witch's house. Through the window he sees the witch tormenting a cat. The father then throws a stone through the window. When he gets home, the children are calm. The children suffered pain when the witch tormented the cat.
25476: Someone once receives an apple from a witch. After he has kept the fruit for a while, it turns into a toad. Children are often warned not to eat apples from witches.
25477: Witches can turn themselves into cats. As cats they sometimes hold a meeting. They also fly through the air on broomsticks.
25478: Warning: at night always stay on the footpath and never go onto the road. After all, you may be driven aside or carried off by a passing funeral procession.
25479: On his way home a scoffer is stopped by a fat black thing. It is the devil. He kicks at the devil twice. You may not kick the devil more than twice.
25480: A man coming back from a party hears a great racket in several places, although nothing can be seen. It turns out to be the devil and his mates.
25482: A card reader predicts to a young man that he will get new clothes. The prediction comes true.
25483: A strange hunchbacked man is lifted from his bed at night by the devil and thrown into the mud. The devil has the man in his power.
25485: A lazy man is rolling in money. It is suspected that the man has sold his soul to the devil. When short of money, the man hangs a pot on the door in the evening. The devil fills the pot with money.
25486: People who own a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) have sold their souls to the devil. A wisseldaalder can never run out. When owners of a wisseldaalder die, they belong to the devil.
25496: A man born with a caul often foresees deaths in passing funeral processions.
25501: A trader short of money goes to the churchyard one evening with a black cat, calling 'Who will buy my pussycat?'. The man then receives a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) and becomes a rich man. Later the man no longer dares to go outside at dusk because he is afraid of the devil.
25507: A witch's son is approached by his mother on her broomstick, asking whether he will help her pick apples from the tree. When the boy runs away in fear, she chases him on the broomstick. The boy is so frightened that he no longer dares to go home.
25508: A man gives a strange cat a whack. Shortly afterwards a witch has a head wound. She had changed herself into a cat.
25509: A sinner is picked up twice and flung into the water, although no one can be seen. When he is thrown into the water, the magpies chatter loudly.
25510: If you get something from a witch, you should not eat it, because it turns into a toad.
25517: Wilde lantaarnen (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) were omens of the bicycle and car lights that came later.
25519: At a haunted spot a sow with piglets haunts the place. They are ghost animals.
25520: At a certain bridge the devil jumped over the canal. On one side of the canal there is the print of a human foot; on the other side the print of a horse's hoof.
25521: A scoffer is roughly flung from one side to the other.
25525: On a journey at night, a mat weaver suddenly sees an enormous head, some two metres high and three metres long. The head chases him for a while, but then suddenly vanishes.
25529: At a certain place the whistle of the tram is said to have been heard before the tram was invented. It is an omen.
25531: A man heard someone outside calling for his wife, but there was no one to be seen. Half an hour later his wife really was called by the neighbour woman.
25532: A man once thought he heard a young girl calling, but there was no one to be seen. Later that day a neighbour girl came calling.
25533: Where there is now a bakery, a big dog used to haunt.
25536: The lights that people used to see in the old days were the car and bicycle lamps of later times.
25537: People born with a caul often had to get up at night to see funeral processions. Some watched from the window, others had to walk a long way outside. Others were sometimes pushed off the road at night when a funeral procession came along.
25542: Germ Godloos was so called because he always swore so terribly. He lived in the Godloos Tolhuis. When he fell ill, two men kept watch over him. They left the room for a moment. When they returned, they found Germ with his neck wrung. The devil had done that.
25544: A witch can change herself into a cat. There are lots of stories of people hitting a cat, and then the next day the witch walks about with a cloth around her arm or something.
25549: People once came to a farmer to say that the train would run where his barn stood. The farmer said that was fine, but that he was not going to open and close the door every time the train passed through.
25550: A man often got out of bed at night to see funeral processions. From the window he would see them float past.
25551: One night a man was lifted off the road several times and set down again somewhere else.
25554: If you step on a toad, it starts to thunder. If someone gets an apple from a witch, it turns into a toad. If someone eats something from a witch, he falls ill.
25558: A man was never short of money. It was said of him that he had sold himself to the devil. He had a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back). He could spend it, but a little later it was always back in his pocket.
25564: Witch cats sometimes hold meetings. A poacher once saw a group of cats dancing and singing in a circle on their hind legs. He shot at them, but they did not react.
25569: It used to be said that the witches flew on a broomstick to the wine cellar in Spain.
25572: A man once rode along with another on the wagon. Suddenly the horses began to rear. The man got off and the passenger heard a hellish noise. The man was a mate of the devil, and was now fighting with him. When he came back, the horses drove on again.
25578: A man could make a bottle of liquor come with a jack of spades. The person he bet with had to take the bottle. The bottle came floating in, and the man grabbed it. If he had not done so, the sorcerer would have died.
25581: In the old days you could see your future partner in the black mirror at the market. Or you saw a coffin. That meant you would not marry. You had to leave the tent backwards.
25582: A woman had lost two children in a short time. She still had a son and a daughter left. She asked her sister to take care of her son soon. She would die soon, and her daughter too. That is how it turned out.
25583: A man made soldiers come out of the hearth pit. He also made them disappear into it again.
25586: At markets Imke de Jong crawled through a post.
25593: Minse Griper could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit with the magic book.
25594: A woman labourer was once sleeping in a farm barn in Groningen when one night she felt a cold child's hand on her cheek.
25601: The wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) that people used to see were omens of the lights of the houses built later.
25602: A young man on his way back was once pushed off the road several times by a hearse.
25604: A man once claimed in the pub that he was not afraid of any devil. But when he came out of the pub, the devil threw him into the canal.
25605: A young man once came home and saw the window open and the curtains flapping. On the floor he saw a small coffin. Not long after, his little brother died. The little coffin had to go out under the window. The curtains flapped exactly as the young man had seen earlier.
25606: A nephew said it would rain on the day of his uncle's funeral; he had already seen it. That did indeed come true.
25609: If a black cat got a whack, the next day the witch had a cloth around her head or something.
25612: Frânse Hinke stuck needles into dolls. Then the child she had bewitched felt pain.
25613: If you get an apple from a witch, it turns into a toad. You must always throw away a piece of the apple. Then the toad never grows up.
25614: A witch bewitched a cake, which he then gave to his visitors. In this way he bewitched one of them.
25615: It sometimes happened that horses refused to pull the wagon any further in the middle of the night. They were seeing a funeral procession.
25618: A girl once got an apple from an old woman. Her mother put the apple under a cup in the cupboard. If after three days the apple had not turned into a toad, the girl would be allowed to eat it.
25622: Someone once predicted that houses would be built all along the dike, because that person had seen toverlantaarns (magic lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) there. It came true.
25627: A man claimed to have seen wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) at a place where the tram later ran.
25628: One night a man heard a dog howling eerily in front of a house. Shortly afterwards someone in that house died.
25629: A man once saw a funeral in advance. He predicted that a black and a white horse would pull the wagon, which went against custom. It came true.
25630: At the house 'het ooievaarsnest' (the stork's nest), people used to hear the churn going every night. And yet there was nothing there.
25631: A lady haunted the Gravenlaan in Sumar. Once a carriage with a lady in it also sank into the ground.
25632: A man who cursed and swore a lot was once suddenly thrown into the ditch for no reason.
25633: In the past it sometimes happened that someone was suddenly pushed off the road by a funeral procession.
25637: The parents of a bewitched child went to the devil-banisher. He said an old woman had done it and that they must burn the wreaths they would find in the child's pillow. They also had to seal all the openings in the house properly: the keyhole, the chimney and the doors. When they burnt the wreath, the witch died.
25638: On the Tike a foal with a porridge pot around its neck haunts the place.
25647: A woman once came to buy flax waste, which she could use as fuel. The seller believed she was a witch and, before she arrived, made three crosses on the threshold. She invited the woman in, but the woman refused to cross the threshold.
25649: A man often looked after a little boy of 3. The child still could not walk. People said the man was a witch, but the parents did not believe it. But when the man died, the child suddenly learned to walk very quickly. And they found wreaths in his pillow. The third was almost finished. Then the child would have died. So he had been bewitched after all.
25654: A little white pig haunts a certain place.
25655: A dog haunts a certain place.
25656: A man once saw a white ghost floating over a field of oats.
25657: In the old days people sometimes saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) floating over the heath. Where they stood still, a new house would later be built.
25658: When a dog howls eerily, there will be a death. Also when a lot of rooks or magpies come into the yard.
25663: A farmer once hit a black cat that was in his house. The next day his wife walked about with her arm bandaged.
25668: A man often heard hammering in the distance at night. Ten years later he heard that same hammering again. That was when a new school was being built.
25672: People born with a caul often had to get up at night to see funeral processions. They then knew that someone would die within a few days.
25674: In Boornbergum a foal with a porridge pot around its neck haunts the place.
25676: When a dog howls eerily, someone is dying.
25678: People who came out of the pub after saying something wicked were quite often knocked down.
25679: A woman was treated rather badly by her husband. After her unexpected death she often came back to haunt.
25680: Little children who are not dressed in grave clothes after their death have no rest. They haunt.
25681: A labourer slept in a barn. One night he saw a white horse on a beam above him.
25687: Imke de Jong could make people stand still. He could also crawl through a beam. He once stole two sides of bacon and hid with them under an upturned boat. Only when the commotion was over did he make his escape.
25705: A horse used to haunt in Houtigehage.
25706: A man's mother had not been dead long. He was having an affair with another woman. One evening he was lying in bed when he saw a tall man with a lit-up cross and his mother come into the house. There was a dog with them too. A little later they vanished again.
25707: One evening a man saw a whole row of lights pass by on the horizon. Later a railway line came.
25709: An old woman warned her daughter not to step on the black ribbon. The daughter saw no ribbon at all. A week later the old woman was sitting outside and again saw a black ribbon. Another week later she died. The black ribbon was the funeral procession. She had seen it in advance.
25717: A few people were sitting together drinking when the liquor ran out. One of them then sent a playing card out the door. A little later there was a knock on the door and a bottle of liquor came floating in. The one who had sent the card was not allowed to take the bottle. Someone else did.
25719: The wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) that people used to see were the roads and houses of later times.
25720: A man was once out on his bicycle when someone with a horse's hoof came walking beside him. He walked just as fast as the man cycled. It was the devil.
25721: Farm labourers used to sleep in a barn. They often heard strange noises there. Someone had once been murdered and probably could not find rest. In the end nobody wanted to sleep at the farmer's any more.
25726: A schoolmistress at a state school could make little soldiers come out of the chimney. She then made them march. When she read the same text backwards, the little soldiers disappeared again.
25728: A group of men in an inn often ran out of liquor. They would then send out a jack of spades. A little later a bottle would come floating in. Someone had to take the bottle, but not the one who had sent the card. The first glass had to be thrown out over the left shoulder.
25729: In the old days there were tents at the market where cards were read, or where you could look into the black mirror. You were then shown something nice – wealth or a pretty girl – or a coffin. The latter meant that a death would come to the house.
25734: A man claimed he was not afraid of the devil. Then he was thrown down so hard that he died of it.
25735: No one had yet been buried in a new churchyard. One evening a neighbour suddenly saw a white figure standing on the mortuary with its arms spread. It looked like a prophet or a disciple. The apparition was never seen again.
25736: A woman once saw two men put a small coffin in the room, but in reality there was nothing. A few weeks later she lost a child, who had died of fits.
25737: A woman often heard hammering at night, but in reality there was nothing. Later lots of new houses were built and she heard the same sound again.
25739: On the way home a father and son once saw the apparition of a woman wearing a fur collar. They made a wide detour around her, and when they looked back, the woman had vanished.
25740: A man once heard hammering early in the morning, but there was nothing to be seen. Later a new house was built.
25741: At a place where a small church was later built, some people had already heard psalm singing beforehand.
25742: One night a man saw two naked little children walking in the woods.
25744: Four men were once fishing. Three of them were great scoffers, and this time too they were mouthing off. Until suddenly a strong wind began to blow and the three saw something strange. They ran away fast. The fourth man saw nothing and stayed calmly seated. Even later the three would not say what they had seen. It was probably the devil.
25745: In Harkema a glowing man haunts, looking like a live coal.
25746: One evening someone saw the shadowy figure of a fellow. A little later the figure had vanished again. It was a haunting.
25747: Two men were once out hunting polecats with their dogs. Suddenly they saw a flock of sheep in the field, but that was impossible, because there were never any sheep there. The dogs sat terrified with their tails between their legs.
25748: Two brothers were once swearing heavily in the pub. When they went home, the devil held the door open for them. They did not even notice.
25749: A young man's courtship once broke off and he ended up in prison. When he got out, he went to visit his former sweetheart. He saw her apparition sitting on the little house, although in reality she was not there at all. He even saw her nod to him. He took it as a sign that the courtship should be resumed. They married.
25750: In the old days you could see in the black mirror whom you would marry. If you were shown a coffin, you would stay single.
25752: One night a man heard a nightmare approaching. It came through the keyhole. He clearly heard footsteps. Then the nightmare jumped onto the bed and went over his feet. A nightmare is one of seven daughters. To avoid being troubled by a nightmare you should put your clogs back to front in front of the door.
25753: A witch can change herself into a cat. Alle Tet was a witch. One evening people struck a cat. The next day it could be seen on Alle Tet's hand. She sometimes conjured wreaths into children's pillows. These had to be burned. People put asafoetida (devil's dung) under the threshold and made crosses in front of the door, so the witch could not get in.
25754: A married couple was on the way home one evening when the wife saw a funeral procession pass. The husband saw nothing. Some time later someone died, and the funeral procession really came.
25755: A farmer's labourers in Groningen slept in a barn. The barn was haunted; at night people felt things floating over them.
25757: A man was often thrown down by the devil. Sometimes he was working at the back of a shop, and people heard him groaning. Then the devil had hold of him.
25760: People once heard cries for help from the Leeuwenpoel. It is said that someone is still bound to drown there.
25761: One evening a woman saw a funeral procession pass. She thought it was the funeral procession of an acquaintances' little child, who was not doing well. Later that child did indeed die, and the funeral procession really passed by.
25766: Two men hunting polecats once saw two naked little children floating. The dogs were terrified.
25767: Some boys were once stealing apples. When they came to a pear tree, it suddenly began to shake and all the pears fell to the ground by themselves. It was the devil who did this.
25768: In the old days people often saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps). Those lights foreshadowed the car and bicycle lamps of later times.
25769: Witches can change into cats. Those cats sometimes hold a meeting. Then they sing psalms.
25771: A sow with piglets haunts the Langepad.
25772: There was a large farm on the Groningen clay. In the barn where the labourers slept there was a whole row of bays for hay and grain. There was one bay where no one could sleep at night. If anyone lay down there, he was thrown out. It was a haunted barn.
25773: Wibe Alma once came out of the pub drunk. He saw a little dog and thought it was the devil. He said there were seven devils and that he would kick them to death. A bit further on he was suddenly lifted up and thrown into a hole in the dike. That must have been the devil's doing.
25774: A young man was once coming back from his girlfriend. His parents were already in bed. The devil held the door open for him and gave him a fork to eat the food that stood ready. He sat down opposite him at the table. Afterwards the young man lay down to rest in the hay, but his parents heard him fighting with the devil. The next day he was black and blue.
25775: A man was thrown over the dike several times in a row.
25776: A strange man was once knocked down.
25777: If a funeral procession passes at night and people do not make way, they are pushed aside.
25784: In a tent at the market you could look into the black mirror. Someone could then see which woman he would marry. If he saw a coffin, he would not marry. He had to leave the tent backwards.
25785: Mike Ruerd could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit with a magic book.
25797: Minse Griper could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. They marched across the floor. He would also sometimes fetch a bottle of liquor by sending out a jack of spades. He then threw the first glass over his left shoulder; that was for the devil.
25802: There are hares that can never be shot dead. Those are witches.
25804: It was haunted by the thick tree on the Betonweg in Harkema.
25806: If you meet a werewolf, you must throw him a handkerchief. A werewolf was once courting his girl. Suddenly he wanted her apron and ran off. When he came back a little later, the threads of the apron were still between his teeth. He had torn it apart.
25807: Old Sije had sold himself to the devil. Whenever he needed money, he got it.
25824: Near Westergeest a witte juffrouw (white lady) always used to haunt.
25826: A carriage once came up to a small boat. A voice from the carriage told the skipper to get in. But the skipper quickly made off. It was the devil who had been sitting in the carriage.
25827: At a certain spot people used to see wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) often. Those were the bicycle lights of later times. Houses were built there too.
25828: At a certain spot a foal with a porridge pan around its neck used to haunt. Somewhere else a girl with a peddler's basket used to haunt as well.
25830: A man once saw ships sailing across a piece of land. Later a lake appeared there.
25831: People used to often see a girl in black silk clothes haunting.
25832: A woman died but was not given in her coffin what she was entitled to. Because of this the dead woman could not find rest, and she regularly appeared to her family. They had the minister address her and ask what she wanted. They then did it. They laid the parcel down. Had they given it into her hand, their own hand would have been burned.
25837: A man always saw funeral processions in advance. Because of this he always knew who would die and what the procession would look like. Once people wanted to keep his prediction from coming true by harnessing a different horse to the wagon. But that animal refused, and then the horse the man had predicted would pull it was put in front after all.
25838: A young couple were once walking together. The young man told his girl not to be frightened if he suddenly disappeared for a moment. A little later he was suddenly lifted up, and the girl saw him walking on the other side of the ditch. The courtship was broken off.
25839: At a certain place a ship could never stay moored. If the anchor was dropped there, it always came back up.
25841: If you dream of fish at night, someone in the house will die soon. If you dream in the second half of the night, it will be a while before someone dies. If you dream in the first half of the night, it will happen soon.
25849: A cat with a long tail was often a witch. As cats, witches hold meetings. Then they sing psalms.
25852: Several people have seen two witte wijven (white women) in the woods.
25857: A man once came out of the pub dead drunk. He was cursing and swearing and claimed he was not afraid of the devil. Then a little dog came up to him and dragged him straight into the ditch. There the man and the little dog fought. The man came home all bruised and covered in blood. He was never drunk again after that.
25861: Minse Griper could make a bottle of liquor come with a jack of spades.
25863: A woman had the habit of saying 'devil' at every opportunity. Once she was on her way to the pump when a small black man stood there. She could not walk any further. Then she began to pray, and she was able to go on again.
25864: Minse Griper had a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back).
25867: A few men were once working on the Jachtveld when they saw a woman come up out of the ground. When they looked away for a moment, the woman had vanished again.
25868: A man came to his sick mother and saw a coffin in her house. But his mother was not dead and she lived another five years. Later the coffin really came.
25871: In the past people often saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) moving at a certain place. Later a tram came there.
25875: A place where a little child was once murdered is haunted.
25876: A dog always haunts by the holly grove in Boelenslaan.
25877: A man always saw funeral processions in advance. Because of this he always knew in which house someone would die.
25878: Some people have heard a voice calling for help from the Leeuwenpoel. People think that someone will drown in it some day.
25880: A mother and daughter could both do magic. In the evenings they flew through the air together on a broom.
25881: In the past people always warned not to walk in the middle of the road because of funeral processions.
25883: Witches can change themselves into a cat. A strange cat often came into a man's house. One day he had had enough and shot at the animal. The next day Rikele Myt walked about with a black cloth over her eye.
25887: A man was thrown off the road as many as three times, without seeing who did it.
25889: On a certain road a big light always came floating past at ten o'clock at night. Later a tram came to run there. It was a portent.
25890: A married couple lived in a haunted house. At night all the doors regularly opened without anything to be seen. Once a black thing also came in that looked like an old stove.
25891: A man was once cycling to his father's when a black thing kept bumping into him the whole time. It looked like a stove.
25892: A man born with a caul often had to get up at night to see funeral processions. Because of this he always knew in advance that someone would die. He also predicted that a major road would be built in a certain place. That came true.
25894: A man was once walking in the middle of the road when a funeral procession came along and he was flung off the road.
25896: A man who had been born with a caul was once at a farmer's. He told the farmer that he saw the little coffin of the farmer's son standing in the room and that this meant the child would soon die. Indeed the boy died fairly soon afterwards.
25897: A man once heard a bang, but his son had heard nothing. Some time later the son died. When a relative took one more look into the coffin, he was so startled that he let the lid fall shut with a bang. The same bang the father had heard earlier.
25900: Two men were once walking along a sand road. One warned the other to step aside because a funeral procession was coming. But the other saw nothing and kept walking where he was. Then he was flung a long way.
25903: If someone dreams about fish, there will soon be a death in the family.
25904: Someone once came home late. From the dung heap behind the house he heard rattling and saw all sorts of things moving. He never knew what it was.
25905: If someone had seen a house burning, it would later really burn down.
25906: A woman once saw a coffin being brought into her house. It bumped against the door frame. Later her husband died, and the situation was exactly the same.
25919: Mike Ruerd could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. They would then start marching. He also led them back into it.
25922: A father and son were once walking along a little road that was haunted. Something black came towards them, as big as a calf. The father prayed: "Let this cup pass from me." And it passed by.
25923: People regularly saw a man standing by a gate who had long been dead. Piter Claus said he would like to see that man too. One evening he did indeed see him, and they had a chat together.
25927: Every year a man went to work for the same farmer with his brother. But one time the man dreamed that he would not go along that year. That came true as well. The two brothers did not speak to each other for years.
25929: A young couple once saw a great light on the way back. When she got home the girl asked her father why the light was on. The father said the light was not on, and that if she had seen a great light anyway, it was an omen. Four weeks later the man was dead.
25930: Two brothers saw a light burning in their third brother's house and a woman standing in the room. They thought he had visitors and turned back. The next day they told their brother. But he said they had had no light on at all, and that there had been no woman.
25931: Old Minse Griper could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
25936: In the past people saw ships sailing over a stretch of heath. Later a small side canal was dug there.
25937: At the spot where people used to see wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) often, new houses were later built.
25938: A certain piece of land was always flooded in winter. One evening two women saw a man come from the churchyard and float over that land.
25939: A man saw a coffin being pushed into his house under the windowsill. Later his wife and children died, and a coffin really did come in under the windowsill.
25940: A wicked woman died but could find no rest after her death. She kept on haunting. Her neighbour then fetched a minister. He prayed, and after that they were never troubled again.
25941: You must never promise anything to someone on their deathbed. Because if you do not keep it, that person will come back later.
25943: In the old days people often saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) on the heath. The light was very bright. Later a farm was built there.
25944: In the old days people often saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) on the heath. Later new houses were built there.
25945: At dusk a man always saw twelve little lights in a row, while in reality there was nothing there. Later a new farm was built, with twelve small cowshed windows.
25949: A man and a woman once had a quarrel. They both pulled so hard at their child that they tore it apart. Since then that place has been haunted.
25951: A black foal haunted a certain place.
25959: People must never walk in the middle of the road at night. Otherwise they may be pushed off the road by a funeral procession.
25963: In the old days men would sometimes look into the black mirror. Then a man was shown the woman he would later marry. If a man was shown a coffin, he would not marry.
25964: In the old days there were people who could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. When people back then wanted to frighten someone, they would say: "Watch out, or I'll make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit!"
25966: A man once ordered two drinks at an inn. He emptied one glass himself, and an invisible man emptied the other. That was the devil. Later the man was found with his neck wrung.
25969: A man had been born with a caul. One Sunday he heard a child calling for help from the water, but there was nothing to be seen. Later someone drowned at that spot.
25970: In certain places boatmen never dare to tow. The towing goes so easily there that they are convinced someone is pulling along with them. And that must be the devil.
25971: At a certain spot people sometimes heard a terrible racket and strange noises. Later a man stabbed his wife to death at that spot. Then the same noises could be heard.
25972: Two men were once walking along the railway line in the moonlight; they were smuggling. Suddenly they saw a fellow wearing a hat. When he passed them, he suddenly vanished.
25974: If people dream about lice, they will fall into poverty.
25975: A woman tells that in the week before the German invasion she dreamed that the sky was black with aeroplanes.
25979: A group of drunkards once celebrated Holy Communion in the pub. When they went home afterwards, they were flung over the trees.
25981: A witch can change herself into a black cat. Sometimes people give a cat a whack, and then the next day they can see who the witch is.
25984: Three men were once coming back from the pub. One of them had been cursing terribly and so on. On the way back he suddenly could not walk any further; he stood stock-still.
25988: A black cat often sat by a man's house. Once the man hit the animal with a club. The next day Rikele Myt walked about with a cloth around her head.
25990: A man saw lights somewhere, but in reality there was nothing. Five years later a tram came.
25994: A man who was born with a caul had predicted in advance that there would be a cinema in the church.
25995: A horse dealer had received a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) from the devil. Because of this the devil had him in his power. When the dealer travelled on the Veenster boat and laughingly took a cup of coffee, everything fell to pieces on the floor. That is why he no longer dared to take the boat alone.
25996: One day a man's face was covered in scratches and bruises. He claimed the devil had got hold of him that night.
25997: One night people heard hammering. Not long afterwards a new house was built on that spot.
25998: At a spot where people had seen wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) in the old days, new houses were later built.
25999: A neighbour heard a clock ticking in an empty parsonage. But there was no clock at all. When the new occupants arrived, they hung a clock in the spot the neighbour had heard the sound coming from.
26009: A man once shot at a strange cat. The next day Jelle Tryntsje had red and blue marks on her neck.
26011: A man had been cursing and swearing in the pub all evening and had claimed he was not afraid of the devil. When he came out of the pub he saw an old kettle lying there. He ran his knife over it. Then he was thrown down three times.
26012: Six men were once playing cards in the pub. The winner had to make a bottle of liquor come. But the winner did not dare to take the bottle when it arrived. What exactly happened after that is unknown, but he came home half dead that night. The devil had got hold of him.
26013: A man could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
26014: A woman once saw in a black mirror the person she would marry. But she was courting someone else and did not believe it. Later, however, she came to live at a farmer's, and began courting his son. He was the one she had seen in the mirror, and they married.
26015: A woman was once on her way when suddenly a big black dog with very large eyes came walking beside her. She was so frightened that she went into a house of strangers.
26018: Farmhands used to sleep in barns. Sometimes those barns were haunted. A woman once saw a fireball fly from one side to the other. She also sometimes heard wagons rattling through the barn.
26022: Late one evening a girl saw the figure of a beautiful woman with long, curly hair. It was a ghost.
26025: Someone always saw a fellow in a white waistcoat floating over the Jankemeer.
26033: A man once looked out of his window and saw a smooth strip across the land, just as if there were a skating rink. A few years later a motorway was built there.
26040: Rikele Myt had a foster child who called her 'grandma'. Once some hunters asked him whether he had seen a hare. The boy pointed to a spot, and the hunters shot at the animal. They hit its eye. The boy shouted: "Run, grandma!" Later Rikele Myt was missing an eye.
26041: The children were warned never to eat an apple from Rikele Myt, because then they would get a toad or a frog in their body.
26042: People always saw two naked little children running near their house. The previous occupants had drowned their children in the moat. The barn doors were open again every morning, even when they had been shut the evening before.
26043: On her deathbed a woman had it promised that her daughter would get all her clothes. But after her death this did not happen. Then the dead woman came haunting the room every evening. They fetched the minister. He said a prayer and the girl got the clothes. Since then the ghost has never been there again.
26045: At a certain place people have regularly seen a plaagbeest (tormenting ghost beast).
26046: A man was once cycling through the woods in the dark. His lamp was not working. Suddenly he was passed by a fellow who did not return his greeting.
26048: In the old days people always heard hammering and sawing at a certain place, but there was nothing to be seen. Later new houses were built.
26051: A man once saw a house on fire, but in reality there was no fire. Later it burned down after all. If you see a house burning in the early part of the night, it will soon really burn down. If you see it in the latter part of the night, it will take a while yet.
26056: Douwe Stavasius was born with a caul. A boy had an accident with the chicken cart. He was carried to the road on a ladder as quickly as possible. Douwe said it was no use, the boy would die anyway. He had already seen the funeral. The boy died on the way.
26060: A man was on his way home one evening. Three times a little man came walking alongside him, who made no reply to his greetings.
26061: A man once came out of the pub drunk, when he was suddenly stopped by the devil. He recognised the black figure by its horse's hoof. He turned around, and there stood Jesus. The man could go neither way. Then he turned around again and said 'away, Satan', and then he could get through. Since then the man never drank strong liquor again.
26062: A man once heard footsteps behind him on the road. But he saw no one. Only when he had to cross a road did he see someone disappear through a hedge. It was someone without a head.
26065: People once heard a terrible noise coming from the woods. They saw the trees bend to the ground in a line about two or three metres wide. Later a railway line came.
26066: One night a man could not sleep because there was so much noise and light outside. Later a national highway came.
26067: A couple were once quarrelling outdoors. Then a thing came, as big as a man. It kept following them, and whenever they stood still, it stood still too.
26068: Two men were going to Groningen together to work. The day before, one of them said he would not go because he had seen that one of his relatives would die. A few days later one of his children died.
26069: Two men once came out of the pub and walked in the middle of the road. One warned the other to step aside because a funeral procession was coming. But the other saw nothing and kept walking where he was. Then he ended up in the ditch. He had walked into the hearse and been thrown off the back of it.
26071: A mermaid is half fish, half human. She is a siren. With their beautiful singing they lure sailors to them. The sailors are then swallowed by the waves. If someone sees a mermaid, the weather turns bad and the ship will be lost. Mermaids sometimes make predictions.
26076: Wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) mean bad weather. They also mean that a new house will be built, or that the heath will fare badly that year. When a beekeeper died, the beehives were moved. Once when a beekeeper was buried, people claimed that lots of bees had been at the funeral.
26084: One night a man saw a shadow, but otherwise he could find nothing and no one. It was probably the ghost of someone who had been murdered there.
26086: In Rottevalle the churchyard is haunted.
26088: A woman once saw lots of little lights on the heath. Later a tram came.
26089: People sometimes saw lights over the land. That meant poachers would come a few days later.
26090: A woman once saw a coffin pass by her mother. Not long afterwards the woman began to ail, and she died.
26091: A man sometimes made a bottle of liquor come by sending off a card. But at night he was punished for it. Then he could not sleep. Sometimes he also made strange noises, as if he were fighting. He then had to atone for his wicked deeds.
26100: People once heard the brass band playing, while in reality there was no band at all. Only later was a brass band founded.
26101: The mother of a son who was soon to go into military service invited a card reader. She predicted that he would not end up in the war, and that he would come out of it safely. That came true.
26112: When people saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, ghost lights) above the heaths, they believed that another new house would be built.
26113: One night a man came across a little dog. He said that if it was the devil, he wanted to fight it. Suddenly the little dog changed into a fellow, and the man was beaten black and blue. It was the devil.
26114: A man was once pushed off the road by a funeral procession and ended up in the ditch.
26116: A shopwoman once quarrelled with a customer because she never paid. Then the woman came to her as a cat. The shopwoman threw a kettle of boiling water over its back. The next day the woman lay in bed with burns.
26119: When a dog howls eerily, a death will come. One day a dog would not stop howling eerily. Shortly afterwards the woman of the house died.
26124: Imke de Jong simply crawled through a beam.
26126: Some people can make a bottle of liquor come with a jack of spades.
