26129: A wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) always returns to you. You keep it as long as you live.
26130: The devil sometimes turns into a magpie. If someone has been up to something, a magpie may be sitting chattering on the house when he comes home. That is the devil.
26133: In Oostermeer there is Jan Koortsland. There the devil wrung someone's neck.
26153: Near the churchyard in Rottevalle, a naked little child haunts at night.
26155: Two young men were once out on the road. One warned the other to step aside for a moment, because a funeral procession was coming. The other saw nothing. Not long afterwards someone died, and the funeral procession really did pass by.
26172: A man had been born with a caul. At night he always saw funeral processions. Once, when he was out walking with someone, he said they had to move to the side because a funeral procession was coming. The other saw nothing, but did come home with soaking wet feet because they had been standing in the mud.
26175: An old woman always heard a voice calling 'too long, too long' in the evening. Once she called back to ask what was too long. 'The shirtsleeves' was the answer. The woman said, "Then take a pair of scissors and cut them off," and she put a pair of scissors on the table. Then she heard the sound of linen being cut, and since then she never heard the calling again.
26177: In Rottevalle a lady in a white gown haunted in the dark.
26178: When a dog howls eerily, it hears a corpse coming.
26184: A man could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
26185: A man could make a bottle of liquor come by tying a jack of spades to an empty bottle.
26191: At a certain spot a spotted dog haunted. People said it was a plaagbeest (a tormenting spirit beast).
26192: A chair-mender often saw a black sheep walking back and forth early in the morning.
26194: In the old days people saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, ghost lights). They were the forerunners of the lights of cars.
26195: In the old days witte wieven (white women) haunted the area. They drank petroleum. Black women also haunted the old sand roads.
26197: A glowing man used to float over the heath.
26199: A man who was born with a caul foresaw that his own daughter would drown. He also saw a train accident between Westereinde and Buitenpost. But that did not happen.
26202: A witch turns herself into a cat. People once saw a black cat leap out of their house and hurt itself. The next day an old woman from the neighbourhood was walking around with a cloth around her head.
26207: A man once jumped over a canal. He thought no one could match him, not even the devil. By chance the devil came by. He too jumped over the canal and left a devil's print behind.
26208: If you walk in the middle of the road, you may be pushed to the side by a funeral procession.
26211: A man who was born with a caul often had to get up at night to see funeral processions. He foresaw funerals, and it always turned out just as he had seen.
26213: A certain spot was haunted because someone had once hanged himself there.
26214: A few men once came out of the pub, where they had not behaved very well. Halfway home they were suddenly thrown over the trees.
26215: A group of boys always held a contest to see who could cross the bridge in the fewest steps. One boy always won. Once he said that not even the devil could stop him. Then suddenly the devil was standing there, and he was much faster. Afterwards there were prints of his horse's hooves on the bridge.
26216: A terrible drunkard said he was not afraid of the devil. The next day he lay in bed with his head turned around.
26218: A foal haunted an old churchyard. People heard it grazing in the churchyard at night.
26220: Back then, a married couple in Harkema, near the Smoorhoeke, sees little lights approaching that come round the corner up the winding path. They are wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, ghost lights). Later cyclists ride past with their lights on. They had seen the bicycle lamps in advance.
26221: Behind the bog near the Wyldfjild, an old woman is sitting one day in the house without doors. Then she sees two beams of light coming straight at her and leaves the house. Later her house has to go to make way for the tramline that runs straight through it. She had seen the tram coming.
26222: Mother goes to visit old Jantsje, and on the way she sees a big black wheel passing by with lots of silent people behind it. She realises this is a funeral procession, but the wheel remained unclear. In those days people are still taken to the churchyard on an ordinary farm wagon. Later the hearse with unequal wheels arrives. Only then does she know what it was.
26223: Roel is twenty and is once coming back from the peat bog. As he boasts that he is in full possession of his senses and comes onto the new sand road, he is lifted up and set down again two or three fields further on. This incident is attributed to the devil, because Roel is a brute, a wild man.
26224: Mike Ruerd has once been up to a lot of mischief and treats his wife badly. He is a carpenter and, with tools over his shoulder, meets lads coming from work. He walks along the paths by the Bomkleaster and is thrown onto the wood. After this fall he is ill for days. It was the work of the devil.
26225: Wibe Alma goes to visit Hindrik Wimke and takes a shortcut across the fields. Then he finds himself facing the Prinses Margrietkanaal and goes back home. The next morning, however, it is just a tiny little stream that he can simply step over.
26226: Wibe Alma is courting Griet and after a quarrel he breaks it off. One day he goes to see her, and between the churchyard and the state school he sees her sitting on the right side of the path wrapped in a black cloth. He becomes frightened and returns home. Later it turns out that Griet was never there that day.
26227: Hindrik Holthuis is a wild man who drinks heavily. After the devil throws him to the ground and lames him, he is converted.
26228: On the road to Readskuorre stands a little house with an upper and a lower door. A man cannot sleep, and at two o'clock at night he gets out of bed and leans over the lower door. When he sees two men in dark clothing pass by, he follows them. Suddenly they vanish again. Later there is a story in the village. They were two wegaanzeggers (death announcers) heading to the village. Panhuizen used to live at that spot; it is on the road that runs parallel to the Langepad.
26229: A mother-in-law is once near a state school and sees two naked children. She is thrown aside, and the children, who were not given burial clothes, cannot find the others and have to pass by. The woman makes way for them.
26234: One night Sjoerd comes home and goes to bed. Then a small, soot-black little man with a black cap appears in the attic. Sjoerd is afraid of nothing. The little man comes onto Sjoerd's bed and they fight. Sjoerd says he is not afraid of the devil. Sjoerd takes some hard blows. Then a little old woman is standing in the attic; she gives the little man a black, square package and leaves again. Sjoerd gets out of bed, goes towards the devil and follows him to the corner under the roof. The devil vanishes and Sjoerd gets scared and goes back to bed. The little man had passed through the closed doors and is the devil.
26235: At the thick tree near Harkema an old person was once murdered, and at night you always see this person haunting by the tree.
26237: When someone from Harkema is in Witveen, he hears something and sees a snow-white horse float through the air and come down in Leijen.
26238: Earde Hut was once lifted up for no reason on the Kleineweg and thrown into a ditch.
26239: Anders-om has made his confession of faith in Droegeham. One evening he passes a big oak, from where a little dog walks home with him. It was the devil. After this walk, Anders has sweat hanging from every hair.
26240: On the Veensterheide a little black man comes and stands by a woman with a washtub. The woman sent him away by saying that she sticks with our dear Lord. The devil leaves.
26241: Hindrik Holthuis from Harkema is the biggest mocker in the village; he has children sit in a row on the dike and then curse. The best curser gets money as a reward. Once the devil threw him to the ground so hard that he was left lame. He is converted and becomes the leader of a Sunday school.
26243: Before the Second World War, Boardzer Bruining from Boelenslaan sees the German army passing by his place.
26246: The big oak in Harkema is always haunted.
26247: A farmer's horse is visited by a nightmare every night. Once the farmer has sprinkled flour on the animal's rump, the nightmare stays away.
26251: Ymke de Jong is at the Hamstermarkt, where he has fixed police officer Tseard van Dekken to the ground. During military service he did the same with a lieutenant.
26252: During his military service Ymke de Jong is locked up in the Kânslerije as punishment, but he breaks out one night. Locks open by themselves, and under the words 'here lions and bears are tamed' he writes 'but not Ymke de Jong'.
26253: Mother-in-law Janke was in service with a family Beitschat in Kollum. When they are having coffee, she is asked to fetch the walking stick. The man places it between his knees with the pointed end down. When he stands up, the stick stays standing. When asked whether he should make the stick jump over the table or make soldiers come out of the hearth pit, she says no. Janke thinks it is all devil's tricks.
26255: In Rotfalle lives a certain Kuipers, who can foresee things. He stood on the Alpen in Harkema and in 1880 saw seagoing ships sailing in the Knjillisdjip. The canal was later widened and seagoing ships regularly sail there. He can also order food from London without an air connection. Later this happened by means of aeroplanes.
26270: In the old days young people from Harkema often went to the black mirror to see whom they would marry.
26271: People often come to Reid Keuning's in the morning to play cards, and Reid then makes little soldiers come out of the hearth pit, which start marching.
26273: Flippusom's brothers call him Flippus Pot, and all three are skippers. Flippesom is always short of money and once lies ill in his bunk, moaning. A little man comes in and starts counting banknotes to buy Flippus's soul. Flippus thinks he is a swindler who later wants to buy his corpse. When he sees the club foot, he refuses the money, and then a great flame with smoke appears in the forecastle and the boat smells of sulphur. The little man is gone. It was the devil. Flippus took part in a ten-day campaign.
26276: When old Bôkke Noordman once walks to Surhústerfean by way of the old Jirren, he meets a bird that keeps whistling and flies close past him from tree to tree. He becomes frightened and flees home. It must have been the devil.
26277: If you get an apple from a witch and put it away, it turns into a toad, and if you step on it, a thunderstorm starts.
26279: According to grandmother, a witch lives in Harkema. When grandma, as a girl, passes the witch's house at two o'clock in the middle of the night, the witch is sitting sticking pins into dolls. Since then she gives the witch a wide berth whenever she meets her.
26292: In my brother's house there are ropes with blocks for hoisting and lowering the mainsail. One evening we hear the blocks fall down, but when we inspect there is nothing to be seen. Two days later they do fall.
26294: Once when father is at the house, he cannot get in because he has forgotten the key. Another man then put a corner of his handkerchief in the keyhole, opened the lock and also locked it again.
26295: A young man is already on his way when he notices he has left something at his girlfriend's. She has bolted the door with two bolts. Yet he only has to strike the door once with his fist and it opens by itself. He takes what he needs and bolts the door again with a single blow on the door.
26296: In the old days it was all heath as far as Mearum. An old woman sees wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, ghost lights) moving over the heath. Later roads come with bicycles, and she again sees lights in the same places, but now they are bicycle lamps. This had been foretold.
26297: When the heath is being reclaimed, people hear hammering at a spot where the Groningen hamlet of Pein later stands. That was the building of it.
26298: Douwe Stavasius was born with a caul and predicts deaths, and he laid out his own mother in advance. They live in a sod house.
26300: Dogs with spots above their eyes are eerie howlers that foretell death by their howling.
26304: On my way home I see a bright light with a tail, as if it is burning. The others do not see it. This happened in 1937 in Groninger Pein. According to my mother it was an omen of the war.
26305: In Groninger Pein, a woman once sees the head of her future husband in the mist during misty weather. She is not yet married at the time.
26306: One evening Gabe Marij from Grinzer Pein is coming from Drachten and sees lights and money all around her. So she says that Drachten will become a big town with factories and wealth. It came true.
26308: When a dog howls eerily, a death will follow.
26312: If you walk in the middle of the road, you can be put aside by a funeral procession.
26313: A man's brother is clairvoyant and grabs hold of the man between Hûs ter Noord and Kollumersweach, then lets him go again later. The man saw nothing apart from a small milestone. Hindrik, however, saw the ghost of a child passing by, and that is why he stepped aside.
26315: Someone was once suddenly lifted up, cart and all, and thrown into a ditch. He never saw anything. According to Hindrik, the man had been in the way of a ghost that had to pass.
26317: One night an uncle in Aldwâld was joined by a ghost boy who said nothing and suddenly vanished by a hedge. Later, at this spot, a blue woollen apron hung over the hedge, which had appeared in place of the ghost. The hedge stands close to the Spookplaats.
26321: With the help of a playing card (jack of spades) you can make a bottle of jenever come. The one who orders it must quickly have someone else catch the bottle, or else the orderer dies. He may not catch it himself.
26322: While in service, my uncle has his silver buckles stolen. The black mirror tells him the buckles have already been sold to others. If a coffin appears in the mirror, you will stay single.
26323: If you want to see your future sweetheart, you must put a garter under your pillow and recite a rhyme. Then that person will appear before you.
26326: Freemasons are also bulletproof and have a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back), so they are never short of money. They are sold to the devil. Once every seven years they draw lots for who must die. The contract is for life and is signed in their own blood.
26327: Stammerige Harm and Meinte Sjouk have a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back), so they are never short of money. They are always renovating their house.
26329: A woman makes a pact with the devil so that she always has money. Someone else has a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back), which the Freemasons also have, so they are never short of money. This daalder is also sold to the devil, and every seven years someone must die. They draw lots for who it will be. The woman sits by the Skutediep in Groningen in the half-dark and says: hi-ho, and gives not a whole hand but two fingers.
26332: A minister from Wylp in Friesland is making house calls, and when it gets late the elder advises him not to take the Langpad, but it is already too late. They are already walking on it, and halfway a white figure appears that stops them the third time and glues them to the spot. The figure disappears when the minister asks it to.
26333: A woman lives in Opende and every evening sees a white thing whoosh past her house. When Schopper, the director of the Wilhelminahoeve, hears this he does not believe it, but he has to admit she is right when they see it themselves too.
26334: In Körnhörn lives a man whose wife has died and was not given what was her due. She finds no rest in the churchyard and comes by his house in the evenings. The man reports this to the minister, who then talks with the woman about what is wrong. She says what she is missing, and when the man lays these things on her grave, they are gone the next morning. The haunting stops after that.
26335: One night Gaatske Gjeltema and his brother are on their way home in bright moonlight, and close to home they suddenly see a very beautiful girl, who vanishes a little later.
26336: The ghost of the murdered girl haunts the house where Jelle and Tryntsje now live.
26341: Piter is bewitched, and his father gets a potion from an exorcist that must be kept out of sight of any stranger, including the witch. So the keyhole of the cupboard must be covered. The neighbour woman drops by, takes the child in her arms and mutters some words. Then the child spits out a three-legged mouse. The father asks the woman to stay away for good.
26342: It has also happened that someone got a potion from the duivelbanner (exorcist) and that a hare broke the bottle on the way. He had to go back. The hare had been the witch.
26345: A woman is married to a German and lives in the Leliestraat in Groningen. One evening at half past seven the door opens and someone wipes his feet. The woman is home alone, but sees no one while the little dog barks. This happens every evening around this time, and because the woman and the little dog become frightened, they have since gone out walking every evening between seven and eight.
26347: In Doezum there was an old café that was haunted by a soot-black woman who stood behind the bar.
26348: A witch can change into a cat. If you hit a cat, the witch lies in bed the next day with a sore head or something similar. They also bewitch people with wreaths in their pillows. As cats they hold a meeting. Someone once heard a cat say: "Thursday evening."
26350: Hindrik Holthuis mocks everything, and once when he is walking home from the pub he meets the devil and mocks him. The devil then throws him away and Hindrik is left with a stiff leg. After that he becomes a faithful churchgoer of the Reformed church.
26351: Albert Alma once comes home drunk and lies down in the hay. But the devil picks him up and throws him away.
26354: With a jack of spades you can make liquor come.
26356: A wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) comes from the devil and it never runs out.
26783: One evening people see spinning lights. They belong to a tram that would come later. It was an omen.
26784: If people in Pein hear hammering, there will later be a celebration in that house.
26814: Alle Beima is digging sand with others and a large cat comes to sit by her. Alle shoots the cat. The next day Rikele Myt is missing an eye. She had turned herself into a cat.
26817: Rudolf de Mepske from Faan chained people up in the stables and then set the building on fire. Rudolf only says: just listen to those mice squeak. Later he is troubled by a plague of mice, which swim to the house through the moat around the new house. At the Roanster market, where the fire once was, the sky is still red at night.
26842: A woman sees in her dream a black woman in rain clothes, after which a death follows in the family or the neighbourhood.
26843: A witch always has one or two black cats in the house and can also turn into a cat herself. Sometimes a cat hurts its foreleg and the witch has a bodily injury. Cats hold a meeting. When someone fetches a potion against short-sightedness from the duivelsbanner (exorcist), a cat leaps at the bottle and breaks it.
26844: Near the tower of Heerenveen stands the pub of Albert Boorn, where it is always haunted. The door opens by itself and drink also appears by means of a playing card. The same happens in café 'De Lauwers'. Gosling has a wisseldaalder (a coin that always returns to its owner) and always has money in his hands. In the 'Omloop' there is a local pub run by Haring and Hiltsje, which is also haunted. There too they have wisseldaalders (coins that always return to their owner) and have the devil bring them drink.
26845: Close to Ketting is a lane where older people never go, because it is haunted. Smook, who lives with his mother, comes out of the pub and says he would like to see the devil, who is welcome to wring his neck. He is a braggart. Near his mother's house the devil comes to him and twists his head around. The next day they find him with his head backwards on his body, and since then the place has been haunted.
26847: A brother of father Klaes is a pleasant man with a quick tongue. If there is something going on, he wants to see it for himself. So he comes from Rotfalle and rides along the Folgersterlaan, where he falls a few times, and he blames it on the devil. After that it does not happen again.
26852: A molecatcher is once working away from home near Almelo and is in no mood for it. A couple of magpies keep chattering around him, and that day he gets a telegram saying his father is very ill and he must come home. The magpies were the harbingers.
26853: When something is coming, for example the police, magpies give warning in advance.
26854: Someone is visiting his neighbours when people tell him his house is on fire. When he goes to look, however, it is not so. Not long afterwards the house does indeed burn down. If you see it in the early part of the night, it will not be long, and in the night itself it may take a while yet.
26855: Someone hears tapping on the window but sees no one. A little later he hears it again, and then someone is standing there.
26856: Durk lives by the Boskreed in Harkema. One night a brother of my father, Aen Klokje, sees from that house a funeral procession pass by for a boy who has died. Durk dies soon after this incident and the funeral really takes place.
26857: Klaes Kooistra is walking with other people on the road to Harkema when he urges them to move aside, because the hearse is coming. He is the only one who sees it.
26858: A boy is coming from De Ham along the Lytse Wei and is stopped by Hearke Haga. It is war and the army is passing by. A soldier opens the door for him and disappears again. He experienced this, even though in reality he was never there.
26859: Old Albert Alma is once coming from the pub in Eastemar and walks along the Skeanpad to get to Harkema. Just as he is about to step over the wood lying there, someone sits down on it. Without knowing how, he gets over it, and at home the other man opens the door for him. His mother does not trust it. Albert gets food spilled over him and the man disappears again. It was the devil.
26860: Sytse Jager is once thrown to the ground and becomes very frightened because of it. When he is out catching polecats he avoids certain spots and prefers to take a detour.
26861: Mike Ruerd is often drunk and curses a lot, and once he is thrown to the ground by the evil one. The evil one had mistreated him before as well.
26862: Foppe Sint from Harkema makes soldiers come out of the hearth pit, which then march through the house.
26863: Foppe Sint got a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) for a black cat. He had walked around the churchyard three times and called out who wanted to buy his cat for a daalder. The devil gave him a wisseldaalder and since then Foppe has never been short of money. Hence the nickname 'Sint'.
26869: Long ago a small farmhouse stood alone on a spot in the heath near the big church by the green cross building. Later a road was built there, and Nijboer now lives on this spot. The house spontaneously caught fire and the fire went out again just as quickly. Because people thought it was malice, people kept watch, but this turned out not to be the case. It remained a mysterious fire and the little house never burned down.
26870: Next to this spot is a path across the heath, and behind it is a large hill, the Voshoogte. Once, when mother has been shopping at Van Houten's, she sees a white human figure floating in the evening twilight. Years later my brother Piter and my cousin Piter saw it too. At first they take it for a white birch tree, but it moves, walks around the lake and goes to the forest road. They run to the end of the road and a little later the figure vanishes.
26871: At the same spot an old spinster lives with her parents. They are called Buikamp. The place is haunted and there are often visitations. The house is altered and rebuilt and the visitations stop. The people later moved away too. It must have been an inn, as it is the only house for miles around. Merchants who stayed the night vanish without a trace, as does a priest. This must have been the white figure. The sand road the house stands on runs between Opende and Noordwijk.
26872: If you cannot hit an animal by shooting, you must put silver in the bullet. Then you will always hit the animal.
26873: My sister's husband's father is mortally ill and keeps getting out of bed to put on his best clothes. He dies and is buried. But every night something happens at the wardrobe, and the daughter hears rattling in it, just as the man had always done all his life. They see nothing, however. The man came to put on the clothes and walk away. The mother gets rid of the wardrobe and the rattling stops.
26874: If a child steps on a toad, a storm with thunder comes, and an apple from a witch that is kept becomes a toad.
26875: Tryn Liger is a devil and lives in Noordwikumerheide with two girls who call her grandmother. Later one of the girls has to give birth and Tryn kills the child. Neither is punished. My uncle later goes to live here alone but does not sleep in one of the box beds, sleeping in the back of the house instead. He gives no reason for this, and when my father is visiting one evening, at nine o'clock they hear a heavy thud on the empty beds. It is not the fat cat, though, and because the house is haunted, he sleeps at the back. Later Hendrik Dam comes to live in the house, and when his wife falls they do not want to say what caused it.
26876: Witches have dolls that they stick needles into.
26878: A farmhand comes to a girl who has heard from a fortune teller in Leeuwarden that he would drown before he turned 21. But the farmhand misheard the age. Until he is 21 he avoids ditches, canals, ponds and small lakes. Nothing happens, and he goes to live in Eiderburen. Around his forty-first year they are building a bridge, and in the evening the light has to be on. Then he trips, falls into the water and drowns.
26879: My mother and cousin are once doing vlakstappen (seasonal farm work) at a farmer's in Zoutkamp. The farmers are two bachelors with a maid. One night the cousin hears a small child, and the next night mother hears it too. This happens every night. When they buy bread from a baker in the village, they hear that the maid once had a child that the bachelors murdered. Since then she no longer goes out alone, but rides in a glass carriage between the brothers.
26890: Grandma once hears so much thundering and noise that the house shakes. She predicts that a tram or train will pass by in the future. That happens. It was a portent.
26891: Folkert Bruining's house on the Kaleweg is not right. One night he hears the loft being torn down, the roof tiles falling off the roof and the planks being thrown outside. When he goes to look, he sees nothing. He moves, and at the same time that he is building a sod hut, the old house is demolished.
26892: When my uncle gets pneumonia, which he also dies of, I am living alone with him. One time he wants to get out of bed and I cannot turn him, so I go to my neighbour Gerrit Smit for help. Outside I hear his footsteps, but it is a good hour before he actually comes. It was a premonition.
26893: Jan de Haan has had a few drinks at Durk van Dellen's, and Durk walks him part of the way home. Jan continues alone and is suddenly pushed to the side of the road. A train passes him. Yet no train or tram ever came.
26894: In Mieden a house is on fire one time, but when people go to look there is nothing to be seen. Later it does indeed burn down. It was a portent.
26895: Taeke Struiksma always attends church in Burum and sets out while it is still night. Once on the Kaleweg he walks into a bare wall at a spot where Arend Bekkema's house later comes to stand. It was a premonition.
26896: Bearn van der Woude sometimes sees funeral processions in advance.
26897: Someone once said that a girl would drown in a pool, but this never came true.
26899: On the heath in Drenthe witte wijven (white women) haunt.
26902: On the road, at the spot where Haring Pama now lives, Bearn Smook meets a little man wearing a felt hat who says not a single word and walks along with him as far as the Puntpaal. Then he disappears. Bearn was frightened. The little man is pitch black and snorts the whole time.
26905: A witch can turn herself into a cat. The mother of Knjillis Boorsma is one, and in the evening they see eight or nine cats sitting on the house. One of those cats once got a blow, and the next day a woman had a black eye.
26906: Witches stick needles into dolls and bewitch wreaths in pillows. The wreaths are burned.
26907: Roel Wonderman does not dare go home alone in the evening. He has talked himself into believing in ghosts. Once he drives as a coachman from home to Kollum at night. When he reaches the canal he sees the treetops bending over the water, although there is no wind.
26913: A witch can turn into an animal. When father is out poaching at full moon, he shoots at a hare. But it is Jelle Trijn, who the next day has a cloth around her head. She was shot in the neck.
26914: Rikele Myt is a witch who once fixed people to the spot in the apple orchard.
26919: Hindrik Pikelhearring is walking with someone else in Pein when he foresees that a dead person is coming by and that they must make way. They step aside. He sees funeral processions in advance because he was born with a caul.
26920: Jochum v.d. Berg once leaves the café of Goaitsen Jager and a thunderstorm starts. A man picks him up and throws him into a canal.
26923: Imke de Jong is a conjurer and makes people stand still. He also crawls into the pump. When the police chase him in Den Helder, he jumps into the water, swims under a big ship and surfaces. He is out of the police's sight.
26931: Fifty or sixty years ago, people from Kompenije and on the Folgerster laan saw lights beforehand and heard railway sounds. Later the tram came.
26933: If you are always looking in the mirror, the devil will wring your neck.
26945: Tsjerk Poel lives in Harkema and has volunteered for the army. He lives in a cottage where a Reformed church later stands. During his service he sometimes has to stand guard and gladly takes over others' duties for money. Tsjerk also stands guard at a place where things are not right and cats come. He cannot chase them away and finally fires his rifle. The next morning he sees that the old potato women are covered in bandages. The cats, which were witches, never came to that guard post again.
26947: Someone lives in Harkema, and when he comes back late from the farmer's he always meets an old woman on the path, whom he greets. She is always sweeping the path and the yard with a broom. One evening at full moon he sees the old woman standing in the yard again, leaning on her broom, although she has been dead for four months.
26949: In Lutsjewâld a man comes from the market who pretends to crawl through a tree, while he actually crawls past it, calling out whether the others can see him. Poortinga is the only one who sees him; he then throws him into the ditch and asks him whether he knows where he is now.
26953: Jehannes Koster always cycles to the oil mill where he works. Once he is very late, because he saw a funeral procession coming and stood behind a tree. First he sees four black dogs, followed by people in black. It was a phantom funeral.
26954: Eatse Kooistra and Sytse van der Ley come out of the pub and cycle home. On the way Eatse is boasting, and three times he is plucked off his bike and thrown into the ditch. Sytse, however, notices nothing.
26962: A mallemoel is a small bird, the size of a starling, that can swim and is only seen at sea. This bird in a net means bad weather the next day. Fishermen on the Dutch coast firmly believe this, just as people believe that a mermaid who shows herself brings bad weather.
26963: The kees is a whale-like mammal whose head comes above the water from time to time. When it appears the fishermen are glad, because it is a sign that a lot of herring is coming.
26977: In Parken there is a double house; an old woman lives in one half and a young couple in the other. One day four magpies are sitting in front of the young couple's half. In the evening a man comes to tell the young wife that Gerrit, her husband, has run off with the money. Gerrit sold fish for him and has gone to Nieuwstad in Groningen. The magpies were the omen of the visit.
26978: My daughter has been visiting my sister in Noordwijk and my brother-in-law takes her home on his bicycle. On the way he has a breakdown and the girl goes on alone. When she sees a woman in a white dress standing on the road, she greets her, but the woman stays silent and does not step aside. Years later the same thing happens to an uncle of Ouwe van der Molen. He sees the ghost woman standing in the pouring rain, and again she says nothing back.
26979: A farmer from Gelderland came to live here with his wife and children. Apart from the farmer, all of them are shy of people. He grows green peas on his land. Despite the farmer's warnings, my sister and a cousin go to the peas. At night she wakes up and sees a fat head with big eyes hanging there. This goes on for several nights and my sister grows thinner and thinner from fear. At my aunt's urging, my mother puts asafoetida on her chest and she is cured of seeing the head.
26980: A niece of mine only discovers after a room is added on that her house is haunted. When her daughter and her boyfriend Hinderik are sitting outside the door, they suddenly hear a heavy, thick footstep going past for an hour. It is full moon. When they go to look, there is nothing to be seen.
26981: My brother and his wife lived in a haunted house in Mieden, which at first they did not believe. However, every night they hear a heavy step cross the attic, go down the stairs, and then a noise in the cellar as if plates are being smashed there. My sister-in-law becomes frightened and they move.
26982: In a haunted house in Almelo a ghost always walks up the stairs.
26984: When Gurbe Steensma is catching moles in Almelo, he sleeps in a hut in the fields, where a little black man stays with him all night, dancing around.
26985: Gurbe also once saw near Almelo the treetops bending down to the ground.
26986: Mâlle Hindrik, Hiltsje's father, can do ventriloquism, fix people to the ground, see funeral processions, and make rhymes.
26989: A nightmare is a little old woman who goes through the keyhole. To be untroubled by a nightmare you must smear asafoetida on your chest and set your slippers in front of the bed back to front.
26991: In Pein in Groningen a cat was once struck, and the next day an old woman from the neighbourhood had a sore arm.
26992: Douwe Stavasius can foresee things, such as someone's death, or a sick person who later dies, whose entire funeral procession he already sees.
26993: At night you must always walk at the side of the road and never in the middle, because hearses drive past then, and otherwise you will be thrown off the road.
26994: Someone from Pein was once thrown to the ground when he came out of the pub. He had said he was not afraid of the devil, and promptly the devil seized him.
27007: A man from Harkema does not care about God, curses and is sometimes drunk. When, on the way back from Oostmeer, he walks along the little path across the Fûgelkamp, someone on the other side of the ditch keeps pace with him all the way to the house and stays standing in front of the door. As soon as the man lies down in the hay to sleep, the other begins to fight. It was the evil one.
27008: Some people see funeral processions in advance, and people have sometimes been put aside at night when a funeral procession was coming, or been lifted over it.
27009: Imke de Jong is at the market in Droegeham, and police officer Tseard van Dekken teases him by saying he does not believe in his magic. Imke then fixes the man to the spot.
27010: At the market someone crawls through a beam, but a man in the audience says this is not so, makes the crawler sit on top of it and hits him with a stick.
27014: If you eat an apple from a witch, you can be bewitched. If you leave it, it turns into a toad. Janne Lys is bewitched once, and once she spits out lots of little fish.
27026: Meint Pama lives in Veensterheide, and during the day a cat always sits on the well cover by his outside door. The cat always stays put; the son cannot manage it either and cannot open the cover. The cat is a witch.
27027: A magpie in front of the house means cheerfulness, and behind the house it means sadness.
27028: Hindrik Hylkema lives by the Leijdijk. Once, on his way to the farm, Hindrik sees two black figures walking across the field straight towards our house. When he reaches the dam, however, he no longer sees them. At the spot by the dam where the two vanished there used to be a convent, and they were two nuns.
27029: Vrouw van der Maar is married to a man who always comes home blind drunk and beats her. Despite being urged to leave him, she stays. When the devil deals harshly with the man, she leaves the house out of fear and misery and goes to live on a houseboat in the town.
27033: Some time after a man's death, he comes to visit his wife every evening. The doctor tells her to pay no attention to it, but the woman moves away anyway.
27036: Frans Rosier goes to prison to serve a sentence, but he keeps freeing himself from his cell. Even the governor cannot keep him in.
27042: Father and uncle Piter are once out hunting polecats in the Fûgelkamp in Harkema when they come across two small naked children holding hands. Father and uncle step aside to make way for them. The children were not given shrouds and therefore cannot find rest.
27043: It once happened that someone celebrated Holy Communion in a pub and afterwards had his neck wrung.
27046: A witch can easily change into a cat, and in that form they hold meetings with one another in the open air. Once every seven years the witch must kill someone, or else she will die herself. She bewitches a child by putting wreaths in its pillow. The wreath must be burned.
27047: Imke de Jong is at the same time at the Veenster market and in Ljouwert as a soldier. Locking him up is pointless because he can open all locks. Once, when the police are looking for him, he asks them for a lift in disguise. After a while he reveals who he is and then jumps across a wide canal.
27048: With a jack of spades you can make a bottle of liquor come, which I experienced myself on the Groningen clay lands.
27051: Near Ingwierum someone hears the sound of a steamboat, which only comes later. It was an omen.
27052: Sjoerd Bennema lives in Wâlden and his sister works as a maid there. At the inn, young farmhands mockingly held Communion. Outside they see a creature with glowing eyes. One farmhand flees into the fields and the next day they find him dead. His head has been twisted around on his body. In the snow they see tracks of very long strides the monster took.
27053: On the Wâlddyk, at the last bridge to Aldwâldumer Aldsyl, boys always try to cross the bridge in the biggest strides they can. One of them boasts that the devil could not do it, and promptly a creature appears that crosses the bridge in one step. It is the devil, who leaves the print of a club foot as proof.
27062: A woman from Westerein lived in Dokkumer Nijesilen. Her child falls ill through bewitchment. They make a fire, let it burn for a long time and put a frying pan with needles and pins in it on the fire, so that the heat makes them burst upwards.
27065: Thijs Pultrum visits his brother in Skieding and sees a light passing on the path behind the house, gets scared and quickly goes inside. He says there is a light there, but it disappears at once. It was voorloop (an apparition foreshadowing an event).
27067: A woman from Haulerwyk tells her son never to walk in the middle of the road in the dark, because a little hearse might come along.
27068: Near Luchtenfeld, close to Houtigehage, lives Halbe Scheper, a brother of Piter Scheper. The dogs pulling the dog cart suddenly stop on the road at a field gate and refuse to go on. There are berries on the cart. Although the dogs see something, they themselves see nothing.
27070: People are sitting at Taeke van der Meer's in Houtigehage, in the back of the house. Someone wants to have a bottle of liquor fetched, but Taeke puts a stop to it. The man already has the jack of spades laid out.
27075: A man who fears drowning drowns on a skating trip. The dead man looks so lifelike that people fear they are burying someone only apparently dead.
27135: On the Veensterheide you often hear hammering at places where a house later comes to stand. This has also been heard in Pein. You also hear knocking on the door while no one is there, and a little later someone really is there. Before a house burns down, people often see fire at that spot. This too is on the Veensterheide.
27136: Someone foresees a funeral. Later there is a death in Pein. He gets out of bed to see hearses.
27137: In Parken there is a deep peat pit. A man from the workhouse foretells that he has seen someone drown, and three weeks later it happens.
27139: Jelle's wife Tryntsje is a witch and flies through the air on a broomstick, sometimes as far as Drachten.
27145: In Parken and in Rottefalle witte wijven (white women) haunt.
27154: When a dog howls eerily, someone dies within three days.
27155: If you walk in the middle of the road, you can be flung aside by a funeral procession.
27156: A woman from Pein has died and her husband has not fulfilled his promise to her. That is why she keeps coming to him. The man approaches the minister to find out what she wants, and when he grants it, the haunting stops.
27157: On the Groninger Klaei there are haunted barns where at night you are simply rolled over or thrown away.
27158: On the Haring Land near Veensterheide it once happened that the devil just lifted someone up and threw him away.
27159: Witches change into cats that hold a meeting in the open field. They sit in a circle and sing. They also have dolls that they stick needles into.
27162: In the house of Lammert v.d. Sluis on the Drachtsterweg, next to Ouwe van der Molen, a neighbour once saw a fire, and two years later it burned down.
27163: Once when I take a horse to the meadow, I see a wilde lantaarn (wild lantern, ghost light) shining over the land, which stops at Wolter de Vries's and at another place where a school will be built. Wolter's house is later renovated.
27164: My mother and brother once come home together in the autumn. They see a light burning behind the house, and once they reach the yard they see that the light has moved. A back house was added to our house, and a new house was built at the other spot.
27166: The wife of Piter Veenstra once saw in advance a tram that went through everything. It later came as well.
27167: At night my brother hears noise at the doors and sees bearers carrying a coffin into the house. They tell him that his son is dead. The son is asleep, and later he does indeed die.
27168: We live on the Drachtsterweg near the woods, and sometimes at twelve o'clock at night we hear three blows of a sledgehammer in the Julianabuurt. Later the heath is reclaimed, and when the fencing is put up we hear the same sledgehammer blows.
27169: If you walk in the middle of the road at night, you can be flung aside by a funeral procession.
27175: A man from Pein is troubled by a witch in the form of a cat. Once the man put a piece of heirloom silver in the barrel of his gun and struck the cat on the head with it. A little later grandma gets a swollen head.
27177: One day there are many cats by the hut, and father has let loose the dogs, which chase the cats. Father himself hit one of the cats with the pitchfork, and a day later grandpa has a sore head. According to him it was from a fall onto the harrow. But it was really the pitchfork.
27179: My grandparents later live in the workhouse. Grandma is already dead and grandpa lies on his deathbed. When my parents are there he cries: come on devil, throw another bundle of sticks on! Grandpa and grandma have both been sold to the devil.
27180: My parents once go to visit my grandparents. When they are close to the house they hear a lot of noise coming from the shed, as if there were thirty people there. Once inside, they see only my grandparents sitting there.
27195: Father saw the tram on the Sumarreheide in advance. He sees the tram lights, and only a year later do they hear about a Belgian company that will build the tramline. Then the tram really comes.
27201: Father and Evert Bergsma from Tike are catching polecats together on the Gariperheide near Tuijen. There are tall trees there, and then Evert sees two trees coming towards him. They go around them. They are two white women wearing large, wide white skirts.
27204: Father is head farmhand for a farmer in Sumar, who also has an under-farmhand. The under-farmhand is often drunk and doesn't care about the devil, which he says out loud. After he has been drinking with someone else, they each go their own way at Albert Bosma's. The farmhand suddenly gets a blow to the head and tells father, who says he feels strange because he is drunk. But it is due to the devil's blow.
27205: From an early age people are warned never to walk in the middle of the road in the evening or at night, because a funeral procession might come. On the Summareweg someone was thrown aside in this way.
27206: Someone born with a caul can see everything. Tsjitske Spinder is such a person.
27212: Little Remmelt de Haan from Garyp is a pig dealer and according to others a freemason, because he has so much money. He has sold himself to the devil and is never short of money. This contract is signed with his own blood and there is no getting out of it. You must lie in a coffin for a while and every seven years one must die. They draw lots for who it will be.
27213: Jan van der Heide and Gjetsje van Eldring live in Drachtster Kompenije and before 1912 see lots of little lights on the Folgersterlaan. They think a waterway will come there and the lights are ships at night. But it is the tram, which comes in 1912.
27217: Someone is sitting in a little pub where the son of Imke de Jong is also present, performing all sorts of tricks. Cards flung against the wall stick there, and on command certain cards come back. He will also make a bottle of liquor come by throwing the jack of spades out under the window.
27222: A maid always has to bind grain in the field, which keeps falling out. She gets thoroughly fed up with it and once says that the devil may help her the next day. The next day a man comes to help her and tells her that whatever she binds first the day after will be his. The farmer suspects something when she comes back so early, and from her story he gathers that she has been sold to the devil. The farmer then prays the Lord's Prayer, the devil stays away, and the maid is saved.
27228: A few years before Wide Pet was built, we heard workmen at work at night, though they cannot be seen. During the building we hear the same sounds again.
27229: We hear our own house being built with hammering before the new house actually stands on the same spot.
27230: One night Wibe Alma and his friends are at the apple orchard of Goaitsen Rot-jonges on the Witveen when Wibe sees someone on a bicycle come right through the wall. They quickly run away.
27231: On the Skalkepad, which runs straight across the lane, a tall white woman haunts.
27233: When Sibe van der Veen comes out of the pub drunk, he is suddenly lifted up. He also always has a plaagbeest (tormenting beast) in the form of a black dog at his heels. According to mother, that is the devil.
27235: Witches can change into cats and bewitch people with wreaths in pillows. Harms Ale from Harkema is also a witch who bewitches children. Once when someone hits a cat, an old woman has a sore leg or arm the next day. If you burn the wreaths, the cats fly up against the window. People stop up the cracks to keep them out. Witches also hold meetings as cats.
27241: Wibe Alma loses his eighteen-year-old brother Paulus, and a man from Harkema had already foreseen this funeral.
27245: You must never walk in the middle of the road at night, because if a funeral procession comes, you will be thrown aside. This once happened in Harkema.
27246: Wibe Alma was once lifted off the road and flung across the canal when he came out of the pub. This happened before in Harkema. Sytse Jager too.
27247: An old woman on the Lytseweg was murdered, and a cross was then placed by the tree. Since then the woman haunts there and nobody dares to pass by in the evening anymore. Even when the tree is cut down, the cross appears in the new shoot.
27249: A witch sticks pins into dolls to hurt someone.
27250: Tseard van Dekken is a police officer in Droegeham and mocks Ymke de Jong at the market. Ymke then fixes him to the ground so that he cannot go anywhere.
27251: With an ace of clubs or jack of clubs and an empty bottle, people make a full bottle of jenever come. The bottle comes floating in, and if it is not taken, the one who ordered the bottle dies.
27252: In a black mirror the image appears of the woman the man will later marry. If he stays single, a coffin appears in the mirror.
27253: Detsje de Haan from Harkema always plays cards when she is pregnant. The child that is born then always has marks of playing cards on its chest and tail. This is the devil's punishment for playing cards, because he is in the cards.
27255: If you wear a caul, you are bulletproof, just like Freemasons who have a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back). You get the daalder if you walk around the churchyard three times with a cat in a sack, calling each time at the gate: 'Who will buy my cat for a daalder?'. The devil then buys the cat for the daalder, so you are never short of money.
27263: On the Goudberg between Noorderdwarsvaart and the Drachtster Kompenije a child haunts who was once murdered there. At midnight it begins to rage.
27265: Thomas and Clare live in Houtigehage and employ the boy Folkert. One day they see a coffin being carried into the house, but they cannot see who is lying in it. A short time later Folkert dies.
27267: The seventh son or daughter in a row is a werewolf or she-werewolf respectively. A werewolf must now and then shout something out or stab someone to death; he is untrustworthy. A she-werewolf is a man-hater. Both can enter the house through any little hole in the wall.
27268: Germ is the son of Ritske and Aeltsje from the Houtigehaagsterwijk. The child is bewitched and the devil-banisher tells them to cut open the pillow and look for three wreaths. If they are all finished, the child can no longer be helped. If not, they must stop up all the cracks and holes in the house and boil the wreaths in water. Lutske the witch comes to their door and cannot get in. She flies against the windows and writhes with pain. The child was indeed bewitched.
27272: Auntie lives in Houtigehage and is ill and old. One night a dog comes to howl eerily at her house and will not be chased away. Shortly afterwards Auntie dies.
27273: Chattering magpies around the house mean that there will soon be a death in that house.
27274: Boardzer Bruining and I are once catching moles, and on the way we see two magpies sitting on the left side of the verge. This is not a good sign, so we keep a close eye on the left side. There stand two policemen who want to catch us, because catching moles is forbidden.
27275: When a woman is expecting, she must not walk under a line, because then cords will wind around the child.
27276: Minse Griper from Boelenslaan can make a regiment of little soldiers, rooks or other animals come out of the hearth pit.
27277: In Groningen there is a black mirror, and if you look into it as an unmarried person, it foretells whom you will marry. If you were not going to marry, you are shown a coffin.
27278: You can make a bottle of liquor come by sending away the jack of clubs, which then fetches the bottle.
27279: Hinke Kaert is a card reader in Nijebrêge, and the devil once wrung her neck. That is how they found her.
27280: Thomas Clare, Antsje Snipel, Tryn Snipel and Durkje Snipel are all card readers. They work as follows. They look at the pictures, get nine cards, lay them on the table counting aloud and look at the cards one by one. Someone will, for example, get into trouble with the police but will not have to go to prison, and a small inheritance also awaits him. She shuffles the cards again and lays them out again. She always adds: 'this you don't expect and that you don't expect' and 'across the broad road a house, but that will surely turn out well'. Then she tells of coming events in a person's life. It costs a quarter.
27281: Some young people are coming back from the speed skating near Stiensgea, and one of them is a mocker who says he is not afraid of the devil and dares him to come. They go from Blaufallaet to Surhuzum, where a canal runs along the path, and the mocker keeps it up. Then a fat black fellow comes walking toward them and throws the braggart into the middle of the canal. The next day the boy comes home black and blue.
27283: I have sometimes heard hammering at night in Homaer. Houses were later built on that spot.
27284: Roanes Pander is a farmhand for Wierd's daughter and later marries her. Once, on his way home, he sees a hearse and goes back to Wierd. He is afraid.
27285: As Klaes and Simen are walking on the Reitsmaweg, Klaes says they must move aside to give the funeral procession room. Simen, however, does not see it.
27287: One evening we are out walking and a cat keeps running in front of someone's feet, although the animal is invisible. His wife can see it and warns him not to step on it. The man wants to kick the animal into the ditch, but he cannot. The animal accompanies them home. It was a witch.
27289: Wibe Alma from Jachtveld comes out of the pub and sees a woman sitting by the door of his house. He thinks it is Griet, but it is the evil one, and the doors open for him by themselves.
27290: Sytse Jager is in Smoarhoeke and goes behind the dike to relieve himself. He is a brute, and the devil throws him down very hard behind the dike. Wierd brought him home on a cart, and when they arrive they see the devil standing by the house as a white figure.
27291: In Homear two naked children are always wheeled back and forth in a wheelbarrow at night.
27292: A naked man haunts the Kruisweg.
27293: A man goes to fetch the midwife from Surhuisterveen and on the way sees a fellow standing by the churchyard, whom he greets politely. On the way back he is still standing there, and out of fear the midwife stayed at their house that night.
27294: When a maid once says she would like a suitor in the evening, even if it is the devil, he does come. He sat with her with a chain around his leg.
27295: Mike Ruerd from Harkema often fights with the devil
27296: During military service people sometimes make a bottle of liquor come by sending away the jack of spades, and they let the first bit run out.
27310: When a dog howls eerily, someone who lives nearby will soon die. It usually takes about three days.
27319: If you got an apple from an old woman, you had to put it in the cupboard. If the old woman was a witch, the apple turned into a spider after a few days.
27323: With a playing card you can make a bottle of liquor come. A group was once sitting at the table playing cards when the liquor ran out. They made a new bottle come. But when the bottle came floating in, nobody dared to take it. A sick, bedridden woman then did so, otherwise the bottle would have burst.
27325: When a dog howls eerily or the magpies chatter, someone will die.
27326: A man once saw a whole row of little lights approaching. Later a tram came there.
27331: A wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) was a rijksdaalder received from the devil. You were not allowed to spend all of it, only all but one cent. Then it always turned back into a rijksdaalder.
27344: At the place where people used to see lights going past, a tram later came to run.
27345: A woman once saw a house on fire, but in reality there was nothing. Later the house burned down after all.
27346: A woman sometimes heard hammering at a place where nothing could be seen. Later a new house was built there.
27348: When a dog howls eerily, someone will die soon.
27349: A woman once saw a light at a small labourer's cottage. Later a farm came there, with a great many lamps.
27352: Two men were out on the road one night. Suddenly one stepped aside. The other fell. He had been knocked down by a hearse.
27353: A man could make a bottle of drink come by sending out a playing card. But someone else then had to take the bottle, and nobody dared to.
27354: If you see a funeral procession at night, someone will die. If it happens after midnight, it may still take a while. It is just the same with wild lanterns and with hammering.
27355: Cries for help have sometimes been heard from a pond. People still expect that someone will drown in it one day.
27361: One must never promise anything to another shortly before their death. Because if one cannot keep it, the dead will never find rest in his grave and will haunt.
27363: Whatever you get from a witch, you must never eat entirely.
27368: Someone who looked into the black mirror saw the portrait of his future wife. If he was not going to marry, he was shown a coffin. Such a black mirror stood in a tent at the market. People had to leave that tent backwards.
27373: The little brother of a girl who had just died heard the coffin being brought. But in reality there was nothing. Only an hour later did the coffin really come. The boy heard exactly the same sounds again.
27374: A woman sometimes saw funeral processions in the evening. Then she would stand at the side of the road. For if she stayed in the middle, she would be thrown off the road.
27376: A certain road was always haunted. Several people saw various ghosts there. A little light was also often seen, and funeral processions were observed.
27377: In the old days it was haunted everywhere in Twijzelerheide. Some people were troubled by a plaagbeest (a tormenting spirit beast).
27382: Witches could fly through the air on a broomstick. When it rained on a Friday, they were baking pancakes. They turned themselves into cats and held meetings that way, with one cat in charge. Once every seven years a witch had to kill someone by witchcraft. If the witch did not, he or she would die.
27388: On the clay land there were haunted barns. If you slept in one, you were thrown from one place to another.
27389: Between the national highway and Twijzelerheide witte juffrouwen (white ladies) haunted.
27390: An apple from a witch turns into a toad. If you eat such an apple, you get a toad in your body and then you die. You must not step on a toad or a snail, for then it starts to thunder.
27391: The card readers in Leeuwarden had a black mirror. When a man looked into it, he saw the woman he would marry.
27392: Whoever sells himself to the devil gets a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back). Such a wisseldaalder always grows back to the full amount.
27394: A boy often saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, ghost lights). Later wagons came by.
27395: On his way back in the dark, a young man once saw a hearse. He stepped over it. Two weeks later an old fellow from the neighbourhood died, and the hearse really came by.
27396: A man once heard hammering on the other side of the water. Half a year later a new little house was built.
27397: Two men once saw a coffin covered with a white sheet being carried to the churchyard, while in reality there was nothing there. Later a woman in childbed from the neighbourhood died and the funeral really took place.
27399: A boy of about ten saw his house on fire. A year later the house really burned down.
27400: Knjillis Veenstra was born with a caul. He saw in advance that his own son would hang himself. He also saw in advance that his daughter would drown in the ditch. And he foresaw the death of his eldest daughter.
27401: Knjillis Veenstra predicted to a young man that he would marry and have a child, but that both would die. Then he would marry again and have a child, and then his second wife would also die. The man did not believe a word of it, but it did come true.
27408: A man once saw a funeral procession pass by. A few days later the funeral procession passed there in reality.
27409: One evening a young man saw a funeral procession pass by. Everyone was dressed in black and silent.
27410: A man was once sitting on the windowsill and saw the funeral of his wife. His wife was still alive at the time.
27411: A man once heard the sound of hammering. Not long after, a new house was built.
27412: Early one morning a carpenter saw a new house being built. But in reality there was nothing there. Later a new house did go up on that spot.
27415: Where the churchyard in Harkema is now, a wit wief (white woman) used to haunt.
27416: Where the football ground in Harkema is now, two naked women used to haunt.
27417: On the little plot of land by the big tree in Harkema there once stood a large house. There were children there who could find no rest and haunted the place.
27418: A dog often howled eerily near a pregnant woman. The woman was very worried. Shortly after the birth the baby died.
27424: A young man once got into a quarrel at the market over his girl. She tried to persuade him to move on, but he said he would move on for no one, not even for the devil. On the way back he could not get across a little bridge; he could not take another step. The devil was holding him back.
27434: Just before the war, three boys heard the bells of all the neighbouring villages ringing in the night. They had no idea what was going on. About half a year later they heard it again. But this time it was real, and it meant the war had begun and the boys had to go into service.
27435: A man once heard hammering coming from a school, while in reality nobody was there. Later a new house was built for the school, and the school itself was also renovated.
27436: Early one morning a young man saw a funeral procession pass by. There was a white sheet over the coffin. The procession came from the direction of the house of a pregnant woman. Indeed, that woman died in childbirth. Then the funeral procession really came by.
27440: Stuttering Harm sometimes lay on the bank and talked with the devil.
27443: Imke de Jong escaped from every prison. They could not hold him behind any door. When he left the town, he was seen at three different places.
27445: Near the Bovenweg in Westereinde a foal haunts with a porridge pot in its mouth.
27446: At a certain spot people sometimes saw two naked little children. They had been buried without shrouds.
27449: A man once let slip in the pub that if there was a devil, he should just grab him on the little bridge. When the man came to the bridge, a little man was standing there who grew bigger the closer he came. On the bridge the devil seized the man and threw him a long way. The man did not get across the bridge.
27457: At the fair young people went to the black mirror. In it they could see whom they would marry. But sometimes they were also shown a death.
27460: With a magic book one can make old rooks come out of the hearth pit.
27461: A girl dreams that her little brother is lying in a small coffin while her grandmother and mother stand looking at it. Some time later her little brother dies and her grandmother and mother stand looking at the little coffin.
27475: Someone with a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) never wants for anything. He can spend as much as he likes, but always a little less than the value of a wisseldaalder. Then he gets the whole amount back again. A wisseldaalder is obtained from the devil.
27476: A woman once saw a big thing standing on the table, but did not know what it was. A week later she got a sewing machine in a cabinet. It stood on the table. That was the thing she had seen before.
27480: When a dog howls eerily, someone from the neighbourhood will soon die.
27482: In the old days witte wieven (white women) haunted everywhere on the heath.
27483: A man regularly saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) passing by. Later the tram came to run there.
27484: A woman became afraid to sleep alone in the house when she regularly heard hammering at night. Later the house was renovated.
27485:
Biesterveld often visited an old woman. He would then say that he had seen her flying through the air on a broomstick again.
In 1880 people thought the world would end. The children stayed home from school.
Some people can make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
Bloodstains made during a murder can never be removed.
There are gates and doors that always open again by themselves.
27487: Durk Wonderman always had a big mouth and claimed he was not afraid of the devil. One evening a black cat was on his heels. That was the devil.
27488: A man sees a woman's funeral in advance; she dies in childbirth.
27489: A man once saw lots of wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps). Later a tramline came.
27490: A man warned people not to walk in the middle of the road at night, because they might run into a funeral procession. When a dog howls eerily, a death is coming.
27492: A man once clearly heard planks and beams being thrown about. But he saw nothing. Later a new orphanage was built.
27493: A man once saw a house on fire, but in reality there was nothing. Later the house really burned down.
27494: A magpie once came to the sister of a sick woman. Then it turned out that the sick woman had died.
27497: A farm maid once had a dog hanging on to her skirts for a whole evening. According to some it was a plaagbeest (a tormenting spectral beast), but according to the maid herself it was the devil in the shape of a dog.
27505: Witte juffrouwen (white ladies) haunted the Surhuisterveenseheide.
27507: A potato plant in a birch tree comes from a witch. While she was flying, her broom got stuck in the branches.
27512: Near the Zuiderdwarsvaart a woman with a yoke and buckets haunted.
27514: Biesterveld and his friend were walking together through the fields. His mate saw something come floating towards them. Biesterveld said that in that case they had to run away fast.
27516: The parents of a bewitched child found a wreath in his pillow. They sealed all the openings in the house properly, burnt the wreath and boiled a black hen. The witch then could not enter the house. The next day she came to the door with a burnt head. The child recovered.
27522: When a dog howls eerily, someone will soon die. When a barn owl screeches, someone will also die soon.
27523: One should not walk in the middle of the road in the evening or at night, or one may be put aside by a funeral procession.
27526: With the help of a jack of spades, some people can make a bottle of drink come. The card is taken outside with the empty bottle. A little later a full bottle comes floating in. That bottle comes from the devil.
27536: An apple from a witch turns into a toad. People never dared accept anything from Rikele Myt.
27541: Imke de Jong could make people stand still.
27544: An old witch could make a bottle of drink come with a jack of spades.
27545: A sorcerer could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. They would then start marching.
27549: A man who was born with a caul often had to get up at night to see funeral processions. That way he knew in advance that someone was going to die.
27550: A man who was born with a caul saw that a healthy man would soon die. It came true.
27552: Even before the railway was there, people heard the puffing of the train.
27553: At a sick woman's bedside the ticking of a watch was heard, though there was no clock at all. It was an omen; that night the woman died. This was called a wild watch.
27555: A house once burned down that people had already seen burning beforehand.
27556: In the Spooklaantje in Eestrum a witte juffrouw (white lady) haunted.
27557: A fellow drank a lot and said all sorts of things. Once he was followed by a little white rabbit. He thought it was the devil. After that he no longer drank.
27560: A boy always had to fetch milk. He was warned not to walk in the wheel ruts on the way, because he might be put aside by a funeral procession. He also had to watch out not to meet the devil.
27568: In the place where there is now a main road, people used to always see wild lanterns.
27573: A man who was born with a caul often had to get up at night to see funeral processions. That way he always knew in advance that someone would die.
27575: Douwe Stavasius (born with a caul) once foretold to a mother that her child would soon die. Within three weeks the child died.
27576: In the past people were always warned not to walk in the middle of the road because of the funeral processions that had to pass.
27577: A brother and a sister lived together. In the evening it sometimes happened that a hand came down from the attic and put out the petroleum lamp.
27580: A married couple were driving their dog cart. A funeral procession passed without their seeing it. They were put aside, cart and all.
27583: Imke de Jong once escaped from the prison in Leeuwarden. The lock had been no match for him.
27598: Early one morning a man saw the trees bend flat to the ground, although the weather was calm.
27601: Boardzer Bruining always saw funeral processions.
27619: Japik Ingberts could never be kept prisoner. He always got the doors open again without breaking the locks.
27621: A man was once cursing and boasting and claimed he would like to meet the devil some time. On the way back he saw a black thing with glowing eyes along the dike. He threw stones at it and the thing made a terrible noise. The man was terribly frightened and ran off quickly. The devil followed him all the way home.
27622: Two men were once hunting polecats when the dogs went for a hawthorn hedge. Behind the hedge the men saw a pair of glowing eyes. It was the devil. The dogs fled, and the men quickly went home.
27623: A young man once drank four shots of liquor at the inn. He said he would kill someone that evening. He went to his girlfriend at a farmer's. In the kitchen he half cut the maid's throat. The farmer stabbed the man with a pitchfork. The young man jumped through the window and was dead. The body was laid out at the farmer's. Later the threshing floor was haunted; the farmer often heard the young man's voice. He then moved away.
27631: People once saw a coffin standing at their friends' house. A few days later one of the friends died and the coffin really stood there.
27638: A man was a drinker and cursed a great deal. Once, as he was again coming out of the pub, he met the devil. They fought, and the man came home black and blue all over.
27639: A man was once cursing along the way. Then the devil came to him and threw him into the ditch.
27646: People who boasted in the pub that they were not afraid of the devil were quite often thrown down by the devil on the way back.
27648: In the past people were warned never to walk in the middle of the road, because a funeral procession might come by.
27656: In the woods at Augustinusga witte wieven (white women) haunt.
27658: Small children must never eat anything from a witch; that is dangerous.
27661: A place where a man had drowned was always haunted afterwards.
27662: A farming couple once secretly had their cow covered by a bull so that they would not have to pay. When they wanted to go back from the field, the gate suddenly burst into pieces. That was the devil's work.
27663: A father often took his son along when he went out in the evening. Once, on the way back, the boy said he saw something coming. The father asked whether it was walking or floating. It was floating, and the two quickly ran away.
27664: Some young people once celebrated Holy Communion in an inn. They received their punishment for the mockery.
27667: A man once saw a nightmare coming. It sat on his chest and squeezed the man's neck shut.
27668: A man often saw lights flying. Later he understood that they had been the forerunners of car headlights.
27669: A young man was once picked up by the devil on the road and flung down.
27670: A man was once coming home from work. The whole time he felt something following him. He said that whoever it was should go away, even if it was the devil himself. Then the man was lifted up and flung down again some way further on. The one who had done it sat in a tree, cackling like a magpie. That was the devil.
27671: A man saw funeral processions passing by at night. A while later there was then always a real funeral.
27682: A man was once put aside by a funeral procession. He ended up in the ditch.
27684: At a place where the tram later came, people had already seen little lights.
27685: People once saw a little light above a fen and thought that someone might drown in it one day. But that has not happened yet.
27688: When a dog howls eerily, someone will die soon. When magpies make a racket, that also means someone will die.
27691: Nobody wanted to live in a certain farmhouse, because every morning all the doors stood open.
27694: Some people could make a bottle of drink come with a jack of spades. If they then did not take the bottle, things did not go too well.
27704: A man once did not see a funeral procession coming and was thrown to the ground.
27705: People heard the sound of hammering and planks being thrown close to their house. But there was nothing to be seen. Later a new house was built.
27706: When magpies chatter close to a house, a death will follow. The same goes for when a dog howls eerily.
27707: People once saw a house on fire, but in reality nothing was wrong. Later the house really burned down.
27708: Even before the mill burned down, someone had already seen its sails on fire.
27716: A man once came out of the pub where he had been cursing. He had also said that he would like to meet the devil some time. When he was almost home, he was suddenly lifted up and thrown onto a tree trunk.
27717: A man was once flung around in a strange way, over dikes and everything.
27719: Four little children once burned to death in a house. Afterwards four small, naked children always haunted it.
27723: On the Groningen clay lands labourers used to sleep in barns. Some of those barns were haunted barns, where people were flung from one place to another.
27724: Someone sometimes had to get out of bed at night to see funeral processions. In the past people were warned not to walk in the middle of the road because of the funeral processions.
27725: Alle Tet was a witch, and she could turn herself into a black cat. Once, as a cat, she got a blow to her eye, and since then she had a black eye. Sometimes she bewitched a child. The parents would then go to Wopke, the duivelbanner (exorcist). He gave them a potion, with the warning that on the way back they would meet someone who would try to break the bottle. At home the wreath was taken out of the pillow and burned, and all the holes in the house were stopped up.
27729: Some people could make a bottle of drink come with a jack of spades. The full bottle would then float above the table. The person who had sent off the empty bottle was not allowed to take the full one. The first drop had to be thrown away; that was for the devil.
27730: In the old days there was a black mirror at the market. In it you could see whom you would marry. If someone saw a coffin, he would not marry.
27731: Some people could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit with a magic book.
27744: In Aldegea a foal with a porridge pot used to haunt.
27753: Ymke de Jong could do magic. He was in the army. When he threw the key against the door, it simply opened. The army could do nothing with him, so they just let him go.
27756: When Ymke de Jong quarrelled with someone, he made that person stand still.
27757: Someone once crawled through a wooden post at the market. Ymke then shouted that he was not crawling through it but around it, and he gave the other man a kick.
27758: In Aldegea a white lady used to haunt.
27762: A man heard hammering at night. Later a new house was built.
27763: A witch sometimes turns herself into a cat. As cats they hold meetings. Then they sing together. Sometimes someone wounded such a cat. Then the next day an old woman was injured. That was a witch.
27767: A man was convinced that a neighbour woman had bewitched his child. When the child was raging once again, he went to her house and smashed all the windows. He saw her busy with lots of dolls on the table.
27768: A man often went polecat hunting with Biesterveld. A witch can turn herself into a hare. Such a hare can never be hit, except with silver bullets.
27776: A group of boys was once doing the long jump. A fellow came up to them and showed that he could jump over the canal. It was the devil. On one side the print of a horseshoe remained, on the other side that of a human foot.
27778: On the Groningen clay there were haunted barns where the labourers slept. The doors would open there, and the horses would go driving off with the wagons.
27779: A farmer warned his labourer not to sleep in a certain spot in the barn, because there he would be lifted up at night and thrown down somewhere else.
27780: A man was once coming back from an evening of dice. Suddenly he was lifted up by the devil and put in the moat.
27782: People once heard the sound of hammering, but there was nothing to be seen. Later a new house appeared.
27783: People already heard the singing of psalms before a church was built in a certain place.
27784: A woman always saw many things happen in advance, including funerals.
27785: If a funeral procession comes along at night, you had best turn your back to it. There are things you are better off not seeing.
27790: Two men had once murdered an old woman. They were both thrown into the ditch.
27791: Wibe Alma was once coming out of the pub when he was knocked down.
27794: When a dog howls eerily, someone will die soon.
27797: A woman always wore a big black thing on her head. She was always going about begging. Her house was haunted: the chairs danced and the ember pot rattled.
27800: Witches fly through the air on a broomstick.
27802: A man had made a pact with the devil. He once saw a coffin being carried into a house. Later someone in that house died.
27805: Some people could make a bottle of drink come with a jack of spades.
27807: People once used to see wild lanterns. Later a new farm appeared on that spot.
27808: If you get an apple from a witch, you must cut it through. After that you can safely eat it.
