27809: A group of men once imitated Holy Communion in the pub. After a while they were shaken about and lifted up. They were thrown about and the doors opened by themselves.
27813: In a little lane near Garijp a dog always haunted. If you struck at the animal, your blow always went right through it.
27815: Every evening a dog howled eerily in front of the house of people with a sick baby. After a few days the baby died. The howling had been an omen.
27816: When a peacock screams, rain is coming.
27817: A woman who was born with a caul saw funeral processions in advance. That way she always knew that someone would die.
27818: Two brothers were walking home along the dike one evening when suddenly they were both flung off the dike. A funeral procession was passing. A few days later their mother died and the funeral procession really did pass by.
27819: A man once foresaw a hearse with a white horse in front. That never happened. A few days later a woman died, and a black horse was harnessed to the hearse. But the animal slipped, and then the milkman's white horse was harnessed to the hearse.
27822: One night someone hit a cat on the head. The next day the witch lay in bed with a black eye.
27829: A group of women were once on their way back home. At the bend in the road they saw a funeral procession, and then they did not dare go on. They turned back.
27830: Two brothers once owned a ship together. One brother had left his wife, and the other slept with her. The married man who had run off was on the ship when one evening a little dog suddenly stood barking in front of him. He was being punished by the devil because he had abandoned his wife and let her sleep with another. The man began to sing psalms, and then the little dog went away.
27832: Witches fly on a broomstick. They enter the house through the keyhole. If the butter will not come, a witch has been in the churn. Witches use books of magic.
27833: In the old days some people could fix others to the spot.
27834: 'Having looked in the black mirror' means you have been to a fortune-teller. In the black mirror you see a woman (whom you would later marry) or a coffin. Another way to find out whom you will marry is to break an egg into a cup. You must beat it and recite a rhyme. Then you can see in the beaten egg the image of the person you will marry.
27836: A man hardly ever worked; he only did a little trading. Yet he lived in grand style. He had made a pact with the devil. But he died a strange death: he fell and broke his neck.
27837: A group of farmers once celebrated Holy Communion in the pub. On the way back one of them was seized by the devil. He was thrown across the fields and through ditches. The next day his face was injured.
27838: One day the smith shod a horse with new horseshoes. But the next day the horseshoes were on back to front. The horse was bewitched; it was a ghost horse.
27839: People heard the sound of a tram at a certain spot. Later a tram really did come.
27840: People once saw a light in a certain place. Later a new house appeared on that spot.
27843: A young man once saw someone walking near the churchyard in the dark. But when he looked more closely, there was no one to be seen.
27849: A woman was out on the road one night when she suddenly ended up off the road in the ditch. A funeral procession had passed that she had not seen.
27851: At the spot where a lifeboat lay, strange noises were often heard.
27853: A married couple was once on their way back home when a man approached. But just as he passed them, the man turned into a horse.
27856: A foal haunted a certain spot.
27857: A certain spot was haunted. People were pelted there at night with stones and mud. When the police went to investigate, they found nothing.
27859: Mermaids can sing very beautifully. If a skipper saw a mermaid, the ship would be wrecked. They lure sailors into the sea so that they drown.
27862: Eight years after a woman has seen her nephew's funeral in a dream, the funeral becomes reality, exactly as she dreamed it.
27863: A woman once saw wild lanterns in a certain place. Later a new farm appeared on that spot.
27864: One evening a few children and their grandmother heard hammering outside. Later a new farm appeared.
27867: People once lived in a house where two old people had been murdered. At night they always heard noises there; the murdered people were haunting it. In the end the occupants became so frightened that they moved away.
27873: If sailors see a mermaid, the ship will meet with an accident.
27874: Near Eestrum a foal haunts with a porridge pan around its neck.
27875: A soldier once did not dare walk past a certain place. He saw a headless corporal walking there. Nor did he dare shoot at that corporal.
27876: In Groningen there used to be haunted barns. The doors there always opened by themselves and the wagons rolled back and forth across the floor by themselves.
27881: If you keep an apple that you got from a witch, it becomes a toad. In the old days farmers had a toad on a post by their house.
27891: A big dog always haunted a certain spot.
27892: A woman treated her husband very badly. After his death he came to her regularly and made the cups rattle. The woman was then very frightened.
27896: Two men were once pushed off the road by a funeral procession one night. One of them ended up in the ditch and drowned.
27897: A young couple were once out walking when they saw a black thing. They quickly ran back home.
27902: People used to often see wild lanterns on the heath. They were the forerunners of bicycle lamps.
27922: A man was out walking one evening when someone came to walk beside him. The man saw that he had a horse's foot: it was the devil. The devil said he was hunting souls, but that the man need not be afraid, because he was an honest fellow.
27932: A man thought only of money. He treated his wife very badly, even though she was very thrifty. Then once the man was suddenly thrown across the road. And all over the road lay money. But the man understood that it was the devil's money, and he learned his lesson.
27935: Two men once went hunting polecats. The path ran across the yard of a married couple. One man had been there before. That time he had seen a polecat on the road. His dog did not dare go at it. When the man tried to grab the animal, it suddenly vanished. This time the polecat was there again. The men approached the animal from either side. That way one of them managed to wound it. When the other came to the couple the next day, the wife had an injured hand. The men believed she had turned herself into a polecat the day before and that they had wounded her.
27937: A man was once lodging in Germany. Another lodger could do more than others; he was a sorcerer. He once asked the man whether he would like to see his dead grandmother again. The man did. Then that evening, when there were three knocks on his door, he had to open it. He did, and there stood his grandmother at the door. Both were silent, and when the man closed the door again, she had vanished.
27938: A sorcerer once wrote on an ace of clubs: "A bottle of jenever (Dutch gin) must come for this." He laid the card outside the door. The other man then had to take the bottle; he saw only a hand. He first threw some of the drink over his shoulder, and then they drank the rest.
27939: A farmer once challenged his labourer to sleep a night in his haunted house. The labourer was fine with that. But at twelve o'clock music came from the attic. Blood also came through the ceiling. Then two men and two women came into the bedroom and began to dance. The labourer stayed calmly in bed. The next day he told the farmer that blood had come through the ceiling, but the farmer did not respond to it. People had perhaps been murdered in the house, and the blood was a sign of that.
27948: A witch can turn herself into a black cat. People with a sick child were once convinced that the child had been bewitched by the black cat that sometimes came into the house. They tried to catch the cat, but could only wound it on its paw. The next day a witch was lame.
27952: Every seven years a witch must kill someone by witchcraft, or else she will die. Witches sometimes change into cats. In that form they hold meetings led by one of them. Then they also sing.
27955: Zwarte Akke was a witch. She pricked dolls with needles and pins. That is how she tormented people.
27958: In the black mirror people could see something of their future.
27961: A group of men once celebrated Holy Communion in the inn. When they went home that evening, one of them was chased by the devil. He flew straight through the ditch and so got home.
27962: A man was a great scoffer. Once when he lay ill in bed, people heard him screaming and raging very loudly. The next morning they found him with his head backwards on his body. That was the work of the devil.
27963: A fisherman was once chased by the devil. The man was so frightened that he sat down in a dry ditch and no longer dared to come out.
27973: A farmhand slept in the box bed in the empty stable. One night he saw himself lying there in a coffin. He was badly frightened and left the farmer. He thought he could escape his fate that way. Years later he came to visit the farmer. There he died suddenly. The coffin was taken into the stable, and so he came to lie there after all.
27974: A woman could always tell from the ticking of the clock that someone would die that week.
27975: A woman regularly heard planks being flung about. She knew then that another new house would be built.
27976: A woman often heard in advance that her son would come by. She also saw in advance that her grandson would get his diploma.
27977: A woman saw a coffin standing in her house, and after a few days it was gone again. Later her daughter fell ill and came to stay in her house. She died there, and then the coffin really stood there.
27978: A man was once walking past a house when he heard all kinds of noises. Stones and planks were being flung about. But there was nothing to be seen. Later the house was demolished, and he heard the same noises.
27979: People once saw a farm on fire. But when they came closer, nothing was wrong. Later the farm really burned down.
27987: A witch was always pricking all sorts of little dolls with pins.
27990: Some people once celebrated Holy Communion in the pub. They certainly received their punishment afterwards, and they also came to a strange end.
27991: People with a magic book can make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. When they read backwards again, the little soldiers disappear.
27992: On a spot where people used to see wild lanterns, a new house later appeared.
27994: In the old days witches conjured wreaths of feathers into people's pillows. Children were never allowed to accept or eat anything from them. If people got an apple and put it away for a few days, it turned into a toad. If they had eaten it, they would have been bewitched. A witch often turns herself into a cat.
27995: When someone takes his own life in a house, that spot is no longer right. It is haunted. Sometimes the ghost of the dead person is seen there. Such a haunted house was hard to sell.
27998: In the past people warned against walking in the middle of the road at night. You could be knocked down by a funeral procession.
28005: One evening a young man saw two men pass by. They made no reply to his greeting and suddenly vanished.
28006: In the old days there was quite a lot of haunting. The wagons would start turning by themselves, the horses jumped over the posts, and the animals became bewitched. The remedy was always asafoetida (devil's dung).
28007: Several people have seen a white lady haunting the churchyard of Wedze.
28008: In Buitenpost a foal haunts with a porridge pot around its neck.
28009: A man once heard noises as if planks were being thrown. There was nothing to be seen. Later a new house was built.
28011: Two men hunting polecats once saw a lamp hanging from a beam, and right after it had vanished. Later a new farm appeared on that spot.
28013: Stuttering Harm had a wisseldaalder (a magic coin that always returns to its owner). Nobody wanted to accept that magic coin, for fear they would never be rid of it. His wife was almost blind and treated him very badly. He could work magic. People never let him near their cattle, afraid that he would bewitch them. When he died, he lay in the coffin with his head turned backwards. That often happened to people who had made a pact with the devil.
28019: People saw tram lights at a spot where there was nothing. Later a tram really did come.
28022: A man was a great scoffer. Once he was walking with another man when they saw a glowing roof sheaf coming towards them. When it came closer, the roof sheaf turned into the devil himself.
28025: In Kornhorn, just outside the village, lived two brothers who were odd ones. Boozing and cursing, that they could do. Once they were sitting together on the pig cart. And then one of them was suddenly thrown off, without anyone being seen. That was the devil's work.
28029: When there are two magpies close to a house, something new will happen within a day and a half.
28032:
Hendrik van der Molen could make a bottle of drink come with the help of a playing card: the jack of spades. Someone else had to receive the bottle. If that was not done, the one who had put out the card with the bottle would die.
He could also make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit by whistling on his fingers. They marched on the hearth plate.
28036: At a spot where people used to see all sorts of lights, a tram later came to run.
28038: A woman often heard hammering in a certain place. Later a whole lot of new houses appeared there.
28039: A big black dog haunted a certain spot.
28040: Before someone died, a man sometimes saw a funeral procession pass by. He then knew that he would soon have to ring the bells again.
28047: A rather strange man was once thrown by the devil from one side of the road to the other. Later the man became very pious.
28049: A man once heard the churns working in the churning house. But when they went to look, there was nothing to be seen.
28050: A man once saw two strange figures approaching. He prayed that if they came from the devil, they would disappear. Then they were gone.
28051: For a long time people saw all sorts of lights. Later a goods train came.
28053: In Nuis a few figures haunted the churchyard.
28056: A woman saw the funeral of her sick husband in advance.
28058: An old fellow with a garibaldi hat on his head and a red cloth around his neck always haunted a certain spot. His gold and silver were buried there. Once three men dug up the chest and the haunting was over.
28059: Someone who eats something from a witch can get a toad in his stomach. That is not good at all.
28060: A little child began crying every night at twelve o'clock. Once the parents took the child into their bed, and then the mother felt the pain. A witch was pricking a doll to hurt the child. The parents went to the duivelbanner (exorcist) and were given a potion for the child. After that things got better. From then on the child also had to carry asafoetida (devil's dung) on them.
28063: If someone looks into the black mirror, he gets to see his future wife. If he is not to marry, he sees a coffin.
28064: By reading from her magic book, a woman could conjure little soldiers from the hearth pit. When she then read backwards, the little soldiers disappeared again. Her granddaughter got the book after her death. But she could not read backwards so quickly and became frightened by it. She burned the book.
28065: Stotterende Harm (Stuttering Harm) had a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back). It was blue. His little nephew was sometimes given money to take to his mother, but by the time he got home the money had always disappeared.
28078: One night people heard hammering in their house. Not long after, the house was renovated.
28079: A mother and her little son once saw a house on fire, but in reality there was nothing. Three weeks later the house really burned down.
28080: A little boy once saw from his bed two men bringing a small coffin into the house. He was too afraid to get out of bed. Later his little sister died and the men really came to bring the coffin.
28081: A woman often saw in advance that someone would die. Once she saw a coffin with a white cloth over it. Then she knew that a woman would soon die in childbed. That came true.
28082: A woman often had to get up at night to see funeral processions. She was forced to do so.
28083: A woman once heard children screaming in an empty house. She predicted that a family with children would soon come to live there. That indeed happened.
28084: When a dog howls eerily, someone will die soon.
28085: If a magpie comes to the window, someone will die. If a magpie chatters in the yard, that also means something is about to happen, but it need not be something unpleasant. It can also announce a birth.
28086: During the war a group of Frisians were once working in the fields. A magpie was chattering a few metres away, and they thought something was about to happen. Half an hour later the Krauts came with big trucks and took the men away.
28087: A man once saw a coffin being brought into his house. Shortly afterwards his wife died. The coffin was placed exactly where he had seen it. Later the man also foresaw his own funeral.
28088: A group of men were out on the road one night when one of them warned that they had to move aside. He saw a funeral procession coming. The others saw nothing. He listed everyone he saw walking in the procession. Shortly afterwards someone died, and a week later the procession really walked there.
28089: Two men were once coming back from a polecat hunt. Suddenly one of them was pushed off his bicycle and ended up in the ditch. A funeral procession was probably passing.
28090: A man once came out of the pub drunk. He had just said he was not afraid of the devil when he noticed someone walking beside him. It was the devil. The devil went with him into his house and gave him a good beating there.
28091: A man always had rather a big mouth. One evening he was thrown off a little bridge straight into the ditch. That was the devil's punishment.
28092: A man had a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back). He had sold himself to the devil.
28100: Someone once hit a cat because he thought it was a witch. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood was lame.
28104: A man once came drunk to his friend's grave. He mocked that he would much rather lie in the sea than here in the churchyard. Not long after, he was fishing at sea. There was no wind, yet he fell into the water. People threw him something, but he covered his eyes with his hands and let himself sink. That was his punishment.
28110: When the evening sun makes it look as if a house is on fire, a strong wind is coming. When the gulls glide high in the sky without moving their wings, a strong wind is coming too. When the sky is completely clear, without a single cloud, rain will come within three days.
28115: Two men were once on the road when one warned the other to step aside. A funeral procession was coming. Not long after, a girl living on that road died, and the funeral procession really did pass by.
28116: A man once came out of the inn. On the way home he was suddenly thrown off the road into the ditch. He said: "Damn it, do that again." Then it happened again. "Again," he said. And again he was thrown into the water. Then he no longer dared to ask, because he realised it was the devil.
28117: A fellow was always mocking, cursing and drinking to his heart's content. One day he was found with his head turned backwards on his body. The devil had wrung his neck.
28118: A few men once celebrated Holy Communion in an inn. When they went home, one of them was thrown into the ditch three or four times. That was the devil's punishment.
28119: Never step on a snail. Then it will start to thunder. If a snail has mud on its tail, we will get rain.
28120: Some people can make a bottle of drink come with a playing card. It has to be a black jack. The jack of spades is the devil; it is the one with the axe.
28121: In Dokkum there lived a fortune teller with a black mirror.
28122: Some people can make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
28134: A man once said that he would like to see the devil, if he really existed. Then he cursed terribly. A little later the devil came and flung him a long way.
28135: A cow haunted a little bridge. It always began to low when people came near the trees.
28136: A dog haunted beneath a dam. It was always there and sometimes barked.
28137: A piebald calf haunted a certain spot and always walked alongside you for a while.
28141: People sometimes saw a naked girl come out of the Leeuwenpoel.
28143: Two girls wearing red aprons once drowned in a small lake. Later people sometimes still saw the girls haunting there.
28144: A man was born with a caul. Once he saw the door of the house open and a coffin come in. A few days later his wife died.
28145: A man had been born with a caul. Once he came to fetch a saw from his neighbour, when suddenly he could not walk any further. He said a corpse was passing by. A few days later the neighbour's father, who lived with his daughter, died.
28146: A small group of boys was once standing by the towing canal. One of them claimed the canal was so wide that not even the devil could jump over it. A little later someone came along and jumped right over the canal. The print of a horse's hoof can still be seen at the spot. It was the devil.
28151: A young man once joked on the way about going to see his girlfriend again. On the way back a huge dog then jumped on his neck. The dog was pitch black. According to his mother it was the devil, punishing him for his mockery.
28153: Stotterende Harm (Stuttering Harm) had a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back). He could also do witchcraft. People never let him into the stable, because when he came near the cattle they fell ill. When someone was bewitched, people went to Wopke in Kûkherne.
28154: A woman was going home late one evening when she saw a black figure wearing a large cloak. He rattled the whole time. The next day the woman received word that her neighbour's child had died. The messenger was a man dressed entirely in black, with a cocked hat on and a large thing on his chest that rattled. What the woman had seen the evening before had been an omen.
28155: One night a young man was chased by a big black dog. The young man had a revolver and wanted to shoot the beast. But he did not have the power to do it. That dog was the devil.
28157: A woman was once bewitched by Alle Tet. She and her husband went to Wopke, the duivelbanner (exorcist). He had her hold two bottles. She was not allowed to let go. Then some cats came onto the barn, wailing and raging. The next day Alle Tet was black and blue all over. But the woman was cured.
28162: Some people could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. Someone could make a pin spin on a needle. And he could turn somersaults non-stop across a whole stretch of land. He had a magic book.
28165: A foal with a porridge pan around its neck haunted a certain spot.
28183: A woman who was born with a caul had seen a funeral. All the men wore top hats except one, who wore a cap. The next day someone from the neighbourhood died. A few days later he was taken to the churchyard. His eldest son walked behind wearing a cap; the other men all wore top hats.
28184: A woman who was born with a caul once predicted that a towboat would be carrying a corpse that day. Indeed, that evening a towboat arrived with its flag at half-mast.
28194: Six soldiers were on patrol one night when they heard galloping horses and running dogs approaching. They quickly lay down on the ground. But they saw nothing at all go by. It was an omen of the Germans who crossed the border in 1940.
28195: A man was once on his way to work when something as big as a person floated past above him.
28196: A boy was once coming back from his girlfriend's. Suddenly a woman without feet floated past him. She did not answer his greeting. He thought it was the ghost of a woman who had been murdered at that spot.
28197: A few men once stood by a little bridge cursing and swearing heavily. Then the devil came and punished the men. The devil's print can still be seen on the bridge.
28198: Two men once came out of the pub drunk. Suddenly one of them was picked up and thrown against the wall of a farmhouse.
28199: In Groningen people were quite often murdered in the old days. A farmer told his labourers not to sleep by a certain beam, because something was wrong there. One of them did so anyway and was thrown away that night.
28203: In the old days people were warned not to walk in the middle of the road at night. Otherwise they could be pushed aside by a funeral procession.
28204: A witch can turn herself into a cat. It sometimes happened that someone gave such a cat a wallop, and the next day the witch turned out to be injured. Witches bewitched children by making them eat something. Then the child fell ill and the parents went to the wonderdokter (folk healer). If a witch gave a child an apple and the child ate it, he got a toad in his stomach.
28207: Small children who are not given grave clothes in their coffin find no rest. They always wander about afterwards. Often they dance around the posts in farmers' barns.
28208: When witches have changed into cats, they hold a meeting. One of them is then in charge.
28210: Witches float through the air on a broomstick. That is also how they go to the wine cellar in Spain.
28219: People saw the lights of the tram beforehand. People had also seen wagons without horses.
28220: In a place where a house was later built, people had earlier seen a lamp.
28221: Near Opeinde, people often heard hammering. A new house would then always appear on that spot later.
28223: In the old days people were warned not to walk in the middle of the road. Otherwise the old fellow would grab them. Then you were thrown from one place to another. It could also happen that you were pushed aside by a funeral procession.
28225: People once saw a coffin being carried into the house of a sick person. A few days later the sick person died and the coffin was really carried into the house.
28232: At the place where Rudolf de Mepsche lived in Faan, people can still be heard wailing. He had chained people there and driven nails through their feet.
28233: In the past there was usually a fortune teller's tent with a black mirror at the fair. In it you saw which woman you would marry. You had to leave the tent backwards.
28234: A couple of brothers could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. They could also send out a card for a bottle of jenever. The one who sent the card was not allowed to accept the full bottle. If nobody accepted it, he would die.
28242: On the Achterweg in Surhuizum a black-and-white dog without a tail used to haunt.
28243: A witch often turned herself into a hare in the evening. The neighbour always tried to shoot the animal dead, but he could never hit it.
28244: At a farm the barn door always stood open. A labourer who had to cross the yard sees a white female figure standing there. He strikes at her with a shovel, right through her. The figure goes through the open door. A woman is said to have hanged herself in that doorway long ago. It turns out another labourer experienced the same thing.
28253: A man could not sleep at night in his caravan because of the noise and all the lights he heard and saw. Later the national highway came. Several people had also seen the tram running beforehand.
28257: A boy once saw a house on fire. The next day the house really burned down.
28258: One night a boy saw a vision of his brother in socks that were far too big. The next day his brother fell into the canal and was given a pair of dry socks by the schoolmaster.
28259: If magpies come into someone's yard and start chattering, they bring news of death.
28261: Two young men were once sitting in the pub drinking and swearing. That evening they each wanted a girl; they would go off with the first one they came across. But when they came out of the inn, a couple came by, and they gave the young men a thorough beating. They belonged to the devil.
28262: Some young people once celebrated Holy Communion in the pub. They came out of the pub in a strange way, and got home in an even stranger way. Our dear Lord will not be mocked.
28265: A man once heard a hammer striking an anvil, while there was nothing to be seen. Later a smithy appeared on that spot.
28266: A man once heard wagons driving where there was not even a road. Later a road was built on that spot and wagons really drove there.
28271: In the old days it happened that the churn was bewitched. Then no butter could be made.
28276: A child was once murdered in a house. Since then the knocking of the child's ghost was heard there every evening.
28278: Where people used to see wild lanterns, new houses were later built.
28279: A young man was once coming back from his sweetheart's when he saw a white woman haunting.
28280: In Harkema four little children once burned to death in a house. Since then the children have haunted the place.
28281: People used to see wild lanterns now and then. Later a new house would appear on such a spot.
28286:
If you dream of a horse, a death will follow.
A man once dreamed of running horses. The following week a relative died. The horses in the dream had been the horses of the hearse.
28287: If you dream of a pike, a death will follow. The finer the fish, the closer the dead person is in the family. If you dream of a snake, you are keeping company with bad people.
28288: A farmer's labourers slept in the barn. One night a few women heard something, but there was nothing to be seen.
28290: A boy once could not get out past his gate, because lots of men in black were walking by. It was probably a funeral procession.
28295: Egbert Sint had a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back). He had sold himself to the devil and so was never short of money. To get a wisseldaalder, you have to walk around a churchyard three times with a black cat in a sack. And then you must say: "Who wants to buy my little black cat?" Then you get a wisseldaalder.
28312: One night a woman heard hammering and the throwing of planks outside. A year later a new house was built.
28313: One night a man saw a funeral procession go by. A week later someone really was buried.
28315: At a certain spot a calf and a black dog used to haunt. The dog would walk along with people and then go back again.
28319: A young farmhand always went to the fields in the morning to milk the sheep. Once a white figure lay in wait for him. He turned back, but the next day it happened again. On the third day someone else went, and he struck the 'ghost' with a piece of iron.
28322: One night a man could not walk on because a funeral procession was passing.
28323: One night Ruerd van der Veen saw someone walking ahead of him. He called out that he should wait for him so they could walk together. But the other just kept walking. Then Ruerd threatened to knock him down if he did not wait. The other then stopped. When Ruerd reached him, the other grabbed him several times and threw him over the trees. The next day they found him unconscious with all his ribs broken.
28324: A young man once saw something floating in front of him.
28327: A man once saw a house on fire. But when he came closer, nothing was wrong. Later the house burned down after all.
28328: People once heard hammering in the night. Later a new house appeared on that spot.
28329: A woman once saw two figures dressed in black put something wooden in the shed. A few weeks later one of her children died, and the men came to put a coffin in the shed.
28330: A woman heard footsteps outside at night and could not sleep because of them. Later that night her brother came to say that the little son of another relative had been run over by a milk cart. Ever since, the child's mother had been walking back and forth at that spot. Those were the footsteps the woman had heard all night.
28331: A boy was once on his way to his girlfriend when he was pushed aside by a funeral procession. Later his girlfriend's grandmother died; he lived in her house. It was her funeral procession he had seen pass.
28332: One night a man was thrown from the dike across the heath, a good fifty metres. And there was no one to be seen. It had been the work of the devil.
28333: In a house with a group of big boys there was a lot of cursing. One day one of the boys suddenly died. That was the work of the devil. After that the boys kept quiet.
28334: A man had treated his first wife rather badly. After her death he remarried. Every evening when he lay in bed, he heard knocking on the bed. It was his dead wife. In the end it stopped.
28335: A farmer treated his maid very badly. She fell ill and died. The farmer and his wife kept the maid's belongings. From then on there was a commotion at the churning mill every evening. It was the maid coming for her things. One evening the farmer put everything in a sack and set it by the churning mill. The next morning the sack was gone. Nothing was ever heard of the maid again.
28336: A woman often read the Bible. Once a black finger kept turning the page back, and the woman no longer dared to read on. The minister told her that she should then turn the page forward again; she had to resist. The next time the woman did so, and then the finger never came back.
28337: A man was once sitting in the pub when another man asked him whether he would like to see his dead mother. The man said he would. That evening there was a knock at his door. He opened it and saw his mother in the street.
28352: People heard wagons driving at a certain spot. Later a new polder was laid out there.
28353: People heard a train going over the rails at a spot, but in reality there was nothing. Later a train really did come to run there.
28354: A man knew he would die by fire. He was struck by lightning.
28355: Two men in a carriage once did not see a funeral procession coming. The horse did, and kept trying to go to the side. Then they were suddenly driven onto the verge and off the dike.
28358: A woman once saw her husband coming home with a sack of rags. But when it took very long for him to come into the house, the woman went outside to look. There was no one to be seen. The man only came home half an hour later.
28359: A couple once saw an acquaintance approaching, and they opened the door. But there was no one outside. A quarter of an hour later that person really did arrive.
28360: A woman once saw a house on fire. Later that house really burned down.
28363: An apple you get from a witch turns into a toad or a frog. A witch can turn herself into a cat.
28365: Some people were once bewitched by a cat. One of them shot at the cat with a gun and hit the animal in the head. The next day there was an old woman who had no eyes left. Then the people knew at once that she was the witch.
28366: Witches can turn themselves into a hare. They can also fly through the air with a broomstick between their legs.
28368: A boy was born with a caul and saw things in advance. Once he said that a woman had come by three times that day. But in reality she only came the next day.
28369: A group of young people once heard people singing psalms in the church. But there was no one at all in the church.
28371: A foal with a porridge pan around its neck haunted a certain spot.
28373: At a certain spot someone with a lantern always haunted.
28374: A man once said that strange times were coming. He had seen a potato with a fork in it in the sky. Shortly afterwards the Second World War began.
28375: Witches fly through the air on brooms. A black cat without any white on it at all is a witch.
28376: A man once heard the barn owls calling. He predicted that the sick neighbour woman would die. That happened soon after.
28377: If the weight of the clock fell, it meant that someone would soon die.
28378:
Just before a boy died, lots of magpies had been sitting around his house. After his death the canary never sang again.
When a man died, a cat kept wanting to sit on his coffin. Not long after, all the cats in the house died.
If a dog howls eerily, someone will soon die.
28380: A place where a man had hanged himself was later haunted.
28381: A few young men once heard a droning in the sky. They were frightened. It was a foreshadowing of the aeroplanes that came later.
28382: Someone who is buried without a shroud appears again later. The dead also cannot find rest if the cloth with which he was washed does not go into the coffin with him.
28386: A woman once predicted that that month would be a very rough month.
28387: A woman was once pushed off the road by a funeral procession. There was a rather sick boy, but she made sure he got better.
28389:
A woman was to come and help at the birth of her daughter-in-law's child. When her son came to fetch her, she said she had already heard him knock twice that morning.
A girl had to marry her boyfriend. A woman told another girl that the same would soon happen to her. Two months later it had already come to that.
28394: Sometimes there was knocking behind the wallpaper. Then a death would come to the house.
28414: A man had promised his wife to do something after her death, but he did not do it. Once, when he was sitting outside on the privy, the woman suddenly stood before him. The man was afraid and promised to keep the promise after all. He did, and since then the woman has never come back.
28415: If you eat something from a witch, you can get a toad in your body. Then you die.
28418: With a jack of spades one can make a bottle of drink come. The devil hands over the bottle.
28419: Imke Modder could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. He also once pulled a ribbon out of his neck that had no end.
28429: A boy once heard hammering in an old school, but in reality there was nothing. Later the school was rebuilt.
28430: At a certain spot, in stormy weather, people saw lots of lights along the roads. Later many houses were built there.
28431: Even before there was a railway line, people had heard a train running there.
28432: Someone heard hammering at night. Later new houses were built.
28435: One evening a man stopped to light his pipe when suddenly someone was standing beside him. This person lit his own pipe from the man's light, and then he was gone again.
28436: One evening two men were pushed off the road. They had seen nothing, but a funeral procession had probably passed.
28439: If someone had died and still had a wish, he later appeared to people. Then they had to lay what he wished for on the grave. It was usually about clothes.
28440: At a certain spot a few naked little children floated about.
28443: When the mermaids sing, a death will follow. A mermaid is half human, half fish.
28444: On the Bovenweg in Westereinde a foal haunts with a porridge pot around its neck. There is also a brown horse standing with its head over the gate.
28447: Two children in a family had been ill for years. An acquaintance often came to visit and would bring something for the children. The man was said to be a wizard, but the parents did not believe it at all. One day they found witches' wreaths, woven from coloured feathers, all over the children's beds. Then the acquaintance fell ill and died. From that time on the two children got better.
28448: A witch pricked dolls. Then the children she had bewitched cried.
28449: If a dog howls eerily, there will soon be a death. Sometimes such a dog lies in front of the door of the person who is going to die.
28471: Some men are playing cards in a pub in Beets when one of them sends off a card for a bottle of drink. Someone else has to catch it, or the sender will die. The card is thrown through the door and a little later the bottle comes through, landing on the floor. An invisible hand then puts it on the table. Nobody drinks from it, though; they go home and never play cards again.
28472: My wife worked as a cleaner for a farmer and his wife in Ljouwert. When the farmer's wife was still in service, she went with a friend to the inn of Lammert de Jong, where there was a mirror that showed whom you would later marry. She saw her future husband in the mirror, while her friend saw a coffin. The friend never married.
28476: Mrs Wiersma of the Salvation Army was born with a caul and saw in advance her own daughter drowning in the water near Snits.
28477: A brother of my wife's grandmother could also predict things. In 1825 he arrives pale at his sister's house and wants to leave again at once, because he has seen that the dikes near his home have burst and has seen the house floating. When he returns, the people in his house have indeed drowned and the house is floating on the water. He is a helmdrager (one born with a caul).
28479: Old Black Jantjse was born with a caul and is a witch. Once, in the middle of a conversation, her face turns pale and she stares at a particular spot on the other side. She sees a corpse coming out of the door. The others do not believe it, because nobody is ill. Three weeks later someone in that house does indeed die.
28480: In Feanwâldsterwâl people hear hammering all night at a certain spot, but see nothing. Later their son returns from America and suggests fixing up and remodelling the old house. These are the sounds they had heard earlier.
28482: An uncle of mine is walking through Terwispel with a mate when he suddenly says they must step aside, because a funeral procession is coming. His mate, however, stays in the middle of the path and is then lifted up and set down further on.
28483: In a pub in Feanwâldsterwâl a man plays curse words on an accordion. After closing time he walks to Feanwâlderhoek at night and is attacked by the devil. When he gets home he is so frightened that he never sees the door and goes in through the windows.
28496: In Harkema people hear hammering at night at a spot near Smoarhoeke, but there is nothing to be seen there. Later a house is built on that spot.
28497: At night in the woods at Harkema, Praamsma sees a funeral procession and becomes frightened. A little later old Melle Dieuwke in Bosk dies. He had seen this in advance.
28499: On the Rijkslaan a group of young people is simply pushed aside and a funeral procession passes. People also sometimes stumble when one comes by, or are set on the front of the hearse and thrown off again at the back.
28500: An old man falls ill and says at one point that there are many people in the house, naming them all. At that moment only one of them is present. When the man dies, the very people he named do indeed come.
28505: Old Wibe Alma was also once thrown away near the Langewijk when he was coming back from the pub.
28506: Hindrik Holthuis was also once thrown away and afterwards was converted into a pious man.
28507: A farmhand from Harkema swears like a heathen, and one day the house of Rinse de Wind is on fire. A number of people go there, but the farmhand is thrown away, bicycle and all, several times in a row. It was the devil's payment for mockery.
28514: Jille Antsje lives in Petten, was born with a caul and sees everything in advance.
28517: In Surhuzum people celebrated communion in an inn. It was mockery, and on the way home they were thrown away by the devil.
28519: A witch can change into a cat. While she is away, her belly lies in bed, and if you prick it the witch dies. As cats they sometimes hold meetings and then talk very busily with one another about what they should bewitch.
28520: If someone is not treated well and dies, he finds no rest and wanders around the people who treated him badly.
28521: A witch's apple turns into a toad if you leave it lying.
28524: Reid Keuning of Koatstertille makes little soldiers come out of the hearth and makes them run across the floor.
28539: In Beets a man swears all evening in a café. Around closing time he is afraid to go home because he expects a beating. He has to go outside anyway, and a little later he is indeed beaten up by the devil. The next day he is black and blue.
28540: Young people once held a mock communion in an inn in Veenwouden. On the way home they are beaten and abused.
28543: Someone is walking on the Gordijk when it starts to rain and takes shelter in a café where men are playing cards. One of them swears like a heathen. Then a jack of diamonds goes missing and they cannot find it. The mocker says that if the devil has the card, he will surely get it back. After he finds the card he is beaten so badly that he lies wailing on the floor.
28544: A blacksmith is murdered at the Goddeloos Tolhek between the Falom and Veenwouden and has haunted the place ever since. He walks from the gate to the bridge. One day some people are standing on the bridge when the blacksmith's murderer comes walking along, and they see the blacksmith and his murderer fighting. The haunting stops.
28546: Friends of ours sail on a ship, and the wife loses her sister. But the sister keeps haunting after her death because something was not done properly at her death. One night she indicates what she is missing, and once this is done the haunting stops. She has found rest.
28547: In Beets my parents-in-law cut peat, and the surveyor often cheats them. He keeps the remaining rods for himself. On top of that, people are obliged to buy groceries from him at outrageous prices. When he dies he is buried. The next day the surveyor stands at the gate with the measuring rod in his hand. When someone asks him what he wants, he says they must forgive him. When they do, they never see him again.
28548: Black Jantsje is doing her shopping in the shop and looks very closely at another woman. She always talks about the dead and funeral processions. When the woman has been served and walks out of the shop, Jantsje says she will be dead within three days. And so it is, for she falls down the stairs at the district court and dies.
28557: Witches stick pins into dolls to hurt people.
28560: In Bulten someone once hit a strange cat on the head, and the next day Alle Tet has a bruise on her head.
28561: Willem Pyk has a dog that sometimes howls eerily. According to his wife Jits this is an omen of a death, while their neighbour thinks the dog is seeing the devil.
28562: On the Bosweg stands a haunted house where a German was once murdered, and he has haunted it ever since.
28571: When someone is standing on the bridge at Veenwouderwal, he hears a sound below as if someone is calling for help. A while later two boys skate into a hole in the ice, and then the same sound as before is heard.
28574: Witches often change themselves into cats, which hold a meeting together. They sit in a circle.
28575: Witches stick pins into dolls to cause pain to those they dislike.
28576: Joukje is a witch and quarrels with another woman, turns herself into a cat and visits the woman in that form. She scratches the woman, but the woman breaks the animal's paw with a hard blow. The next day the woman hears that Joukje has fallen out of bed and broken her leg. She contradicts her neighbour and says that she herself smashed Joukje's leg.
28586: An apple given by the witch should not be eaten but put away, and it later turns into a toad.
28588: Harm Schievink once predicted that Harkema would become a town, though he would not live to see it himself. Now it is starting to look that way, and Harkema is the largest place in the municipality.
28590: Tseard van Dekken is at the market in Hamster and mocks Imke de Jong, who then nails him to the ground for an hour. Tseard is a policeman.
28592: People are sometimes born with a caul. It makes one bulletproof and doctors are very keen on it. A sea captain who carries one will never lose his ship. Freemasons are also bulletproof and have made a pact with the devil. If they run out of money in a café, they make it on the spot by holding a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) up to the light. Egbert Sint and Mike Ruerd both have a wisseldaalder.
28593: Hindrik Schievink lives in Harkema and his daughter in Brabant. When she is pregnant, a bird comes to his door and Hindrik knows he is going to be a grandfather. It always comes true.
28596: One evening, as father walks along a narrow path on his way to the shop in Smoorhoek, he suddenly sees a coffin in front of him, but he cannot see who is in it and the coffin quickly disappears. On the way back there is nothing to be seen. Two weeks later a dead person's coffin stands in the same spot. The hearse cannot get along the narrow path, so they carry the coffin. At the very spot where father saw the coffin earlier, they now stop to rest. It was a portent.
28597: Father can read cups and predict the future from coffee grounds. He gets paid for this.
28599: Ruerd van der Veen has a foul mouth. Once, when he has finished thatching a farmhouse in Boomklooster, he sits on the barn and says he is not afraid of the devil, cursing as he does. On the way home on the Skeanpad a woman blocks his path. He thinks it is Janne, the wife of Anders Nikolai. Though he asks, the woman does not move, and when he tries to grab her, she grabs him and throws him over the trees. Ruerd was out of action for a while because of the woman's rough treatment.
28600: Ruerd van der Veen is threshing in his own barn one day when a small black dog appears that cannot be chased away or hit. Finally it leaves. He has the hammer in his hand, and when the dog turns up again he strikes at it, making it twice as fat, with eyes like teapots. Ruerd sees that the dog is not right and becomes frightened. But the dog grabs him and throws him over the collar beams.
28601: In winter you should not go onto the ice of the Leeuwenpoel, because someone with red hair still has to drown there. A woman with red hair often lies there calling 'help'. Later a girl with red hair drowned in this pond. I myself have heard cries for help at night, so someone else still has to drown.
28602: Wibe Alma from Harkema was born with a caul and can foretell things. When something is coming, he is knocked out of bed in the middle of the night, and later he tells what he has seen and who will die. It always comes true.
28603: Van der Wal is walking along the Turflaan at night when a funeral procession comes and he is pushed aside. Afterwards he tells everyone never again to walk in the middle of the road in the evening.
28604: Father is clairvoyant and knows already at his wedding that he will have a bad life. It is a bad marriage; he is very unhappy, cannot get along with my mother and falls ill. He went about with cancer for years. It was deep poverty.
28605: I hear omens myself too, because I worked in the mines in Limburg and heard hammering sounds there, at places where something later changed.
28606: In Hamsterpein I once saw a fire at a farm beforehand, as did others. A few months later the farm does indeed burn down.
28608: On the Langepad between Harkema and Surhuzum a tall woman with long hair, dressed in white, haunts. She just runs up and down and does not see people.
28609: On the Pauwlaan in Smoorhoek, in Boelenslaan and in Zwaagwesteinde a naked ghost child wanders about, unable to find rest after its death.
28610: One night Tsjip van der Bij from Harkema is out catching polecats with his friends. They all have a polecat dog with them, which run ahead and point out the polecat. Suddenly his dog is seized by a big dog. Tsjip swings his axe at the dog but keeps missing, and the dog keeps getting bigger. When Tsjip mocks the devil and then looks this dog in the face, he becomes afraid. It has eyes like fire. After this encounter Tsjip stops mocking and is converted.
28611: Sikke Hoeksma and Douwe Wedzinga often go to Twizel on Saturday evenings for a drink. Once, after such an outing, Sikke continues on alone and sees a dark little dog lying on the path, with eyes like little teapots. It will not be chased away and keeps getting fatter. When it comes close to Sikke, he becomes frightened, shoots and injures his little finger. This can still be seen.
28612: Another time Sikke Hoeksma and Douwe Wedzinga are on their way to the pub in Twijzel together with Jan Klamer, when Jan alone sees a man on the Twijzelerweg who is mocking him. He jumps across the canal and goes after him. The others simply continue on their way. Jan does not come to the pub that evening. On the way back they see Jan's clogs still standing where he left them. When Jan is not at home, they go looking for him and find him dead in the bushes along the Twijzelerweg. He had always been a mocker, and the devil killed him.
28613: Alma from Augustinusga is a mocker. Once, coming out of a pub in Surhuizum, he was thrown into the Spookpoel.
28614: Sytse Jager from Harkema is a mocker and gets his mocker's payment when he once goes behind the dike to relieve himself and is then thrown over the trees on the dike. He swears to the Lord never to do it again.
28615: Oeds Holthuis from Harkema was also once thrown away. Since then he has stopped mocking and has been converted.
28621: If you put a witch's apple in a cup with a lid on it, it turns into a toad.
28622: A few girls want to pass three hussars on horseback, but the hussars corner them. Jantsje comes along and holds the horses by the nose one by one so the girls can get through. Then she fixes the hussars to the spot on the Flapbrug in Fliet for another hour.
28627: Paulus Alma, son of Wibe Griet, is lying in bed with a broken foot and hears hammering at a spot right next to the house. Later two houses are built there and the neighbours Albert and Wopke van der Veen come to live in them. He lives on the Hoge Kamp.
28637: In Bergum two people are walking on the road in the dark, and one of them is full of resentment and on his way to beat someone up. On the way he is flung away and is nearly dead. The other never saw who did it. It was the devil.
28638: On the Earmhústerweg in Bergum a man haunts the road and harasses everyone. Everyone is afraid of him.
28639: Jan Huizinga is a butcher in Bergum who likes a drink, is often drunk and then curses. One evening, on his way to the house of the cantonal judge Schaafsam, he is suddenly lifted up and thrown into the canal. Since then he has never been drunk again, has stopped cursing and goes to church.
28640: In Noordermeer people regularly hear hammering at the corner by the Simmerdijk, on the spot where Jan Vonk's house was later built. It was an omen.
28641: Someone on the Langelaan in Noordermeer was born with a caul and sees funeral processions in advance. Another person from Bergum can predict that someone will drown, and that comes true too.
28643: Jehannes has a pub on Veenwouderwal, and some people come by rolling an oil drum ahead of them. At Jehannes's pub, however, the drum goes no further, and then they themselves are fixed to the spot. He also knows devil's arts.
28645: At Doede Postma's, Jehannes makes the little soldiers come out of the hearth.
28649: A plaagbeest (tormenting beast) is the devil in the form of a dog.
28652: Freemasons have made a pact with the devil and are never short of money. They meet at night and instead of a fist they offer two fingers.
28668: Father once saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns) that looked like a train and also heard the whistle. That was at the Readskuorre near Drogeham. He claims the train will come there later, but so far no train has come.
28674: A man who has never been to Amsterdam nevertheless knows his way around there; he knows exactly where he has to go.
28688: In 1949 people hear cries for help from the Leeuwepoel, but when a farmer goes to look, he sees nothing.
28690: A man from Skoat (Schoot) is on his way to Wolvega when halfway a fellow comes to walk beside him who does not answer his greeting. Both carry a stick, but the man does not dare to strike him away, because he thinks the other is the devil.
28691: Once when grandpa goes to work early in the morning, there is a man wearing a hat standing there who does not return his greeting. As he approaches the man he is startled, because he can see right through him. This happened in Oudehorne.
28692: With a card one can make a bottle of drink come, which is brought by the devil.
28693: In Jubbega some people murdered their own child, who has visited their house at night ever since. When people stay the night, they are advised not to leave their bed during the night. In the morning the child is gone.
28694: A man in the work crew sometimes clearly sees someone and even talks to him, while in reality that person is not there. He only really arrives later.
28695: My neighbour in Nieuweschoot is expecting a child, and when the time comes he will knock on the window. One night I hear someone knock and say that it is time. Then my wife can assist the family. Nothing is happening yet, but the next day the child is born. It was an omen.
28696: My neighbour has a cow that is about to calve and needs my help. One night I hear knocking and go to the farmer, but the cow is not ready yet. That only happens a few days later.
28697: Oebele Wagenaar was a farmhand for Albert Land in Harkema, later lives in Witveen and is the biggest second-hand dealer in Friesland. While still a farmhand for Albert Land he says a railway or tram line will come, because he hears noise every night. Later a road came with a lot of traffic (cars and lorries), but no train or tram. He had heard the bustle of the traffic.
28699: If you pull funny faces in front of the mirror, you get slapped with hands. The devil wrings your neck if you stand looking in the mirror, or the mirror flies against your head.
28700: If a child hits its mother, its hands fall off or the hand later grows out of the grave. If you sew buttons onto a coat on a Sunday, you cannot die. Nails cut on a Sunday no longer grow, or you must gather them up after your death.
28701: A woman often sees a small funeral procession and is then lifted up and set aside. She herself has lost two husbands and five children as well.
28706: A sorcerer walks over the water with great strides.
28709: When a skipper at sea sees a pestvogel (plague bird), he becomes afraid, because then plague will break out on the ship.
28712: Father is once walking on the road at night when a shadowy figure appears in front of him. Father recites an incantation, and it turns out to be the devil, for he steps aside. This was in Twijzelerheide.
28714: In France a pious man lives alone in a house on a bare plain, past which runs a poisonous canal. In bad weather he suddenly sees four men in black sailing in a little boat on the water. He starts reading, and a little later a small man stands on the threshold and says he is the mightiest. With his eyes fixed on the cross of Jesus, he sends the devil away. Then the four men are standing beside him, and when he grabs the first, he is holding only a black cloak, which falls to the floor and bursts into flames. He puts out the fire, and now six men stand before him. The devil says they already have his fiancée, and they abuse him. He too ends up in the boat on the poisoned canal. His fiancée is already completely black, but the man begs God for help and receives it, so that the men on the river burn up. The woman is healed when he lays the cross on her lips. They suffered no harm from the poisoned water.
28715: A maid would like a suitor, even if it is the devil, and that same evening a suitor stands at her door. While washing up, her mother says the man has two club feet and she does not trust it. It is the devil, and to chase him away she has to hurl all the plates onto his toes. He leaves after that.
28718: If you walk around the churchyard three times around midnight with a black cat in a sack and call out three times that you have a black cat in the sack, you get a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back). The third time you must not walk all the way around, because then you will die.
28719: Sije van der Veen from Harkema has a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) and is never short of money. Later he died of a drink-induced stroke.
28736: A little light burns in the Leeuwenpoel, and once people hear hammering there while there is nothing to be seen. Later part of the pool is drained, and on the spot where they saw the light and heard the sound a house is later built.
28738: Father is on his way from Harkema to Drachtster Compagnie and sees little lights on the Folgersterlaan in the evening. Later a tram comes at the same spot.
28760: People go to work on the Groningen clay and walk home along the railway, among them mother-in-law, who sees two men in black walking. She does not see her nephew Piter. Finally she sees the men turn into a funeral procession. She quickly runs away.
28761: As a boy, on his way to the baker, father meets a big black dog, and only with an incantation does it go away.
28762: Two men have agreed that whoever dies first will report what the afterlife is like. When one of them dies, he does indeed knock on the door in the middle of the night. The other is terrified by the knocking, and when they meet, the dead man says it is not good there.
28764: My grandfather is in the army with three soldiers, one of whom always has money because he is a Freemason. Another goes with him to the Freemasons' building, where he has to get into a coffin, curse God and His commandments and follow the devil. He calls on the Lord for help and they chase him away.
28766: One night Eatse hears hammering close to his house in Twijzelerheide, but there is nothing to be seen. Later a house is built on the same spot.
28768: Witches can change into cats, which sometimes hold a meeting. Sometimes a cat gets a blow, and the next day Piters Willemke has something wrong with a leg.
28770: Father hears hammering at night in Harkema. Three years later his old house is demolished and a new one is built. This is what he heard.
28771: When my eldest brother is sent to the shop he soon comes back, because he has seen the devil in the hedge on the way. My other brother wants to see that for himself, and at widow Mozes's house they see the sheep still standing outside, which is the devil. Taeke was born with a caul and goes along. On the way back, at his insistence, they walk along the little dike. Later he hears that Taeke saw a funeral procession approaching with Jille van Houten. A week later one of Jille's children dies quite unexpectedly.
28772: Taeke was born with a caul, which was destroyed at his birth; otherwise he would have foreseen everything. Now he only sees what crosses his path. Doctors sell cauls for a lot of money to officers and sailors, because they then become bulletproof or safe from shipwreck.
28773: At the corner of the Kleineweg, where cycle repairman Hager now lives, Tseard tells father they must step aside, because there is a big pig that is flying into the ditch. Father, however, sees nothing.
28774: Sjoerd Rienkje lives on a road with an old house at the end, which is on fire two evenings in a row. A year later it does indeed burn down.
28775: In Harkema, Anna and Baeije live in the woods, which belong to the municipality while the house belongs to the family. When the municipality buys the land too, the house is demolished. Father had heard this beforehand.
28776: Wild lanterns are often seen, and they later turn out to be bicycle lamps. It is an omen.
28778: On the spot in Harkema where Warmolds later had a small wooden church built, people already heard trumpet and horn music beforehand. Later these instruments are played there during the sermons.
28779: Ruerd van der Veen from Harkema works with father at the Kloosterplaatsen, where Bindert Japiks lives in the middle one. While thatching at Bindert's, Ruerd mocks terribly and says that if the devil exists, he would like to meet him. That evening he walks alone on the Skolkepad and wants to cross the planks, where the devil is waiting for him and throws him through the trees. Ruerd was ill from it for some time.
28781: In Hardegarijp there is a ghost gate that never stays shut and opens by itself at night. It is said that someone was murdered who has no rest and passes through the gate every night.
28783: If a dog howls eerily, someone will die. A chattering magpie brings news or foretells a death. According to father, magpies are witches dressed in black.
28789: Heabel is a witch who sometimes gives us a sweet, which we always throw away at once. If you eat it, you get a toad in your body.
28790: When I am on my way to Jouk after school to bring something, I see her at Anders Janne's, but decide to go on to her house anyway and leave the parcel there. A little further on, Jouk is standing in front of me. She is in two places at once.
28793: Sikke Helder lives in Smoorhoeke and always stays in bed late on Sunday mornings. He is a mocker. His mother goes to the neighbours for coffee. One time a crow jumps onto the bed, but when he tries to stroke it, it keeps getting bigger. Finally the crow flies away. Sikke knows this is a warning from the devil and changes his ways after this incident.
28794: If you step on a toad, a thunderstorm comes. You must never kill the animal, because people say it is a witch. An apple received from the witch and kept in a tin had turned into a toad a few days later.
28795: If the churn is bewitched, the butter will not come. The churn is destroyed and a new churn is used.
28796: When father cannot sleep at night, he goes for a walk. After one such night he predicts the building of a new house, because he has heard hammering by the Bosweg. Some time later Lubbert Elzinga does indeed put up his house there.
28797: Taeke Postma was born with a caul and dies young. One night a funeral procession passes him and he steps aside. The next day he predicts a death. It comes true.
28798: Tsjerk Boonstra's wife was born with a caul, and when we visit her once she accuses us of having stolen apples from the orchard the night before, because she saw it. When I ask why she did not come outside when she knew, she threatens to box my ears.
28800: Near the paupers' graveyard in Harkema, someone was once thrown into the ditch by the devil
28802: Alle Tet is a witch and, according to others, can turn into a toad. When a child is bewitched, people go with a bottle of urine to Wopke van Kûkherne, who gives them a potion and warns them about a black cat that will try to break the bottle on the way. Dukje Haije is also a witch who has bewitched a child. Under the child's pillow they find wreaths that must be burned, and everything in the house must be closed, even the keyhole. There are sometimes witches who stick needles into dolls to hurt people.
28804: With a jack of spades you can make a bottle of drink come, and the first bit must be thrown over the left shoulder. You have then been sold to the devil.
28805: If a woman plays cards a lot during pregnancy, the child is born with a card on its head, back or chest. From that you can tell they were the devil's cards.
28808: A plaagbeest (tormenting ghost beast) is a big dog that sees people home and disappears when you open the door. People are afraid of it.
28809: The devil sometimes throws people who mock everything into the ditch.
28813: Father and Mike Ruerd are coming out of the pub in Jachtveld when Ruerd, just past the baker's, is lifted up and flung over the tree bank. That evening Ruerd had been mocking. He scrambles to his feet and together they walk home. Mike, however, does not dare go to bed because a big black dog with glowing eyes is lying on it, which only he can see, so he sits at the table
28814: Hindrik Holthuis was also a mocker in Harkema, and whoever could curse best once got a cent for a swear word. Because of this the devil once seized him at the Langewijk, and since then he has been converted and is one of the most pious people in Harkema. From being thrown, though, he was left with a stiff limb.
28815: Tetsje Wibe was thrown away at the Langewijk, and the same happened to Syste Jager three times in a row one evening at the dike where the doctor lives. Both are sinners.
28816: The site of the football ground of the Christian footballers, the Saturday players, has always been haunted. On one corner is the Nikus pool, from which noise always comes, and a man often stands in it. My cousin doesn't dare go past it.
28823: On the Taekeland in Harkema a witte juffer (white lady) haunts.
28824: Teake was born with a caul and also saw Martens Wip's funeral procession in advance when it came towards him one evening. He can only say how many people there are, but not who.
28825: A woman regarded as a witch sticks a pin into a doll, after which a child falls ill.
28826: If a witch does not kill someone every seven years, she dies herself. They bewitch wreaths into pillows, which must be burnt, and the stench released must stay in the room. After that the room is aired. The witch in question is out of action for a few days, and people know who it was.
28828: A farmer has a loft full of grain and falls ill. Although they promise him to turn the grain after his death, they fail to do so after he dies. From then on they hear the old farmer doing this work in the loft every evening. When someone finally has the courage to look in the loft, the farmer is busy at work. The next day they do it themselves and sell it in bales. After that the farmer stayed away.
28834: Bouke has bewitched Gjalt by sticking a needle into the foot of a doll. When they boil his urine with pins and needles, Bouke stands crying at the window. Because Gjalt is bewitched, he has been given cat's blood. Bouke can turn into a cat, and then only her paunch is left lying at home.
28837: When people walk past the churchyard in the evening, it sometimes happens that they are pushed aside because a funeral procession has to pass.
28838: People who come out of the pub using foul words have been thrown away by the devil.
28851: In Harkema live witches who stick pins and needles into dolls to hurt people.
28852: On the Saeiland in Leeuwarden, at the site of the former cattle market, Tseard van Dekken gets into a quarrel with another man, whom he calls a snotnose. The other man then fixes Tseard and his friend to the ground for a while, and only after long pleading are they released.
28854: With an ace of hearts you can make a bottle of drink come.
28856: At a fair in Amsterdam one can see in the black mirror whether or not one will marry later. If a coffin appears, you stay unmarried, and the image of a woman becomes your future partner. Father sees a woman unknown to him in the mirror. Later he meets her at the market in Leeuwarden and she does indeed become his wife.
28869: De Vries from Groninger Opeinde sees a row of little lights before the tram from Drachten to Groningen exists. He foresaw the tram in an omen.
28870: Rikele Myt from Skieding is a witch. Once people throw something at a strange cat, hitting it on the head, and the next day Rikele has only one eye. It is said that she can turn herself into a cat.
28875: Father's grandmother is very ill, and once while she is sitting in a chair, a pigeon flies into the window outside and is killed. The woman says this is an omen of her death, and a few days later she dies.
28877: For a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) you have to sell yourself to the devil by walking around the churchyard three times and reciting an incantation. Then you are never short of money. Freemasons also have a wisseldaalder.
28879: In Hardegarijp the father of red Haite lived in a castle, and he got the maid pregnant. She then killed herself, and that is why the gate never closes anymore.
28888: I am once out with a friend on the sheep track and, at the spot where the reed fence now stands, hear a strange sound coming from the Knjillisdiep. Later factories are built here and people hear the same sound we heard back then.
28890: Mike Ruerd can make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit with the help of a magic book, and can read just as fast forwards as backwards. He can also make the table dance.
28891: Fat Reinder and I go to Groningen together on a Saturday evening, where in a building there is a black mirror that predicts whether or not you will get a wife. According to the mirror Reinder will not get a wife, but fifty years later he does. So the mirror does not look that far ahead.
28892: Imke de Jong is a sorcerer and once fixed Tseard van Dekken to the ground at the Hamster market, because Tseard had been mouthing off at him. After saying it three times, Imke frees him from the ground.
28893: The brother of Linse Houwink in Suawoude dies and Linse is utterly devastated. He hopes he can see him one more time. Once, when Linse is standing in the hayfield sharpening his scythe, his brother suddenly stands beside him and looks at him. His wish has come true and now he no longer wants to see him. And that did not happen again.
28899: By the thick oak tree on the Betonweg in Harkema a glowing man comes floating along and flies into the Vliet. He goes right through Piter Hountsje's bicycle.
28901: On the Kleineweg near Drogeham a black woman is seen haunting the place, who was murdered there long ago. In the bank of the dike there is a cross in an oak tree as a sign that the murder took place there, and it never goes away.
28902: A hare that cannot be hit, however much you shoot at it, is a witch.
28904: A friend of mine from Bos works for Edzer Witteveen and every day passes water where he sees his late grandmother standing in a white cap, whom he treated disgracefully. Only he sees her.
28906: There have been people who, on their way to the milking place, hear the sound of milk squirting into the pails while they are not there yet. It is an omen.
28907:
Imke de Jong can make people lose their way and open the locks of closed doors.

wizard, losing one's way, lock (opening), door, doing magic
28912: Ruerd van der Veen from Harkema is roofing one of the houses at the Boomklooster. According to Klaes-om, Ruerd is mocking a great deal. That evening Ruerd goes home and is walking on the Skoltepad when a dog gets in his way. He says he will kick the animal, but is lifted up by a stick and thrown away. It was the evil one, who stayed with Ruerd all night but did nothing else.
28913: When three men are out walking, one of them sees the devil coming and says it wants to get him. Although he walks between the other two, he is lifted up and thrown into the ditch. This happened in Harkema.
28914: When my sister is standing on the quay in Visvliet, a skipper moored there tells her that a funeral procession will pass, because he saw it that night. That same afternoon there is indeed one. The skipper was born with a caul.
28919: Imke de Jong visits markets as a conjurer, and at the one in Ham he fixed Tseard van Dekken to the ground, who was later released.
28923: Freemasons have made a pact with the devil and often go out at night.
28924: Wild lanterns foretell the later bicycle lamps, and we used to see them very often in Bos.
29143: A building in Leeuwarden is built on cow hides.
29290: A foal with a porridge pan around its neck haunted a certain spot.
29291: In a farmhouse people sometimes heard a clock strike, even though there was no clock at all. Later a clock did come, and it made exactly the same sound.
29292: A man had once misbehaved in the pub. On the way back he was seized by the devil and flung over dikes and ditches.
29295: A man had behaved rather strangely in the pub. On the way back the devil walked beside him the whole time. When the farmhand got back to the farm he could not get the door open. Out of fear he then hanged himself behind the wall.
29300: Ships moored at a certain spot as little as possible, because it was haunted at night. A tree would be knocked over, or something else would happen, while nothing could be seen.
29302: The parents of a sick little boy once found three wreaths in his pillow. The third was not quite finished. The child was bewitched. So they boiled the wreaths, and from that the witch died or suffered terrible pain.
29303: A certain spot was haunted. If you lay there with your ship, there was knocking against the blocks all night long.
29305: One night a woman heard hammering. Within a year a new house was built.
29306: Early in her marriage, a woman once dreamed that she would have three children, all three of whom would die. After that she would have one more child, and that one would live. It came true exactly like that.
29308: Big Wibe from Eestrum was a wizard. He could creep into people's houses through keyholes. So everyone in the area had asafoetida under their threshold, in their keyhole and even on their owl boards.
29309: Two friends were once walking together. One of them was never very careful with his words; he was a scoffer. Suddenly he was terribly frightened. He saw the devil walking beside him. He gave the devil a kick, but it was immediately walking beside him again. His friend saw nothing.
29311: Two men were once walking at a spot known to be haunted. Suddenly a little dog appeared. There was not a single house nearby, and they thought it was the devil.
29312: A foal with a porridge pan around its neck haunted a certain spot.
29316: On the clay lands the labourers slept in barns. It was said that those barns were haunted.
29317: A man cursed a lot. One night he was on the road with a dead cow when his horse refused to go any further. He had to lead the animal on by hand. The devil was said to be standing in the middle of the road. The man never dared to take that road again.
29318: A scoffer was once flung some distance by the devil.
29321: Some people can make a bottle of drink come with a playing card, a jack of spades.
29326: Two men decided one night to steal potatoes from the barn of a man who had been dead for some time. But in front of the barn doors they saw the dead man standing, in a blue smock and wearing a tie. The men quickly ran away.
29327: One night two women saw two naked little children haunting.
29329: A woman sometimes heard hammering. Later a new house would always be built on that spot.
29330: A man claimed to be afraid of nothing. One day he had been doing carpentry work. On the way back the devil threw him into the ditch, toolbox and all.
29331: A godless man was once thrown down by the devil.
29332: People once heard a sound coming from the water. A little later someone came driving along, ended up in the water and drowned.
29333: If you do not spend all of a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back), it never runs out. To get a wisseldaalder, you have to walk around the churchyard three times with a black cat. Then you must call out: "Who will buy my cat for a daalder?" The third time someone took the cat and gave a wisseldaalder.
29334: A strange man was once set in the water with his dog cart for no reason.
29335: A man could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. They would then march around the room two by two.
29337: At a certain spot a foal with a porridge pan around its neck haunted the place.
29338: Alle Tet could turn herself into a cat and then she raged terribly. Together with other cats she would hold a meeting. Then they sang together. It sometimes happened that someone hit that cat, and then the next day Tet was covered in bruises.
