29339: If a dog howls eerily, there will soon be a death in the neighbourhood.
29341: Near a churchyard people sometimes ended up in the water. Then they had not seen that a funeral procession was passing.
29344: The children were not allowed to accept anything from a certain woman. If they kept an apple she had given them in the ember pot, it turned into a toad.
29346: Alle Tet pricked dolls with needles and so tormented people. Once a potion was fetched from the duivelbanner (exorcist) for a bewitched woman. But the witch had turned herself into a black cat and broke the bottle. Then the woman died.
29349: If you sell yourself to the devil, you are never short of money again. You must walk around the churchyard three times with a black cat, calling out: "Who will buy my cat for a daalder?" The third time the devil is there. He then gives you a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) in exchange for the cat. As long as you do not spend all of the daalder, it always comes back into your possession.
29350: Mike Ruerd could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. He would then make them march across the floor.
29351: A man once claimed not to be afraid of any devil. When he wanted to cross a little bridge on his way back from work, a woman stood there who refused to make room for him. She seized him and flung him some distance. The man was ill from it for some time.
29352: Two brothers were once out hunting polecats. Suddenly the hunting dogs began to howl. Then the men saw two naked little children. They went over the dyke and vanished into the ground.
29354: One Sunday a man had been cursing and mocking a lot. Then he was suddenly lifted up and flung over the dike. After that the man no longer dared to be out alone at night.
29356: Wild lanterns were lights that people saw from afar. When they came closer, the lights had vanished. Later a real lamp post or a house would always appear on that spot.
29360: In the old days a big fellow wearing a large bowler hat haunted a certain dyke.
29361:
In the old days people warned never to walk in the middle of the road at night. Otherwise you could run into a funeral procession.
A woman was often outside at night. She was born with a caul.
29363: A maidservant always heard someone haunting at the churning mill at one o'clock at night. But when she went to look, there was never anyone to be seen. The previous farmer had hanged himself at that churning mill and always haunted it afterwards.
29364: In the old days people were sometimes pushed off the road. Then there was a funeral they did not see.
29368: With a jack of spades some people could make a bottle of drink come.
29372: In the past there was a black mirror at the market. In it young men got to see the woman they would later marry.
29375: Sometimes there is a hole in a house that can never be kept closed. That has to do with haunting.
29378: A man always cursed like a heathen. One day he was escorted home by a big dog. That was the devil.
29380: One night a woman saw a horse pawing the ground. The animal was harnessed to a black wagon. It was a vision, and the woman predicted that something would happen soon. Not long afterwards the neighbours' son died. The hearse horse pawed the ground.
29381: One night a woman saw herself sitting with a dead man. Someone came and asked her to step away for a moment so the measurements for the coffin could be taken. Not long afterwards her nephew died. As she kept watch by the body, the carpenter asked her to step aside so he could measure the body.
29382: On a farm people sometimes heard hammering coming from the barn, while in reality there was nothing there. Later the socialists held noisy meetings there. Sermons were also preached there, and a pulpit was built for them. And later still the Reformed held Sunday school there.
29383: Two men were once coming from the market when the dogs would no longer pull the cart. The men quickly moved aside, and the cart was simply thrown off the road. A funeral procession was passing without them seeing it.
29384: In the old days people sometimes saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps). Usually someone had been murdered at those spots.
29385: In the old days people were warned never to walk in the middle of the road at night, because they might be pushed aside by a funeral procession.
29386: A man was born with a caul and therefore saw funerals in advance. He then knew who was going to die.
29387: A woman missed her dead mother so badly that she often wished to see her once more. Then one night her mother suddenly stood before the bed. The woman was terrified and never again wished to see her mother.
29389: One evening a few people had to pass a spot known to be haunted. There at the roadside they saw a giant, fully twice the size of a normal person. A large cloak flapped around him; otherwise he stood completely still. It was a ghost.
29391: A man always cursed a great deal and was often in the house of correction. One evening someone without hands came towards him and threw him into the canal.
29392: Minse Griper could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
29393: Rikele Myt was a witch. She could turn herself into a cat. Once someone threw a heavy object at a black cat with glowing eyes. He hit the animal in the eye. A few days later he noticed that Myt had injured her head in exactly the same places where he had hit the cat.
29400: In the past one could see in the black mirror which woman one would marry. If one saw a coffin, it meant that the person would not marry.
29407: Witches could turn themselves into a cat. The next day they would come back with their whole head split open.
29408: A man did not believe in ghosts. Until one time he was chased by a black thing with fiery eyes.
29409: A girl lived with her grandmother, who treated her very badly. Then the girl died. From then on the grandmother often saw the child haunting around her, and she never again dared to be alone.
29410: If a dog howls eerily, there will soon be a death.
29411: A woman often heard hammering at night and predicted that new houses would be built. That came true.
29412: A man did not believe and was a great scoffer. One evening outside he was terribly mauled by a big black dog. Perhaps it was the devil.
29413: In the old days people warned not to walk in the middle of the road at night. For if a funeral procession happened to pass, you were pushed off the road.
29414: A woman once saw in advance a funeral procession with horses passing by, and so she knew that someone would die.
29418: A woman often saw wild lanterns. Those were the later bicycle lights.
29419: Dreaming of fish or of horses means a death.
29420: In the old days, when the children went to school, they made a cross on the road. Then no witch could come near.
29421: A woman once saw lots of little lights. She predicted that new houses would come. That came true.
29422: If a dog howled eerily, there would be a death within a short time. This was also the case if the clock made a different sound than usual.
29424: A certain spot was haunted. A man was once chased there by a black beast.
29426: A man was once suddenly lifted up and thrown over a ditch.
29427: A rough man had once been out drinking. When he needed to pee on the way back, he was suddenly lifted up and thrown over the dike.
29428: Some people could make a bottle of drink come with a playing card.
29431: In Harkema a foal with a porridge pan around its neck haunted the place.
29432: At a certain spot a foal with a porridge pan around its neck haunted the place.
29444: A fellow once summoned the devil in the pub. On the way back he was given a thorough beating by the devil.
29445: If a dog howls eerily, a funeral procession will later pass by that spot.
29446: If small children were not given burial clothes, they would later come back to haunt.
29447: A man often heard hammering and planks being thrown at a certain spot. When he went to look, there was nothing to be seen. Later a large farm was built on that spot.
29448: At a certain spot people often saw lights in the evening. Later a new house was built there.
29449: In the old days people sometimes saw a light flying over the heath. Later a tram came to run there.
29457:
Witches bewitched children by conjuring wreaths into their pillows. People burned those wreaths.
A witch could turn herself into a cat, and in that form went to the neighbours every evening. Once those neighbours were warned not to let the cat near their chickens. That evening the man shot the cat dead. The next day the witch turned out to be dead too.
29458: At a certain spot people always saw the ghost of a foal with a porridge pan around its neck.
29460: At a certain spot people often saw a little light. When they came closer, the light went out. This happened up to three times. Later a new house was built on that spot.
29461: In the old days people sometimes saw a house on fire when in reality there was nothing. Usually such a house did burn down later. A man once also saw a little house on fire. When he came closer, nothing was wrong. Later that house was demolished.
29462: A man often had to get out of bed at night to see funeral processions. Later there was then always a real funeral procession. But the man did not yet know who would die.
29463: A dog sometimes howls eerily when someone is going to die. It then stands with its head towards the place where the funeral procession will pass.
29464: A farmer had treated his parents rather badly. When he himself died, his inheritance was not divided as he had wanted. Every morning his household then saw him standing behind the house. They had the minister address the ghost. The farmer expressed his wish and the people carried it out. Since then the farmer has never come haunting again.
29465: In the past unwanted babies were sometimes done away with. Such children found no rest and danced naked around the post of the barn.
29466: People who were not given grave clothes after their death came back to haunt later. Then they were addressed by the minister, and he made sure the matter was put right.
29473: At a certain spot a foal with a porridge pan around its neck haunted the place.
29474: On the heath people used to often see wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns). They were the harbingers of the later tram.
29475: A German had been murdered at a certain spot. Since then he haunted it as the Langesleatterman. Skippers did not dare moor their boats there. If they did, the boat always came loose by itself.
29477: A witch can turn herself into a hare and into a cat. Someone once hit an unknown cat. The next day the neighbour woman walked around with a cloth around her head. Then everyone knew she was the witch.
29481: Freemasons are bulletproof. When you become a Freemason, you curse everything and sell yourself to the devil. Freemasons are never short of money because they have a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back). Freemasons sometimes hang up an empty purse, which the devil then fills with money.
29483: An unmarried, reserved woman often has foresights of funerals at night. The foresights almost always come true shortly afterwards, about three days later.
29484: You must never run in the middle of the road at night, because you may run into an invisible funeral procession.
29485: A woman is lifted up for no reason and thrown into the ditch, although no one is to be seen.
29486: A man dreams that he gets a flat tyre on his bicycle. The dream comes true: the next day he gets a flat. The man was very frightened by it.
29487: People who regularly foresee deaths in funeral processions are caul-bearers.
29488: If a dog howls eerily, a death is coming. It is an omen.
29489: The father of a sick child suddenly sees a magpie hopping around him. It is an omen: two days later the little boy dies.
29490: People hear psalm singing and organ music at a certain place. It is an omen: later a church is built on that spot.
29495: A girl on her way home in the evening suddenly comes upon a big dog. The animal keeps following her annoyingly. It is suspected that the animal is the devil.
29497: A certain woman born with a caul must have a foresight of a death every so often, so as not to die herself. The same is true of witches.
29503: People see a light burning at a certain place. It is a portent: later a house is built on that spot.
29504: People see little lights moving back and forth on the road. It is a portent of the later bicycle lights.
29505: At a haunted spot a blue dog haunts the place. It is a ghost animal.
29509: The nightmare enters the house through the keyhole and visits people in their beds. To keep nightmares away you must put your slippers upside down in front of the bed, keep the key in the keyhole and sprinkle yourself with flour, for if the nightmare gets flour on her, she can no longer get away. Of seven girls in a household, one is a nightmare.
29511: A pregnant woman is very frightened when a clairvoyant man visits her, because the clairvoyant always foresees deaths. The clairvoyant keeps looking at a certain corner of the room. The child the woman gives birth to dies after 23 weeks. The little coffin stands in the corner where the clairvoyant kept resting his gaze.
29512: A clairvoyant man visiting the narrator keeps staring at a house across the street. Half a year later a young woman dies in that house.
29513: A clairvoyant man is driven out of bed at night by an invisible force to receive foresights. Outside, the railway gates spring open for him.
29514: A clairvoyant farmhand foresees that the farmer's wife will die in childbed. The foresight comes true. The clairvoyant foresees the whole funeral in detail. He also urges them to lay a white nappy over the coffin, because he has foreseen this.
29515: A mocking sinner, who would later have foresights himself, ridicules a clairvoyant man. The clairvoyant, who has just foreseen a death in a funeral procession, says the sinner will be able to have foresights too. He urges the sinner to look over his (the clairvoyant's) left shoulder. The sinner sees the funeral procession as well. Later it turns out that the clairvoyant transferred his second sight to the sinner as punishment for the mockery. All of this was brought about by the devil.
29517: A clairvoyant man sees a coffin standing in the house. Shortly afterwards his daughter drowns herself.
29518: A clairvoyant man always foresees exactly how many women and men will walk in a funeral procession.
29519: Warning: you must never walk in the middle of the road at night, because you may be struck by a passing funeral procession.
29520: A young man is suddenly lifted up and set down on the other side of the ditch, although no one is to be seen.
29521: It sometimes happens that someone urges another person to step aside for a passing funeral procession. The other, however, cannot see the procession.
29522: A clairvoyant man sometimes has to travel enormous distances, straight through ditches, to receive a foresight of a death.
29523: If a dog howls eerily, a death is approaching.
29524: If old rooks or crows fly over the house, there will soon be a death in the house.
29525: Magpies come to the house to bring a message, not necessarily news of a death. If the weight of the Frisian clock falls down, there will be a death in the family. If the bell clangs at a funeral, there will soon be another funeral. Wild watches ticking behind the wallpaper also signify an approaching death.
29526: At a haunted spot by the railway two little children with red bands around their necks wander about at night.
29527: A man is suddenly startled by a white thing. He cannot take another step. Shortly afterwards the trees begin to rustle. The man turns back and takes another route. He never dares to pass that spot again.
29530: People heard the sounds of the train before the train even ran. Other people predicted that there would be wagons without horses. Those wagons were the later cars.
29531: A clairvoyant man keeps having foresights.
29537: A farmhand jumps easily over the canal and boasts 'that no devil can match him'. At once the devil jumps over the same canal and leaves the print of a horse's hoof in the stone. The horseshoe is still visible.
29539: A man gives a strange cat a wallop. The next day a woman - a witch - has a sore neck. She was the witch in cat form.
29541: If someone is born with a caul and the caul is pulled off the face the wrong way, that person has foresights all their life. Greedy doctors often try to push cauls backwards because they can resell them at good prices.
29546: Some people, usually in the pub, send off a jack of spades to fetch a bottle of jenever (Dutch gin).
29547: In the black mirror you can behold your future wife.
29548: A sorcerer, Lammert, can make rooks appear from the hearth pit. Later the birds go back into the hearth. From then on the sorcerer is called 'Lammert Roek'. His children are called 'Roeken' (Rooks).
29551: A card reader tells the fortunes of two brothers. The predictions come true.
29555: From the appearance of a hearse in the farmyard, a mother foresees the death of her daughter. She also hears the coffin bump against the door and the window.
29556: If you walk in the middle of the road at night, you may be driven aside by a funeral procession.
29557: If a dog howls eerily, there is usually a death three weeks later. It is an omen.
29558: A man is often driven out of bed at night to see funeral processions.
29560: If seven black rooks fly over the house, a death is coming. It is an omen.
29561: If magpies come to the house, a death is coming.
29563: At a haunted spot a white lady haunts.
29564: A boy is very ill and keeps getting weaker. When someone sees a suspicious white cat walking in the house, the animal is kicked hard. The next day a neighbour woman - a witch - walks around with her arm in a sling. She had turned herself into a white cat the day before. When the sick boy's pillow is opened, two complete witches' wreaths are found. The third witches' wreath was not yet finished. So the boy is bewitched. When the witches' wreaths are burned, the boy recovers.
29569: A witch flies through the air on a broomstick. A certain sorcerer first rolls himself up as a cow's tripe when he goes out to do magic. The sorcerer's wife is rolled up in a cat's skin.
29570: At a haunted spot a foal roams about at night with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a ghost animal.
29577: Two old people hear a chugging sound and see lights. It is a portent: later the tram would run at that place.
29578: At a haunted spot near the churchyard a man sees a young black-haired girl in nightclothes wandering about. The pious man only dares walk on because he trusts in the Lord. When the girl has come quite close to him, she suddenly raises and lowers her arms. Then she sinks into the ground. A farmer from the area tells exactly the same story. Behind the churchyard a married man is said to have murdered his twenty-one-year-old mistress because she was expecting his child. The murdered girl cannot find rest.
29579: A woman, born with a caul, foresees that her little son will die and predicts exactly where the little coffin will stand. The vision comes true: soon afterwards the boy dies of pneumonia. The coffin is also placed where the woman saw it before.
29580: During the Second World War a woman predicts that on 5 May the flag can be hung out because the Netherlands will then be liberated. The prediction comes true.
29582: A man sees a funeral procession at night. He recognises everyone walking in it. It is a premonition: shortly afterwards his neighbour dies. He had also noticed that she was missing from the procession.
29583: In the old days it often happened that someone urged his companions to step aside for a passing funeral procession. That person was then the only one who could see the procession.
29584: Witches have magpies in their power. If a magpie starts chattering in the morning on the windowsill or in the trees near the house, something bad is about to happen to the livestock or the people of the house. It is an omen. The witches have brought it about.
29592: Freemasons sell their souls to the devil in exchange for money. They are never short of money. Now and then they hold a meeting at which one of them is chosen to murder someone.
29594: A cursing sinner is picked up and flung over the trees.
29599: At a haunted spot a foal with a porridge pot around its neck haunts the place. It is a ghost animal.
29607: You must never walk in the middle of the road at night, because you may run into a funeral procession.
29609: If a dog howls eerily, a death is coming.
29611: On a lonely path a woman is suddenly startled by someone with two goat's legs. The woman drives the devil away by reciting the Lord's Prayer. When she speaks the words 'deliver us from evil', the devil has suddenly vanished.
29612: At a haunted spot a white lady wanders about.
29613: In the old days floating lights were often seen at certain places. They were said to be portents of the later bicycle lights.
29614: At a certain place singing can be heard without anything being seen. It is a portent: later a house is built.
29615: At a haunted spot a horse roams about with a foal in its mouth. They are ghost animals.
29616: A mother urges her little son to step aside for a passing funeral procession. The son, however, does not see the procession. It is a premonition: four weeks later a real funeral procession passes at that same spot.
29618: A sick father warns his daughter to keep her distance because a fat brown horse, a nightmare, is sitting in front of his bed. The daughter cannot see the nightmare.
29626: A man sees ships sailing before the canal has even been dug. It is a vision of the future.
29628: At a certain place where a church will be built, church singing can already be heard before the church stands there. It is a portent.
29631: A certain witch has a little doll that she is always pricking.
29632: A witch kills all the sons of a family by witchcraft. She also often flies through the air on a broom.
29634: At a certain place people hear the sound of the train on the rails before the train even runs. It is an omen.
29637: You must never walk in the middle of the road at night, because you may run into a funeral procession.
29640: At a certain place noise can often be heard at night. It is a portent of something that is going to happen in the future.
29642: You must never run in the middle of the road in the evening, because you may be driven aside by a funeral procession.
29643: If a dog howls eerily, a death is coming. It is an omen. The dog foresees the death.
29644: Sometimes hammering sounds are heard at night. It is an omen: later a house is built on that spot.
29645: Two horsemen see a strange man walking. One horseman decides to shoot the man, despite warnings from the other. Only the horse of the rider who fired the shot comes home: the rider is found dead with his head turned round on his body. He had shot at the devil. Since this happened the place has been haunted.
29647: An indifferent man boasts that he is not afraid of the devil. At once he is thrown down by the devil.
29652: A boy hears the sound of people skating although there is no ice. It is a portent: a few days later there is skating.
29653: People hear someone calling for help, although there is nothing to be seen. It is a portent of an approaching death by drowning.
29654: At a certain place the sounds of hammering and planing can sometimes be heard in the evening. It is a portent of work that will be done shortly afterwards.
29655: Music is said to have been heard in a clearing. It is a portent: later a church is built on that spot.
29656: A man hears footsteps at his door and recognises from the steps who it is. But when he goes to look, there is nobody to be seen. It is a portent: later the person whose footsteps he heard actually appears.
29662: In a certain place a witch killed someone by witchcraft. Some witches travel by flying on a broomstick. To ward off witchcraft you must put asafoetida under the threshold. Every seven years a witch must kill someone by witchcraft so as not to die herself.
29663: At a haunted spot a foal runs about with a porridge pot around its neck. It is a ghost animal.
29668: With his magic book, a devil's book, a sorcerer can make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit. He can also make someone stand fixed to the spot or make women's clothes slip down. The sorcerer also makes chickens that annoy him stay indoors.
29669: A man craving herring hurries outside when he hears someone calling 'Herring with roe!' But there is nobody to be seen outside: a colleague has been ventriloquising. The ventriloquist, a sorcerer, has all animals in his power: he can, for example, fix them to the spot.
29670: In the old days wild lanterns were often seen. They were the portents of the later bicycle, car and train lights. Other people saw the train running before the railway was there. It was a vision of the future.
29673: A scoffer who boasts that he is not afraid of the devil is at once seized and thrown down by the devil.
29674: People born with a caul foresee deaths in passing funeral processions. They are driven out of bed at night to walk ahead of the processions and accompany them. If you walk in the middle of the road at night, you can be pushed aside by a funeral procession. People born with a caul never lose their second sight.
29675: If a shroud does not fit a dead person properly, the dead keeps wandering restlessly.
29676: Witches sometimes hold a meeting as cats.
29678: Witches have little dolls that they stick needles and pins into.
29680: With a jack of clubs you can make a bottle of drink come. The drink comes from the devil.
29682: Freemasons have sold their soul to the devil because they have made a pact with the devil. Every seven years a freemason must die, chosen by lot. A freemason is never short of money. When the money runs out, he hangs an empty purse on the door handle. The next morning the purse is filled with money. Once you are a member of freemasonry, you can never leave. Freemasons die a strange death: they are found with their heads turned around.
29685: The devil is said to have once jumped over a wide canal, leaving the print of a horse's hoof in the stone.
29690: People are afraid to go to a certain spot because it is said to be haunted. A white horse with a porridge pot around its neck is said to run about there. It is a ghost animal.
29691: If the bell rings strangely, a death is coming. It is an omen.
29693: People born with a caul are often driven out of bed at night to foresee deaths in passing funeral processions. One man born with a caul was once struck by a hearse when he did not step far enough aside as it passed.
29694: A fisherman is sometimes urged by a voice to go home at once. The man obeys the command because the voice assures him that strange things will happen if he does not. No one is ever to be seen: the fisherman only hears the voice.
29695: In the old days wild lanterns could often be seen. Some people did not dare to pass the will-o'-the-wisps, because the lights would then come at them.
29696: A man sailing in a small boat one evening suddenly sees a big, pitch-black dog with glowing eyes on the bank. The beast, which seems as big as a calf, keeps annoyingly running alongside the boat on the bank. At some point the animal stops and no longer follows the man. The man is so terribly frightened that he never goes out sailing in the evening again.
29697: One night a strange young man is thrown out of his bed by the devil.
29702: A sick woman suffering from tuberculosis says she hears the sound of hammering. It is an omen: she hears her coffin being made. Shortly afterwards she does indeed die.
29703: A woman expecting twins gives birth to two stillborn babies. A woman in the neighbourhood declares she had already suspected something was going to happen, because her dog kept howling eerily with its head turned towards the house of the twins' mother.
29704: When a witch goes out at night to do magic, she leaves a cow's tripe in her bed. The witch flies through the air on a broomstick.
29705: When stillborn twins are buried, a woman makes sure the little ones are wearing grave clothes in the coffin. For if they are buried naked, they keep wandering restlessly because they still want to receive a shroud.
29707: At night a group of headless children wanders about by the railway bridge. They are ghost children. Nobody dares walk past the railway bridge at night.
29712: You must never walk in the middle of the road at night, because you may be struck by an invisible hearse.
29713: If someone is born with a caul and the caul is removed the wrong way, that person must get out of bed all their life to watch funeral processions pass.
29716: When a dog starts howling eerily, an old woman and her son suspect that a death is coming. The old woman fears she will soon breathe her last. The son is very afraid of losing his mother. Shortly afterwards the son shoots four police officers dead. The dog had been howling for the death of the four officers.
29717: You can get an omen of many things that are going to happen in the future. If hammering sounds are heard at night, you can be sure that a new house will be built. If you see a house on fire, it actually burns down shortly afterwards. If you hear cries for help from the water, someone will soon drown.
29718: A scoffer coming out of the pub is seized by the devil and flung into the ditch. Yet he saw no one.
29719: You need not be afraid of witte juffers (white ladies) haunting about. The white ghost women can be driven away, the black ones cannot.
29723: If you look into the black mirror, you can see what will happen to you in the future.
29724: Freemasons are bulletproof. Freemasons have sold themselves to the devil for good. The devil gets the freemason's soul when he dies. Freemasons receive a wisseldaalder (a coin that always returns to its owner) from the devil. If they need more money, they hang an empty purse on the door handle in the evening. The next morning the purse is filled with money. Once you are a member of freemasonry, you can never get out.
29726: At a certain spot by a little bridge the devil jumped over the canal. The print of his horse's hoof can still be seen.
29728: A woman hears her neighbour wailing loudly in the field. The neighbour denies it. It is an omen: when two of the neighbour's children die four weeks later, the same wailing is heard.
29729: A mother and daughter hear the neighbour crying out in panic at night: 'My child! My child!' But when they go to look, the neighbour is simply asleep. The mother suspects that something is going to happen. It was indeed an omen: ten weeks later the neighbour's child drowns and the same wailing is heard.
29730: A girl often foresees deaths at night in passing funeral processions. Once she sees a lot of children walking behind a hearse. It is an omen: later, when someone from a family of dwarfs dies, the very small relatives walk behind the hearse.
29731: One night a girl sees two small coffins being carried to a hearse, followed by a funeral procession. It is a premonition: shortly afterwards two children die one right after the other.
29732: A clairvoyant girl predicts that something is about to happen in the family. That night she sees a funeral procession coming from her brother's place. The vision comes true: shortly afterwards the girl's brother dies.
29733: A clairvoyant man often has to get up at night because he has a vision. Once he sees his son hanging dead in an apple tree. The vision comes true: the next day the son hangs himself.
29734: A clairvoyant man sees his daughter lying dead in the lake. The vision comes true: a few days later the girl drowns herself.
29735: Near the house of a gravely ill man, strange sounds come from the ditch every evening. When the man lies on his deathbed, both his sons have to come home from abroad. The sounds were an omen: the dying man makes exactly the same sounds. When his boys come home, the man stops making the sounds and dies.
29737: Every evening a big light shines into a man's house. It is a portent: later the man has to leave his house because the train is going to run at that place.
29738: A man on his way one evening to help a baker suddenly finds it has gone completely dark around him. The next moment he is lifted up and put in the ditch. As long as it stays dark, he cannot climb up the bank. When it suddenly gets light again, he hurries out of the ditch. The man was seized by a funeral procession because he was walking in the middle of the road. Once the procession had passed, it became light again.
29739: A clairvoyant man is constantly driven out of bed to have visions. When he tries to stay in bed, a hand lifts him off it. Once the man has to walk a long way before he has a vision. He sees a decorated cart drawn by a white horse. He also sees a great many people and all sorts of other carts. He has foreseen the Queen's Day celebrations.
29745: A woman notices that every night at twelve o'clock her calves are standing loose in the stable. When the woman's sister keeps watch in the stable, she catches two cats, a big one and a small one. The small cat manages to escape; the big cat gets a good wallop. The cats are witches. The next day one of the two witches - the one who, as the big cat, took a heavy blow the day before - feels ill and has to stay in bed. The witch is suffering from the beating she got as a cat the day before.
29748: A cat catcher sells the skins of cats after flaying the animals. When the man once sees a whole bunch of cats sitting in a tree, he thinks he will make a good haul. When he hears that the cats are singing psalms, he quickly runs off. The cats are witches.
29749: A girl gets a fine big apple from a witch. The girl keeps the apple in the cupboard for a few days. When she wants to eat the apple, it has vanished. There is only a toad in the cupboard.
29750: A girl keeps an apple she got from a witch in a cupboard drawer. After a while the apple has turned into a toad.
29754: A reckless boy who does not believe in nightmares boasts that he would like to be visited by one. That night a nightmare climbs on top of the boy from the foot of the bed. The nightmare then squeezes the boy's throat shut. The boy resolves to grab the nightmare the next night as soon as he feels her at the foot of the bed. But the nightmare beats him to it: she grabs the boy by the neck straight away. The boy never again wished to be visited by a nightmare.
29755: A man is always visited by a nightmare at night.
29756: A man who is often tormented by a nightmare is advised to scatter flour on his face and blankets. The man follows the advice and the next day sees a girl sitting at his table. The girl, the nightmare, cannot get away because there is flour on her. The nightmare had entered the house through the keyhole. Every night the nightmare climbs on top of the man. The nightmare, who comes from a very rich family, promises the man a gift. With the large sum the girl gives him, the man buys a horse and cart.
29758: One night a boy is suddenly startled by a big black dog. The animal keeps following him annoyingly. When the same dog stays on his heels again another time, he throws a knife at it and later a pair of clogs. But the animal cannot be hit. The boy breaks off his courtship because his girlfriend turns out to be a witch. The dog was probably the witch.
29760: A witch has little dolls that she pricks with needles. Her son can also work magic. He likes to bewitch pigs. When the sorcerer throws some tobacco into the sty, the pigs lie deathly ill on their backs the next day. Wopke the duivelbanner (exorcist) gives asafoetida (devil's dung) to cure the animals.
29761: A dying woman urges her husband to take good care of her clothes after her death. When the man fails to do so, the woman cannot find rest and keeps wandering around the house.
29762: When you bury a dead person, you must make sure the shroud is not too long. Otherwise the dead keeps wandering restlessly, calling 'too long - too long'. Once, when a dead person was told to tear a piece off the shroud, the sound of tearing cloth was clearly heard. The dead then found rest and never appeared again.
29763: At a certain place psalm singing can be heard. It is an omen: later a church is built on that spot.
29764: Somewhere a house is ablaze. When people approach the house, it turns out not to be burning. It is a premonition: a few days later the house actually burns down.
29765: Wild lanterns are said to have been portents of the later bicycle, car and aeroplane lights.
29766: People born with a caul often foresee deaths in passing funerals and funeral processions. Their visions almost always have to do with death. It is told of one man born with a caul that he is driven out of bed at night to have a vision. An invisible force opens gates for him so that he can continue unhindered to the place where the vision is to appear.
29767: You should never walk in the middle of the road at night, because a funeral procession may drive you to the side.
29768: One evening a cursing card player is lifted up and thrown over the ditch. A playing card is displayed on his chest. The devil had got hold of him.
29769: A cursing rascal is suddenly startled by a black dog as big as a calf. The animal keeps annoyingly at his heels. The boy becomes terribly frightened because he realises that the strange animal has something to do with the devil.
29770: The ghost of a murdered girl keeps haunting.
29773: At a haunted place there is a chest of money in the ground. The money belongs to a lord who once lived in a castle that stood on that spot. When someone tries to get the treasure chest out of the ground, it keeps sinking deeper.
29775: The narrator was once visited by a nightmare. The nightmare jumped onto her feet like a cat and gradually crept towards her chest. At first the woman cannot utter a word, but shortly afterwards she manages to curse. The nightmare disappears. The woman's mother-in-law claims that, besides cursing, saying a little prayer helps to chase the nightmare away.
29776: A boy is sometimes tormented by a nightmare. When he sees the nightmare standing beside his bed, he wants to scream. But he cannot make a sound because the nightmare is squeezing his throat shut.
29780: A certain witch can turn herself into a cat and enters people's houses as a cat. When the witch goes out to do magic, she leaves a tripe behind on the bed. The witch can also fly.
29781: Witch cats sometimes hold a cat meeting at which they seem to be singing. At such a meeting the cats carry on terribly and discuss who is going to die. Soon after such a meeting someone dies.
29785: When a dog howls eerily or a magpie chatters close to the house, a death is coming. These are omens.
29786: One evening people see a strange cat walking near their house. A man throws a clog at the cat. The next day there is a big lump on the neighbour woman's head. The cat was a witch's cat. The neighbour woman had turned herself into a cat the day before.
29788: A girl receives an apple from an old woman and keeps it for a while. When the girl finally wants to eat the fruit, it has turned into a toad. The old woman is a witch.
29789: A witch sticks needles into a little doll.
29792: The wizard Imke de Jong can open any lock.
29796: The witch Harm has received a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) from the devil.
29797: At a haunted spot two girls wander about at night. It is said the girls were murdered long ago. It is also whispered that the girls were joined together.
29801: A woman suffers greatly from her frequent visions. She is very upset when she foresees deaths in passing funeral processions. One night, when she has to go out to have a vision, she stumbles. Through the fall she loses her second sight.
29802: It happens that at night someone urges another person to step aside for a passing funeral procession.
29803: At a haunted place there is a chest of money in the ground. If you try to dig up the chest, it keeps sinking deeper.
29804: At a haunted place an old lord haunts who once lived in a castle on that spot. He also has a chest of money in the ground.
29805: In the old days many wild lanterns were seen at a certain place. They are portents of the later car and bicycle lights.
29808: Witches often turn themselves into cats. As cats the witches often hold a meeting at which they sing. Witches can also fly on a broomstick. When witches leave the house, they leave a tripe behind.
29815: Freemasons have sold their souls to the devil. When their money runs out, they hang up a purse for the devil to fill. Once a freemason hangs up a bottomless boot for the devil. The devil does not manage to fill it. Freemasons die a strange death: they are often found with their necks wrung. Once you have sold yourself to the devil, you remain in his power.
29817: The sorcerer Stammerige Harm has received a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) from the devil. When Harm buys something for a guilder, the guilder always comes back to him. If you accept a guilder from Harm, you lose it again shortly afterwards.
29818: Freemasons sell their souls to the devil forever by accepting a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back).
29821: A witch - sister of the sorcerer Stammerige Harm - can turn herself into a cat. Another witch once got a good wallop as a cat. The next day the woman was lame.
29822: You must not eat anything you receive from a witch: it can turn into a toad in your stomach.
29824: Some witches fly through the air on a broomstick in the evening.
29923: The seventh of seven sons is born with a caul.
29925: You should never walk in the middle of the road, because a funeral procession may pass you.
29926: At a certain place it happened more than once that an indifferent man was thrown down by the devil.
29927: At a haunted spot a large beast with glowing eyes roams about. You not only see the animal coming, you also hear it coming, because its feet sound like shod horses' hooves. When the animal approaches you must get away quickly, or else you will be thrown. The animal is the devil. If you throw the devil-beast a bread crust over your left shoulder, it goes away. Many night walkers carry a bread crust in their pocket.
29931: A horse dealer treats his horses very badly. When the horses are dead, the ghosts of the animals keep wandering around the dealer's house at night.
29932: At a haunted spot a woman in white haunts. The ghost woman can only be seen at night. The horses are very afraid of her.
29933: Omens of various things that are going to happen in the future can often be perceived. If hammering sounds are heard, a new house is later built on that spot. If a house is seen on fire, it later actually burns down. If cries for help come from the water, a death by drowning soon follows.
29934: The narrator often saw wild lanterns floating above the land in the old days.
29939: When the dead keep wandering after their death, they cannot find rest because they did something wrong or because a promise made to them was not kept. The souls of murdered people also wander at night. A man who treated his wife badly during her life is constantly harassed by her ghost after her death.
29940: When people make a bottle of drink come with the help of a jack of spades, that is the devil's craft. The one who sent off the empty bottle with the playing card must not take hold of the filled bottle. If he does take it, things may end badly for him. The first glass must not be drunk but thrown over the left shoulder.
29942: In a mirror tent you can behold your future in a black mirror.
29943: Sorcerers can make rooks appear from the hearth pit.
29945: At a spot where the devil once jumped over the canal, there is the print of a horse's hoof.
29951: A woman hears the sounds of hammering and sawing and other work. It is a portent: later new houses are built on that spot.
29953: One evening two brothers see a funeral procession. It is a premonition: a few days later someone dies.
29954: A man born with a caul is often driven out of bed at night to have a vision. At the time of the Spanish flu (November 1918) the clairvoyant sees as many as seven funeral processions at once.
29955: When a dog howls eerily, a death is coming. When magpies chatter loudly, something is also about to happen. With magpie chatter it is less clear what is going to happen.
29957: When the village bell clanks as it is rung, a death is coming. It is an omen.
29958: One winter evening a married couple is suddenly startled by a big black dog that keeps annoyingly following at their heels. It is a ghost animal.
29959: If a dead person is buried in a shroud that is too short, he cannot find rest and keeps wandering at night. If the dead holds out a hand to you, you must not take it, because you risk losing your hand.
29960: Because people suspect that sick cows are bewitched, a test with salt is done. On three evenings in a row salt is scattered in the stables. The people scattering it walk backwards. If the cows have not recovered after three days, they are bewitched. The cows show no signs of recovery; if anything they seem to get sicker. When one evening a strange cat is spotted in the outbuilding, a boy gives the animal a wallop with a pitchfork. Later it turns out that a woman - a witch - has to stay in bed because of injuries. She was the witch in cat form. The same witch later bewitches the boy as well. According to the narrator there have always been witches and they are still active today: you can look it up in the Bible.
29961: The narrator's mother twice sees a woman's head at the window. The woman later flies away: she is a witch.
30024: When a funeral procession passes at night, usually on a sandy road, a death is coming. It is an omen. Such a procession cannot be seen with the ordinary eye. If you do not step aside for it, you are driven off the road.
30025: In Dokkum it happened several times that scoffers were flung off the road. It is the work of the devil.
30026: It is said that a big black dog roams about a certain place. People suspect that the animal is the devil. At that very place, a man does indeed come upon a dog with glowing eyes.
30030: A wagon with a load of hay starts moving by itself, without a horse in front. It is a portent: later the tractor is invented.
30031: Some people are said to have seen a fire in advance.
30032: In the old days wild lanterns were often seen at a certain place. The will-o'-the-wisps are said to have been portents of the later bicycle and car lights.
30033: In the nineteen-thirties a man often heard the sounds of milk churns and machines. He suspected that a dairy factory would come. His suspicion did not come true. Later, however, the land was reclaimed. During the reclamation all kinds of sounds could be heard as well.
30034: People hear cries for help coming from the water. It is a portent: later a drowning person really is in mortal danger.
30035: An odd man sits down at the table with a pan of beans. The devil then sits down opposite him with another pan of beans. The man then says, 'If it is of the Lord, come to me. If it is of the devil, depart from me.' The devil then flies around the man like a roaring lion.
30041: A man who is milking is addressed by a little man with a beard that almost drags along the ground. The little man warns him to leave this place at once, because strange things are about to happen. The man leaves immediately.
30049: People heard the train rumbling before it even ran. It was an omen.
30053: Every seven years a freemason must die, chosen by lot. Freemasons are never short of money because they get money from the devil. The devil has them in his power. Sometimes one of them must lose an arm.
30054: People born with a caul often foresee deaths at night in passing funeral processions. If you walk in the middle of the road at night, a passing funeral procession may drive you off the road.
30068: A woman on her way home is suddenly approached by a big black dog that will not leave her side. It is a phantom animal.
30070: A man born with a caul often has to get up at night to foresee deaths in passing funerals. He even foresaw the deaths of his own son and daughter, but he did not foresee that they would hang and drown themselves respectively.
30071: You should never walk in the middle of the road at night. An invisible funeral procession may drive you off the road.
30073: At a haunted spot two girls with red cloths around their necks wander about. The ghost girls cannot find rest because they were murdered long ago. Everyone is terribly afraid of the girls.
30075: In a haunted house everything is bewitched: livestock gets loose at night, strange noises can be heard, dishes suddenly break, bookshelves break of their own accord. A fat cat is found in the attic of the house. A woman hits the strange animal with a pitchfork. It was a witch's cat: the next day the witch in question has to stay in bed. In the form of a cat she had been struck with the pitchfork.
30078: At a haunted spot two white girls wander about. Such a witte juffer (white lady) is also said to have haunted another place.
30079: At a haunted place there is a chest of money in the ground. When someone tries to pull the chest up, it keeps sinking deeper into the ground. Long ago a gentleman was murdered at that place. He is said to still haunt it.
30083: If you eat something you got from a witch, you get a toad in your body. The narrator says that as a child she was never allowed to eat an apple from a supposed witch. If she first worked the apple with a knife, it could do no harm.
30084: A mother forbids her children to eat an apple they got from an old woman. She keeps the fruit in a locked drawer. Later there is a dead toad in the drawer. The old woman was a witch.
30086: Freemasons have sold their souls to the devil. A certain Freemason is never short of money because he received a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) from the devil. The man died in a strange way - cursing.
30087: Stammerige Harm has received a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) from the devil. Harm was also said to be able to do witchcraft.
30089: When short of money, a witch hangs an empty purse on the door in the evening. The next morning the purse is full of money.
30093: A man looks into the black mirror to find out which woman he will marry in the future. The woman he sees in the mirror does indeed later become his wife.
30094: A woman sees a coffin in the black mirror. The frightened woman is reassured: she will soon marry her brother-in-law. Before she can marry, however, the brother-in-law's current wife must die. The prediction comes true.
30095: At a place where a railway line now runs, wild lanterns could be seen in the old days. The will-o'-the-wisps were a portent of the later train lights.
30096: People heard the sound of the train before it was even running. The sounds were a portent.
30097: A sorcerer can fix people to the spot, and can also make them dance without stopping.
30102: A woman who knitted a great deal all her life keeps haunting after her death. The dead woman goes to the cupboard and holds her knitting in her hands. Her daughters know where they must take the knitting. When it arrives at its destination, the woman finds rest.
30105: A witch plays with little dolls at night: she makes them dance on the table and sticks pins into them.
30107: A group of people sees a woman with loose hair approaching in the evening. She stays silent when one of the men asks her something, and floats away. She is a woman who was once murdered and now haunts the place.
30108: A woman dreams that her husband comes home with a clock and a table. A few weeks later he buys a pendulum clock and a table.
30109: A woman foresees that her neighbour will die, and so it happens.
30110: A woman's prediction to some children that their father will not live much longer comes true.
30111: A woman is not frightened by terrible things, because she knows everything in advance, although she was not born with a caul. Children born with a caul whose caul is removed forwards are bound to see everything. If the caul is removed backwards, there is nothing to worry about.
30112: Because funeral processions need the space, it is best not to walk in the middle of the road at night.
30113: A boy falls ill after eating a biscuit he was given by an old woman. The boy turns out to be bewitched. The devil-banisher gives the boy's father a remedy but warns him about a big dog that will try to take the medicine from him. The father is given two pieces of rye bread to throw to the dog. The devil-banisher advises him to carry the potion on his chest with his hand pressed firmly on it. The prediction comes true. When the father has given the animal the second piece of rye bread, it keeps quiet. The father must give his son the medicine when no one is in the room. All the holes in the house must also be sealed. When the boy has taken the medicine, he raves, just as the devil-banisher predicted. Shortly afterwards a loud knocking is heard that no one can explain. When the ominous knocking continues, the devil-banisher is consulted again. He declares that there will be a wreath in the boy's pillow. The wreath must be removed and burnt together with the pillow. The wreath must be burnt in a remote place with no one else present. When the wreath has burnt up, a sound will be heard. As soon as this sound is heard, one can go home, because the boy will then be released. The boy then only has to tell who gave him the biscuit, according to the devil-banisher. The father does what the devil-banisher told him and learns that an old woman from Hallum is the culprit. The devil-banisher claims that the old woman, the witch, will be completely burnt if she is the culprit. The woman does indeed have all sorts of burns. The cured boy, named Wâtse, is from then on nicknamed 'Wâtse Klop' (Wâtse Knock).
30114: A young woman is bewitched and shows hardly any signs of life. The young woman is laid on the floor and a chalk line is drawn around her whole body. An approaching white mouse cannot cross the line to reach the woman. When one of those present wipes away a bit of the line with a wet finger, the little animal immediately flies into the woman's mouth. The woman at once starts breathing normally again and recovers.
30116: A midwife pulls the caul of a newborn backwards off its face. The child will be spared from visions. (Only if the caul is removed forwards does the person foresee, for example, deaths in passing funeral processions.) A greedy doctor is furious because the midwife has burned the caul.
30117: When a dog howls eerily, a death is coming within a certain time. It is an omen. People used to be very afraid of it.
30118: At a certain spot the sounds of carpentry can be heard. It is an omen: later a new house is built there.
30119: People see a place on fire. It is a premonition: later the place actually burns down. At a certain spot where psalm singing is heard, a church later rises. The singing is also an omen.
30121: At a certain place by the water people hear cries for help. It is an omen: later someone drowns and the same sound can be heard.
30123: While drunk, a man buries a chest of money in the ground. Once sober, he cannot remember where he buried the treasure. The money has never been found.
30133: A man born with a caul often foresees deaths in passing funeral processions. His visions always come true.
30136: A farmhand wants to go to the market, but there is ploughing to be done. When the plough gets stuck, the farmer allows him to go to the market. Once the boy is gone, the farmer finds a treasure while digging out the plough. The farmer, who had never been well off, has become a rich man.
30140: In the black mirror you can see your future foretold. A man is shown the likeness of his future wife. He also gets information about the number of children he will have and about his age.
30141: Freemasons must keep to certain rules so as never to be short of money. If they do not follow the rules, they die within a few weeks. Freemasons sometimes meet underground. They meet once a week. A freemason must first put every decision he makes before the other freemasons. Freemasons have made a contract with the devil. When short of money, they hang an empty purse on the door. The next morning the purse is filled. Every so many years a freemason must die, chosen by lot. Once you are a member of the order, you can never leave. A freemason who becomes a widower may not remarry right away.
30147: During the German occupation, many young men always stood guard at night to detect any trouble. On one of those nights two boys very clearly hear a plaintive voice calling for help. One morning a married couple repeatedly hears the same cries of someone in distress. When the couple follows the sound, they find someone who has fallen under a train while hurriedly trying to jump onto it as it moved. The victim dies shortly afterwards. The earlier sounds in the night were a portent.
30151: Grandfather tells that there were witches who could change into cats.
30173: A man makes rooks come out of the hearth by reading from a magic book. The rooks go back into the hearth when he reads the same thing backwards.
30304: A father and son hear the sounds of bricklaying, carpentry and sawing at night, although nothing can be seen. It is a portent: shortly afterwards the same sounds are heard when a farmhouse is renovated.
30305: A boy predicts that a canal will come somewhere because he has seen a sailing ship floating on the land. The prediction comes true: later a canal is dug.
30306: A woman predicts that her son will come. The prediction comes true.
30307: A woman born with a caul often foresees deaths in passing funeral processions. The visions always come true.
30311: If someone dies and the body lies unburied over a Sunday, another death will soon follow.
30313: A big black dog roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal.
30314: One night a man is suddenly startled by a big black dog. The man does not dare to pass the animal, which is as big as a calf and has glowing eyes. It is a phantom animal.
30324: If you hit your mother, your hand grows out above your grave.
30325: A poor woman who is always short of money sighs that she would like to have a bit more money at hand. When shortly afterwards she finds a large sum of money, she walks past it because she suspects the money is the devil's.
30327: A man neglects his cows, which are half starving. One morning during milking one of the animals says: 'I must have more food. We give no milk today, because we are hungry.' The frightened man suspects his cattle are bewitched and has his brother milk the cows. Shortly afterwards, to his horror, the man sees a pedlar drive a cart through the keyhole. The man leaves his house and flees to the minister to convert and become a Baptist.
30330: You should never walk in the middle of the road at night, because a passing funeral procession may strike you.
30331: A rough, cursing sinner who often mistreats animals is one day harassed by the devil. The devil, a black figure, seizes him and flings him against the ceiling. The man is so badly hurt that he has to stay home for weeks. After his recovery he repents and joins the Reformed church. Since the beating by the devil the man walks with a stick.
30334: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal.
30335: A sorcerer conjures little soldiers out of the hearth pit and makes them march. A man visiting the sorcerer becomes very frightened by it.
30337: Wilde lantaarnen (wild lanterns) are a portent of the later bicycle lamps and street lighting.
30343: A cheese merchant sees a man burying a dead baby with the words 'Lord, I now give this child over to You'. The man's daughter had given birth shortly before. The baby, however, died soon after the birth. Later the place where the baby was buried is haunted.
30350: A man promises his wife on her deathbed that he will not remarry. The man does not keep his promise and marries a second wife. His first, dead wife keeps harassing the man: at night she lies stiff against him in bed. When he tries to touch her, she has suddenly vanished. From then on the man wants to sleep in a separate bed.
30351: At a haunted spot near a farm naked children dance about at night. The children are said to have been murdered there long ago and unable to find rest.
30353: At a haunted spot witte wieven (white women) haunt.
30356: Someone was once murdered at a haunted spot. The ghost of the murdered person still wanders about.
30357: At a certain place someone was thrown off the road by a passing funeral procession. Another man once urged his companion to step aside for an approaching funeral procession. The companion, however, could not see the procession at all.
30359: Witches from a certain place can fly through the air on a broomstick.
30362: Two lazy people never seem to do anything. They can afford not to work because they own a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back). If you spend a wisseldaalder, you always get it back. If you have a wisseldaalder, you have sold your soul to the devil.
30363: Early in the morning a man is pushed off the road, bicycle and all. A funeral procession has to pass.
30364: A boy has repeatedly seen a funeral procession pass at night. When the boy greets it, his greeting is never returned. It is an omen.
30365: A man born with a caul is constantly forced to foresee things.
30366: Children are warned never to walk in the middle of the road at night, since a passing funeral procession may strike them.
30367: When a girl falls ill, a notorious witch is suspected of having bewitched the child. The devil-banisher gives them a medicine. When they open the girl's pillow, a wreath of feathers appears. The wreath is burnt. The next day the witch goes about with a cloth around her head because burning the wreath has given her burns. The burns are the proof that this woman is the culprit, the witch.
30369: At a certain spot, around midnight, the sounds of carpentry and other work can be heard. It is a portent: later a farmstead is built on that spot.
30370: A butcher's children often hear animal body parts fall to the ground with a thud, although their father has not yet started work. It is a portent.
30378: A girl looks into a witch's house and sees the witch at the table playing with a doll. The witch sticks needles into the doll.
30379: A witch can fly. A man once saw a witch fly from one plot of land to another.
30380: Children are forbidden to accept anything from a witch because she can bewitch them. The witch once also bewitched to death a dog belonging to her husband's son.
30383: Cries for help can be heard by the canal, although there is nothing to be seen. It is a portent: later someone drowns at that spot.
30384: At a notorious haunted spot a silent woman passes a group of young people. The woman runs between the rails of the horse tram. Another boy says that something has fallen on the road, which he cannot see. The woman is a ghost woman. She cannot find rest because she was murdered long ago.
30385: A woman speaks to a schoolgirl who is picking blackberries. When the girl looks up, there is no one to be seen. It is a ghost woman.
30388: A woman sees a funeral procession pass. It is a premonition: later someone really does die.
30389: A woman born with a caul often has to get up at night to foresee deaths in passing funeral processions. The visions always come true.
30390: You should never walk in the middle of the road at night, since a passing funeral procession may drive you off the road.
30391: Strange things happen in a certain barn: a haunted barn. There is a spot on the floor where you cannot lie. Workers spending the night there are roughly thrown off that spot. A dog once got a hard blow as well. A woman sees a ghost walking in the barn at night. Someone was once murdered in the barn.
30394: Of seven girls in a household, one is a nightmare. It is also said that the seventh is a kween (a barren woman). The nightmare enters the house through the keyhole. The nightmare climbs up from the foot of the bed and squeezes people's throats shut. If you grab at the nightmare, she is gone. You can stop a nightmare by laying a cross in front of your bed.
30395: A man sees wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns) flying. It is a portent of the later car headlights.
30401: At a haunted place there is a chest of money in the ground. When someone tries to dig up the treasure, it keeps sinking deeper. An old lord who once lived in a castle there haunts the place. The treasure is his property. The man cannot reach his treasure. Each year he comes only one tiny step closer.
30402: In the past you were often warned not to step on a toad, because thunder would then come. A woman who coughs a lot is advised to wear a live toad on her chest. If children eat something they got from a witch, they get a toad in their body.
30403: Sometimes the sound of the butter churn can be heard at night. It is a portent of work that is to be done later.
30405: During his military service the mischievous wizard Imke de Jong is often thrown in jail. The wizard always frees himself effortlessly.
30407: People can make a bottle of drink come with the help of a jack of spades. It is claimed, however, that it is trickery.
30408: A sorcerer can conjure little soldiers and birds out of the hearth pit by whistling. The little soldiers immediately start marching.
30420: At night a woman suddenly hears terrible screaming, although there is nothing to be seen. It is said to be a portent of an approaching death by drowning. According to the narrator, nobody drowned afterwards.
30422: At a haunted place there is a chest of money in the ground. When someone tries to dig up the chest, it keeps sinking deeper. One night a group of diggers is startled by the ghost with the yellow heels. The driver of the wagon the diggers came on is not at all afraid of the ghost and invites it to sit beside him on the wagon. Then the driver can no longer get the horses to move. When the clock strikes two, the wagon suddenly shoots forward into the pond. The wagon sinks and is never seen again. Later people said it ended badly because the diggers talked instead of keeping silent while digging. Only if you know the words spoken by the person who once buried the treasure may you say them, and then you can dig up the treasure.
30423: A drunken, indifferent man is startled at night by someone at his door. When he says 'let that devil come in', it turns out really to be the devil. The next day the man lies dead in bed: the devil has wrung his neck.
30424: Two fishermen hold a companion overboard and he drowns. Later the place where the man drowned is haunted.
30427: A strange cat is often a witch, because witches often change themselves into cats.
30428: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place.
30429: At a spot where a new church is being built, organ music had been heard earlier. It was an omen.
30430: People born with a caul often foresee deaths in passing funeral processions. You should never walk in the middle of the road at night, because you may end up in a funeral procession.
30431: A drunken sinner is often seized by the devil and thrown into the ditch.
30432: Someone once came face to face with a big black dog at night. It is probably a phantom animal.
30450: A sorcerer makes little soldiers appear from the hearth pit and drill. Sometimes he also stops the clock.
30451: A sorcerer brings a dog cart to a standstill on the road.
30452: When a dog howls eerily, a death is coming.
30453: When the owl sits on the same spot on the house every evening and calls, there will be a death close by. It is an omen.
30454: People born with a caul often foresee deaths in funeral processions at night.
30455: At a certain haunted spot the well-known ghost the Lange Sleatterman, once a sinful blacksmith, wanders about because he cannot find rest. The ghost is the terror of many skippers. A skipper's daughter once sees a man standing on the foredeck of the ship and suspects that he is the Lange Sleatterman. She is so frightened that she quickly runs away. A few days later she died of the fright.
30456: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal.
30458: One evening someone suddenly comes face to face with a big black dog. It is probably a phantom animal.
30459: It brings bad luck to see a black cat crossing the road.
30460: A coffin maker knows in advance when he will get an order, because he hears the sound of hammering beforehand.
30477: Freemasons have sold their soul to the devil and die a strange death. They are usually found with their head turned around on their body. Freemasons are never short of money because they have a pact with the devil. If you try to leave the freemasons, you die. Freemasons are always hammering away because they never finish anything.
30478: An indifferent scoffer, on his way home from the pub at night, is startled by a black thing. When he bursts into frightened wailing, the thing suddenly disappears again. It was the devil.
30479: Someone is said to have been startled on the road by a big black dog: a phantom animal.
30480: A curser is suddenly seized and thrown over the trees. The devil had got hold of him. The sinner stops cursing at once.
30481: At a haunted spot two girls with red cloths around their necks wander about. The girls are said to have been murdered long ago.
30482: A white horse haunts a haunted place: a phantom animal.
30485: Before the war broke out, a woman already saw a whole army. The vision came true.
30486: A man born with a caul foresees the suicide of his son and daughter. He is often driven out of bed at night to see a funeral in the churchyard. When he is out at night, all gates open for him. The man's visions always come true.
30487: In a certain place people are sometimes driven aside at night by an invisible funeral procession. It is a portent of an approaching death. It is wise never to walk in the middle of the road.
30491: Of seven girls in a household, one is a nightmare. The narrator was once visited by a nightmare and could no longer breathe. To scare nightmares off you must scatter flour, for if the nightmare gets flour on her, she cannot get away. Putting slippers with the heels against the bed also helps. Nightmares also torment horses by tangling their manes.
30493: Witches have little dolls that they stick needles into. When witches go out to work magic, they leave a paunch behind.
30494: If you eat something you got from a witch, you get a toad in your body. A worried mother held back an apple her child got from a witch. The apple later became a toad.
30495: The sorcerer Imke de Jong can fix people to the spot. Imke is often thrown in jail but always manages to free himself effortlessly.
30496: In the black mirror you can see what will happen in the future.
30502: Wilde lantaarnen (wild lanterns) are portents of the later moped lights.
30503: At a haunted spot a zwarte juffer (black lady) haunts. If you do not step aside for the black ghost woman, she drives you to the side.
30504: A witch can change into a cat. As a cat she often holds a meeting with other witch cats at which there is singing. Witches must bewitch someone to death at least once every seven years so as not to die themselves.
30505: The sorcerer Stammerige Harm likes to bewitch cattle. Harm is a freemason and owns a wisseldaalder (a magic coin that always returns). Freemasons are never short of money because they have a wisseldaalder. A freemason eventually has his neck wrung by the devil. Once every seven years a freemason - and a witch - must die. A certain freemason once tried to get away from freemasonry but was then chased by the devil. In his pursuit the devil jumps over the canal. He leaves the print of a horse's hoof in the stone. The devil seizes the fleeing freemason and wrings his neck.
30506: A sorcerer makes rooks appear from the hearth pit. Later the rooks fly away up the chimney.
30509: At a haunted place there is a chest of gold in the ground. The owner of the treasure was murdered long ago. The dead man has always haunted, restless, the place where his treasure lies in the ground. No one manages to dig up the chest: it keeps sinking deeper into the ground.
30511: At a certain place there is a gate that keeps springing open: a ghost gate. A witte juffer (white lady) wanders about near the gate.
30514: A dead man keeps wandering restlessly because he was buried in a shroud that is too long. When he keeps knocking on his family's window, calling 'Too long! Too long!', the family calls in the minister. The minister addresses the man about his unfulfilled wish and lays a shorter shroud on his grave. Now the dead man finds rest.
30515: A man promises his wife on her deathbed that he will not remarry. The man breaks his promise and marries again. His first, dead wife then keeps wandering: she lies down beside him in bed, follows him everywhere and knocks on the door. The man becomes so desperate that he hangs himself.
30517: In the past, the sounds of threshing could often be heard at night. It was a portent of work that would be done the next day.
30520: A married couple hears sounds at night as if a lot of work is being done. It is a portent: later a farmhouse is built on that spot.
30521: At a haunted place there is a chest of money in the ground. When someone tries to dig up the treasure, it keeps sinking deeper into the ground.
30522: At a haunted spot the ghost of a dead man wanders about. Will-o'-the-wisps are also often seen at the same place.
30525: Someone hears loud wailing. It is a portent: a few days later someone drowns.
30526: A father and son suddenly see smoke rising from chimneys on the water. It is a portent: later farmhouses are built on that spot.
30528: At a certain place black cats haunt the area. They are witch cats.
30529: Before the war broke out, a woman already saw Hitler's troops on the moon. It was a vision of the future.
30530: A man born with a caul foresees deaths in passing funeral processions. The visions always come true.
30531: At a haunted place where a castle once stood, an old lord haunts. Long ago the old lord buried a treasure in the ground. After burying it, he rode back sitting backwards on his horse so he could keep looking at the place where the treasure was buried for as long as possible.
30533: People hear the sounds of hammering and chiselling without anything being visible. It is a portent: later new farmhouses are built on that spot.
30535: When a barn owl sits calling on the owl board, a death is coming in that house.
30536: When fish leap out of the water, a death is coming. It is an omen.
30543: At a certain spot many wilde lantaarnen (wild lanterns) used to be seen.
30546: A man can tell from the deathly sound of the bell that a death is coming. It is an omen.
30565: When a little bird flies against the window, a death is coming. It is an omen.
30566: A mother stops her child from eating an apple and a pear received from a witch. The next day the fruits have turned into a big frog and a toad.
30583: A father and son very clearly hear the sounds of threshing at night. It is a portent of work that will be done later.
30584: You can get a bottle of jenever (Dutch gin) from the devil with the help of a jack of spades. A few people want to get a filled bottle and tie the playing card with a string to the neck of the bottle. One person then hands the bottle out at the door. Another promises to take the filled bottle, but does not dare after all, for fear of the devil. If the one who sent off the empty bottle then also takes the full bottle, he will suffer greatly.
30854: Someone hears the sound of the train on the rails before the train is even running. It is a portent.
30855: A woman born with a caul urges people to step aside for a passing funeral procession.
30856: A cursing sinner is visited by the devil and has his neck wrung. The sinner is found dead in bed.
30857: A hunter and his dog suddenly come upon a black thing. The dog does not dare to pass it. The black thing disappears as suddenly as it appeared. It is a ghostly thing.
30858: A farmer who wants to go milking in the morning is frightened by a round thing, like a wheel, that rolls into the ditch in front of him. It is a ghostly thing.
30859: Someone hears terrible screaming, although there is nothing to be seen. It is a portent: when someone later drowns, the same sound can be heard.
30860: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place. Many people are afraid of this phantom animal.
30863: A witch can turn herself into a cat and fly on a broomstick.
30884: A man tells of his dream in which a skipper jumps in after his daughter to save her from drowning. The skipper and his daughter then both drown. It is a prophetic dream: the next day a skipper and his daughter die in that way.
30885: A man who lost his daughter had already foreseen her death weeks in advance: one night he saw the coffin standing in the room. He also saw his daughter being taken to the churchyard.
30886: A man foresees that another man will lose his daughter: he sees the funeral procession.
30888: A woman dreams that a milkman comes to her bed to say that something bad is about to happen. The dream comes true: a few days later the same milkman comes to tell the woman that her friend is dead. It is whispered that a doctor poisoned the man.
30889: Whenever a certain woman dreamt of horses, a death in the family would follow within a short time.
30890: An indifferent, godless sinner boasts that he would like to have the devil as a companion. At once he is seized and thrown down by the devil. The sinner is converted out of fright.
30891: A mortally ill little boy makes his mother promise never to sell the silver buckles on his shoes. The mother promises to follow her son's wish, but after his death she sells the buckles out of poverty. The boy's ghost then keeps wandering. When the minister addresses the boy about his unfulfilled wish, it becomes clear that the boy wants his buckles back. The mother manages to buy the buckles back and the boy finds rest.
30892: At a haunted spot naked little children wander about at night. The dead children cannot find rest because they were buried without a shroud.
30893: A boy claims that a devil in the shape of a fat black dog comes at him to grab him.
30952: When a father fetches asafoetida for his bewitched little son, he is approached by two cats with glowing eyes. He gives one of the animals a wallop. The next day an old woman has bruises all over her face. The father immediately names her as the one behind the bewitchment. She was the witch in cat form.
30953: A skipper notices that his boat often suddenly comes loose. One evening when he comes back from a party, the whole boat has disappeared. The skipper then sees two ghosts wandering about. They are the ghosts of two small children who were murdered at that place long ago.
30955: A man often finds wreaths in his pillows and suspects a witch is at work. When he once sees a strange cat, he shoots at the animal with his gun. The next day an old woman is lame. She was the witch in cat form.
