30962: When you are out at night, you should keep well to the side of the road, or else a funeral procession may drive you aside.
30963: A drunken sinner is suddenly startled by the devil. The man is so frightened that he later repents.
30964: The wizard Imke de Jong always frees himself effortlessly when he is locked up.
30966: The sorcerer Imke de Jong fixes an annoying sergeant to the spot.
30968: A drunken sinner is seized and thrown down by the devil. The sinner repented afterwards.
30970: At night someone is driven to the side of the road by an invisible funeral procession.
30972: Stammerige Harm is never short of money because he received a wisseldaalder (a coin that always comes back) from the devil.
30973: Freemasons never lack money because they have received a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) from the devil.
30997: When it is foggy in a certain place, people say the witte wieven (white women) are holding a meeting.
31005: A man dreams that a farmhouse burns down. He sees very clearly a glowing ball on the owl board (gable ornament). The dream comes true: the farmhouse burns down fourteen days later.
31006: A man dreams of the funeral of a relative. The dream comes true: two days later a relative dies.
31007: When a cyclist tries to remove a branch from his front wheel while riding, he goes head over heels. The man has a sprained little finger but predicts that this will be his death. The prediction comes true: he dies within the year.
31008: When a man smells the odour of a corpse near the churchyard, a death is coming. It is an omen.
31014: Around midnight a man is suddenly startled by a black cat. The man kicks the animal so hard that its paw is broken. The next day another man has a broken wrist. He was the sorcerer in cat form.
31015: Three devil banishers try to drive away a ghost. The ghost is an old lord, sitting backwards on a donkey, who long ago buried a chest of money in the ground at that place. The devil banishers catch the ghost in a large chest and tie the donkey behind a horse-drawn wagon. Both horses pulling the devil banishers' wagon bolt and run straight into the canal. The ghost and one of the devil banishers drown.
31016: A chest of money is buried at a haunted spot. The treasure cannot be dug up because it sinks deeper into the ground every time it is touched.
31018: A man born with a caul who is fond of a drink often foresees deaths in passing funeral processions.
31021: A witch pricks a little doll with a needle to make people ill.
31022: A sorcerer can fix people to the spot.
31026: A girl wants a fortune teller to predict her future. At first the fortune teller does not want to say, but when the girl keeps insisting she gives in: she has foreseen the girl's funeral. A few weeks later the girl does indeed die.
31029: A poor man makes a pact with the devil to get out of his money troubles. When he is later bursting with money, he wants to escape the devil's power again. In a dream the man promises a doorman of a banquet hall, the devil, that he will return to the feast forever the next day. When he wakes up, he reasons that it was only a dream, and so he does not go back to the place. But on his way to town he falls from his horse and breaks his neck: the devil's work.
31030: Two men own a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin). You never lose a wisseldaalder and always get it back, as long as you make sure not to spend all of it.
31040: At a haunted spot witte wieven (white women) always haunt around midnight.
31042: An odd bachelor who lives somewhat secluded and never seems to do anything always sets the table for two. It turns out the devil joins him for a meal every day. The bachelor once sold his soul to the devil. Every day the devil leaves a rijksdaalder (two-and-a-half guilder coin) for him under a stone. One day the bachelor is found dead, his head twisted round on his body.
31043: A sinner is picked up out of nowhere and flung across the room. Afterwards he became quite reformed.
31044: A curser is seized and flung across the road.
31049: An old woman gives an apple as a present to a girl she does not much like. The girl's mother forbids the child to eat the apple and keeps the fruit in a flowerpot. Two weeks later the flowerpot is full of little toads: the old woman is a witch.
31050: At a certain spot people hear a tremendous noise, although nothing can be seen. It is an omen: later a house is built on that spot which collapses shortly afterwards. When it collapses, the same noise is heard as before. Nobody dares to build on that spot any more, because the devil is said to be in the ground.
31051: A certain witch makes people ill by pricking little dolls with needles.
31052: Certain sorcerers can fix people to the spot. One of these sorcerers can make tables and chairs dance and turn paper money into newspaper.
31056: If you want to get money from the devil, you must run around the churchyard three times at night with a black cat in a sack. If you see someone, you must give him the cat. At home you must hang a black, or possibly grey, sock on a line. The next morning the sock is filled with money: the devil's work. Fourteen days later, however, you are dead.
31099: A wizard manages to calm a dangerous dog that mauls everyone. He sends the animal away for three days and it comes back completely changed.
31106: At a certain place the tram is heard before it even runs. It is an omen.
31107: If hammering is heard at a certain spot, new houses will come. It is an omen.
31113: A clairvoyant foresees a death in a passing funeral procession. The vision comes true.
31114: A man born with a caul foresees the death of his brother-in-law in a passing funeral procession.
31116: A man suddenly sees a person who died long ago standing by the water and becomes very frightened.
31117: At a certain spot lights can often be seen in the evening. It is a portent: it is the lighting of houses that will be built later.
31119: When sorcerers fly through the air on a broomstick they are called witches. In a certain place a mother and a daughter were both said to be witches.
31121: To get a bottle of drink you must send off a jack of hearts. The one who threw the card outside must not take hold of the filled bottle. The first glass of drink is thrown over the left shoulder with the words 'Here, devil, this is for you'.
31122: A woman has received a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) from the devil and so never lacks money.
31150: A whole crowd of people watches a man who supposedly crawls through a beam. A wizard who wants to show that it is a deception kicks the beam and turns it into straw.
31179: At a certain place people saw a house on fire that really did burn down a few days later. It was a premonition.
31180: A clairvoyant man is often driven out of bed at night to foresee deaths in passing funeral processions. Sometimes he can predict exactly who will die when he recognises the people in the procession. The visions always come true. The man was born with a caul - a membrane over the head. Greedy midwives are often after cauls to sell them dearly to doctors. If the caul is burned immediately after birth, the child has no clairvoyant gifts.
31185: When there are white crests of foam on the waves, people say the witte wieven (white women) are riding on them.
31187: Freemasons never lack money because they have a pact with the devil. Every so many years a Freemason must die. The dead man then belongs to the devil.
31192: People with a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) have a pact with the devil. A wisseldaalder can never run out.
31194: In some houses there is a hole that can never be closed again. It has to do with the devil.
31196: At night a foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal.
31200: In a certain place there is a bottomless pool. A child once drowned there. Later the child's ghost still haunted the place.
31203: A horse haunts a haunted place, only at night. It is a phantom animal.
31204: Witches can turn themselves into a cat. When such a witch's cat gets a wallop, the witch shows signs of injury on her arms or legs the next day. Witches' cats hold meetings, sitting in a circle in the field, to catch up.
31205: In a certain place it happens that someone is seized for no reason and thrown down by an invisible force. After such an incident a person often converts.
31206: In a certain place the witches fly through the air on brooms. Children are warned never to step on toads, or the thunder will come.
31209: A man born with a caul often has to get up at night to foresee deaths in passing funeral processions. The clairvoyant also foresees other things.
31211: A man sees little lights on a stretch of heathland in the evening. It is an omen: later houses are built on that spot.
31212: A man hears the sound of a moving train and a voice saying 'Harkema-Opeinde, all change!', although no train runs there yet. It is perhaps an omen.
31213: At a certain place a gate keeps springing open: a ghost gate. Twelve men who take turns trying to push the gate shut at night see it spring open again every time. Someone was once murdered at that place. The ghost of the dead person still wanders about and keeps opening the gate.
31214: A woman warns two men not to go fishing: their boat will capsize and come back without them. The men ignore the woman and go fishing anyway. Her prediction comes true: both men drown; an empty boat comes back.
31217: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal.
31228: A woman suddenly turns deathly pale: she says she has seen a black dog that came to bring news of a death. A family member will die. A few days later someone in the family does indeed die. The dog was the messenger of death.
31230: One night a naughty boy is suddenly startled by a big black dog. It is the devil. After this incident the boy becomes a lot calmer.
31231: About seventy years ago the narrator saw the devil in the shape of a gnome.
31232: A nightmare is a woman who comes into people's houses through the keyhole at night. When the nightmare reaches people's beds, they can do nothing against her. If they manage to lift their foot, they are freed again.
31234: A woman makes her insane daughter live in a hole in the hay. When the daughter finally dies, she goes on haunting the hay barn for a long time.
31238: A woman practises black magic. She sticks a needle into a photo of someone she dislikes. That person then falls ill and dies.
31239: Freemasons never lack money because they have a pact with the devil. They must pay for this pact later. Every so many years a Freemason chosen by lot must die: a sacrifice to the devil.
31240: A sorcerer can fix people to the spot. He can also make people's hands stick together.
31250: At a certain place people hear the train before it even runs. It is an omen.
31261: Sometimes someone sends off a jack of spades and gets a bottle of jenever (Dutch gin) in its place. The first glass is for the devil and must be thrown over the left shoulder.
31262: Some people can make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit.
31263: A white horse haunts a haunted place at night. It is a phantom animal.
31284: When people hear hammering or see flames, it means houses will be built or burn down, respectively. These are omens. Helmdragers (people born with a caul) have to get up at night to foresee deaths in passing funeral processions. When a dog howls eerily or black rooks appear at the door, a death is coming. Wild lanterns were foreshadowings of the later bicycle lights.
31303: A man is coming back from skating and suddenly sees a strange, floating light. The light floats to a churchyard and disappears into a grave. It is a wilde lantaarn (wild lantern, a will-o'-the-wisp).
31309: A man sees a farmhouse on fire. It is an omen: a week later the farmhouse actually burns down.
31310: A woman born with a caul foresees a death at night in a passing funeral procession. The vision comes true: a week later the real funeral takes place.
31311: A man has had a vision and predicts that a strange yellow flower will grow at a certain spot in the churchyard. The vision comes true: when the man dies shortly afterwards, a yellow evening primrose grows on his grave.
31314: A certain man was said to fight regularly with the devil. He can handle the little devils; the old devil gives him more trouble.
31315: A few people very clearly see a house standing at a certain spot, although there is no house there. It is a portent: later a house is built on that spot.
31316: A few people see the tram before it even runs. It is a portent.
31317: A group of men spending the night in a tent suddenly feel something heavy coming over them. It is a portent: later a dike is built on that spot.
31318: The portents of the tram are called wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns).
31321: A sorcerer makes sure that someone who has ridiculed him cannot drive on with his wagon: he makes a spoke of the wheel break without going near the wagon.
31322: A farmer has a son who can do magic. Once the son enters the house through the keyhole.
31325: You should not walk in the middle of the road at night: a funeral procession may drive you aside.
31386: A skater suddenly notices he is being followed and tries to stay ahead of whoever is accompanying him. A little later it turns out to be the devil: the devil ends up in a hole in the ice.
31398: When a barn owl or a magpie sits near the house, something serious is about to happen: it is an omen of, for example, death. When two magpies sit near the house, visitors are coming.
31399: A man out at night suddenly hears a dog howling eerily and becomes very frightened. Shortly afterwards he hears a strange sound and sees something black approaching over the water. When the thing then also moves over the land, the man quickly gets away. It is a portent: later a canal is dug at that place and the steamboat sails there.
31400: A sorcerer fixes a horse and wagon to the ground.
31401: People make a bottle of jenever (Dutch gin) come with the help of a playing card, usually a jack of spades.
31403: A dog with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place. Many are afraid of this phantom animal.
31404: A place where someone once hanged himself is haunted. The dead person has kept wandering about.
31405: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal.
31406: A man suddenly sees a white figure floating across the road. The ghost looks like a human being.
31411: A skipper is suddenly beset by all sorts of cats. Because he suspects they are witches' cats, he throws a knife at one of them. A little later he finds his knife in a farmer's wife's house. She was the witch in cat form.
31416: At a certain spot, boatmen hear the sound of wagons driving over a bridge. Only much later is the bridge actually built. It is an omen.
31417: If the caul of someone born with one is destroyed just after birth, that person is not tormented by visions. People born with a caul often foresee deaths in passing funeral processions.
31418: A woman claims to have heard the tram before it even ran.
31480: A man sees the tram go by before it even runs. It is an omen.
31481: At a certain spot little lights can be seen again and again. It is an omen: two years later a farmhouse is built on that spot.
31482: People born with a caul foresee deaths in passing funeral processions.
31483: Two friends agree to walk to meet each other. When one woman sees her friend approaching in the distance, she says 'There you are already'. As soon as she has spoken the words, the friend suddenly vanishes. When she walks on to her friend's house, it turns out the friend has not even left home yet. It was a vision of the future.
31484: An old woman can tell who stole her gooseberries without having seen the thieves.
31490: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck runs about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal.
31492: An indifferent curser is seized by the devil and flung against the collar beam. After the beating he repents.
31493: When the bell rings in a certain way or a dog howls eerily, a funeral is coming. It is an omen.
31498: In the attic of a farmstead lies a skull. The skull must not be moved, or strange things happen: the doors, for example, fly open by themselves.
31500: Two lawyers are possessed by the devil and are confined by the exorcist in a circle on the ground. The two lawyers can never leave the circle and keep haunting that spot. Since then the piece of land has been called 'Advocatenland' (Lawyers' Land).
31502: A farm maid often hears the hay wagon driving at night. It is a portent of what is going to happen the next day.
31503: At a certain place wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns) can often be seen. It is a portent of the tram.
31505: People born with a caul often have to get up at night to foresee deaths in passing funeral processions. From the procession it is often possible to tell who will die.
31506: When a dog howls eerily, a death will come very soon. It is an omen.
31507: When the bell tolls deathly, a death is coming. It is an omen.
31508: When a corpse remains unburied over a Sunday, another death will soon follow.
31517: At a haunted spot a witte juffer (white lady) haunts.
31518: A red-and-white dog roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal.
31519: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal.
31520: A nightmare is a little woman who squeezes people's throats shut. You can keep the nightmare away by putting your slippers upside down in front of the bed.
31522: A man with a black-haired wife suddenly misses his purse. A card reader predicts that a 'black figure' has taken his purse. It turns out his own wife did it.
31526: A boy hears his father coming back from a meeting while he has not actually come back yet. It is an omen.
31528: The sorcerer Imke de Jong can fix people to the spot. Once Imke also makes his handkerchief grow bigger and bigger until it covers a wagon.
31530: Sometimes people send off a jack of clubs to fetch a bottle of drink. The one who sent off the card must not take hold of the full bottle.
31535: A labourer on his way to the farmer greets a passer-by, but his greeting goes unanswered. When he addresses the passer-by with the words 'Well devil, can you talk or not?', the passer-by accompanies the labourer to the farmer, floating along. On arriving at the farmer's, the labourer gets a sound beating. It was the devil. From then on the labourer minded his words better.
31541: On a sand track, a sound is suddenly heard as if a wagon is driving over a stone road. It is a portent: only later is a paved road built.
31542: Someone sees a carpenter's shed on fire while it is not actually burning. It is a portent: shortly afterwards it really goes up in flames.
31563: Someone who never lacks money must own a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin). The wisseldaalder, which comes from the devil, can never run out.
31572: At a certain place a terrible noise can always be heard at ten o'clock in the evening. It is a portent: later the tram runs there.
31573: At a certain place a lot of noise is heard and steam is seen. It is a portent: later there is a station of the steam tram at that place.
31574: A man's dream that a certain woman has died comes true.
31575: One evening a man sees a hearse pass carrying the coffin of a young person. It is a premonition: shortly afterwards a fourteen-year-old girl dies. On the day of the funeral the man stands at the same spot where he had the premonition.
31576: A man sees a beautiful new farmhouse with blue roof tiles. It is a vision of the future: later a man who had long been planning to build a new farmhouse builds one that looks just like it.
31577: A man urges a companion to step aside for a passing funeral procession. The companion pays no attention to this 'talk', but a moment later he is driven aside by an invisible funeral procession. Later the new cemetery was built on the spot where it happened.
31578: Two men are spending the night in a small tent when one of them suddenly wants to leave because he feels something heavy pressing on his head and chest. It is an omen: later a dike is built on that spot.
31579: A man keeps hearing hammering at a certain spot, although nothing can be seen. It is a portent: later new houses are built on that spot.
31580: A glass carriage with a horse in front of it is suddenly pushed off the road. It is an omen: later the road in question is rerouted.
31581: A labourer greets a passer-by three times, but each time the greeting goes unanswered. When the labourer indignantly says 'Devil, won't you or can't you talk?!', the figure suddenly disappears. When the labourer arrives at the farmer's a little later, he is suddenly seized and thrown in front of the cows.
31582: Floating figures are often seen at a certain place. It is a voorgezicht (a vision of the future): later cyclists ride at that place.
31583: At a certain place a kind of pigsty with two lights is seen. It is a voorgezicht (a vision of the future): later the tram runs at that place.
31598: A glass carriage suddenly gets stuck on the road right in front of an inn: the horses cannot move another step. The coachman goes into the inn and borrows a large axe from the innkeeper. He then knocks the lower spokes out of one of the wheels. Afterwards the sorcerer who had fixed the coachman and his carriage is sitting in the inn with an injured foot.
31605: An innkeeper conjures little soldiers out of the hearth pit and makes them march on the table. When the drinkers, who are soldiers too, become very frightened, the innkeeper sends the little soldiers back into the hearth one by one. The innkeeper then tells one of his guests that he can pick up a bottle of liquor by the door. The soldier does indeed come back with a bottle of alcohol in his hand.
31606: A curser is seized out of nowhere and flung down.
31607: Two scoffers in a café decide to challenge the devil and God and go to the churchyard together. The most unbelieving of the pair challenges the devil and is promptly pinched very roughly. The devil's claws remain in the sinner's arm forever.
31611: A sorcerer fixes a group of marching soldiers to the spot.
31622: A farmer pays his labourers so little that many of the labourers' children, who hardly wear any clothes, die. When the farmer and his wife then hear children's voices in their barn every night, they consult Piter Poes the exorcist. Piter says the farmer must lay clothes in the barn. The farmer obeys Piter's order and the children's ghosts find rest.
31623: A woman often sees two rows of little lights floating in opposite directions at night. It is a premonition: later a motorway is built at that place.
31624: A group of people saw the tram before it even ran.
31633: At night a farmhand sees a corpse being laid out: a voorloop (an apparition foreshadowing an event). Because he wants to know who the dead person is, he cuts a bit of hair off the corpse. When the farmer's wife asks him the next morning why there is such a strange chunk missing from his hair, the farmhand is terrified and leaves the farm at once. When he later returns to the farm, he dies that same night.
31635: A man born with a caul often foresees deaths.
31637: Whoever has received a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) from the devil never lacks money.
31640: At two haunted places foals with porridge pots around their necks run about. They are phantom animals.
31641: At a certain place a kind of pigsty with two lights can be seen in the evening. Strange sounds are also heard. It is a portent: later the tram runs at that place.
31642: At a certain place a few people see a little lamp floating. It is a premonition: later a house is built at that place.
31658: While pole-vaulting, the devil leaves a footprint in a stone.
31789: In the past, wild lanterns were often seen at a certain place. They are the forerunners of the later car headlights.
31791: A boy who often has premonitions predicts that a sick man will not recover, as his son thinks, but will soon die. The clairvoyant has already seen the hearse. The premonition comes true: a few years later the sick man dies, and the hearse is exactly the one the boy saw before.
31792: A man born with a caul often has to get up at night to foresee deaths in passing funeral processions. He sometimes also has visions of other things.
31793: A clairvoyant who often has to get up at night to see funeral processions takes along his friend, who refuses to believe he has premonitions of deaths. When the procession does approach, the clairvoyant urges his friend to step aside, but the friend sees nothing and stays put. Shortly afterwards he is flung onto the verge, struck by the horse pulling the hearse.
31797: At night a girl hears threshing sounds very clearly and becomes very frightened. It is a premonition of the work that is to be done the next morning.
31800: One night a married couple hears all kinds of sounds, although there is nothing to be seen. It is a premonition: later a new farm is built at that place.
31801: In the evening people often see a little light burning at a certain place. It is a premonition: later a house is built at that place.
31802: A group of people see the light of the tram on the heath and also hear the tram running, although the tram is not actually running yet. It is a portent.
31803: An old woman sees a light coming straight at her and suspects she is having a voorgezicht (a vision of the future) of a road that will be built later. It is indeed a voorgezicht and it comes true: twenty years later a road is built.
31804: A man hears carpentry sounds and suspects it is a premonition of something that will be built later. Later a carpentry business does indeed come to that place.
31805: When a dog howls eerily, a death is coming.
31810: A fortune-teller tells a widow that the first man who treats her well will become her second husband. The prediction comes true: shortly afterwards the widow marries her late husband's brother.
31811: A carpenter with a rather foul mouth is overtaken on his way home. The carpenter greets the passer-by, but the greeting goes unanswered. When the carpenter rudely voices his disapproval, he is seized with a great deal of noise and thrown down. The carpenter had to stay in bed for six weeks.
31883: A sorcerer makes little soldiers appear from the hearth pit.
31892: A man claims to have grazed his hand on a coffin during the night and suspects something is going to happen. It is an omen of his wife's death.
31893: At a certain place psalm singing can clearly be heard. It is a premonition: later the Reformed church is built at that place.
31894: A young man sees a funeral procession approaching. According to him the coffin is not that of an adult. It is a premonition: shortly afterwards a young girl dies.
31895: A woman sees a man drown. The vision later comes true. When the woman hears that someone has drowned, she knows at once who it is.
31896: An old man keeps saying that a certain woman had died that night. The man is right: the woman in question turns out to have died that same night.
31901: The exorcist Piter Poes once banished two lawyers to a piece of land that later came to be called 'Advocatenland' (Lawyers' Land). The lawyers are trapped within a circle that Piter drew around them before pronouncing the banishment over them. The two lawyers still haunt the place.
31903: When a dog howls eerily, a death is coming.
31907: A sorcerer conjures little soldiers out of the hearth pit and makes the likeness of the narrator's father-in-law appear on a coin.
31908: A skipper's wife hurls a black cat against a post. The next day an old woman walks about with her hand wrapped in a cloth.
31909: A girl dreams that a certain man has died. The dream comes true: the man does indeed die.
31913: A certain farmstead where a farmer was once murdered is said to be haunted. The doors spring open at night. A farmhand sees a ghost with eyes as big as teacups in the loft above the cowshed. Although the ghost does him no harm, the farmhand is terrified.
31914: A man sees a certain house on fire three times. They are premonitions: right after the third premonition the house actually burns down.
31915: A certain dog howls eerily whenever a death is coming.
31916: A man sees a magpie in his yard and suspects a relative has died. The suspicion proves well founded: a mourning letter arrives in the post.
31918: People born with a caul foresee deaths in passing funeral processions.
31925: Many young people consult an old woman who owns a black mirror.
31926: A certain witch can change herself into a black cat. Once a hunter shoots out one of the witch-cat's eyes.
31927: Freemasons are men who never lack money because they have sold their souls to the devil.
31928: A man who owns a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) never lacks money.
31930: A will-o'-the-wisp is a premonition of a road that is built later.
31939: A man sees a wilde lantaarn (wild lantern) floating. It is a portent: later the tram runs at that place.
31940: A witch fixes apple thieves to the spot. Only when the thieves drop the fruit can they walk again.
31941: At a haunted place a hunter suddenly sees a glowing thing floating. When the ghostly thing disappears into the ground, the hunter starts digging in the ground. Shortly afterwards the hunter can hardly breathe, because he feels as if a heavy weight is resting on his shoulders.
31943: A hunter shoots a hare, but he fails to hit the animal properly and kill it, though it does leave a trail of blood. The next day a woman, a witch, goes about with a cloth around her head. She had been the witch in the form of a hare.
31944: A young couple about to marry decide to keep their wedding plans secret for a while, but the following week everyone knows. A witch has spread the news. The witch had overheard the news as a black cat.
31945: A witch fixes a pig in place on the road.
31960: A boy sometimes sees a wilde lantaarn (wild lantern) floating at a certain place. It is a portent of, for example, the tram.
31961: A man sees a house on fire: a premonition. The premonition has not yet come true.
31964: A man sees a very strange thing lying on a path and hurries home in fear.
31965: On a Sunday evening a boy sees such a frightening thing on a certain path that for a long while he does not dare to go there.
31966: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal.
31971: When a dog howls eerily, a death is coming in the neighbourhood. It is an omen.
31973: A man born with a caul foresees a death in a passing funeral procession. The premonition comes true.
31974: The sorcerer Imke de Jong can fix people to the spot.
31975: With the help of a jack of clubs you can have a bottle of drink brought. The first glass must be thrown over the left shoulder with the words 'That is for you'.
31981: A curser is suddenly picked up and thrown to the ground: the work of the devil.
31982: At a certain place a man hears carpentry sounds, although there is nothing to be seen. It is a premonition: later a house is built at that place.
31983: A farmer's wife and her son hear carpentry sounds at night. It is a premonition of work that is done the next day.
31984: One night a man sees a long wagon with lights. It is a portent: later the tram runs at that place.
31985: At a certain place psalm singing can be heard. It is a premonition: later a church is built at that place.
31986: A woman foresees that a man will drive his horse and cart into the canal. The man does not believe it, but the vision comes true all the same.
31987: A man sees an inn on fire, but when he goes there, there is no fire. Later the inn burns down.
31988: A man sees a small farmhouse on fire. It is a premonition: only years later does the farmhouse actually burn down.
31989: A man born with a caul is often driven out of bed at night to foresee deaths in passing funeral processions.
31990: People never walk in the middle of the road, because a funeral procession may push them aside.
31991: When a dog howls eerily, a death is coming.
31994: An old gentleman haunts a haunted spot. The gentleman is after a buried treasure.
31995: At a haunted spot a roll of vijfschacht (five-shaft woven cloth) rolls across the road.
31997: A man is picked up for no reason and flung away.
31998: A drunken curser is suddenly seized and thrown a long way.
32007: A knife grinder is said to have sold his soul to the devil. When short of money he slips away for a 'little walk' and comes back a while later with money. He is said to have got the money from the devil.
32009: A cursing scoffer boasts that 'no devil' can jump ditches better than he can. At once the devil himself appears and jumps effortlessly over the water. The devil leaves the print of a horse's hoof - a 'duivelsprent' (devil's print) - in the stone. The sinner later fought with the devil once more. His careless behaviour cost the sinner dearly: one day he was found dead with his head turned backwards on his body.
32011: A man pokes a black cat, a witch's cat, in the eye with a stick. The next day the witch walks about with a patch over her eye.
32012: Will-o'-the-wisps are premonitions of houses or roads that are later built.
32014: A woman born with a caul often has visions of all sorts of events, such as deaths. The same woman can also make a bottle of liquor appear with the jack of spades.
32015: People saw and heard the tram before it even ran: an omen.
32017: Someone once had a vision of a death by drowning. Children are anxiously kept away from the water. The vision has not yet come true.
32030: A boy and a girl hear a woman plaintively cry 'O my boy! O my boy!' It is an omen: shortly afterwards the woman's son drowns and she cries the same words.
32032: As a child the narrator was once visited by a nightmare, a man on a horse. The boy was terrified but unable to call out.
32035: A man born with a caul foresees deaths in passing funerals. People born with a caul can do all kinds of things that 'ordinary' people cannot.
32036: A supposed witch was said to bewitch children and fly around on a broomstick. The witch could also supposedly turn herself into a cat. The narrator did not believe that the woman in question really was a witch. In cases of witchcraft the exorcist is consulted.
32040: The dead who keep haunting cannot find rest because they are struggling with an unfulfilled wish.
32043: A folk healer predicts that a soldier is very ill and that even the best doctor cannot cure him. A few days later the soldier dies.
32047: A man has received a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) from the devil. The wisseldaalder can never run out: if you spend the coin, it is back in your purse a little later.
32049: At a spot where the devil jumped over the canal, there is the print of a horse's hoof in the stone.
32050: A certain sorcerer who could fix a horse and wagon to the spot on the road could also make a bottle of liquor appear with the help of a jack of spades.
32052: A man sees something floating in the air that looks like a big cigar. It is a voorgezicht (a vision of the future) of the later zeppelin.
32058: The devil-banisher Piter Poes fixes a shepherd and his sheep to the spot on the road.
32060: A man hears carpentry sounds, although there is nothing to be seen. It is a premonition: later a farm comes to stand at that place.
32061: A man hears a rattling sound and sees two glowing eyes. It is a portent: later the tram runs at that place.
32062: A father and his two little sons very clearly see a newly built farm standing there, although it does not actually exist yet. It is a premonition: only a year later is the farm really there.
32063: People foresaw the coming of the tram and the building of a road.
32064: An indifferent heathen greets a passer-by, but his greeting goes unanswered. When the heathen boasts that he is afraid of 'no devil', he is suddenly lifted up and thrown over the trees. The heathen repented afterwards.
32065: A certain place is haunted because a farm maid once murdered and buried babies there that the farmer had fathered with her. The maid buried the babies without clothes. As soon as it gets dark, the three naked little children dance around. The little children cannot find rest.
32066: A certain place is haunted because three sisters were murdered there long ago. A man was once chased by the three naked women.
32067: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place.
32069: The exorcist Piter Poes banishes two wicked lawyers who exploit the people to a piece of land that afterwards bears the name 'Advocatenland' (Lawyers' Land). The lawyers wander that piece of land forever.
32112: Carpentry sounds are heard at a certain place. It is a premonition: later a new house is built at that place.
32113: At a certain place wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns) can be seen. It is a portent: later the tram runs at that place.
32114: Wild lanterns can be seen at a certain place. It is a premonition: later a road is built at that place.
32115: When a dog howls eerily, a death is coming.
32116: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal. Strange things also happen at another place: people do not dare to go there at night.
32121: One morning a curser is thrown over the dike by the devil. The man repents after the incident.
32124: A farmhand has special gifts because he has a pact with the devil. For example, he can work a piece of land very quickly.
32127: A freemason woman who deals in rags never gives her whole hand when she shakes hands with someone. The woman never lacks money because she owns a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin). Every so many years a freemason has to die. The woman's turn also came once.
32132: In the evenings a woman often sees a fat black dog walking beside her. It is perhaps a phantom animal.
32142: Wopke the devil-banisher punishes a bunch of rascals who ridicule him: he fixes the boys to the ground.
32143: People born with a caul often have to get out of bed at night to foresee deaths in passing funerals.
32144: A cyclist is suddenly put at the side of the road, bicycle and all. Perhaps a funeral procession had to pass.
32145: A strange man tells two companions that the devil is coming. The man is seized twice by the devil and thrown down.
32147: In exchange for your soul you can get a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) from the devil. You will never lose the wisseldaalder again.
32148: A boy boasts that he can jump over water just as well as the devil. At once the devil appears and jumps over the canal. On both sides of the water the devil leaves the print of a horse's hoof in the stone.
32151: A man sees two lights floating in a certain direction. It is a premonition: later a road is built at that place.
32152: An indifferent curser is on his way home drunk. When he reaches his house, the doors are wide open and there is light everywhere. Shortly afterwards he is suddenly grabbed by a black hand and a light hand. The man remembers nothing more of the incident and is only found unconscious the next morning. It took several days before the man regained consciousness. After the incident the man repents.
32153: A woman, a supposed witch, always brings bewitched fruit to sick children. If a bite is taken from each piece of fruit and spat out again, the danger is gone. The witch was said to change into a black cat in the evening. Once, when the witch-cat is pelted with a stone, the witch has a bruise on her head the next day. A sick girl turns out to have been bewitched by the witch: feather wreaths are found in her pillow. Had three wreaths been completed, the girl would have died. The wreaths are burned. Once the witch throws a handful of mud over the grave of a girl who died of witchcraft.
32156: A woman is afraid to cross a certain little bridge because the devil is said to roam there. When she sees a figure standing on the bridge, she quickly begins to recite the Lord's Prayer. The devil is scared off by the prayer and disappears.
32159: A skater who always beats everyone suddenly feels someone skating right behind him. The one behind soon passes him and the skater gives up. The skater turns out to have been overtaken by the devil.
32161: A conjurer buys a horse at the market and pays the dealer in guilders and rijksdaalders (two-and-a-half-guilder coins). When the dealer has put the money away, the conjurer quickly turns the coins into slices of carrot. When the dealer notices, the conjurer makes sure there is money in the purse again. Once the dealer is reassured, the coins turn back into slices of carrot.
32163: A witch, who also sells bread, flies through the air on a broomstick. A hunter mistakes the witch for a duck and tries to shoot the 'bird' down. The hunter does not hit the witch: only a few loaves of bread come tumbling down.
32173: The devil was once busy sawing a willow in half lengthwise when a group of men saw him. When the men recite a text from the Bible, the devil quickly runs away. One half of the tree later lies as a 'bridge' across a ditch.
32176: You must beware of black cats. A black cat is said to have once made a boy ill.
32177: People who were troubled by witchcraft once burned a heksenkrans (witch's wreath, a clump of feathers found in a pillow). When burning such a wreath, all the openings in the house must be sealed. The people had sealed all the openings except one small window. Through the window a cat escapes, which immediately turns into a person outside.
32181: People are very afraid of a dog starting to howl eerily, because that is supposed to be an omen of something.
32182: At a certain place a man sees a fine farm standing, although it does not actually exist yet. It is a voorgezicht (a vision of the future): only a few years later is the farm built.
32188: Horses become frightened when they pass a certain place. It is a premonition: later a slaughterhouse is built at that place.
32190: Several places are haunted. The cry of a barn owl is often a premonition of something bad.
32191: When magpies chatter loudly near the house, there will be a death in that house within three days. It is an omen.
32194: When a dog howls eerily, someone is dying.
32200: People foresee all kinds of things.
32201: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal.
32213: Two women spending the night in a farm barn are startled by a white ghost woman. It turns out to be the farmer's dead wife. Because the farmer treated her badly while she was alive, the woman keeps wandering restlessly. When the farmer hears about the ghost, he intends to call in the minister to address the dead woman.
32218: A man has visions because he has sold his soul to the devil. At night he often foresees deaths in passing funeral processions. The devil drives him out of bed to see the procession. The seer also predicts exactly how the funeral of the narrator's father will go. The man later hanged himself from the pear tree.
32221: With children born with a caul, you must pull the caul off downwards. If you do it the other way round, the child will be troubled by visions. Nurses are often keen to get cauls because carrying one keeps them safe. (After all, if you carry a caul, you are bulletproof.) Cauls are also often sold on. Many Freemasons are said to have a caul.
32222: If you walk in the middle of the road at night, you can be put aside by an invisible hand.
32223: In the middle of the night a man sees a funeral procession. From the people walking behind the hearse he concludes that his neighbour has died. It is a premonition: a week later the neighbour dies.
32224: A mother urges her children to walk on the verge late in the evening, because a funeral procession could drive them off the road.
32225: Cursers and scoffers are often afraid to go out on the road at night because they might be flung down by the devil.
32227: A widely hated policeman ridicules the sorcerer Imke de Jong at the market. As punishment Imke fixes him to the ground for twenty minutes.
32229: The wizard Imke de Jong is seen in several places at once.
32230: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal.
32231: If a magpie chatters close to the house, a death is coming in one's own circle. It is an omen.
32232: If a dog howls eerily, a death is coming. It is an omen.
32241: A man playing cards holds up a jack of spades. The card disappears and a little later a bottle of jenever (Dutch gin) stands on the table.
32247: A woman born with a caul foresees deaths in passing funeral processions. Some people also have visions of a fire. Others hear the sound of carpentry at a certain spot, although a house is only built there much later.
32252: A fat, spotted dog roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal.
32254: People do not dare to ride on a certain cycle path at night, because funeral processions are said to pass there.
32280: A man sees a funeral procession floating a metre above the ground. It is a premonition.
32281: A man is suddenly followed at night by someone with a tail like a broom. According to the man it is the devil, who wants to tempt him.
32283: One night a man sees two little lights floating. It is a premonition: later a road is built at that place on which cars and bicycles drive.
32284: At a certain place a bread seller hears a rushing and whooshing sound, although there is nothing to be seen. It is a premonition: when a butter factory is later built at that place, the same sounds can be heard.
32285: A clairvoyant boy (born with a caul) predicts that his little brother will die. The prediction comes true. The boy often foresees deaths.
32286: A clairvoyant boy predicts that a man who has been in poor health for a long time will soon die. The prediction comes true: shortly afterwards the man dies.
32287: According to the minister, a new church must be built at a certain place because he once saw or heard something there.
32288: At a haunted spot witte wieven (white women) dance at night.
32298: Floating lanterns are premonitions of houses that are built later.
32299: If a dog howls eerily, a death is coming. The narrator tells that a dog began to howl eerily when a farmhand was about to shoot his girl and himself through the head. The girl survived the attempt on her life.
32310: People hear a sound as if a ship is passing, but the ship is nowhere to be seen. Shortly afterwards the same sound is heard and the ship really passes. It was an omen.
32313: Exorcist Piter Poes, who is also a herb gatherer, is once reading his magic book. As Piter reads, murmuring, all sorts of rooks appear in the room. Suddenly little soldiers also appear and go into the hearth pit. When a man visiting Piter becomes frightened, Piter turns the book around in front of him and starts reading backwards. The little soldiers come back out of the hearth pit and disappear through the door. The rooks and the magpie that had been sitting on Piter's arm all along also fly away. Piter Poes was also said to have been born with a caul.
32322: At night a dog always runs about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal. If you get in the dog's way, it may bite you. The dog always walks on the left side of the road. Many people walked on the right side of the road with a club in their left hand to scare the animal off.
32340: Two women are talking about a certain witch and at once that very witch appears in the doorway. When one of the women says they were just talking about her, the witch angrily goes back outside. Shortly afterwards a big black cat appears in front of the window. There is no way to get the cat away from the window.
32401: A wicked man is lifted from his bed at night by the devil and given a thorough beating.
32413: If a watch ticks strangely, a death is coming. Such a 'doodstikkertje' (death ticker) is a harbinger of death.
32414: When a certain witch went out bewitching at night, her body lay on the bed as if dead, because her spirit had left her. The witch bewitched her own children.
32416: Wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns) are a portent of the tram that runs much later.
32417: A married couple sees fire above a house, although the house is not actually burning. It is a portent: later the house really burns down.
32418: A shoemaker pulls his cart to the side because a funeral procession has to pass. His daughter cannot see the procession. It is a portent of a death.
32420: A cursing mocker boasts that he would like to see God, if he exists. On the way home the sinner is suddenly seized and thrown over the trees.
32421: Someone does all sorts of things with playing cards, for example having a bottle of drink brought. When a playing card is sent outside, a filled bottle comes back and floats around the lamp.
32424: A man hears a bang as if planks are falling down, but nothing happens. It is a premonition: later the same bang is heard when the planks really fall down. The storyteller calls this 'voorklank' (a sound heard before the event).
32425: In a sugar factory the sound of an engine is heard at night, although the factory has no engine. It is a premonition: later the sugar factory disappears and the engine is used in the dairy factory built at that place.
32426: A woman who assists at childbirth knows when she has to go out to tend a new mother and baby, because she hears knocking beforehand.
32433: An indifferent roofer behaves strangely. On his way home he is suddenly startled by a ghost woman.
32437: A married couple hears carpentry sounds, although there is nothing to be seen. It is a premonition: later a new house is built next to the couple's house.
32438: People heard the tram before it even ran. It was a portent.
32444: A man born with a caul often has to get up at night to have visions.
32448: A man is flung over the hedge by the devil near a café.
32449: A man hears carpentry sounds, although there is nothing to be seen. It is a premonition: later the railway is built at that place.
32450: People see the lights of the tram before it even runs.
32451: A man is often driven out of bed at night to have visions.
32453: A man sees another man busily hammering. When he comes closer, there is nothing to be seen. It is a voorgezicht (a vision of the future): only a few days later does he find the same man hammering away at a pigsty.
32458: Two women see a large shed with two lights on it floating. It is a voorgezicht (a vision of the future): a few years later the tram runs at that place.
32464: An innkeeper set a house on fire, hanged his mother and drowned his wife. Afterwards a lady in black always wanders around his house. The innkeeper has taken to drink.
32466: A man foresees that a farmer with a white horse will come to live on a farm. The voorgezicht (vision of the future) comes true.
32467: A lord of the castle haunts a certain place. At another place the ghosts of dead children wander about. The children cannot find rest because they were buried without a shroud. A witch is said to fly around houses with a glowing lath and to conjure wreaths into pillows.
32469: An old woman gives three children a carrot each. The children's mother forbids them to eat the carrots and keeps them in a pot. The next day there are three frogs in the pot. The old woman is a witch.
32471: People see a fire burning above the poplars although there is no actual fire. It is a premonition: later a fire really breaks out at that spot.
32472: People see a certain farmhouse on fire although there is no actual fire. It is a premonition: later the farmhouse really burns down.
32480: A man often hears carpentry sounds at night, although there is nothing to be seen. It is a premonition: only later is real carpentry done there.
32481: At a certain place the ghost of a dead woman wanders about. Several people have seen the ghost woman.
32483: A man suddenly sees a white thing fly past but cannot catch hold of it.
32484: A man born with a caul often has to get up at night to have visions.
32485: A carpenter is knocked over three times by a ghost woman who cackles like a magpie. The woman always wanders about a certain place and bothers other people there too.
32487: On a plank across the ditch witte juffers (white ladies) can often be seen.
32491: A labourer suddenly sees a farmhouse standing in a certain place, although it is not really there. It is a premonition: later a farmhouse is built on that spot.
32492: A man sees glowing lights and hears a rattling noise. It is a portent: later the tram runs at that spot.
32493: A man is suddenly picked up and set over the hedge, although no one is to be seen.
32494: A man is suddenly seized and flung into the ditch. The man declares that the devil walked along with him.
32495: A man has to step aside for a funeral procession that is not really there. It is a premonition: later someone dies and the funeral passes by at that very spot.
32496: A man with duckweed in his hair claims that the devil, floating behind him without feet, grabbed him by the hair and threw him into the ditch.
32600: A big black dog, a phantom animal, is said to roam about a haunted place at night.
32602: A freemason has sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin). The wisseldaalder is kept in a little basket on an unfinished uilenbord (owl board, a gable board with an opening under the roof). The man never lacks money.
32603: If you accept an apple or a pear from a witch, the fruits can turn into toads or frogs. Asafoetida is used to ward off witchcraft. All witches can fly.
32605: A cursing veterinarian who has a pact with the devil, and who is also an exorcist of the devil, gets into a fight with the devil. After the fight his clothes hang in the tops of the trees.
32616: A man born with a caul tells his girlfriend that he has to step aside for a passing funeral procession. The girl cannot see the procession and thinks the young man is out of his mind. It is a vision of a funeral. Many people are keen to get cauls because they protect against shipwreck, for example. The caul must be removed the right way at birth.
32618: A peat skipper who is repeatedly startled by a naked little child behind his boat consults the minister. The minister asks the child, who died long ago, why it cannot find rest. It turns out the child drowned at that spot and was then buried without a shroud. The child asks the minister to request a burial shirt from the middle one of three women. The wish is granted and the minister hands the child the shroud with a wooden spoon. Now that its wish has been fulfilled, the child finds rest.
32621: If you stamp a toad to death, thunder and rain will come.
32633: In 1940 a man hears a column of soldiers passing the house at night, although the Germans have not yet invaded the country. It is a portent: a week later the German troops really come and the same sound can be heard.
32634: Every night a woman hears the sound of hammering and suspects that new houses are going to be built. Her suspicion comes true: the hammering was a portent.
32635: At night a fat black dog roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal.
32639: A girl's parents forbid her to see a certain boy. When the girl becomes pregnant, she takes her own life. When the moon is bright, the dead girl sometimes still wanders about with the child in her arms. A woman has seen her a few times.
32640: In a household of seven girls, one is a nightmare. The nightmare torments you when you lie on your back. To keep nightmares away you must put one shoe with the toe and the other with the heel against the bed. Laying a white floorcloth in front of the bed also helps. Horses are tormented by nightmares too.
32641: In a dream, a man foresees that his sheep will die while carrying three lambs. The dream comes true.
32642: A man born with a caul keeps having to get up at night to have visions of funerals.
32643: A woman often has to get up at night to foresee deaths in passing funeral processions. If the caul of someone born with a caul is burned straight away, that person is not troubled by visions of the future.
32645: A cursing scoffer boasts that he is not afraid of the devil. The devil promptly grabs him and throws him over the trees.
32647: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal.
32649: You should never walk in the middle of the road at night, because you can be driven to the side by a funeral procession.
32651: A woman dreams that one of her sons-in-law dies. The dream comes true.
32653: A mother warns her children never to accept anything from a witch, an apple for example. If you eat the apple, you can get a toad, frog or mouse in your body.
32654: Witches make journeys on broomsticks, even abroad.
32655: A scoffer boasts that he is not afraid of the devil. He is promptly seized and thrown away. The sinner is so frightened that he no longer dares to say anything.
32656: A cursing scoffer is roughly seized and thrown away.
32657: With the help of a jack of spades you can have a bottle of drink brought.
32659: Freemasons have a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin). They usually hide the coin in the barn.
32662: Little lights can be seen in a certain place in the evening. It is a portent: later a road is built on that spot.
32663: People hear the train from Leeuwarden to Groningen running before it even exists. It is a portent.
32664: A man urges a man on a wagon to make way for a funeral procession. But the man on the wagon cannot see the procession. It is a vision foreshadowing a death.
32665: In the old days people warned never to walk in the middle of the road. If you did, you could be struck by a passing funeral procession.
32666: If a magpie sits on a fence post, a death is coming. It is an omen.
32669: One should not go to a certain place, because a girl in a little red apron is said to wander there. The girl has haunted the spot ever since she drowned.
32670: A woman does not dare walk past the churchyard after midnight, because the ghosts of the dead are said to wander about then.
32671: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal. Children who are still outside in the evening are warned that the foal might grab them.
32672: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place. It is a phantom animal.
32678: A fortune-teller makes predictions about the future. The predictions all come true.
32680: A young lad jumps over the canal and boasts that 'the devil can't match him'. At once the devil himself appears and jumps over the water. He leaves the print of a horse's hoof in the stone.
32681: An owner of a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) can draw everything to himself. Others become his victims because the money he spends always comes back to him.
32695: A group of apple thieves is fixed to the spot by a witch while a fire comes towards them. Only when the thieves drop their loot can they take a step again.
32696: One night a ship suddenly finds cats all over it. There is no way to get rid of the cats. They are witches.
32703: In a certain house the cellar door keeps springing open, even when it is shut with a sturdy ring. One day a stove comes out of the cellar door and starts beating the occupants.
32708: At night a farmer suddenly hears noises and shortly afterwards sees two coffins being slid over the stones. It is a vision: soon afterwards both his daughters die.
32710: A person born with a caul often foresees deaths in passing funeral processions.
32711: A woman suddenly sees the ghost of a dead man in the room. When she shakes her head, he disappears again. He has never come back.
32713: Every evening a widower is startled by an apparition climbing down the ladder. The man cannot bear it and fetches the minister. The minister says to the ghost: 'If you are of God, come to me; if you are of the devil, depart.' The ghost disappears and never comes back.
32714: On her deathbed a woman makes her husband promise that no one else will wear her clothes after her death. The man agrees. When he remarries, he breaks his promise by letting his second wife wear his first wife's clothes. At once the ghost of the dead woman appears at the house every evening. The man has the minister address the dead woman. When she makes it known that it troubles her that the other woman wears her clothes, the minister decides that the woman will no longer wear them. The woman's wish is fulfilled after all and she finds rest.
32715: A godless sinner boasts, 'If there is a devil, let him come and meet me.' On his way home, the man three times comes across a man lying across the path. The third time, the man jumps up and crushes the sinner. The sinner dies of his injuries a few months later.
32716: A godless scoffer is suddenly seized by a fellow and flung down. A companion of the sinner, however, saw nothing of the incident.
32720: Two brothers are suddenly startled by a floating woman. The woman, who has no feet, silently keeps the two men company. The brothers recognise her: she is someone's dead daughter.
32721: A godless scoffer is suddenly startled by a gate that springs open by itself: the work of the devil.
32726: A woman sees a funeral pass by very clearly. She knows the people walking in the procession. It is a vision of the future: shortly afterwards someone dies.
32740: A farmer advises a farmhand not to sleep in a certain hay bay, because anyone who spends the night there is said to die. The farmhand does not believe it and sleeps in that bay anyway. The next morning he is not dead, but he has been flung by his feet into another bay. The farmhand thinks the farmer has played a trick on him. Only when the farmer shows him a calf dying in the bay is the farmhand convinced.
32741: With the help of a jack of spades you can make a bottle of drink come.
32742: A churn that keeps turning all night is a portent of work that will be done the next day.
32743: A man hears hammering in the middle of the night, although there is nothing to be seen. It is a portent: later a house is built on that spot.
32744: A clairvoyant woman keeps having visions of all sorts of things at night.
32745: In the past people were often afraid of black cats because they were thought to be witches. A certain witch was once given a good beating while she was a cat. The next day the witch's face was all black and blue.
32748: Witches can fly, usually on a broomstick.
32750: The narrator's mother sometimes did sewing for a supposed witch. The children were never allowed to accept an apple from the witch. According to the mother, they would then get a toad in their body.
32752: In the past one could consult black mirrors at markets that foretold the future. In the mirror you could see the likeness of your future wife. If you were to stay unmarried, a coffin appeared in the mirror.
32757: Of a small group of cursing sinners, one is seized and beaten by the devil.
32758: At a certain place an old horse always stands rattling a gate. It is a phantom animal.
32759: At a certain place a chain is fastened to a post. The chain always rattles, even when there is no wind.
32760: A hole the devil once made in the ground always remains there.
32772: In the evening a child hears the sound of skipping rope when she is going to do it the next day. It is a portent.
32773: If you walk in the middle of the road in the evening, you can be driven aside by a passing funeral procession.
32774: A person born with a caul keeps foreseeing deaths in passing funeral processions.
32776: In the old days, when will-o'-the-wisps were seen, a new road would soon be built on that spot. It was a portent.
32778: Of seven girls born in succession, one is a nightmare. Of seven boys, one is a werewolf. At night nightmares sit on people's chests and squeeze their throats shut. A piece of rye bread helps to keep the nightmare away.
32782: Owners of a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) never lack money. To get a wisseldaalder you have to sell your soul to the devil.
32786: A woman born with a caul foresees that her husband will fall out of the window. The vision comes true: three days later the man falls.
32787: An old woman urges someone else to make way for a funeral procession. It is a vision of the future: a few days later a real funeral passes.
32792: Certain little lights turn out to be a portent of the tram that will later run at that spot.
32806: A man hears a rumbling in the sky just before the train comes.
32807: Someone predicts that a relative will die six weeks later. The prediction is exactly right.
32808: A phantom foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about a haunted place.
32811: Men from Surhuisterveen were said to get a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) from the devil. A wisseldaalder can never run out and always returns.
32819: A woman predicts that things will go badly for the narrator's brother because she has seen a funeral procession pass his house. The prediction comes true: the brother dies.
32820: A woman born with a caul often has to get up at night to foresee deaths in passing funeral processions.
32821: A man hears the sounds of cars and aeroplanes before those means of transport even exist. The same man also sees the lights of the tram before it runs.
32822: One night a mother foresees that her son will have an accident. The vision comes true.
32823: A mother predicts that her family will not live much longer in a certain place because she has heard sounds as if the house were being demolished. The sounds were indeed an omen: a few months later the house is really demolished.
32824: When a neighbour of a man born with a caul dies, it is hard to find someone to lead the funeral. The man born with a caul advises choosing a certain man to lead it. He had earlier had a vision that this man would lead that funeral.
32825: An old woman is taken into a nursing home. One time, in the room she is given, she sees the ghost of a dead person wandering about. The little dead woman lived in that room of the nursing home during her life. When the old woman looks away from the ghost for a moment, it has vanished.
32826: A man suddenly sees lots of soldiers marching and suspects war is coming. The vision comes true: shortly afterwards the Second World War breaks out and German soldiers appear.
32827: A mother foresees that she will lose her son. The mother resigns herself to it when a voice speaks to her. The vision comes true.
32829: A man sleeping in the loft hears someone climbing the ladder. Suddenly the man feels someone sitting on top of him. When he tries to grab them, they simply slip out of his hands. It was a nightmare.
32831: When magpies chatter close to the house, one of the residents will have an accident or something of the kind. It is an omen.
32834: An unbelieving scoffer exclaims that the devil, if he existed, should come and get him. When the man gets into bed a little later, he sees a little man sitting on the bed shelf. When the man asks his wife whether she has seen the little man too, she answers that there is no little man anywhere to be seen. In the time that follows, the little man appears to the scoffer every other night. The little man keeps appearing for about half a year, in other houses too. When the scoffer once spends the night in a hut, he is rid of the little man. The devil did this to the man because he mocked God and the devil.
32912: Some time beforehand, a boy dreams that a drowned girl is lying in a woman's arms.
32914: One evening a farming family heard a clattering of buckets of water and brooms. But when the eldest son went outside to look, there was nothing to be seen. A few days later someone came who really set about cleaning, and they heard exactly the same sounds again.
32915: A boy loved his dog Nero. But one evening he was terrified of the animal. It walked with its tail between its legs, and the boy would not let it into the house. The next day they found the animal lying dead on the tram track. The dog must have had a premonition, but why was the boy so afraid?
32916: A man once saw a funeral. He named all the people he saw walking behind the coffin, but he could not say who lay in the coffin. Two weeks later he himself was dead; he had seen his own funeral.
32917: A farmhand once got carrots from a woman known as a witch. The next day there were no carrots left in the basket, but toads.
32918: It once happened that butter could not be made. Grote Wopke, the devil banisher, said they had to boil a cheese in water. When the water began to boil, a maid began to rage and carry on terribly. That is how they knew she was the culprit, and she was dismissed on the spot.
32920: A man had seen the tram running across the heath before the tram was really there.
32925: At a certain spot people saw witte wijven (white women).
32928: A man was always cursing and scoffing. Once he went to see why there was so much noise on the roof. When he got up there, he was flung off the ladder. The devil had done that.
32950: People came to dislike more and more a red tomcat that turned up now and then. Once they gave him a good thrashing. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood walked about with a bandage around her head. She had been the cat.
32959: People sometimes heard hammering along a sandy road, but there was nothing to be seen. The hammer blows did not follow each other quickly. Some time later a new house was built, and they heard the slow blows again. The carpenter was rather lazy and so did not hammer very fast.
32960: Once something flew right past a man. It was as white as a corpse and had glowing eyes.
32961: Two boys were once out cycling. One of them saw a huge fellow, but the other saw nothing.
32966: Witches sometimes hold meetings in the shape of cats. They sing, and discuss who the next victim will be. Every seven years a witch must bewitch someone to death. Witches can fly on broomsticks.
32969: If a child eats an apple from a witch, he gets a toad or a slug in his body.
32971: A man haunted by the thick tree in Harkema.
32978: Some people could make a bottle of drink come with the help of a jack of spades. Such a person would give the order: "Jack of spades, bring us drink." A little later the bottle would come floating in. If nobody dared to take the bottle, that was not good.
32979: Some people could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit with a magic book. They would then start marching. A magic book could only be made to disappear by saying the same words as when one received the book. But usually people no longer knew them. Such a book could not be burned, nor destroyed with water.
32981: A man once saw a funeral procession with a white horse pass by. That was not customary. When his neighbour died not long afterwards, no black horse could be found anywhere, and a white horse had to be used.
32983: A woman believed in nothing and mocked the eternal. One evening she went out dancing in her new shoes. She danced so hard that nothing was left of the shoes. On the way back she was seized by the devil. The next day she sat in church, and a week later she made her profession of faith.
32984: One evening a scoffer had once again drunk a lot and said strange things. On the way home one of his mates was suddenly lifted up and flung over the dike. That was the work of the devil. From then on the young man never again dared to go out alone in the evening.
32986: People have sometimes heard cries for help coming from the Leeuwenpoel. It is believed that someone will drown in it one day.
32987: A rather wild young man was once grabbed by the devil and flung over the dike. From then on the man was a believer and pious.
32988: In his young years a man was a great scoffer. He cursed and drank a great deal. He sometimes had children curse for a few cents. Once he was flung over the dike by the devil. He was left with a stiff leg. He then had to sit with that leg in a kind of wooden tub and keep it wet. When he was better, he wanted to go straight back to the pub. But his mother sat down to pray. Then he came into contact with very pious people. They talked with him for a very long time, and after that he repented. He became a very pious man.
32992: A mother dreamt that her son would go to live in a new house. When not long afterwards he did indeed move, she recognised the house from her dream.
32993: A boy was often troubled by a nightmare. If he did not turn over in time, she had him. It was always a girl who fancied him. When he got a sweetheart, the nightmares stopped.
33003: A big black dog, as big as a calf, haunted a certain spot.
33005: Sometimes on a dark summer evening you would get little moths on your bicycle lamp. That was a bad sign.
33013: One evening a man had fought with the devil, who had taken the form of a tree trunk.
33014: One night a man saw a funeral procession. At the new churchyard the people stopped.
33015: In the moonlight a man saw a goat jump over four steps. He thought it was his own goat, but when he got home, his own goat was there. So it must have been a strange goat (the devil).
33016:
If seven magpies sit at the front of a house, a death will come. If they sit behind the house, there will be a celebration.
A man heard a magpie chattering, and when he came home his little goat was dead.
33018: Sometimes people heard knocking, but when they opened the door, there was no one there. Later someone would come.
33019: A man once saw a funeral procession approaching in the dark. When he had passed it, he saw nothing more.
33020: Before a train ran at a certain spot, people had already heard a train running there.
33021: In Twijzelerheide people heard the sound of a German airship even before the First World War.
33022: A witch often changes herself into a cat. If you hit such a cat, the witch is injured the next day.
33032: In the evening a man always heard the drone of some kind of engine, but he could not find where it came from. Not long afterwards his sons, who both had a lorry, came to visit. That was the sound he had heard before.
33034: A woman once saw a funeral pass by. A week later the funeral really took place.
33037: When Piter Poes, the duivelbanner (exorcist), came along, the children quickly made a cross with their clogs, because he was supposed to trip over it. But they never saw that happen.
33041: A man drank rather often and a lot. Until one day he was picked up by the devil and flung over the dike. After that he never drank again.
33049: One night the horses suddenly reared and moved aside. Then the two men saw a white chaise drawn by a white horse pass by. A man was sitting in the chaise.
33051: A child was bewitched by a cat that followed the child around all the time. So they gave the animal a kick. The next day the neighbour woman was lame. In the child's pillow they found a wreath.
33053: If the rooks made a racket while people were working with the potatoes, it meant there would be a funeral. Likewise if the magpies chattered loudly.
33054: A man was born with a caul. He always knew in advance when there would be another funeral. He also said people should never walk in the middle of the road at midnight, because they might run into a funeral procession.
33055: A man wanted to meet the devil. Not long after, he did indeed encounter him. Things went badly for him then.
33058: One night a married couple saw that the pane had been taken out of the window in the front wall of the house. Yet it was not really so. When there was a death later, they could not get the coffin out of the house. Then the window had to be removed, exactly as they had seen before.
33059: A man always worked on a praam (flat-bottomed barge). Once he had a strong feeling that he should not go to the barge. He also kept forgetting something, so that he had already gone back home three times. That same week he drowned while swimming.
33060: A man told his sons he had seen a funeral procession and that he feared their mother would die soon. Not long after, he himself died; it was his own funeral procession he had seen.
33061: A man had once cut off another man's nose. He cursed a lot and was always drunk. Once he was flung over the trees by the devil.
33062: A cat often lay down next to a baby in the pram. Once the father thought he recognised a neighbour in it, and he struck the animal. The next day that neighbour had a head injury.
33063: At a certain spot a woman with long black hair haunted.
33065: People often heard hammering nearby at night. Not long afterwards new houses were built.
33073: One night a man saw a funeral procession approaching, but he kept walking in the middle of the road. Then he was driven aside and ended up on the verge.
33074: A man once boasted that he was not afraid of the devil. When he came out of the pub, the devil grabbed him and flung him some distance.
33075:
One night two young men saw a female figure floating across the road. 
No one dared to drink coffee at a certain woman's house because she had such steel-blue eyes.
33082: Two brothers once saw an old man pricking a doll. That was how he caused other people pain. They also sometimes saw lots of pigs and chickens in his house. When they went inside to look, they saw nothing anymore. The man had made them disappear into the hearth pit.
33092: A man could conjure little soldiers out of the hearth pit. He would then make them march through the room. He could also make the horses in the stable dance. His coffin had a little window in it. Nobody had that back then. He is buried facing his farm, so that at the resurrection he can see his land again.
33112: A farmhand often had prophetic dreams. Once he told the farmer he would stop working because he was going to get an ailment. The following year the farmhand got asthma, and then he did indeed stop working. He had been born with a caul.
33116: Three men once celebrated the Lord's Supper mockingly. They were punished for it. One became paralysed, and the others drank their lives away.
33121: The cats always met at a certain spot. Tsjitske was always there too. Sometimes there were as many as a hundred. People tried to shoot at them with guns, but they could never hit one.
33122: Once butter could not be made. The maid was blamed, and they held her head in the churn. She was rescued just in time by her master.
33123: The churchyard of Marum was haunted.
33124: A man always cursed terribly. Once, when he was working alone in the factory, he fought with the devil. People later found him dead.
33126: In the evenings, shadows were always seen moving back and forth behind the curtains at a woman's house. She was then busy with her dolls. She was a witch.
33127: A witch often changes herself into a cat. If you hit a strange cat, it sometimes happens that the witch has a sore arm or leg the next day.
33130: People used to say that if you ate something from a witch, you would get a toad in your body. But when the narrator once kept two apples he had been given by a witch in a storage jar, they did not turn into toads.
33132: A woman flew through the air on a broomstick.
33134: White beings always floated over a churchyard. They came out of the graves.
33135: A man often had to get up at night to see funeral processions. Because of this he always knew when another funeral was coming.
33140: Someone once saw a lot of wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps). Later a railway line came at that spot.
