33141: A woman had told her husband where her jewellery should go after her death. But when she died, the man kept it himself. Then she came to the cabinet where the jewellery was kept.
33142: In Groningen there were haunted barns. It happened that people lay down to sleep on the hay and woke up the next day on the threshing floor.
33150: Duivelsdrek (asafoetida, literally devil's dung) is the excrement of the devil. In the old days people put it under the threshold so that no witch could cross it. There were also children who walked around with a little bag of duivelsdrek around their neck. People also made a cross on the road when they saw a witch.
33155: People once heard a coffin being pushed through the door. Three days later someone in that house died.
33156: A woman once saw a house on fire. Three days later the house really burned down.
33158: A man always saw funeral processions. He would always say whom he had not seen among them. That person was always dead a few days later.
33168: Early in the morning on their bikes, two brothers sometimes saw someone riding ahead of them, who went through the hedge at the baker's. But they could never catch up with him, and he always suddenly vanished. They thought it was a ghost.
33169: A grandfather told his grandson, who lived with him, that he had heard hammering that night. Not long afterwards the man died. The grandson refurbished the room the old man had lived in. The man had heard that in advance.
33170: A woman once saw her house on fire and ran to it to get her little one out of bed. But when she arrived, nothing turned out to be wrong. Later the house really burned down, but by then she no longer lived there.
33171: A woman once saw a funeral procession at a house. Not long after, a little boy died in that house.
33172:
If a dog howls eerily, there will soon be a death.
Once when a dog howled terribly, its mistress died the next day.
33173: A woman once heard wood being unloaded from a wagon. Later a new house was built and she heard the same sound.
33174: Early one morning a man saw a man on the verge. The stranger made no reply to his greeting. He hurried off, and the man could not catch up with him at all. It seemed as if the stranger was floating; the man could not find any footprints of him either.
33177: A few men once celebrated Holy Communion mockingly. On the way back one of them was seized by the devil. The next day they found him dead in a ditch, with his head above the water.
33178: A man was once coming back from work when he was lifted up and flung down by the devil. The next day others had to fetch his toolbox.
33179: A man could conjure little soldiers out of the hearth pit. He would then make them march through the room. He could also make white mice run around the mantelpiece.
33183: A prisoner pretended to have repented so that he would be released sooner. But when he was free, he was thrown into the ditch by a little dog. That was the devil.
33187: A grandmother heard her newborn grandchild screaming. When she inquired, it turned out the child had indeed been carrying on around that time.
33194: Anyone who eats an apple from a witch gets a toad in his body.
33196: A woman always heard in advance when the lime trees were going to be sawn down. One night she had heard it again. Her husband wanted to prove her wrong and ordered that the tree should not be sawn but chopped down. But when the labourer could not reach a branch, he took the saw, and the woman was proved right after all.
33198: A man sold himself to the devil to obtain a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin). Whenever he needed money, he only had to hold his cap under the table, and it would be full. But he did not die a pleasant death.
33199: A young man was once lying in bed and saw that the road to his girlfriend was blocked. The next day the road was indeed completely covered with trees because of a storm.
33200: A few men were once stealing potatoes from a field when suddenly a big black dog was standing beside them. The animal had large glowing eyes. Frightened, they quickly left. It was the devil.
33201: One night people heard hammering outside, but there was nothing to be seen. Later new houses were built.
33202: In the old days people sometimes saw will-o'-the-wisps flying along the road. They were the forerunners of bicycle lamps and car lights.
33203: A woman was born with a caul. At night she often had to get up to see funeral processions.
33205:
A man was often troubled by a nachtmerrie (night-mare). It would come and sit on his chest and squeeze his throat shut. He scattered flour on his blankets, but that did not help at all.
Night-mares can change into a black cat, just like witches. They also sometimes sit on horses, which would then stand in the stable wet with sweat the next day.
33209: A man had been swearing and drinking heavily in the pub. On the way back the devil threw him into the ditch.
33212: Some people made a bottle of drink come with the help of a jack of spades.
33213: It sometimes happened that the churn was bewitched. Then no butter could be made.
33214: People would sometimes hit a strange cat, and then the next day a witch would walk about with her arm in a sling.
33219: A man always saw funeral processions in advance, and he would warn people about them. He also saw naked people. Those were the people who had been buried without grave clothes.
33220: An old woman once bewitched a salamander into a boy's body. From then on the boy could run terribly fast.
33221: If magpies come close to the back door, someone in that house will die within three days.
33225: If you saw a will-o'-the-wisp, it meant an accident was going to happen. The eerie howling of dogs usually meant a death.
33243: In the evenings a witch always stuck needles into dolls. Some people then felt pain.
33250: One night a woman heard hammering, though there was nothing to be seen. Later a new inn was built.
33251: A man used to see wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) on the heath. Later the tramline came there. They were omens of the lit carriages.
33252: In the past people saw wild lanterns on the heath. Later a canal came there. The little lights were the future masts of the ships.
33253: All the will-o'-the-wisps seen on the heath were omens of things that came later.
33261: One night a man was followed by a big black dog.
33263: A man was a great scoffer. Once he was thrown to the ground by the devil. Another time he was thrown up against the rafters.
33266: At night one should not walk in the wheel ruts of the road, or else one might run into a funeral procession.
33268: In a haunted barn the horses were harnessed to the wagons at night and the milk churns put on the wagon. The labourers were very frightened.
33273: A man sometimes saw naked little children haunting a certain spot. Those children were said to have been murdered and to have found no rest since.
33275: A woman who was born with a caul often had to get up at night to see funeral processions. One night she saw her own daughter's funeral. Not long after, the daughter died.
33277: A boy once got two apples from a woman. But his sister would not let him eat them, because the woman was known as a witch. She was afraid her little brother would otherwise get two toads in his body.
33278: One night a man closed the doors of the barn he was sleeping in three times, but each time they opened again. When the doors opened for the fourth time, he ran away fast.
33279: In Hardegarijp there were gates that could never be kept closed.
33280: The mowers slept in tents. One time a man heard the Lange Sleatterman (a tall ghostly figure) scraping against the tent. Then he moved the little tent a short distance and was never bothered again.
33281: In the old days some people could make a bottle of drink come with a jack of spades. The first drop was not to be drunk.
33283: Two men once saw a shed on fire, but when they came closer, nothing turned out to be wrong. Later the shed did burn down after all.
33284: A man was in France, and one night he saw someone smash a window at his parents' house. When he came home a week later, a window had indeed been smashed on that very night.
33285: One night a man saw three men in black tailcoats and top hats. They made no reply to his greeting. A few days later a neighbour woman died and the three men in black were really there.
33286: One night a young man was pushed to the side by a funeral procession.
33287: One evening people heard hammering. Not long afterwards a new house was built.
33288: A man once saw a farmhouse on fire, but when he came closer, nothing turned out to be wrong. Later the farm did burn down after all.
33289: Older people in Harkema still do not walk in the middle of the road, because they fear they might otherwise run into a funeral procession.
33290: A witch can turn herself into a cat. If you get something to eat from her, it can turn into a toad. Someone once took a bite of such an apple but quickly spat it out. He kept the rest of the apple. The apple turned into a toad, but because he had already taken a bite, the toad had a defect.
33291: If a group of magpies sits near a house, a death is coming.
33295: A woman always bewitched children by giving them pancakes. When the children ate them, they afterwards spat out snakeskins.
33296: Mike Ruerd made little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
33299: A man once saw lots of people and bicycles at his house, but in reality there was nothing. A week later one of his children had died and the people and bicycles were really there.
33300: A man was once driven to the side of the road by a funeral procession.
33301: A man was once thrown over the dike by the devil.
33302: At a certain spot a plaagbeest (tormenting ghost beast) haunted the place.
33309: Three little children once died when their house burned down. Because they were not dressed in shrouds, they could find no rest. In the neighbourhood they could be seen walking about naked at night.
33311: A phantom dog haunted a certain spot and frightened people.
33312: At a certain spot a white figure haunted the place.
33315: After his death a man is still often seen, holding two girls by the hand.
33316: One evening a rather cruel man could not walk any further. When he began to swear angrily, he was thrown some distance.
33322: People often heard hammering while there was nothing to be seen. Not long afterwards new houses were built.
33323: People once clearly heard a railway running through the land. Later a road came, but the railway line has yet to come.
33325: At a house the wagon always went back and forth on the threshing floor at night.
33329: A man once asked another whether he wanted to come sailing. The stranger made no reply, but went zigzagging across the water ahead of the boat.
33330: A man always saw funerals in advance.
33331: One night a man saw a naked little child walking ahead of him. When he tried to grab the child, it vanished into a pool.
33333: In the old days people saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) above the fields at a certain place. Later a road came there. The earlier lights were the portents of the later cars.
33334: In the old days plaagbeesten (tormenting ghost beasts) haunted a certain spot.
33338: A man was born with a caul. He always saw all kinds of things in advance.
33340: If you promise someone something before he dies, you must keep that promise, otherwise the dead person gets no rest.
33341: Early one morning something came walking beside a man. The man could not tell whether it was an animal or a person. It did not answer his greeting.
33343: If a dog howls eerily, a death will soon come.
33344: A man sometimes heard hammering at night while there was nothing to be seen. Later new houses were built there.
33345: Two men had been swearing a good deal in the pub. On the way back the devil lifted them up, dog cart and all, and threw them into the canal.
33346: One evening a woman heard a bump against the frame of the back door, but there was nothing to be seen. A week later her son-in-law died, and a coffin had to go through the back door. Then she heard the same bump again.
33348: A woman once dreamt that her husband had died, that there was snow on the ground, and that her shoes still had to go to the shoemaker. When her husband died the following winter, there was indeed snow, and her shoes had to go to the shoemaker.
33349: People sometimes heard moaning at a certain spot. Later two people were run over by the tram.
33350: The wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) that people used to see on the heath were the omens of the later tram.
33351: In the old days a foal with a porridge pan around its neck haunted the heath.
33352: One night two women saw a very small little man, about half a metre tall.
33353: De Lange Sleatterman was a giant who roamed around the Kruiswateren.
33355: A young man once saw two white women floating, but his father saw nothing.
33357: A man once saw someone fill his wagon with clay mud in one go. That man was being helped by the devil.
33358: A man always drank a great deal, yet he still managed to keep his inn going. He was a Freemason and had a contract with the devil. In his attic he had a barrel that the devil always filled with money.
33364: Some people could make a bottle of drink come with a jack of spades.
33365: A woman sometimes heard sawing at night. Years later a new house was built.
33366: One morning a man was accompanied by a silent stranger. When the man said that he was the devil, the stranger grabbed hold of him and only let him go again some distance further on.
33371: Some animals could not be hit with a bullet. A man once found it impossible to catch a polecat.
33372: A great scoffer once threw some chewing tobacco on the ground and said it was for the devil. Immediately he was lifted up and thrown down. That was the devil's work. Later the man became Reformed.
33405: At a certain spot a man haunted with a porridge pan around his neck.
33409: A man often bewitched cattle. After his visit they soon died. He also once bewitched a baby in its cradle.
33410: A man was once thrown to the ground. This was not done by a human, for otherwise he would have stabbed him.
33412: People sometimes heard hammering at night in a certain spot. Later new houses were built.
33413: A man once saw a funeral procession coming from a house. A few days later a girl in the house died unexpectedly.
33414: A great scoffer was once coming out of the pub when the devil knocked him unconscious.
33416: Three little children who had burned to death were once laid in their coffins without grave clothes. Because of this they could find no rest, and people still sometimes saw them haunting.
33417: A man had sometimes heard cries for help from a pool, and was convinced that someone would one day drown in it. That is why his children were never allowed to skate there. People also thought there was a monster in the pool.
33418: Just after midnight a drunk man said: "Between twelve and one, everything is about." Immediately he flew through the trees. He was very frightened. It was the devil's work.
33421: At a certain spot women sentenced to death were drowned. Later the place was haunted.
33425: People warned a man not to go and live in a certain house, because a woman in a colourful apron was said to haunt it.
33426: A skinned horse haunted a certain place.
33429: A married couple was once followed by a cat. In the house the woman shut the animal in. But the next morning the cat had vanished.
33435: Whenever a girl sat outside on the privy, a small baby always came and sat on her lap. A baby was said to have been murdered there once. On her father's advice she laid baby clothes there. The clothes disappeared, and she never saw the baby again.
33436: A great scoffer once came out of the inn drunk. The next day he was found hanged in a tree. The devil had done that.
33438: A man sometimes heard an alarm clock ticking at night, but there was no alarm clock at all. Later a bedroom was built, and an alarm clock was put in it.
33439: A man once saw a funeral procession. A few days later an acquaintance died and the procession was really there.
33440: A certain place was haunted by an enter (a yearling animal) with a porridge pan around its neck.
33441: A man known as a witch often arrived at a place before others, even though he had left later. People believed he flew through the air on a broomstick. When people sometimes heard a thump on the roof in the evening, he would be at the door shortly afterwards.
33448: A man mistreated his wife and was a bad person. Then the devil once threw him over the electricity wires as punishment.
33449: You must never eat anything at a witch's house, or else you will be bewitched.
33450:
If you killed a snail, it would start to thunder.
If a dog howled eerily, someone would die.
If a magpie sat on a post, visitors would come, from the direction of its tail.
If a cat passed its paw over its ear while washing, talkative visitors would come.
33458: A certain place used to be haunted by a big black dog.
33514: One evening a woman saw a white figure outside.
33517: People once heard hammering on the heath, but there was nothing to be seen. Later new houses were built.
33518: A man once saw a house on fire. Later the house really burned down.
33519: One evening two girls saw wild lanterns passing by.
33520: In the old days people saw will-o'-the-wisps in a certain place. Later houses and a road were built there. The little lights were omens.
33521: Two men once heard cries for help from the water. A few days later someone drowned.
33522: One evening a married couple saw a funeral procession.
33523: One should never walk in the middle of the road at night, or else one may be driven to the side by a funeral procession.
33525: One night two men saw a funeral procession pass.
33526: If a dog howled eerily, a death would come. The dogs never howled as much as during the Spanish flu in 1918.
33527: When magpies chatter, talkative visitors will come.
33528: In Hardegarijp there used to be a castle whose gates would never stay shut. People once saw a foal with a porridge pan around its neck walking around there. They also saw a man who had been cut open hanging in a tree there.
33529: A man was once accompanied on the road by a silent stranger. According to the man it was a guardian angel.
33531: At night, night-mares squeezed people's necks shut so that they could hardly breathe. To keep them away, people would put asafoetida (devil's dung) under their thresholds.
33532: One night a man saw a few girls wearing bloodstained aprons. Those children were said to have been murdered there.
33534: A scoffer once came out of the pub drunk, when he was beaten up by the devil.
33535: People sometimes saw little lights at a certain spot. Later a tram came to run there.
33536: A farmhand slept in a box bed in the cowshed. Once he saw a bucket dancing.
33537: On a farm, people sometimes heard the wagons driving over the threshing floor at night, but there was never anything to be seen.
33549: In Hardegarijp there is a gate that never stays shut. Ghosts also walk about there.
33550: Black cats always gathered at a certain spot. But when a person approached, they vanished.
33554: A foal with a porridge pan around its neck haunted a certain place.
33555: A man once noticed he was being followed. After a while he became angry and said that it should just come and get him, then. Then he was horribly beaten up by the devil.
33565: A man was born with a caul and often saw funerals and funeral processions in advance.
33566: A man who was born with a caul once saw a funeral procession coming from a farm. A few days later one of the farm's daughters fell through the ice and drowned.
33573: A few scoffers once celebrated Holy Communion in the pub. On the way back one of them was punished by the devil: the next day he was found dead in the ditch.
33575: In the past you could look into the black mirror at the market. If you appeared black in it, you would die young.
33576: One should not walk in the middle of the road at night, or one may run into a funeral procession.
33578: In Hardegarijp there are gates that can never be kept shut. A horse once refused to go past them.
33579: Swallows' nests bring luck. But if someone destroys them, they bring bad luck.
33581: When a dog starts howling eerily, it is a bad sign.
33582: At a certain place people sometimes heard a voice coming from the sea that said: Stand still, for you cannot go any further.
33584: A drowned child was once not dressed in grave clothes in its coffin. Then it could find no rest and haunted a skipper's boat. The skipper laid out some little clothes, and since then the child has not come again.
33588: A witch can change herself into a cat. A woman known as a witch was quite often laid up in bed injured. Then she had been hit again while she was a cat.
33589:
When witches change into cats, they sometimes hold meetings together. One of them is then the leader.
Some witches stick pins into dolls to torment people.
33590: A man promised his wife that if she died, he would give a certain object to their daughter. But because he did not do this (he remarried), the woman could find no rest after her death and came back to haunt. Only when the widower gave his little daughter what she was entitled to did she stay away.
33593: If you have a swallows' nest and leave it alone, it brings luck. If you take the eggs away, it brings misfortune. The eggs are poisoned.
33595: A woman was once upset for a whole day because she had the feeling her husband was dead. The next day her husband really died.
33596: Someone once saw a house on fire. Later the house really burned down.
33600: A foal with a porridge pan around its neck haunted a certain place.
33607: A scoffer was once lifted up and thrown down by the devil.
33610: One night a man was out when someone came walking beside him. The stranger did not answer his greetings. Then the man said that if he was of the devil he must vanish; if he came from God he could stay. Then the stranger suddenly disappeared.
33613: Witches could change themselves into all kinds of animals, sometimes a hare, but usually a cat. Sometimes such a cat was hit; then the witch was injured the next day.
33619: One night a young man saw a white car standing in the middle of the road. Ghosts got out, and these spirits took him home.
33620: One night a man was followed by a white female figure. She floated alongside his bicycle all the way to his house.
33621: A woman was thrown off a path three times in a row. She understood that a funeral procession she could not see was passing.
33623: A young man sometimes saw a lamp burning at a certain spot. Others saw nothing. Later two new houses were built there.
33624: One night a man saw a great light pass by; he did not know what it was. Later cars came to drive there.
33625: A man once saw a glowing piece of fire in the dark.
33626: A woman was born with a caul and saw funeral processions in advance. Once she knew that it was not a sick man who would die, but his wife. It came true.
33627: A woman saw ghosts, but others saw nothing.
33628: One night a man saw a white woman float past. His colleague saw nothing.
33629: As a soldier in the jungle of Java, a man had once seen the apparition of a woman.
33630: A horse with a porridge pan around its neck haunted a certain place.
33641: A man once claimed he was not afraid of the devil. At once he was lifted up and thrown into a sand pit.
33642: Mike Ruerd was a great scoffer. One day he was lifted up and thrown down by a white woman. The woman chattered like a magpie as she did it. The man lay sick in bed for weeks.
33643: Mike Ruerd could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
33644: A scoffer was once coming out of the pub when he was thrown down by the devil.
33646: A man bewitched children and animals. They would then fall ill and die.
33649: People once got a few apples from a woman known as a witch. After a few days the apples had turned into toads.
33651: A foal with a porridge pan around its neck haunted a certain place.
33662: At a place where a tram came to run, people had already seen the tram beforehand.
33663: A week before renovations were to start in a house, hammering could already be heard there.
33666: A man sometimes saw a dead woman haunting.
33667: In the old days people sometimes saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, wandering lights). They were omens of the houses and bicycles that came later.
33668: A man once heard chopping in the back of the house. Shortly afterwards his wife died and straw was chopped to put in the coffin. Then he heard the same sound again.
33669: A woman once heard cries for help from the water, but she saw nothing. Later three children drowned there.
33675: In the old days some people saw funeral processions in advance. If one did not step aside quickly, one was flung off the road.
33676: A man often had to get up at night to see funeral processions. He knew that someone would then die again.
33677: At night one should not walk in the middle of the road; one must make room for the funeral processions.
33678: Early one morning a man heard something fly over him that greeted him. It must have been a witch.
33679: Scoffers were lifted up and thrown down by the devil. But occasionally this also happened to people who did not scoff.
33686: A foal with a porridge pan haunted a certain place.
33698: Witches in the shape of cats hold meetings on a hill.
33700: Some animals are bulletproof; they cannot be hit.
33703: A man was once lifted up, bicycle and all, and a moment later set down again in the same spot.
33704: People were sometimes suddenly put to the side of the road. Then a funeral procession was passing.
33713: A woman was born with a caul. One night she had seen a corpse in the water. Two weeks later someone did indeed drown.
33714: A woman was born with a caul. Once she had seen a funeral procession. All the men except one were wearing a hat. Later a man was buried. His eldest son wore a cap.
33716: At one spot, people once heard planks and beams being carried around and thrown down. But there was nothing to be seen. Later a farm was built there.
33717: It happened that at the homes of the mortally ill, people heard a coffin being brought in, even though nothing could be seen. That was an omen that the sick person would soon die.

33719: People had sometimes heard on the water the sound of wood and tools being thrown onto a praam (flat-bottomed barge). A few days later someone drowned in the water. To fish out the body, tools and wood were taken along on a barge. So then the men heard the same sound again.
33720: In the old days people warned not to walk in the middle of the road at night because of the funeral processions.
33721: If a dog howls eerily, a death is coming. Also if magpies sit chattering near a house.
33722: One morning a woman chased away a magpie several times. That afternoon her little son drowned.
33723: If someone on a ship was very ill, the sharks would come to it.
33731: In the old days people sometimes saw witte wijven (white women).
33732: A foal with a pan around its neck haunted a certain place.
33746: In the old days people sometimes heard hammering. Then a new house would later be built there.
33750: In the past witches bewitched people by conjuring wreaths into their pillows. The person then felt pricking pains all over, like pins. To protect themselves, people put asafoetida (devil's dung) under the threshold. Children also wore it in a little bag on their chest. A witch could also change herself into a black cat. If such a cat was hit, the witch was injured the next day. Bewitched people went to the duivelbanner (exorcist). He gave them a potion to take home, and the bottle often burst on the way.
33752: A woman was born with a caul and sometimes saw funeral processions. Then she knew that someone would die.
33754: One should never walk in the middle of the road at night, or else one may be put to the side.
33755: In the old days the churn was sometimes bewitched, and then no butter could be made. Then people went to the duivelbanner (exorcist).
33759: A woman had seen in advance that the boy next door would have an accident.
33760: At a certain spot an old man haunted. He had a treasure buried in the ground there.
33761: Some people, for example those who were not given a burial shirt, find no rest after their death. They come back to haunt. Then a minister was fetched. When the Lord's Prayer was said, the ghost disappeared.
33768: People used to see wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) on the heath. Later a motorway came.
33772: A man was born with a caul. At night he often had to get up to see funeral processions.
33773: A farmhand had seen that the farmer's wife would die in childbed. It came true: a white cloth lay over the coffin.
33774: If a dog howls eerily, a funeral procession will pass by. Once a dog howled eerily towards the house of a pregnant woman. The baby was stillborn.
33775: Dreaming of fish or lice means a death in the family.
33776: A woman had seen bearers bring a small coffin into the house, and knew that her child would die. 33778: A woman once heard a night-mare step onto the chair by her bed at night.
33788: On the way back from the market, a married couple were once lifted up, dog cart and all, and thrown over the trees.
33789: Witches could change themselves into black cats. If such a cat was hit, the witch lay sick in bed the next day. If someone was bewitched, they burned the wreath in the pillow. People would also go to the duivelbanner (exorcist) for advice.
33791: A man sometimes fought with the devil.
33797: Some people could make a bottle of drink come with a jack of spades.
33800: The foundations of the church in Bolsward consist of ox hides.
33801: People once heard cries for help from a pool in Houtigehage. Someone is still to drown in it.
33806: A woman once saw a light. Later a new house was built on that spot.
33807: People once saw a house on fire, but in reality there was nothing. They were convinced the house would burn down someday, but that has yet to happen.
33808: A woman was born with a caul. She often had to get up at night to see funerals. She then knew that someone would die, but not who.
33809: People once heard knocking on the window, but no one was there. Later that evening they heard exactly the same knocking again. Then someone came to tell them they had to fulfil their duty as neighbours because someone had died.
33810: It sometimes happened that people on foot or on horseback could not go any further at night. Then a funeral procession came by. Once it had passed, they could continue.
33811: When people had been drinking in the pub, the devil sometimes threw them down on their way back. That was their punishment.
33812: One summer evening people were playing games. They scoffed freely. Suddenly the cards and dice burst into flames. That was their punishment.
33813: When people were playing cards, the devil often joined in. Whoever won often was of the devil.
33814: If a dog howls eerily, a death is coming. Usually in the direction in which the dog howls.
33815: If magpies come into the yard in the morning, something pleasant will happen. If they come in the evening, there will be a death.
33816:
If butterflies fly close to the house, visitors will come.
If a cat washes itself, visitors will come.
If the cat washes itself with its paw over its head, a man wearing a cap will come to visit.
33817: If a wild watch ticks by the bed, a death is coming.
33818: In the old days people sometimes saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, wandering lights) on the road. They were omens of the bicycle lamps and car lights that came later.
33819: People once heard cries for help from the water. Later someone drowned.
33821: A man was once on his way back with his cart. Suddenly he was lifted up and thrown over the ditch. The next day he went to fetch his cart. This was the devil's work.
33822: A witch could fly on a broomstick. She could also change into a white cat. In that form they held meetings with one another, led by one of them. Then they sang. 33836: A woman was bewitched. They burned the wreaths they found in her pillow. Then her son sat down in the yard with a gun. When a cat came, he shot it through the head. The next day a girl from the neighbourhood had a head injury. She was the witch.
33841: A woman once made a cross on the road in front of her door with her clog because she knew a witch would come by. The witch could not get past and went on through the ditch.
33842: Stuttering Harm and his wife were witches. Harm had a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) from the devil. Because of it he never lacked money.
33843: A man once saw a witch come out of her house and fly away into the air on a broomstick.
33846: Apples received from a witch once turned into toads after a few days.
33848: People sometimes heard the sound of iron on iron at a certain spot. Later a tram came to run there.
33849: The wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, wandering lights) that people used to see were forerunners of the bicycle lamps that came later.
33850: People once heard hammering, knocking and so on. Later a new church was built on that spot.
33860: People once heard a sound in a house as if the place were on fire, but there was nothing to be seen. Some still claim the house will burn down one day.
33864: A woman saw lots of blowflies at her house and was afraid her goat would die. Indeed, a few days later the animal was dead.
33865: A woman was once troubled by a night-mare and quickly said the Lord's Prayer. When she said 'and deliver us from evil', the night-mare was gone. She was never troubled by it again.
33867: In the old days people sometimes heard ticking in bed. These were forerunners of the clocks and watches that came later.
34444: People once heard someone come in, but nobody came. Later someone really did come, and they heard the same footsteps again.

When magpies chatter by a house, someone there will die. When dogs howl eerily, someone will soon die as well.

34446: A man was born with a caul. He often saw funeral processions. A few days later there was always a funeral.

34467: Two girls are said to have once drowned at a certain spot. People still sometimes saw them haunting there.

34476: People who were born with a caul often saw funerals in advance.
34478: Witches prick dolls with needles. The person they have bewitched then feels those stabs.
34482: A man could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit and march around the table. By dangling a cross-shaped key over a certain Bible verse he could tell whether someone was lying.
34485: Freemasons got a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) from the devil. Because of it they never lacked money. You could recognise them because they were always rebuilding their houses. Every seven years someone had to die; that person was chosen by lot. He then had to commit suicide. If he did not, the devil wrung his neck.
34492: People did not let a witch near their livestock, or their animals would be bewitched. A witch can change herself into a cat. If such a cat ever gets hit, the witch has an injured leg the next day. To keep witches away, people put asafoetida (devil's dung) under the threshold and in the keyhole.
34495: When people walked at a certain spot, they were always followed by a big black dog.
34496: A man was a great mocker and claimed to be afraid of nothing. Then the devil once lifted him up and threw him down some distance further on.
34497: A man was born with a caul. Because of this he often had to get up at night to see funerals. He always knew in advance that someone would die.
34498: In the old days people were warned not to walk in the middle of the road, or they might be driven aside by a funeral procession.
34500: Stuttering Harm had made a pact with the devil. Because of it he never lacked money. He had a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin). If he threw it into the air, two daalders came back down.
34502: Some people could make a bottle of drink come by giving away a jack of spades.
34503: A man could make hussars march out of the hearth pit.
34504: In the past there were black mirrors in market stalls. In them young men could see which woman they would later marry.
34510: Wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, wandering lights) are omens of houses, bicycles or cars.
34515: Wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) were the omens of the later bicycles and cars.
34517: One evening a man was driven off the narrow road into the little ditch three times. Later it turned out that the woman in the nearby shack had died. The next day she was taken away in a coffin. The man had probably been pushed off the road by her funeral procession.
34518: One night a man saw a funeral procession made up entirely of very tiny people. He was lifted by an invisible hand and set down in the ditch. Later a real funeral took place.
34521: One day a dog sat outside by a tree the whole time, howling eerily in the direction of a house. Later that day a little boy who lived there was brought home dead.
34528: When a dog howled eerily, people believed someone would die. Someone would die in the direction the dog pointed its head.
34531: A man was afraid of nothing. Until one time he was picked up by the devil and flung over the dike. There he got a terrible beating.
34535:
Witches could change themselves into black cats. If someone hit such a cat, the witch was injured the next day.
Witches bewitched people by conjuring wreaths into their pillows. People then went to the duivelbanner (exorcist) for a potion. They also burned the wreaths. Then the witch appeared and began to rage. If the wreath was already completely finished, that person died.
34538: Some people used to look into a black mirror. In it they saw the person they would later marry.
34545: A man saw funeral processions in advance. He was also able to tell details of his own daughter's funeral beforehand.
34546: A man had seen a coffin and so knew that someone in his household would soon die. Not long afterwards an old lady who lodged with them died.
34547: A man always saw all sorts of things in advance. He would then tell his wife. What he told her always came true.
34557: A maid once saw a funeral procession pass by. She saw the cloth over the coffin blow up. A week later someone died. Then she saw the same funeral procession really pass by.
34558: People used to see wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps). Those were the omens of the later bicycles and cars.
34559: People once heard at a certain spot the sound of a train running on a track. But there was nothing to be seen. Later a train really came to run there.
34560: People once heard a noise in the sky, but there was nothing to be seen. When they later heard that noise again, they saw an aeroplane.
34562: A woman had seen a funeral procession at a house. A week later the man of the house died.
34566: People had once hit a cat. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood was injured: she was the witch. A witch has to bewitch someone to death every seven years, or else she dies herself.
34570: Some witches could fly, on a broomstick.
34572: A man was suddenly thrown over a hedge for no reason. He had been pushed aside by a funeral procession.
34582: In Hardegarijp there is a castle with a gate that will not stay shut. They have fastened heavy locks and chains to it, but the gate always opens again.
34583: Father often tells about Ymke de Jong, with whom he served in the army in Leeuwarden. Ymke never wants to obey and is often punished. Once he is even sent to prison, but he always gets every door open, whatever the locks.
34586: In the pub Ymke asks for a guilder and promises to give it back. He gets a guilder, swallows it, takes a pan and starts to retch. Guilders come pouring out of his throat and nose until the pan is full. But those guilders disappear again. The soldier does get his guilder back, though.
34587: Ymke de Jong gets into a quarrel with a nasty policeman. The policeman laughs at Ymke, whereupon Ymke tells him he can make it so the policeman can no longer walk. The policeman would like to see that, but indeed cannot move his legs until Ymke says he can move again.
34592: We lived next door. It was said that something would happen someday. They had heard a hellish racket and saw a red light. "It will burn down one day," they said, but it hasn't happened yet.
34594: In Zwaagwesteinde we used to see witte wijven (white women) often.
34595: People said the world would come to an end, but an old merchant said: "The world will only end when the sea becomes land and straight roads appear on which things drive, without horses, all by themselves." Some of those things have come true.
34604: On the road from the bridge, two girls wander about in white robes with a streak of blood around their necks. Long ago those girls had their throats cut. Now they can find no rest.
34608: When someone who has died comes back, the minister is fetched, who asks what he wants.
34609: In the old days wandering lights were often seen. They were the lamps of bicycles and cars.
34611: A rich man lived on the Goddeloze Singel. He died in an accident with a horse and now his treasure lies there under the ground. The old man haunts the place and people are terrified. The old man keeps coming closer.
34614: Three witte wijven (white women) used to haunt the Lange Laan. People did not dare to pass there at night.
34618: Everyone is afraid of the witch, Alde Willemke. We make a cross on the road with the tip of a clog, because she would not be able to cross it.
34621: Willemke can change herself into a black cat. Once they caught that cat and beat it, and the next day Willemke was ill.
34622: For the witches' meeting they change into cats and then sing in a circle.
34623:
Stuttering Harm is a sorcerer. When he needs money, he hangs his purse outside and the next day it is filled. He also has a wisseldaalder (a magic coin that always returns).
Ritske Bottema, a shopkeeper, is never short of money either. He too hangs his purse on the door. He is with the Freemasons. He has sold his soul to the devil. He can no longer leave the Freemasons. The devil has him in his grip.
34624: Willemke also bewitches the livestock. People do not let her near it. At Heideloantsje all the livestock fell ill, but I no longer remember who the witch was who did that.
34625: Some people are seized by the devil. That has happened in Zwaagwesteinde too, but I no longer remember who it happened to.
34626: Witches make wreaths in pillows with lots of threads. When the threads have gone, the witches' power is broken. If you accept an apple from a witch and eat it, you get a toad in your stomach. If you step on a toad, a thunderstorm comes.
34627: If the churn is bewitched and no butter comes, people go to Wopke, who gives good advice.
34629: Marijke Westra sees in a black mirror that a coffin is coming for her. A few weeks later she dies, almost twenty years old.
34632: A werewolf is a person who sometimes has to tear something apart.
34633: In Hardegarijp, by a doctor's house, there is a gate that will not stay shut. Three children were murdered there.
34637: A man takes the shadowy figure of a man coming out of a thicket for a ghost.
34638: In Oostermeer a man tells another, who was born with a caul, that he must step aside because a funeral procession is coming. And Willem Mulder's grandmother was also born with a caul, and she has to see everything.
34639: Some people can make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
34643: If the churn does not produce butter, it is bewitched. Then the devil banisher has to come to set it right.
34644: Fifty years ago there was a farmer whose cattle were bewitched. The milk was not good. The devil banisher was fetched and he set it right.
34645: Imke de Jong can fix people in place.
34646: Some people can make a bottle of drink come with the help of the jack of spades.
34762: A cruel knight captures and tortures every passer-by. However, a merchant manages to escape from him. Then the knight gets lost in a bog; the merchant comes and offers to help him if he releases his prisoners. The knight refuses and sinks into the bog. Since then a procession of ghosts is seen there.
35011: A robber has mastered sorcery. While drinking a dram in an inn, he notices constables coming in to arrest him. As soon as he puts his empty glass upside down on the table, he fixes everyone to the spot. The robber calmly leaves and on the way asks a little old woman to set the glass in the inn upright again. When she has done so, everyone starts moving again. They immediately want to arrest the woman, but she makes it clear that she was only told to set the glass upright.
35039: A witch wants to teach someone else kollen (bewitching cattle). When it turns out that the apprentice must swear loyalty to the devil, the apprentice runs away in fright.
35910: Little lights used to be seen on the heath: a voorloop (an apparition foreshadowing an event) of cars on the national highway.
35912: Someone sees a ghost that grows bigger and smaller; he picks up his clogs and runs away fast.
35913: A rough drunkard is thrown away by the devil.
35916: A man has to make way for a funeral procession and ends up in the ditch.
35924: In my childhood I heard that a foal with a porridge pot around its neck haunted Eestrum.
35950: Harm, a witch, had a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin); it never ran out. He had sold himself to the devil for it. If he hung his purse on the door, it was full in the morning. His two daughters were witches too.
35953: If you kicked a cat, it could happen that the witch stayed in bed the next day. Or she had bruises.
35975: Witches meet in the shape of cats on a field or in a tree. Sometimes they sing, or they discuss whom they will bewitch.
35976: A man visits his friend, peers through the shutters and sees the friend and his mother busy with little dolls into which they stick pins. With these they caused pain to people they had it in for.
35977: A girl loses one of her red garters, and it is found in the pillow of a woman who was bewitched, woven into a wreath [of feathers].
35982: One of seven boys from one family is a werewolf. One such was with his sweetheart one evening and suddenly said: "Now I must do something. Give me something I can go at." She gives him a cloth and he tears it apart with his teeth; the shreds hung from his mouth. Had he been given nothing, he would have torn his girl apart.
36025: I was standing in Jistrum and heard hammering behind me while there was nothing to be seen. Could it be some kind of omen? It turned out to be, because later we would get a house there.
36026: Old Tamme Hooijenga told that he was once near the old tramway, when no tram ran yet, and heard a whistle. That was the whistle of the steam tram built later.
36029: On the Skulenburgerweg a black beast, a kind of dog, always haunts. It runs along with people and they cannot shake it off.
36030: Age Bergsma went to visit Evert, who was rather lonely. Age made jokes and also said he was not yet afraid of the devil. When he went back, there was someone beside him who kept looking at him sideways over his shoulder. Age broke into a run but could not shake off the figure. He understood it was the devil and came home soaked in sweat.
36032: It is said that in Skulenburch a foal with a porridge pot around its neck runs about at night.
36036: A minister had visited a farmer with an elder. They left late and had to cross a little bridge. A courting couple in front of the bridge warned that you could be thrown off the bridge for no reason, because the place was haunted. They went anyway, and in the middle of the bridge something came at them. The minister said bravely that they were servants of the Most High, and then "it" quietly disappeared.
36038: Uncle Hindrik went to see his sweetheart in Droegeham one Sunday evening. He was in a silly mood and said he would like to see the devil some time. When he came home that night he threw his only good pair of trousers, completely torn, onto the oat stack. On the way he had fought with the devil in the shape of a horrible black dog. He said he never needed to see the devil again.
36044: In the old days people saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, wandering lights) above Grinzer Pein. Later houses were built on that spot.
36045: In the east of Grinzer Pein a man was riding a bicycle in the middle of the night. Suddenly he was picked up and flung aside. He saw nothing, but later he was told that a funeral procession had passed.
36046: In Drachtster Compagnie there lived a man who often ran over the planks across the ditches at night to see a funeral procession. He could then predict who would be the next to die. It always came true.
36047: Boardzer Bruining was born with a caul. He also always saw funeral processions.
36056: Jehannes Mijnheer had a little shop on the spot where a school later stood. That is gone now too. Some people had seen Mijnheer's shop on fire, and later that indeed happened.
36057: Boardzer Bruining always had to watch funeral processions. Others had to get out of bed at night for them and sometimes ran long distances to see them.
36060: On the Muzegroppewei a foal with a porridge pot haunts.
36062: Sorcerers were usually little old women. Janne Luts was one of them, and we were afraid of her as children. She always gave us food, but we didn't dare eat it. Sorcerers often change themselves into a black cat. Once someone in the village found a strange black cat in his house. He threw it outside. The next day we saw the old woman walking about with a broken arm. Then we knew she was a sorcerer.
36063: In Rottefalle I saw cats holding a meeting. A grey cat was at the head. Later you could hear psalms being sung.
36072: If the butter will not churn, it is bewitched. At the farmer's where I lived, they put a little bottle by the churn against bewitchment.
36073: The devil is in playing cards. Some people can make a bottle of drink come with a card.
36074: Ielke Snipe could make little soldiers appear from the hearth pit.
36075: A black mirror at the market could foretell: the woman a man would marry appeared in the mirror.
36076: You got a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) from the devil. It always grew back. You had to take care never to spend all of it.
36082: My grandmother heard the sounds of a train on the rails long before there was a railway between Leeuwarden and Zwaagwesteinde.
36083: Stammering Harm had a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) through his pact with the devil. He always had money, lent out a lot and had money earning interest. He always looked unkempt. He dealt a little in rags and scrap iron and seemed able to work magic: he could make cattle sick.
36090: In the old days we often saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, wandering lights) floating through the air. They were forerunners of the aeroplanes.
36091: An 11-year-old girl went with her father to Grinslan. There people often played cards and drank gin in a barn. Once the gin ran out. One of the men sent the jack of spades to fetch a bottle. A little later a bottle of gin stood at the door. The one who had sent out the jack of spades was not allowed to pick it up himself.
36092: Father always warned us not to run onto the road at night. If a funeral procession comes, you get flung aside.
36093: It happened that the devil would throw someone down because they used foul language or had had too much to drink.
36094: In the past we would sometimes draw a cross on the path with our clog so that sorcerers could not cross it. A sorcerer can change into a black cat. If you give such a cat a wallop, the witch walks about with a bandage around her head the next day. Children in particular are bewitched. You can tell by the wreaths in the pillows. They had to be burned before a certain time, or the child died. Bewitched children were often given a potion.
36096: Some cowsheds were haunted. There the cows came loose by themselves after being tied up. This always happened at night.
36105: One evening I saw a bicycle approaching behind our house, or so it seemed, because the light did not come any closer. Later 2 new houses were built on that spot. It was by the little wood.
36107: My mother-in-law lived on Alllardseach. Some people said they saw fire behind her house. Later, when she was already dead, the house indeed burned down.
36113: Using a playing card, people had a bottle of liquor brought to them. The one who had sent the card away was not allowed to accept the bottle.
36114: In the past there were black mirrors at the market. If you looked into one, you saw your future spouse.
36133: A family lived in an old house that no longer stands. One night the eldest of four sons woke up. He saw an old man sitting at the table smoking. It turned out to be his grandfather, who had once lived in the same house.
36134: One evening Gabe de Haan and his wife saw a strange man approaching. They saw him clearly and reached the bridge at about the same time as he did. The woman wished the man good evening, but at that moment he seemed to have vanished from the face of the earth. Gabe never saw the man again.
36135: 82 years ago the narrator's father-in-law was out hunting polecats. At a certain moment a big black dog came running beside him. He said it was a ghost dog.
36136: One evening the narrator's husband and his cousin had been to the inn 'De laatste Stuver'. When they were standing on a bridge, they saw an animal coming across the meadow. The animal was pitch black and as big as a cow. It had the shape of a dog. The beast looked at the two men. They became so frightened that they quickly ran off.
36137: The narrator was lying in bed and in her dream saw men with tin headgear coming over the dike. A year later the Second World War broke out, and the Germans came over the dike wearing helmets, exactly the way the woman had dreamed.
36138: In the old days little lights were sometimes seen on the path. They were not people with lanterns, however, because they never came any closer.
36139: The narrator's sister had a little son who was in hospital. She and her husband received word that their child's condition was critical. The husband wanted to hurry to the hospital, but his wife stayed calm. She had seen the sheets of the little bed being carried outside: so their son was already dead.
36140: A father and mother had twins. At nine months one of the children fell ill and died. At the churchyard the father said that their other child would die too. He had seen it lying in a little coffin. When they came home the other child had died as well.
36141: Running across the road at night is dangerous, because you can be thrown over a funeral procession.
36142: An old bachelor was regularly at odds with the devil. They fought every night, and everything in his house rattled and clattered. Afterwards the bachelor was covered in bruises and scratches.
36143: A witch could change herself into a cat, usually a red-spotted one. The witches gathered as cats in an old shed. In Kollumerzwaag these witches stole potatoes. First a cat came to scout things out, and then the thief came. This was a man who had also changed into a cat.
36145: Stammering Harm had sold himself to the devil. He had received a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) from him. Whenever he spent the daalder, it came back. That is why he always had enough money, including to keep sheep and lend money.
36148: A foal with a porridge pot haunts behind the military police barracks in Buitenpost.
36150: Stammering Harm bewitched the cattle. Within seven years, witches kill at least one person or animal with sorcery. Accepting something from a witch is dangerous. If you eat it, you get a toad in your body. There was also once someone who passed salamanders in his urine.
36154: With the jack of spades people had a bottle of liquor brought to them.
36155: In a black mirror you can see whom you will marry. If you do not marry, you see a coffin in the mirror.
36160: A friend of the narrator heard hammering. He said a new house would surely be built soon. The narrator himself heard nothing, but a new house was indeed built.
36161: When dogs howl frighteningly, a death will follow.
36162: In Nijega two old people were murdered. A man was walking along the Wytfeanster paths pushing his blind father in a wheelbarrow. The blind father saw the murderers coming. At that moment they were walking some way further on.
36163: The narrator's father and brother were on their way to Surhuisterveen when they saw a black plaagbeest (tormenting spectral beast) pass by. The beast did them no harm.
36164: When the drunkard Jan Hinses once walked along the Zwarte weg, he was given a thrashing by the devil. He has not drunk since.
36167: The Groene Weg to Eastemar used to be haunted.
36168: If you run across the road at night, you can be pushed aside by a funeral procession.
36171: The narrator's father once took Bouke Schievink home. Bouke always had the devil with him. That evening the father saw them both.
36174: Magpies and dogs can announce a death.
36175: People with supernatural gifts go out at night and can foretell deaths.
36176: An old woman from Harkema could make the devil come out of the hearth pit.
36178: In the past young people often looked into a black mirror to see the future.
36181: With a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) from the devil you always have enough money.
36183: In Boelenslaan people often saw in advance that a house would burn down, or that a new house would be built.
36184: A man went outside at night to see funeral processions. He could predict who would die.
36185: If you run down the middle of the road at night, a funeral procession may come. You are then pushed aside or flung away.
36186: Someone who brags, curses or mocks can be lifted up and flung away.
36187: A strange man from Rottefalle wanted to see the devil in the graveyard. When a girl standing there at her mother's grave said something, the man took to his heels.
36188: A man sees a big black dog at night that keeps growing bigger. It turns out to be the devil.
36191: The frightening howling of a dog announces a death.
36203: Because a woman did not keep a promise to her son, she could find no rest after death.
36204: Some farm barns were haunted. Guests were not given shelter there.
36206: With her card readings Tryn Snipel always predicted wealth, which people liked to hear.
36208: In the old days, during card games, the devil sometimes emerged from a card in which he had hidden himself.
36210: At the holly hedge near the Blauhuis there is a werewolf with a porridge pot around its neck. You must eat from it with the spoon that is in it.
36211: On the Boelenswei a big black dog came at the narrator, so that he ran into the house so fast that he did not even open the lower half of the door.
36217: Sjouk, an old woman, had a shop. One day she did not open. She was floating around the lamp in her living room.
36219: Before Albert de Boer's house was built, someone had already seen a light burning on that spot.
36221: Polecat hunters often used to see lanterns at places where a road would later come. Piter Kloosterman could see the tram in advance.
36235: Black cats bring bad luck. It may be a witch in the shape of a cat.
36236: Jehannes v.d. Zee mocked everything. One day, on his way to work, he was beaten black and blue by the devil. He has been converted since.
36238: A man dreams at night that someone is murdered. That same night his brother is murdered.
36239: When both her parents died, the narrator suffered from melancholy. Both times she sensed that something bad was happening, while she did not yet know anything about the deaths.
36240: Shortly before he was murdered, Piter [Veenstra] heard groaning sounds on a trip to the toilet. When his brother went to listen, he heard nothing. Piter's brother later said that he had heard his own death throes then.
36259: A man who was out one evening was suddenly joined by a big black dog. The man was terrified, because it was a plaagbeest (tormenting spectral beast).
36260: Teade was a cattle dealer. Once he sold a cow at the market. When he came back with his money he was robbed and murdered. He still haunts the spot where it happened.
36261: Various places in Friesland are haunted.
36262: A night-mare is a woman. They appear on people's chests at night. They come in through the keyhole. To keep them away, people place their slippers back to front in front of the bed and scatter flour on their faces.
36265: A clairvoyant man can see funeral processions pass by at night. If someone is running on the road when such a funeral procession passes, that person can be pushed aside.
36274: In the old days there was a plaagbeest (tormenting spectral beast) in the 'old corner'. It ran from the baker's yard to the neighbour woman's.
36275: Nobody dared to eat anything from the witch of Twizelerheide, for fear of being bewitched.
36277: In the old days people in Westerein saw lights in the place where cars would later drive.
36279: Hanne Kramer could fly very fast. When the farmer drove to Leeuwarden with horse and cart, Hanne got there sooner.
36282: The narrator's father-in-law once met a funeral procession at night. He was pushed off the road.
36287: Many people still believe that the frightening howling of a dog announces a death.
36296: The narrator's mother could see things before they happened. For instance, she saw the neighbour woman lying in her coffin before her death. The coffin could not be carried through the door. Later everything went exactly as she had predicted.
36297: The narrator's mother saw in advance that two of the neighbours' children would die.
36298: The narrator's father wanted to drown one of their two dogs because they were short of money. His wife, however, warned him that the dog would not die in the water. The father nevertheless went to the water with the dog, put him in a sack with a stone in it and drowned him. But when he got home, the dog was standing at the window. The family then kept the dog, and he later died at their home.
36299: The narrator's mother predicted that Marten van Kammen, who suffered from TB, would soon die. After his death she took her daughter to his body. She rubbed her wrist over his forehead, and so the daughter got rid of her warts.
36300: The narrator's mother predicted that two houses in their neighbourhood would burn down. In one of the fires all of Dedde Wybenga's livestock would perish.
36301: Marten van Kammen was once in the middle of the road at night. He was lifted up for no reason and thrown to the side of the ditch, while no one was to be seen.
36302: Knjillis Veenstra could see funerals before they happened, including that of his own daughter.
36304: The narrator's father saw the moon landing before it took place.
36305: A narrator's mother saw a corpse come floating over the water from Dokkum. A little later a corpse from Dokkum was indeed found in the water.
36312: In some farm barns in Grinslan, people were simply lifted up and thrown aside. The doors also opened by themselves at night. In Hardegarijp there is a gate that opens by itself.
36317: Whoever looks into a black mirror can see whom he or she will marry.
36322: A man from Sanbulten was clairvoyant. He predicted a train accident. Others saw car lights where a road would later be built.
36324: On the Boppewei there is a ghost that comes a little closer every year.
36327: In some farm barns, people lying there were simply picked up and thrown down. Sometimes the doors also opened by themselves and wagons started moving on their own.
36328: A man from Westerein regularly went to get drunk in the pub. He would curse and swear a lot. One evening on his way home he was stopped by the devil, who forced him to walk through the ditch.
36329: A woman often had trouble with her husband. After she died, the girl next door saw her standing in her nightclothes.
36330: The Boppewei is haunted. The ghost will only leave once the treasure that lies there has been dug up.
36331: The narrator's little sister died as a child. Before it happened, her father had already seen her little coffin standing in a particular spot in the house.
36332: Some children are born with a caul. That is a thin membrane over the eyes. If you remove it, you must stroke it backwards. Otherwise the child will later have to see everything [become clairvoyant].
36333: A witch could change into a cat. When an old woman from Westerein had broken her arm, people said she had flown into the wires.
36336: Witches often held meetings at which they took the shape of a cat.
36343: Knillis Veenstra could predict deaths and often saw funeral processions travelling along the road. Whenever a funeral procession came, Knillis had to go to it. He could no longer stay at home and ended up in a poorhouse in Kollumerzwaag.
36344: If you went out on the road at night, you could be pushed aside by a funeral procession. That sometimes happened in Westerein.
36345: Once, long ago, something floated over the road, and nobody knew what it was.
36346: On the Lange Loane a plaagbeest (tormenting spectral beast) ran about that looked exactly like a dog. People were terrified of it.
36347: People did not dare to go along the Lange Reed because it was haunted.
36348: An old woman and her daughter were once outside in the evening. They heard the trotting of a horse but saw nothing. They became frightened and went to a man who lived nearby. Then they went outside with a lantern and the man saw a horse come flying towards them. The others, however, saw nothing and only heard it.
36358: An old woman could see lights on the road. These turned out to be bicycle lamps, which would only come much later. There were no bicycles yet at the time.
36359: A witch lived on the Swemmer. She once killed someone by magic, and she could also bewitch people who ate something of hers.
36360: There was a witch who had horns on her head. She was not allowed near children. Other witches bewitched pigs by putting asafoetida (devil's dung) in their feed.
36361: Age Bruining became a widower. After six weeks he was woken at night by a bumping noise. He saw his wife standing in the house. He took her outside and then she went away.
36362: A man was at the tailor's and was afraid the devil would come to meet him. When he walked back at night, three times a man was lying across the road. Each time he walked around him. But the third time the man grabbed him and beat him up.
36365: During the war the narrator's wife once walked to Kollum in the evening. On the way she had to stand on the verge because a funeral procession was passing.
36402: A farmer lived in an area with a lot of water. Once he heard the rattling of milk churn lids there. Later farms were built on that spot.
36404: A witch could change into a black cat.
36412: Father went out early with his dog cart. Mother meanwhile stayed at home making rope. One morning it just would not get light. Mother grew afraid and prayed to God for light. Father was on his way and saw three burning coals lying in the middle of the road. He did not dare pass them, but did so anyway. When he was past them, they had vanished. According to him this fire was the evil power. The long darkness, however, was caused by a broken alarm clock. Father had set out at two in the morning instead of six.
36414: Hanne Kramer could fly. He worked for a farmer, who one day ferried him across the water. The farmer asked what time Hanne wanted to be picked up. But Hanne said he would manage by himself. The next day the boat was simply lying at the bank, yet Hanne had come home. He had flown. The farmer became afraid of him and sent him away.
36415: Hanne never went along with his mates to work when they came to fetch him. He left later, but he still got there first. The same was true of the journey home. People said this was because he could fly.
36420: Witches change themselves into cats. They hold meetings and sing psalms there. If you give a cat a smack, you can see it on the witch the next day.
36421: In a house a dead girl always came to the table at night. That girl had been murdered and now could find no rest.
36422: Knjillis Veenstra was clairvoyant. He could see things in advance, and they always came true. So his prediction that a white horse would pull a hearse also came true: it snowed that day.
36424: The narrator's father was once thrown out of bed against the table by the devil.
36426: Sometimes someone kicked a cat, and then the witch had a sore leg afterwards.
36427: A cat that is really a witch can only be hit with a silver bullet.
36428: When a dog howled frighteningly, someone would die.
36429: A woman from Westerein predicted that a child would drown in the canal.
36431: The devil of Earnewald once jumped over the canal. That is why there is still a footprint of the devil in the ground.
36433: In Westerein (Zwaagwesteinde) some people could already hear the sound of the train before any trains ran.
36466: A man from Westerein was always cursing. Once he walked out of the pub with a group of young people. At a certain moment he saw something that frightened him to death. The others saw nothing. The man ran home and fled into his bed.
36467: Magpies can announce a funeral or visitors. The frightening howling of a dog announces a death.
36471: Jehannes Meerstra came round selling Edam cheese. The girls would not open the door for him, because he made their skirts fall down. His hands would also sometimes suddenly be full of dimes.
36472: Kei and Tjitse had a farm. Kei once went to collect the eggs, but the hens said they were not laying that day. The cow said she was giving no milk today. Jantsje, a witch from the neighbourhood, was blamed. When Kei and Tjitse opened a pillow, a wreath came out.
36473: In the past the children used to discuss witchcraft among themselves. When Wiger came by, he said he had kicked a black cat. Antsje, the witch, walked with a limp after that.
36474: The narrator's mother heard at night the sounds of building work that would later take place on that spot.
36475: The neighbour was upset because the cradle in her attic kept rocking all the time. Later she had a baby, who was laid in that cradle.
36476: In the old days people already saw lights passing by in the place where the railway would later come.
36478: At the Skilige Piip the ghost of someone who was murdered there roams about.
36479: At the Skansebrege the horses always stopped dead. They would not cross the bridge until it was daylight. Apparently they saw something that people did not see.
36480: The narrator's little sister was clairvoyant. She saw funeral processions travelling along the road. She also saw her grandfather's funeral pass by. She often got out of bed at night to see the funeral processions.
36481: In Feanwalden lived a man who went to the pub in Hardegarijp. He was cursing terribly. On the way back he had to pass through the Foksegatten. He was then thrown away and flew high through the air over the trees.
36482: Jehannes Meerstra could simply make women's skirts fall down. One day a woman came to buy cheese from him. She claimed she had been given a dime too little in change. Jehannes looked at it, and suddenly all the coins in her hand had turned into dimes. The amount was exactly right.
36483: A group of boys went to steal apples in Tsjibbe Gratema's orchard. Jehannes was to help them. At that moment the pigs were being loaded into the wagon. Tsjibbe saw the boys in the trees, but did not go after them because the pigs began squealing terribly: Jehannes had caused this.
36484: Jehannes could do remarkable things. He could make someone stand still so that they could not take another step, and he could make the roosters on the roof crow. Once he was in the pub with a group. He said there was a bottle of liquor under the fifth tree. That was true. He did these things with cards.
36489: A little woman was walking outside one evening. Suddenly she saw something black. She asked it to come if it was of the Lord, and to go away if it was of Satan. It went away. The woman fled home, frightened to death.
36490: At Skilige Piip a chest of money lies in the ground. However, it is impossible to dig it up. Every time you hit it, it sinks a little deeper into the ground.
36491: Schoolteacher Foekje v.d. Bos had to get up at night to see funeral processions.
36492: Sjouke-petroalje was a witch. He once flew with his dog cart through the keyhole into people's house. Wreaths were also found in the pillows of those people. They burned them. Some way further on lived old people whom Sjouke bewitched.
36493: Tjitse and Ke could talk with the rooster, the hens and the cow.
36494: On a path in Jistrum a woman always haunted at night. She wore a white garment and a yoke with buckets. She stood still.
36495: Piter Kooistra murdered old Liuwe on the Iestwei. Just before this happened, he walked along that road with his father-in-law. At a certain point his father-in-law could not walk any further; he saw a black streak running across the whole road.
36496: Children were not allowed to walk on the path at night. You could then be pushed aside by a funeral procession.
36497: Someone once came out of the pub claiming he was not afraid of the devil. On the way to Jistrum he was violently thrown back and forth, so that he arrived in Jistrum more dead than alive.
36498: Jehannes [Meerstra] could make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit. He could also make the table and stove dance.
36499: Abraham had a dog cart. Once, when he was on his way to Leeuwarden with it, the dogs suddenly stood still. Jehannes [Meerstra] just then came along on foot. He managed to make the dogs run again.
36500: Jehannes could tell exactly what was in your purse. If you had no money left, you had to hang the empty purse on the door. Then the devil would fill it again. Jehannes could make people stand still and make women's skirts fall down. But he did nobody any harm.
36501: Piter Koop swore and scoffed a lot and played cards. One night he left his friend's place. On the way he met someone in black wearing a cape, who bumped into him. He said nothing. Piter was terrified when he got home.
36504: Don't look in the mirror too much, or the devil may wring your neck.
36505: If a card falls during a card game, you must not pick it up. Otherwise the devil may wring your neck.
36506: At the market in Leeuwarden there was sometimes a black mirror. Two men looked into it. One saw his future wife, the other a coffin: the latter would not marry but die.
36509: In Burgumerheide lived a witch who could talk with a cow. The cow also talked back.
36512: Some time before the neighbour's house was demolished, a loud thud could already be heard. It sounded as if a wall was falling.
36513: A clairvoyant midwife often foresaw things. She often went out at night. She also saw the death of her daughter in advance.
36514: Knjillis Veenstra could see in advance who would die during the measles epidemic. He also saw his daughter's death before it happened.
36515: A man had seen that a little shop where someone lived was on fire. A little later it indeed burned down.
36517: The narrator could hear the singing of the 'Latter-day Saints' two years before they arrived.
36518: When the narrator and her husband were visiting her mother, she got a rash on her head. One day her mother said they had better leave. She was afraid her child would die, because a dog had howled frighteningly the night before.
36519: When a cat washes itself, visitors are coming. If it washes behind its ear, they will be strangers. Magpies around the house announce a death. Just before an uncle died, there were black birds sitting on the roof.
36521: At the dam in Hiltsjemoaiwalden a white lady always haunts.
36522: Behind Kollum there was a place where the horses could go no further. They became frightened of something only they could see.
36524: Near the Twizeler Weg people used to see lanterns, which are said to have been the bicycle lights of later times.
36525: In Uithuizen there was a haunted barn that always stayed empty. In the stalls the cattle would not stay tied up.
36527: In Grinslan people heard at night the sounds of the churning mill and of the horse running round, even though no churning had been done there for years.
36531: Shortly before her death, a young woman from Westerein saw a funeral procession. The names of all the people walking in it were called out, but her own name was not among them.
36532: A couple who bought a house in Westerein sold it again after they had seen a funeral procession. The woman's sister then went to live in the house and died shortly afterwards.
36534: One evening a man from Westerein saw a big cat and a small cat. He gave the big cat a wallop. The next morning he met a mate who could not come to work because his wife was laid up in bed. She was a witch, and so was her mother.
36535: Witches sometimes held meetings as cats, at which they sang beautifully.
36536: Aeltsje was a witch. Once she stood by a tree making strange movements. She was then brought into the house, foaming at the mouth. People said she could fly.
36539: Witches change themselves into black cats.
36541: Clare was a card reader. A squeaking sound came from her chest. She predicted that the narrator would meet a man at a party, and that came true.
36543: Saekje was a witch. People who looked in through her window saw that she had little dolls on the table and was pricking them with pins.
36549: A young man claimed he was not afraid of the devil and that he would accept money from him. When he came out of the pub, he saw someone on the Twizelerwei swinging a purse back and forth. But he did not dare take it and hurried away.
36551: The narrator's mother and a friend were once at the market in Leeuwarden. There they saw a black mirror. When the friend looked into it, the mother's brother appeared in it. But she did not marry him. The mother saw an unknown man, whom she did later marry.
36552: At Minke's house they could make black birds fly out of the hearth pit and back into it.
36554: You should never walk in the middle of the path at night, because a funeral procession may come.
36556: Someone in Westerein drowned when he went out skating. Before it happened, people had already heard wailing.
36557: Every seven years witches must bewitch someone to death, or else they die themselves.
36558: A tramp was walking down the street when a dog came running at him. According to the tramp, a dog that comes at you and snaps at your calves announces a death.
36559: When a dog howled frighteningly, it meant someone would die.
36560: Ymke de Vries's grandfather had seen that a church would be built. He also heard organ music. Later it happened exactly like that.
36561: Auke [de Vries] saw a funeral procession come out of old Tryn's house. Tryn died about a year later.
36562: Knjillis Veenstra is clairvoyant. He often had to go outside at night. The gates would then open for him by themselves.
36563: The mother of Kees, who drowned, knew before his death that someone would drown.
36565: One evening the narrator's grandfather was walking outside. On the way he saw a big black dog. When he told his brother, the brother said there would be a death in the family. Some time later the grandfather fell ill and died.
