36568: On the Koopmansweg a woman haunts, dressed entirely in black and wearing a cap on her head.
36571: People sometimes used to see lanterns, which they later said belonged to the future bicycles. Some people also saw the train before it was there.
36575: Jitske became pregnant while unmarried. When the baby came she was just working in the fields. Her boyfriend buried the baby, which later became known. After its death the child could find no rest. Every night the child comes to Jitske's house and knocks on the windows.
36576: Two men came out of the pub drunk and were boasting freely. On the Lange Laan one of them was lifted up and thrown aside. This was the devil's work.
36577: Bontsje Keke said that at night people were sometimes pushed aside when a funeral procession came.
36578: Witches who had changed into cats sometimes held gatherings. Then they sang psalms.
36582: Some people could have a bottle of gin brought to them using a playing card (the jack of spades). They had to throw the first glass over their left shoulder.
36584: Magpies around the house announce a death.
36586: Stammering Harm had a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) from the devil.
36602: The place where the devil wrung a man's neck is haunted.
36603: Between Durk Reitsma's and Hindrik Koostra's a foal haunts with a porridge pot around its neck.
36607: Witches are women by day, but at night they change into cats. People would sometimes hurt such a cat, and then the next day a woman was lame.
36608: Jehannes once saw an apparition approaching. He thought it was no good. So he said it should come if it was of the Lord and go away if it was of the devil. The being flew around him like a roaring lion, but then disappeared.
36614: Douwe Jager once saw a white lady haunting the Reidfjildsdyk.
36615: In the old days people saw many wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, wandering lights). They were omens of the bicycle lamps that came later.
36618: Witches who changed into cats at night often lay together under the hedge.
36619: Ever since a man was murdered on the Godloas singel, it has been haunted there.
36620: Some clairvoyant people saw funeral processions at night. They would then warn others to step aside. Sometimes people were held back and could not go any further.
36621: Evert Willems did not pay much attention to what he said. One time the devil came to him and flung him over the trees. Evert has been converted since.
36622: A man said that he had walked on the water of the Sneekermeer.
36632: One night we were out hunting polecats. There was no wind outside, and yet we saw the branches of a willow thicket swaying hard back and forth.
36637: When magpies come into the farmyard, someone in the house will die. Magpies foretell death.
36643: Someone was murdered on the Godloassingel [godless men's lane]. It is still haunted there.
36647: The Stobbehoek is also called Teadehoekje because a man named Teade was murdered there long ago. People did not dare to pass by there because it was haunted.
36650: Long ago a woman is said to have haunted the area near the Dwarsfeart.
36651: When a dog howls eerily, someone in the neighbourhood will die within 4 days.
36652: In Drachten there lived a boy who was not quite right in the head and who had been bewitched by Binne Vogeltsje. The only way to cure him was through the sorcerer himself. He examined the boy's urine and then said that the boy had taken in a salamander and that this was why he could run so fast.
36655: Juke Spukguler was clairvoyant. Other people also saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, wandering lights). They were forerunners of bicycle lamps.
36656: In a black mirror a man could see whom he would later marry. If someone saw a coffin, it meant there would be a death in the family within a few days.
36657: Sometimes someone was pushed aside by a funeral procession that he could not see.
36658: Someone coming out of the pub drunk was sometimes beaten up for no reason.
36663: One night two men were walking to the Westerend. On the way they saw three cats sitting in a tree singing psalms. You could hear very clearly that they were singing Psalm 68.
36664: An old man haunts the Boppewei. There is said to be a lot of money in the ground, but as soon as you try to dig up the chest with a spade, it sinks deeper into the ground.
36666: Imke de Jong could work magic: he could make people stand still, make women's skirts slip down, and make soldiers appear from the hearth pit.
36667: Tovenaars (sorcerers, witches) can change themselves into cats. If such a cat gets a blow, the woman walks about with a sore arm or leg the next day.
36668: In the old days people saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, wandering lights) in places where the train would later pass. They had been omens of its lights.
36673: Piters Willemke was a sorcerer. He travelled at night on a broomstick and could turn himself into a black cat.
36674: Mother often told us that even before a tram ran on the Folgesterloane, people heard the sound a tram makes on the rails, and hooting as well.
36675: Long ago a woman drowned in the Jankedobbe, probably Janke. Later people now and then heard weeping and then saw a woman floating above the water.
36682: One evening Petrus saw a ghost in human form float and come down to the ground. He was so frightened that he ran away as fast as he could.
36690: On the Muzegroppewei a yellow foal runs about with a porridge pot around its neck and a porridge spoon with it. Whoever meets it at night must stir the pot with the spoon or eat a spoonful from it.
36694: One morning, when we were lying with the ship in Petersburch to load potatoes, my sister said she had very clearly seen in her dream that Jehannes Boom suddenly died. That simply couldn't be, since he was perfectly healthy. A little later a skipper came with the news that Jehannes Boom had died suddenly.
36698: One night Jan Tolsma came home late. From afar he saw a fire at his parents' house. He ran home as fast as he could, but there turned out to be no fire. Later, at Christmas, everything on that spot burned down.
36699: Before the canal at Beets existed, people already saw a ship with sails and a mast sailing straight across the land. Later the canal was dug there.
36703: Wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) were omens of the lights in the houses that would later be built there.
36705: A dog that roams about like a ghost is an omen of a death, just like the hooting of owls.
36706: Magpies in the farmyard mean that visitors are coming.
36713: In Boarnburgum lived a witch who could fly. She once also caught a polecat with her bare hands, but she had first quickly changed herself into a dog.
36724: A skipper always has to carry cows for a certain Sytsma. One time he dreams that he has to carry sheep instead, and the next day those sheep turn out to be on the ship.
36725: An old man haunted the Skilige Piip. Several people saw him there.
36732: When someone is sick at sea, sharks come swimming around the ship. They wait until that person is dead. Sharks are the harbingers of death.
36733: It is haunted at the Lange Sleatten. Once a daughter was alone on the ship. In the twilight she saw someone beckoning from the other side. She rowed over to ferry the man across, but as she came closer she saw that he had no feet: he was floating. She died of fright.
36735: A nightmare is a dream that later comes true.
36737: Father and a few others once heard wailing at night from the direction of the canal, but nothing had happened. Later, in winter, three people drowned there, two of them from one household. Someone had also seen it in his sleep the night before.
36738: My parents said they often heard hammering at night in places where houses were later built.
36740: My father was once fishing at night. He saw little lights moving along the canal for hours. The following summer people drowned there, and they were searched for with lanterns for a very long time.
36743: Riemer and Jehannes were out hunting polecats with their dogs one night. Suddenly they saw a gentleman on the other side of the canal, wearing a top hat and dressed in black. His eyes were like glowing egg-shaped coal briquettes. The dogs and the men were terrified and ran for their lives. That had been the devil.
36744: A father wanted to lift his 10-year-old son across the canal. The boy suddenly said he saw something: a donkey or a piebald horse with a man on it. The father saw nothing, but the dog ran home terrified. The boy then saw the apparition run into the fields, and never dared to go to that spot again.
36745: An old man could find no rest after his death. He had a treasure in the ground that he always rode to at night.
36748: Ael, Minne's wife, is a witch. When Minne came late to work, he explained that his wife was in bed with a headache, so he had to look after the children. His colleague said that did not surprise him, because the day before he had given a cat under his bed a hard blow on the head. Ael also bewitched my wife's brother to death. They say a witch must kill at least one person every seven years, or else he or she will die.
36753: A small group of boys stood by the canal. No one dared jump over it. Only the devil can do that, one of them said, and at once a little gentleman jumped over the canal. He left the print of a horse's hoof (a stallion's hoof) behind. It was the devil.
36755: Lytse Wyberen had been drinking. The evening before he had let slip that he would like to be thrown aside by the devil for once. That evening he was suddenly picked up and thrown down. He never repeated that wish.
36759: A boy swore quite often. One day his mother said that if he kept it up, the devil would appear by his bed. That night a man with a big shock of hair suddenly stood before his bed, his finger raised threateningly. The boy was terrified and never swore again.
36761: A lot of card playing went on at Durkje's. It was for money, and there was much noise and swearing. One day Durkje had to go out for a while. When she came back, the devil was sitting on the mantelpiece. He looked like a man dressed in leather.
36763: If a ghostly dog is roaming about, it is a sign that someone will die soon.
36776: In Aldegae the lord with the hoe, who had once lived in the castle, used to haunt the place.
36777: In Aldegae a foal used to run about with a porridge pot around its neck. People were afraid of it.
36778: One evening, when she was home alone, a fisherman's daughter heard someone calling to be ferried across. She went outside to help. Through the fog she saw only the top of the man, but when she came closer the man suddenly vanished. She was so frightened that she later died of it.
36780: Imke de Jong was a conjurer. He could make a rooster walk around with a beam (in its tail), apples came out of the back of his trousers, and he could make people stand still.
36784: A man once drove through Staphorst in his wagon with two horses. Church had just let out. He grabbed the horses by their tails and drove through the village shouting loudly. He raved so strangely that the horses were terrified. People scattered, shouting: there is the devil!
36792: Before the first church was built, people already heard psalms being sung on that spot.
36794: In Harkema wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) often floated over the heath. According to father they were omens of fine weather.
36795: A gentleman and a lady always used to haunt the area by the oak tree. The woman wore a cap on her head. They were the former landowners, keeping watch in this way.
36800: When a dog howls eerily, someone nearby will die soon. A cat washing itself with its paws foretells visitors. If the cat washes behind its ears, the visitors come from the neighbourhood.
36801: Wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) are the omens of the lights of the cars and bicycles that came later.
36804: My brother and I often used to go fishing in a little boat. But between the 11 and 12 o'clock trains at night there was often a black beast resembling a dog by the railway bridge. It had a long shaggy tail that dragged over the ground in an arc. We were afraid and waited until the ghost beast had disappeared.
36805: One night my cousin saw a man go up the stairs, stand by her bed, go back down the stairs and sit on the stove. It seemed like a dream, but it was not. The man was a ghost, someone who had died.
36808: When I was a boy, we got a new house. We went there by praam (flat-bottomed boat) at eleven o'clock to look, when the house was not yet finished. From afar we saw lights, but when we came closer there was no light to be seen. Those were omens.
36810: My father went long-jumping with friends. One of the boys said that even the devil couldn't jump as far as he could. Then by the bridge they saw a man step from one gravestone to the other. On one stone he left the print of a horse's hoof, on the other that of a human foot.
36816: When a dog howls eerily, it is an omen that someone nearby will die soon.
36817: At the bridge people heard cries for help while no one was there. Later a young man drowned on that spot, and the same cries for help were heard.
36819: When dogs howled eerily, someone would die. Dogs were afraid of funeral processions.
36820: The old Hear haunts the Boppewei. It is said that every year he comes one step closer to the treasure that lies in the ground there.
36822: Minne Ael was a witch. She could turn herself into a cat. She had even bewitched her daughter's child. Sometimes witches meet together after turning into cats. Then they sing psalms. A grey cat usually leads.
36825: Every seven years a sorcerer must bewitch someone to death, otherwise he will die himself.
36828: A neighbour saw lots of little lights: wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps). A road would later come there. At first there were only two houses, but many more were built there.
36829: A man was thrown off the path into the ditch. He went under water, but nobody saw who pushed him in.
36833: Magpies in a tree in the farmyard foretell visitors or news. Black jackdaws foretell death.
36834: When my father was run over by a truck, my mother had seen it coming: eight black rooks flew into the farmyard and kept coming back whenever she chased them away. A few days later father had the accident and was killed instantly.
36836:
If the thread with which a shroud was sewn is bitten off, all your teeth will later fall out.
The comb of the corpse must always go into the coffin. If someone combs himself with it, all his hair will fall out.
36843: My wife always had to get out of bed at 4 in the morning to let a labourer in. Once it was only 3 o'clock, but she clearly heard footsteps and the door handle. Yet there was no labourer to be seen. When she heard the same sound at 4 o'clock and got up again, it really was the labourer.
36846: Stammerige Harm [Harm the Stutterer] was not allowed near the cattle. He was possibly a sorcerer. He also had a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin).
36847: A sorcerer must bewitch someone to death at least every seven years, otherwise he will die himself.
36848: Witches can change themselves into cats. Sometimes they hold a cats' meeting. You can hear them singing psalms then. If someone beats a cat, the witch is cross-eyed the next day. Some witches fly on a broomstick. As protection some people put asafoetida (devil's dung) on the threshold. Others go to Wopke for a potion.
36849: At Christmas we always went with the family to the sugar factory. When another telegram came, my brother and I were sent out to tell a woman further along that the time had come. We walked there at dusk. We got bread and an apple as thanks for the message and walked back. Then I saw beet-gleaners with forks on their shoulders. One of them could float over the gates. On a path there were puddles I wanted my brother to jump over. But I could not take another step, because one of those men stood in front of me. Suddenly he was gone. I saw all these things, but my brother did not. When I got home I was as white as a sheet.
36852: If you looked into a black mirror, you got to see the woman you would later marry.
36853: On one side of the canal there is the print of a horse's hoof in the concrete, on the other side that of a human foot. That is where the devil jumped over the canal.
36857: Hearing psalm singing was a portent of the radio and television that came later.
36858: We once saw the house of Hindrik and Ael across the Swadde burning. There turned out to be no fire, but later that whole house burned down.
36863: Minne Ael could change herself into a cat. At her daughter's house cats were singing psalms. Her husband hit the cats with a post. The next morning the daughter lay sick in bed.
36865: Every seven years a witch must bewitch a child to death.
36869: In one house cards were played every day until late at night. Once Alberts Rinse was going home from there when he saw a big grey dog outside with eyes like coals. It accompanied him home and did not leave his side. He arrived home drenched in sweat. It had been the devil.
36870: A group of people went by boat to Groningen. Jan Petroalje was dead drunk and using foul language. Suddenly he stepped over the side of the boat and fell into the lake. It was night, and it was said he had been thrown overboard as punishment for his mockery. He was rescued, though, and recovered quite well.
36871: If you see a funeral procession, you must always step aside. That is why we were never allowed to walk in the middle of the road in the evening or at night when we were young. A person born with a caul always has to get up at night to see funeral processions, whether he wants to or not. Bontsje Keke sometimes had to go to the churchyard or some other place. He often had hardly any clothes on, so hastily did he have to get out of bed.
36872: It was said that Hanne Kramer could fly. When my father and others had to go to work in the polder with Hanne Kramer, he would tell them to go on ahead, because he still had to get dressed, wash and eat. But when the men arrived, Hanne was already there.
36873: Stammerige Harm [Harm the Stutterer] had received a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) from the devil. He was not allowed near the cattle, because then they would fall ill or die. Freemasons also always have money. When they are broke they simply hang their empty purse on the door handle, and the next morning it is full again.
36876: At night two girls with welts on their necks haunt the railway near Westereind. They were murdered there: their throats had been cut.
36877: A chest of money lies in the ground along the Boppeweg. In Uithuizen there was a haunted barn where nobody wanted to sleep.
36879: A dead person should not wear a shroud that was too long, because then he would trip at the resurrection. A shroud that was too short was not good either. In both cases the dead would find no rest and would start to haunt.
36882: Whoever looked into a black mirror saw his future wife in it. If he was not to marry, he saw a coffin.
36883: Harke and Gels could make marching soldiers appear from the hearth pit.
36886: A chest of money lies in the ground near the Skilige Piip. It belongs to a man who lived there. As long as that chest is there, the dead man gets no rest and always rides around there on a donkey at night.
36900: I used to often see lights over the fields by the farm. Those were wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps): portents of the cars that came later.
36901: A woman predicts that they will get a snow-white cow. Her husband thinks she is out of her mind, but not long after he comes home from the market with a cow in calf. It gives birth to a white calf. It was even in the newspaper, it was so white.
36902: My brother was poaching in an orchard at night with friends. They heard noises: beams being thrown, and mud, while no one was there. Later that spot was built on.
36904: One night Klaes Schuurman had seen a funeral procession with a white and a black horse in front. Soon afterwards he died, still young, but his own black horses would not pull the funeral procession. In the end the neighbour's horses were borrowed: a white and a black horse.
36905: Karste Iebeltsje was very devout. One evening she was walking across the heath in the dark when a strange beast started following her. She asked whether the beast came from the Lord or from Satan. If it came from the devil, it had to clear off. The beast disappeared.
36906: Iebeltsje warned me not to go out too often in the evening, because she had seen Hanne Akster flying over the haystacks.
36907: I saw in advance the spot where our dog would be buried. I saw snow, mud and the spade it was done with.
36911: Near Marrewijk there was a small wood where we were not allowed to go in the dark when we were young, because a foal with a porridge pot ran about there.
36912: Wytse told that he was once out walking when a big, piebald beast came running beside him. It was a plaagbeest (tormenting spectral beast), and it only went away when he took out some rye bread.
36913: We were always warned not to walk in the middle of the road at night. People told of those who ran ahead of a hearse in the middle of the road, tripped and were run over.
36924: People who talked foully and said they were not afraid of the devil were sometimes thrown by the devil.
36925: When a dog howls eerily, it usually means someone will die.
36931: Magpies in the farmyard mean news. Rooks and jackdaws foretell a death.
36934: With a jack of spades you could have a bottle of gin brought to you.
36935: When Wytse was sitting by the fire, soldiers came marching up. Then they disappeared again.
36950: Mother had once seen two lights across the heath between two places. Later the tram ran there.
36951: Mother could see funerals in advance. So it was with our old neighbour, whose funeral procession she had already seen two weeks earlier.
36952: The Janke-dobbe is so named because Janke drowned there. She still haunts the place.
36953: Near the hamlet of Topwear people saw little lights in the evening. Later a house was built on that spot.
36954: A headless horse is said to haunt the farm of Klaes Simensdaem.
36955: When a dog howls eerily, it means a death.
36956: If magpies chatter in front of the house, visitors are coming; if they chatter behind the house, it means a death.
36959: A witch can change herself into a black cat. If you throw a piece of wood at such a cat, the witch walks about with a cloth around her head the next day.
36960: One day a girl got a suitor who looked respectable and was pleasant to talk to. The girl was Catholic and made the sign of the cross before eating. Suddenly there was a stench of sulphur and the man disappeared up the chimney. It had been the devil.
36961: A wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin) always returns to its owner. You get it from the devil.
36963: When I was a child an old woman with a strange look in her eyes lived nearby. She was a witch. I was never allowed to eat food from her. If I came home with a currant bun, I had to hang it in a kettle in the attic. A frog or a snake would then come out of it.
36964: Marten de Vries had a child that was bewitched. The neighbours' cat often sat in his pigsty. It was said that the cat could change into a human. One day Marten, who was a hunter, shot at the cat so that the animal was lamed. The next day the neighbour woman was lame.
36965: Mindert Slof [Tuinstra] was picking heather with his wife and son. It was foggy and they saw something floating over the heath. The father asked his son whether it floated or shuffled. When the son said it floated, they took to their heels.
36966: People saw little lights floating over the field and carriages driving. Those were the portents of the tram that began running there in 1912.
36967: Many people had seen a house on fire in advance that later burned down.
36968: Long ago Janke drowned in the Janke-dobbe (Janke's pond). Some had already predicted that someone would drown there.
36969: Before the Reformed church stood there, people had already heard psalm singing.
36971: In her sleep Mrs de Graaf saw details of the murder of Jan Modderman, 70 years ago. The murderer took the money to a small field and buried it there. The police went there and found the hole, but not the loot.
36972: A boatswain of a steamboat carrying pleasure-trippers went overboard. He called for help, but nobody heard him and he drowned. His cries for help had already been foretold by people.
36973: By the Marrewijk wood, near a big hollow willow, a foal with a porridge pot around its neck used to haunt. Nobody dared to pass there.
36975: I used to go polecat hunting at night sometimes. Then a big grey dog would come running beside me.
36980: Close to us was a farm where the horse always came loose by itself. That was the work of Sierde Jets, a witch. The horse was actually a nightmare, and as protection people placed their slippers upside down in front of the bed.
36983: A woman told the Reformed minister that the previous evening she had had the devil in her wheelbarrow. The minister said he would have tipped him out, but the woman said the wheelbarrow had been far too heavy.
36985: We were never allowed to run in the middle of the road, because then you might be pushed aside by a funeral procession.
36986: At night lawyers haunt the Advocatenlandje.
36987: By the bridge over the Boarn three of the French soldiers who were killed with pitchforks by the farmers back then still haunt the place.
37000: Some witches have dolls that they prick with pins.
37001: Ymke liked to crawl through a beam at the market. One day someone told him that he was not crawling through it but past it.
37003: Some people sometimes sent out a jack of spades to fetch gin. A little later the bottle would float above the table. The one who had summoned the bottle was not allowed to touch it.
37012: Father liked a drink and often came home drunk. Mother and I would wait up for him. Once we were waiting and heard the sound of the loose attic ladder falling over. Father only arrived a quarter of an hour later; he bumped into the ladder and then we heard exactly the same sound.
37013: Ruerd, the brother of the painter Jan Planting, was a bit peculiar. Once he stood gazing into the distance. Asked what he saw, he answered that he saw a fire. The next day a house burned down there.
37014: A man once said he had had a strange dream: a child had fallen into the water and then drowned together with the father who had tried to save it. The next day I heard that my son-in-law and his child had both drowned.
37015: Tabe said he had seen the death of his child days in advance: he had seen the coffin standing on the chair and foreseen all sorts of other details of the funeral.
37017: After Teade was murdered, he haunted the so-called Teadehoekje for a long time.
37027: A man always predicted that one day he would go suddenly. Once he gave the cows two buckets of water, and as he stepped back he said: there's the trouble already, and dropped dead.
37086: Tsjerk always told stories about haunting. One evening he had to go through a gate. There he saw a little old woman. He asked who should go first: he or she. At that moment the little woman vanished as if she had never been there. It was a ghostly apparition.
37087: When the church bells ring clearly, it means someone will soon be added to the churchyard.
37088: Sytse Wijma often had to get out of bed at night to watch funeral processions. He saw them best in the middle of the road. It always meant that someone would die soon.
37089: Hindrik once saw a lamp burning with faces around it. But when he came closer, there was nothing to be seen.
37095: With the jack of clubs you can have a bottle of gin brought to you.
37097: A sheet haunts the place, belonging to a man who was not given a shroud in his grave.
37098: Black rooks around the house foretell death. Magpies in the farmyard mean a visit from people who rarely come. A dog that howls eerily foretells a death. A bell that rings foretells a death. The same goes for a painting falling off the wall, a weight falling off a clock, or death knocks in wood. When someone died, a cloth was hung over the mirror and the clock was stopped. The flowers were taken away from the windows.
37099: In Harkema people saw lights that were not there. They were the portents of the bicycles.
37100: In the evenings Boele sometimes secretly took his cow to the breeding bull to save on the stud fee. One evening, after it had worked, he could not get his cow through the gate. He began to curse and rage. At that moment there was a flash of lightning that smashed the gate to pieces as punishment for Boele.
37101: Once people heard cries for help in the Leeuwepoel. Later someone drowned there.
37102: Some people had to get out of bed at night to see funeral processions. You should never run in the middle of the road at night.
37104: A carpenter who sometimes said the grace backwards and was not afraid of the devil had to walk home one evening. A dog kept running along with him. When he wanted to cross a plank, the dog blocked his way. The man put down his toolbox and shouted that he was not afraid, but then he was lifted up and flung away. He landed on his knees on the plank and was lame for the rest of his life.
37119: Father sometimes saw funeral processions. Later a real funeral would follow.
37120: At a certain spot a horse drowned with a bucket around its neck. A headless horse is also said to haunt somewhere. Perhaps the same one?
37134: In Oudega a foal runs about at night with a porridge pot around its neck.
37135: Ymke de Jong was untameable and untouchable. If he was locked up or put in chains, he simply came free again. He could make people stand stock-still. He could tame the wildest horses and they followed him of their own accord; he needed no rope for that.
37140: My uncle once felt a gust of wind pass him at the spot where a tram would later come.
37143: Woodworms, howling dogs and chattering magpies announce a death.
37144: Someone was walking in the middle of the road in the evening. His mate suddenly said they had to walk on the verge. At that moment, he said, a funeral procession was passing.
37150: Ymke could make people stand rigid.
37151: In a tent at the market there was a black mirror. If you saw a portrait in it, it was of your future spouse; if you saw a coffin, you would stay single.
37153: Things were getting rowdy in an inn when suddenly the door opened by itself and a big black dog came in. It walked once around the table and disappeared again. Afterwards everyone was dead silent, for that must have been the devil.
37158: We were telling each other stories in a dry ditch when we suddenly heard hammering very clearly. Then it stopped. Later the Reformed church was built on that spot.
37163: A boy once came running hard: did you see that wagon without horses? It was a portent of the trains.
37164: Albertsje Brjit was clairvoyant and could see into the future.
37194: At the spot where a woman later drowned, people had earlier heard cries for help.
37196: The same fellow once predicted a fire, which happened six weeks later when lightning struck.
37197: My wife is disabled and can see funerals in advance. She also says that you should never walk in the middle of the road at night.
37201: A labourer who was murdered long ago still haunts the area.
37208: Witches must kill someone once every seven years, or else they die themselves. They can change themselves into a black cat. If you give such a cat a wallop, the witch walks with a limp the next day. If you fry a wreath in the pan, the witch has a burned face the next day.
37209: Wyberen was a scoffer, a gambler and a drunkard. Once when he came out of the pub at night, he was thrown to the other side of the road: that was the devil's work. Wyberen had been terrified.
37211: Some had heard the sounds of the train beforehand; some had also seen the lights beforehand.
37213: A skipper once saw a strange cat on the gangplank. He kicked it, and the next day an old woman walked about with a bruise on her cheek.
37214: A beurtschipper (skipper of a scheduled barge service) heard a cat wailing and shot the animal dead. The witch then turned out to be dead as well.
37217: Eabele predicted that Veenwouden would become a suburb of Leeuwarden. He also heard a bell ringing, which foretold the later station bell.
37219: Jehannes could make the cheeses in his cart dance. He could also make people stand stock still. Women were always afraid he would make their skirts drop. He could also make soldiers march out of the hearth pit.
37220: A dog howling eerily foretold a death.
37224: A swearer and scoffer was once lifted up and thrown over trees. That was the devil settling accounts with him.
37229: A child that was murdered by drowning has haunted that spot ever since. A resident of a house where the child haunted moved away for that reason.
37230: On the spot where the Reformed church now stands, people heard psalm singing even before that time.
37235: A man once saw a woman in white approaching. Because he thought he knew her, he wanted to greet her, but when he came closer she went up in smoke.
37238: Close to home a man meets a little black goat. He does not trust it and hurries home. When his wife goes to look, she hears a loud bang.
37239: A man who had drunk too much is found dead the next morning, standing up to his waist in the water. His neckerchief is hanging in a hawthorn. It is clear there has been a struggle. It must have been the evil one, who also threw him into the water.
37241: A violinist who played at dances was picked up at night and thrown over the trees. It was said to be the devil's punishment, because dancing is sinful. After this the man did not go home until the next morning.
37242: At night you should not walk in the middle of the road, because then you can be pushed aside by a phantom funeral procession.
37249: A man could make little soldiers march out of the hearth.
37315: The wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) that were seen were said to mean the lights of the houses built later.
37316: On their way, some boys had come across a wheelbarrow that moved towards them by itself. The little man sitting on it was the devil, who cursed and swore.
37318: A magpie by the front door means a death. Because of its white and black colours, a magpie looks like a mourning letter. A magpie brings mourning.
37327: One evening a man thought he recognised his niece in a woman coming towards him. However, he was lifted up and thrown away, after which the woman floated off.
37328: A man saw phantom funeral processions, and not long afterwards there were real funeral processions.
37329: Before a woman died, the vases had fallen off the cupboard.
37330: A man could make soldiers come out of the hearth and march.
37333: One evening we had to move to the side because father-in-law saw a funeral procession.
37335: There was always something going on at night on the singel. A dead person haunted it. When they removed the tall trees, a skeleton came to light.
37345: A dead man who could find no rest wandered about near the railway.
37347: Maei once gave someone an apple; when he wanted to eat it, the apple turned into a toad.
37348: Harm went to the shed outside because his wife thought something was going on. There he saw seven cats with big eyes. He fired his gun and hit one in the leg. The next day Sjoerde Lamke had been in bed with an injury, and since then she walked with a limp.
37349: Uncle Jan had an experience with a black witch's cat. He wounded the cat's leg with a pitchfork. Afterwards Old Griet was always lame.
37365: Before the train was there, people had already heard it puffing.
37371: A carpenter could make people stand still.
37372: A Belgian refugee knew all kinds of tricks. He could make people sit still. And when he put his hands on the table, nobody could move them.
37374: A farmhand takes a run-up and jumps over the ditch, boasting that the devil couldn't match him. The next morning the print of a stallion's hoof is clearly visible at the same spot: the devil evidently did jump after him.
37376: If someone married and it went badly, people said he had looked into the black mirror. The black mirror meant misfortune.
37378: A werewolf wants to have everything. One of seven brothers is a werewolf. A werewolf must always have something to tear apart.
37380: In the past, when building a church, they used a cow hide as a foundation when the ground was soft.
37446: Between Dokkum and Anjum people saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) as portents of the train.
37449: From afar people see a house on fire, but at the house nothing is wrong. A few days later the house burns down.
37460: The ghost of a headless soldier, rattling his bayonet, who was murdered in a wood.
37462: A witch sometimes turns herself into a black cat. Flying through the air on a broomstick. Within seven years a witch must have bewitched someone to death, or else she dies herself.
37464: A ghostly howling dog means a death. Black rooks near the house mean a death and are portents of mourning.
37522: The lights that floated above the road were the portents of the carbide lamps on bicycles that came later.
37523: At a farm, a strange cry of fear was heard coming from the barn one evening. There turned out to be nothing to see. The next morning they heard the same cry again. It was the farmhand, who had fallen from the loft. The first cry had been a portent.
37526: At night, the sound of carpentry was often heard at a spot where a house was later built.
37527: In a family there was a sick child who had been bewitched. The father went across the ice to the duivelbanner (exorcist) to fetch a potion. On the way back the little bottle was almost broken by a hare. At home he saw a large black cat. He threw a stone at the cat, and later Durkje had a mark on her head. She was no longer allowed in the house, and soon afterwards the child recovered.
37529: Witches fly through the air on their broomsticks.
37534: Sometimes people are thrown aside at night by a funeral procession they cannot see. Others see funeral processions in advance.
37572:
The grandparents are already in bed when uncle comes home and says there is a fire nearby. The grandparents see nothing, but uncle says many people are standing watching. As uncle goes towards the house, at first he sees the fire very clearly. When he reached the house it was not on fire at all.
About a year later the house burned down.
37573:
A man was born with a caul and foresaw funeral processions. Once he again saw a phantom funeral procession in which, along the way, one of the traces of the harness of the horses before the hearse broke. He told others about it.
A few days later a well-known person from De Pein died. When he was taken to the churchyard, the traces of one of the horses broke.
37574: Mother had a sister who had died young, and she could not forget it. One evening, as they lay in bed, she told her husband that she wanted to see her sister once more. The husband did not agree. A little later the sister stood by the bed and said they need not worry. The husband saw and heard everything, and said he never wanted to go through this again. Now the wife agreed with him. They never saw the sister again.
37575: It was said that some people already heard organ music at the place where the church was later built.
37576: In the old days people always said never to walk in the middle of the road at night, because then you might run into a phantom funeral procession.
37577: A coarse, uncouth man shouts in the pub that he is not afraid of the devil. That evening on his way home he is attacked by a black beast.
37578: At night one can sometimes see the white apparition of a murdered woman.
37605: A woman meets a big black dog one evening that jumps up at her, puts its paws on her shoulders and asks how she knew the dog.
37606: One evening a man heard a lot of strange noise, and a farmhouse was later built on that very spot.
37608: An old woman sometimes saw funeral processions when she got out of bed at night.
37610: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck walks about near the Hoogzand.
37613: In Oostermeer lives a sorceress who turns herself into a cat from time to time. Once, in her cat form, she was hit by a stone, which left her lame.
37622: In the old days you saw wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) everywhere; later people said these had been portents of bicycle lights.
37641: In the old days, people saw lights in the evening of those who were yet to come.
37642: A man says that in the old days, when he heard carpentry at night, he called it voorloop (an apparition foreshadowing an event), because a house would later stand there.
37643: In the vliet, the water, she heard someone cry 'help!'; later someone drowned there who had cried for help.
37647: In the old days lights were seen; later people said these were the portents of bicycle lamps and car lights.
37648: A man had the gift of seeing funeral processions. When he saw one, a death would follow in the near future.
37649: Bontsje Keke was born with a caul, and because of this he sometimes saw funeral processions. He walked straight through ditches and gates; gates opened for him by themselves. He also saw his daughter's funeral in advance.
37650: A funeral procession must have a path, otherwise one is made. Escaping or avoiding it is impossible; everything that stands, walks or sits in the way is driven aside.
37652: Some people who mock God or the devil get knocked down. It matters what is said.
37656: In the evenings the devil always walked along a little driveway in Opperkoaten. In the verge where he jumped away, marks of his hoof can still be seen.
37657: In Twijzel a foal walks about with a porridge pot around its neck.
37659: Stammerige Harm (Stuttering Harm) was considered a sorcerer; above all he bewitched cattle. He owned a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin), devil's money. He was not trusted around the cattle.
37660: Bontsje Keke must never be late when he received word of a hearse, otherwise he himself would die.
37662: In Opperkoaten lived a man who could make people stand still.
37665: In Groningen there were haunted barns; at night you could not go inside, because you would simply be thrown aside. Farm wagons started moving on their own and the church bell began ringing by itself.
37666: With the jack of spades some people could have a bottle of liquor brought to them.
37668: At the fair they had black mirrors; that was a kind of fortune telling. The future could also be foretold with them. As many white spots as you have on your nails, that many children you will have later.
37670: Freemasons are bulletproof. They have a pact with the devil, who buys them for a sum of money. After the purchase the money was thrown down the chimney. The contract is signed in blood, which is why it is impossible to leave the freemasons. The freemasons also own a wisseldaalder (ever-returning coin); nothing is impossible with that coin. They are also always rebuilding their houses, which are never finished. When a freemason dies, the devil comes to fetch him.
37680: One evening Thomas Bruining saw a deceased acquaintance standing by the driveway gate and became so frightened that he burst into someone else's house to ask if they would come and look with him. When they reached the gate, they saw nothing.
37682: Klaas Tyssens's barn is haunted; the farmhands cannot sleep there at night because there is always noise. Albert Scholte, however, was a farmhand there for three years and was not easily frightened. He too had to deal with the noise, but said, 'You can stop, I'm not getting out of bed anyway.'
37683: An old resident saw, very long ago, long before the tramline came, a wilde lantaarn (wild lantern, will-o'-the-wisp) flying over the road. That lantern went all through the neighbourhood, where the tram later came.
37685: One evening, near her house, Mr Pultrum's wife heard the thud of a load of wood, just as if it were thrown off a wagon. Later a new house stood there, which they came to live in.
37686: A woman could see what would happen from the vapour of a paraffin lamp. She could also read coffee grounds. Once she said to her sons: 'There are two policemen in the cup, they are going to come here to fetch you. You must have been up to something again.'
37687: People tell that they had voorloop (an apparition foreshadowing an event) in the form of the doorbell ringing. Nobody was at the door then, but a little later somebody was.
37691: Jan Hellinga's sister never likes to go shopping on Saturday evenings, because she always sees someone in a raincoat whom she fears. One evening Jan goes with her, armed with a sickle. He sees the apparition in the raincoat and greets it. There is no answer. He greets it again, and again hears nothing. 'You have legs, and if you don't answer, I'll cut your head off!' When there was again no answer, Jan swung the sickle, but it went straight through the apparition. Then the apparition was suddenly gone.
37701: The wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) that used to be seen above Boelenslaan were the portents of the later aeroplanes.
37703: A boy walking home from his girlfriend one evening was suddenly thrown into the ditch near Bethlehemsreed. The devil had done it, he said.
37704: At night you should not walk in the middle of the road, because you may well be pushed aside by a funeral procession.
37705: Boardzer Bruining had voorloop (apparitions foreshadowing an event) in the form of visions. He would see funeral processions. Once he was asleep in the evening but woke up and had to get out of bed; he was compelled. He stood at the window and saw there the funeral of an old man. That same old man was in good health but died a few days later, and Boardzer saw in broad daylight the same funeral he had seen a few days earlier in the evening.
37711: The narrator was warned by his parents when he was young never to walk in the middle of the road at night but always at the side, otherwise a funeral procession would push him aside.
37712: When a dog howled, a death was coming; that is what people used to believe.
37713: There were people who saw a house burn down beforehand, and a little later this really happened.
37714: Sixty years ago some people saw a big black dog simply walk through the wall.
37718: A witch can turn herself into a cat. If you strike such a cat, the witch is wounded the next day. There were also witches who had little dolls that they stuck pins into; the people they had bewitched then felt pain.
37719: In Zwaagwesteinde there lived a sorceress who could fly.
37721: Freemasons have sold their souls to the devil; they are never short of money. They are also always rebuilding their houses, which are never finished.
37722: Wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) were seen as portents of bicycle lamps.
37724: In Zwaagwesteinde some people sometimes see two naked girls floating above the railway bridge. These are said to be the ghosts of two murdered girls.
37725: When playing cards, some sent the jack of clubs to fetch a bottle of liquor. The story went that the devil brought the bottle.
37731: One evening a man saw a vague figure that he took for an acquaintance; when he tried to come closer it was gone. Two weeks later the wife of that same acquaintance died.
37734: On a piece of meadow, the narrator had a strong premonition that something would come to that very spot. Later a high-voltage line was put up on that same spot.
37735: It was haunted near Lemmer; once a white figure appeared by the water and quickly vanished again.
37736: A man said that one evening he heard the sound of high heels. When he looked up, a woman stood beside him and asked him how to walk to Leeuwarden. He told her which way to go and wanted to watch her leave. She could no longer be seen, as if she had vanished into the ground.
37737: A mother and daughter were out together when suddenly they saw a ghostly couple approaching. This couple did not walk but floated. Suddenly a gust of wind blew out their storm lantern, and the ghostly couple was gone.
37745: A girl told her father that men in black were coming and pushing a coffin through the window. The father saw nothing. Later someone died in that house. The coffin would not go through the door and had to be brought in through the window.
37746: Ghost lanterns or wilde lantaarns (wild lanterns, will-o'-the-wisps) were the forerunners of car lights.
37747: The narrator's mother once saw a night-mare. It was a living creature about 15 cm tall; it was black, smooth and cold and had two glowing eyes. It came right through the porthole.

37854: Some people could have a bottle of liquor brought to them with the jack of spades.

37859:
As children we were afraid of witches, who we knew could turn themselves into black cats. That a black cat was once hit by a thrown clog was a miracle. Only a silver bullet could hit a black cat. The next day an old woman was lame.

37860: Mother was afraid the children would accept something from a witch and eat it. The children would then be bewitched.
37866: There are people who saw the lights of the tram and heard the track beforehand.

37878: The Foksegatten was haunted. Near the high mound there, things were not right.

37931: Some people should not go near the cattle, because they can make the cattle sick.
37935: Some people could have a bottle of liquor brought to them with a playing card.
37936: In a stall at the market one could look into a black mirror. One then found out whom one would marry.
37953: Mother often heard hammering at night at a carpenter's. She said someone would soon die, because he was then making a coffin. It always came true.

37963: A man was not stopped from coming in by a locked door.
37964: Brother told his little sister to keep her mouth shut when they passed the house of an old woman who could work magic.
37966: At the Godless toll gate a horse haunts; at the Godless lane an old man haunts.
37969: Some people can have a bottle of liquor brought to them with the jack of clubs.
37975: One evening a woman seemed compelled to go outside. There she saw a house that seemed to be on fire. A few days later the house really was on fire.
37984: The Spooklaantje in Boelenslaan was always haunted.

38005: The illegitimate child of a witch's daughter falls ill and dies when it comes into the house of the witch, its grandmother.

38012: A foal always haunted a road at night.

38015: Witches change into cats in a meadow and discuss what they are going to do.
38019: A man who had played cards on Sunday was suddenly thrown some distance on his way home.

38022: His son was accused of the same. One night he had been mistreated by the devil.
38036: In the middle of a bridge a foal with a porridge pot haunted.

38046: A witch sometimes changed into a black cat.
38050: A man conjured soldiers out of the hearth pit.

38055: Hammering can be heard near a bridge, but nothing is ever seen. Not long afterwards the bridge is demolished.
38057: People see a house burn down in advance.

38060: A foal walking about with a porridge pot around its neck.

38093: A man who had been raging in the pub was lifted up and thrown away by the evil one on his way home.

38103: A wizard makes a horse that strangely can no longer pull a full wagon walk again.
38105: At night, Father heard an iron going over a tailor's suits. It meant the tailor would get orders again.
38106: A number of people had heard cries for help from a pond. It was supposed to mean that someone would drown.
38116: From a group of men coming out of a pub, the devil just lifted one up and hurled him into the canal.
38121: In a black mirror at the market the image of the future wife can be seen.
38127: A man sees at night a fireball full of fire. He believes something will happen to him. He is right, for that same day his house burns down.

38132: A chest of money sinks deeper and deeper whenever people try to dig it up.
38138: Looking into a black mirror revealed the future.
38156: One evening a woman meets a large black dog with glowing eyes, which walks with her until she reaches her house.
38158: At night the narrator hears a ladder being set against the wall. The next day the neighbours return the borrowed ladder to the spot where she heard it.

38172: Shortly before a railway line is built, the sound of a passing train is heard.

38201: A woman hears beforehand how a nephew falls into the water and drowns.
38203: A woman meets a large black dog in the evening.
38206: Do not walk in the middle of the road at night; you can then be pushed aside by a phantom funeral procession.

38235: A witch can change herself into a black cat. Sometimes several black cats hold a meeting.

38259: A man fixes a horse to the spot, and then lets the horse go.
38260: A man fixes a horse to the spot when he is not allowed to ride along.

38263: A man can come in even though the door is locked and barricaded.
38267: A man foresees a road and a bridge.
38268: A man predicts that he will die of a spot on his nose. He does indeed die of cancer of the nose.

38278: A woman can turn herself into a cat. One evening the cat is kicked, and the next day the woman has a wound on her head.

38283: Hauntings by a woman in white.
38284: Haunting by a foal with a porridge pot.

38289: A man who plays cards and swears is seized by the devil on his way home. After that he never swore again.

38310: A dog howling eerily means a death in the family.

38318: Witches sometimes left their belly behind in bed.

38331: A woman sees beforehand that the farmer she works for is murdered.
38332: A dog howls eerily on seeing a funeral procession. Shortly afterwards a man dies.

38404: A girl is suddenly picked up and flung away, landing in a ditch. The devil did it.

38459: A few days before someone dies, a boy sees a man in black standing in front of the house.

38461: A man sees beforehand that his daughter drowns.
38462: Do not walk in the middle of the road at night, so as not to be pushed aside.
