130910: Witch's neighbour is bewitched, as shown by a wreath in the pillow; sees two little dolls standing on the windowsill.
130911: A man born with a caul dies a few days after a dog has sat howling by his house.
130913: A man born with a caul sees the funeral procession of his own funeral.
130919: A schoolmaster believes that a sound like planks being thrown about is an omen of later building. It turns out pigs are the cause, but the schoolmaster holds on to witchcraft.
130925: At a place where it was said blood would flow and hammering was heard, a slaughterhouse has been built.
130929: On the spot where a stable has been built, the sound of hammering was heard beforehand.
130931: Witch bewitches pigs and churn, after which a duivelbanner (exorcist) is fetched. Witch makes dogs stand still; according to the duivelbanner, the first person they meet is the culprit. Duivelbanner gives something against bewitchment. On the way back nothing happens.
130932: A man bewitched by a witch shoots at cats with a silver bullet. One of the cats hit is the witch, who is wounded.
130941: At a place where a murder was committed, a big black dog roams, wearing a collar with an illegible inscription.
130942: Conjuring rooks out of the hearth pit.
130944: Fright of a witch; a duivelbanner (exorcist) has a heksenkrans (witch's wreath, a knot of feathers found in a pillow) burned in a room with darkened windows, whereupon the witch turns into a cat that prowls around the house.
130945: In the evening a large black dog walks along and suddenly vanishes.
130946: A black cat that walks along with someone is a witch.
130948: A man whose hair is pulled in his sleep believes he is being pursued by the devil.
130952: Girls haunt at night the place where they were murdered.
130953: After a lady asks whether the children are picking blackberries, she has disappeared.
130954: After hearing a voice say that it is dark while no one is to be seen, a farmhand takes a lantern with him when he goes to the fields early in the morning.
130955: Sighting of a young lady walking between the tram rails.
130956: Boys see someone pass by; a person coming from the other direction has seen no one.
130957: A figure is not struck, because it might be a ghost.
130958: A witch poisons chickens and a dog; children are not allowed to shake her hand or accept an apple from her.
130959: After a girl tells her suitor that they must part, a horrible thing is sitting next to him.
130962: Witch stabs a doll to make the person she wants dead die.
130963: A warning to keep a path clear in the middle of the barn at night. Someone who sleeps there is picked up and thrown down further on.
130970: Despite their fear of bewitchment, children do not dare refuse a cup of coffee from a witch, but nothing happens.
130971: A witch says she went to a wine cellar in Spain during the night. An apple she gives a child is put away, and it has vanished when a lizard is found.
130972: A death occurs in the direction in which the head of a ghost-howling dog points.
130973: A chattering magpie is a good omen, a silent magpie brings misfortune.
130974: A bird tapping on the window is a sign of a letter coming.
130981: A man who mocks the devil is lifted up and flung back and forth.
130982: People are afraid of haunting in the churchyard. Bells that ring wrongly are a voorloop (an apparition foreshadowing an event) of death.
130989: A black cat is often seen as a witch.
130990: A man uses a deck of cards to conjure little soldiers out of the hearth pit.
130991: Sighting of a ghost animal with hair reaching the ground.
130992: A few days before his wife's death, a man sees a funeral procession coming from the farmyard.
130996: A wizard uses a stick to make people walk or stand still.
130998: Forbidding the eating of sugar bread from a witch.
131000: Witches who can turn themselves into dogs and cats. Someone shoots at a black cat; the next day a witch is missing an eye.
131002: A man who drinks too much talks about a little black goat that often accompanies him. Once the goat picks him up and throws him into the ditch; the goat has left a mark on his coat.
131003: A warning not to walk in the middle of the road, so as not to have to walk over a funeral procession.
131004: Phantom animal in front of the wheel prevents going on; it has vanished when someone looks, but when they go on, it is there again.
131008: At eleven o'clock at night a calf stands in the road and will not move aside for anyone. When a man jabs at the animal with a stick, it is suddenly a dog.
131009: A cat that has been shot is not dead; the next day a witch has a head wound.
131010: Sorcerers make a bottle of liquor or little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
131014: Horses are spooked by black cats; the farmer gets scared and flees.
131016: At night someone in the street is picked up and lifted over a hearse.
131017: Before someone dies in a house, a woman sees a coffin being carried out of that house and who walks in the procession.
131019: At the house of a man who swears sits a dog that will not be chased away; instead it grabs the man's stick and shakes him back and forth.
131021: After a man names the witches and threatens to shoot them dead, the black cats stay away.
131022: A wonder doctor gives a little bottle of potion for a bewitched child, with the instruction that no one may see the bottle, especially not black cats.
131023: In the evening girls in the street are picked up and set down across the ditch. They see no funeral procession, but they do hear cloths flapping.
131024: In the evening a drunken man is seen hanging over a gate, and he has vanished when a man goes to look.
131026: A woman is fixed to the spot and released from the spell by a wizard.
131033: The duivelbanner (exorcist) says of a bewitched child that it is getting too much milk and that a toad must be beaten. The toad's leg is broken by the blows, and the next morning the woman from whom the milk is fetched turns out to have a broken leg.
131035: A devil banisher gives a bewitched man a little bottle of potion, warning him to keep it hidden, especially from cats. At home the man is attacked by a cat.
131036: Seeing a funeral procession; a man's prediction that it concerns his daughter comes true.
131037: Little lights that floated through the air are later seen as an omen of bicycle lamps.
131038: A man who has seen a coffin standing in the bedroom no longer wants to live in the house and leaves his wife. Shortly after he has gone back to his wife, he dies.
131039: A murdered noblewoman haunts the area; a man thinks there is nothing to it. When at midnight at the scene of the murder he asks the woman to appear, she comes forth and accompanies him.
131044: By calling on God, men can pass a spinning woman by the roadside.
131045: A large black dog walks along in the evening and cannot be touched.
131048: A man sings and makes little soldiers march out of the hearth pit.
131050: A man who has seen a funeral procession at night predicts it will be a large funeral, and this comes true.
131051: Nightmare when sleeping in fresh hay: a cat then walks over the person, who becomes short of breath and cannot make a sound.
131053: The sound of a screaming child from a pool is a voorloop (an apparition foreshadowing an event) that someone will drown.
131054: Seeing a witch flying through the air on her hoop skirt.
131062:
Potatoes that will not grow are bewitched.
For a sick child, a devil-banisher advises boiling a darning needle in water, after which the witch comes. A wreath is found in the pillow.
131063: Mother advises walking at the side of the road; she sees a funeral procession the evening before someone dies.
131066: A magpie is a voorloop (an apparition foreshadowing an event) of a death.
131070: At the place where a woman was murdered she comes out of the ground, floats over the land and disappears.
131071: A calf runs in front of a horse and cart, is thrown into the ditch, pops up again and is thrown into the ditch once more.
131073: A son who sees a coffin standing in front of the door fears that his sick mother will die. She says she will live another five years. After five years she dies, and the coffin stands in front of the house with the pall blowing up, as seen before.
131074: A witch flies through the air on a broomstick.
131077: In the evening, men in the street are flung aside by something.
131078: Sometimes little soldiers come marching out of the hearth pit when someone does not believe in witchcraft.
131079: A man sees a coffin being brought to a house; later someone in that house dies.
131081: A woman gets up at night to see a funeral procession; her husband notices nothing.
131082: As punishment, a wizard fixes a boy to the spot and later releases him.
131084: During evening visits people talk about ghosts, witches, a devil banisher who gives a potion for a sick person and advises keeping a close eye on the bottle, and a witch's cat in the house.
131086: A man sees a funeral procession; very soon afterwards someone dies. The funeral goes as he saw it.
131087: Encounter with a woman in a white cap who suddenly disappears.
131088: A man tells a woman that her husband will come home dead, because he has seen his funeral procession. The funeral goes as foretold.
131089: After a polecat hunt there is a ghost: a woman sits spinning, the dogs are afraid, and the dead polecat in the sack is alive again and sits on someone's shoulder.
131090: The evil one accompanies a drinker and curser home, gives him a spoon and fork to eat with, and sits on top of him all night.
131095: A drunken devil banisher counts out money to pay the devil with.
131098: A hare that was shot at must have been a witch, because it suddenly vanished and there are no tracks.
131099: Footsteps in the attic are thought to be a witch's, but turn out to be a polecat.
131100: Many people who drink coffee at a witch's house fall ill. She can turn herself into all sorts of things, including a black cat with fiery eyes.
131102: A person born with a caul sees ghosts everywhere.
131104: Fleeing from something that floats through the air.
131107: Witches float through the air with swirling skirts.
131109: The father of a sick child hits a hare, but it escapes. The father accuses a woman with a head wound of witchcraft and wants her to cure the child. The witch strokes the child with her hand and says it is cured.
131111: A witch uses magic wands to make little soldiers come out of the hearth pit.
131112: A witch sews a toad into the hem of her skirt to ward off misfortune that other witches could bring upon her.
131113: Magpies by the house bring messages, or if two magpies chatter, someone is bewitched.
131114: The top of the lamp wick burning is a sign that a witch is coming.
131117: Farmhands do not stay long with a farmer because of noise in the cowshed at night, but one farmhand is not bothered by it.
131118: If the reed of a loom is not loosened, the loom often makes noise at night.
131122: Warning to step aside for a funeral procession.
131127: A churn that is set up in the evening makes the churning mill turn at night without a horse.
131128: At a child's funeral people enter through the churning house, just as someone had seen beforehand.
131130: A cat that walks around near a couple about to marry turns out to have been a witch.
131131: A man hits a hare, which escapes nonetheless. Immediately a woman with a wounded face comes outside.
131132: A man sees a woman floating through the air in the evening. The next morning a woman tells him that he was out late.
131136: A man has to get up at night to see a funeral, the course of which he can later describe. He warns not to walk in the middle of the road at night between twelve and one, because then you can be pushed aside.

131149: White ghosts seen in the churchyard at night turn out to be white greyhounds.
131150: A white ghost that floats over a gate into the field at night turns out to be a sheep.
131151: Out of fear of hauntings, a boy is afraid to close the shutters in the evening.
131152: A cock crowing and a dog howling at the same time is a voorloop (an apparition foreshadowing an event) of a death.
131153: A prediction of the place and time a house will burn down comes true.
131156: Wizards fix girls to the spot; with a wave of the hand they make their skirts fall down.
131157: The seller of a sheep that drowns shortly after the sale says he already knew it would happen.
131160: A sorcerer's fiddle playing makes little soldiers come out of the hearth pit, and they go back when he plays backwards.
131162: Being startled in the dark by horses on the roadside.
131163: A falling star is a voorloop (an apparition foreshadowing an event) of a death.
131167: The story of the foal with a porridge pot around its neck is known.
131170: A light in the sky is a portent of a later tramline.
131171: On seeing two white ghosts, a drunkard calls on God for help.
131172: A man often has to get up to see a funeral procession. The unknown person he once sees turns out to be himself.
131175: Someone who has sold himself to the devil has a boot with a daalder hanging in the place of the uilebord (owl board, a gable board with an opening under the roof). As soon as money is taken out of the boot, it is topped up again to a daalder.
131176: A foal with a porridge pot around its neck roams about.
131177: Transport of the Lange Sletteman on a cart drawn by seven horses.
131179: A witch was said to turn herself into a black cat.
131183: A farm is haunted: the churning mill turns at night, and beds that were made are a mess by evening.
131185: Haunting at an uninhabited farm where livestock still in the stable, though securely tied up, is soon loose again.
131187: Seeing will-o'-the-wisps or wild lanterns, which were later said to have been the first bicycle lamps.
131192: The ghost at a haunted spot is a man with a pitchfork of hay rising above low-lying mist.

210892: Several variants of sightings of the ghost called the Lange Sleatterman. A fisherman's daughter, while operating a small ferry, saw a man without a face. He chased her and she died two days later of fright. Someone else saw a man without a head and died of it. Later the apparition was seen many more times. When the skipper Sipke in the Mearssleat had looked the ghost in the face, he had the ship steered away from the bank at once, because he never wanted to see him again.
